aib-c01-d1-001@1.title: Distinguishing Prediction Operations from Model Updates
aib-c01-d1-001@1.prompt: The support department uses a model built from historical churn outcomes to calculate the churn probability of new customers every week. An executive believes that the model relearns recent churn patterns each time it calculates a probability. The operations team has not configured automatic updates. How should you explain this to the executive?

learning.reason: Inference uses a trained model to predict outcomes for new inputs. To update the model with recent outcomes, first confirm those outcomes, then run a separate training and update process that includes evaluation.
learning.concept: Distinguish inference during operations from model updates using confirmed new data.

A.text: Overwrite the prediction file every week and use its modification date as the record of the model update date.
A.explanation: Saving prediction results and updating the version of the model that generated them are separate operations.

B.text: Treat unconfirmed predictions as new ground truth and use them to reflect the latest churn in the next update.
B.explanation: A prediction cannot confirm whether churn actually occurred. Using it as-is can carry the existing model's errors into training.

C.text: The weekly calculation is inference using the existing model. Use confirmed outcomes for evaluation, and update the model through a separate training and approval process when needed.
C.explanation: Running a prediction does not change the trained parameters of the model.

D.text: Because the probabilities differ by customer, treat the model as having been retrained on each customer's information.
D.explanation: Predictions vary with different inputs even when the same model is used. Different values are not evidence of an update.

aib-c01-d1-002@1.title: Evaluating Demand Forecasts Separately from Staff Briefings
aib-c01-d1-002@1.prompt: A retail business wants to forecast next week's demand for each store as a number and also create a written explanation of the forecast and verified inventory data for staff. The forecast accuracy and the evidence supporting the written explanation must be validated separately. Which design is appropriate?

learning.reason: Numerical forecasts and explanatory text have different evaluation targets. Use a predictive model to forecast demand, then give generative AI that forecast and verified supporting evidence to produce the narrative.
learning.concept: Choose models for their respective purposes, and measure numerical accuracy and the evidence behind explanations independently.

A.text: Create a templated narrative from aggregated historical sales and treat the actual values as the forecast for the following week.
A.explanation: Describing what happened in the past does not validate the accuracy of an estimate of next week's demand.

B.text: Use predictive AI to estimate demand, then use generative AI to create an explanation from the result and verified inventory information. Measure forecast error and the narrative's supporting evidence separately.
B.explanation: Each output is produced with an approach suited to its purpose, making it possible to identify which stage failed.

C.text: Have generative AI produce the numbers and reasons together, then treat an easy-to-read narrative as evidence that the demand forecast is correct.
C.explanation: Readability does not show forecast error or the accuracy of the inventory information.

D.text: Measure only numerical forecast accuracy and do not check whether the narrative matches the figures or inventory information.
D.explanation: Even if the numbers are correct, the explanation may include unsupported information.

aib-c01-d1-003@1.title: Creating Training Data from Case-Linked Attachments
aib-c01-d1-003@1.prompt: A maintenance department wants to use AI to analyze a case table with defined columns and free-form PDF files for the same cases. Because the results will support incident reports, extracted content must be traceable to the original documents for later verification. The same equipment can have multiple cases on the same day. Which TWO actions should be taken first?

learning.reason: The case table has defined columns. Extract the text from the free-form documents, then retain stable case IDs and document references so extracted values can be validated and compared with their sources.
learning.concept: Ensure reliable linking and source traceability when combining data with different structures.

A.text: If the case table and PDF counts match, sort both by update time and join the items with the same row number.
A.explanation: Update order does not guarantee that the documents correspond, and cases for the same equipment on the same day could be mismatched.

B.text: Treat the free-form PDFs as structured data with the same columns as the case table, and skip extraction checks.
B.explanation: The layout of text and tables within a PDF is independent of the column definitions in the case table.

C.text: Save only the extracted values and delete references to the original documents.
C.explanation: Without identifying the original PDF, you cannot verify the content during an audit.

D.text: Verify the case IDs in the case table and use the IDs associated with the attachments to link them.
D.explanation: Using case IDs prevents different cases from being combined even when the equipment name and date are the same.

E.text: Treat the PDFs as sources of text to extract, retain references to the documents, and compare the extracted results with the originals.
E.explanation: This makes it possible to verify later that the extracted content came from the original document for the correct case.

aib-c01-d1-004@1.title: Keep unrecorded outcomes distinct from no attrition
aib-c01-d1-004@1.prompt: In a pilot to predict employee training attrition, some branches record completion or attrition outcomes late. A data analyst wants to treat cases with blank outcomes as “no attrition” and include them in training. What should the business owner prioritize?

learning.reason: An unobserved outcome must be distinguished from a confirmed negative label. Even with many records, differences in label collection across locations such as branches can lead to incorrect conclusions.
learning.concept: Distinguish confirmed positive and negative outcomes from outcomes that are still awaiting observation, and check data quality across collection channels.

A.text: Replace every blank with no attrition, then add rows until the counts are similar across branches.
A.explanation: Matching the counts still leaves inaccurate labels and can teach the model the wrong patterns for branches that report late.

B.text: Fill blanks with model predictions, then use that same data as ground truth for measuring prediction accuracy.
B.explanation: The predictions have not been checked against independent ground truth, so errors can go undetected.

C.text: Exclude all blanks from training uniformly across branches, and do not compare reporting patterns by branch.
C.explanation: This avoids treating blanks as ground truth, but it does not reveal whether evaluation is biased toward branches that report outcomes more readily.

D.text: Treat unrecorded outcomes as a distinct state, investigate reporting delays by branch, and rebuild training and validation sets using confirmed outcomes.
D.explanation: This avoids confusing the absence of an outcome with a confirmed case of no attrition.

aib-c01-d1-005@1.title: Check whether legacy records apply to a newly eligible group
aib-c01-d1-005@1.prompt: A municipal support center is considering a pilot model to predict repeat visits. Historical center data included only people who used an appointment-based service. Starting next month, people without appointments will also be eligible. A random split of the historical data showed high predictive performance. What should be done to support the rollout decision?

learning.reason: High performance on historical data supports conclusions about the groups represented in that data. If a newly eligible group was not included, evaluation requires new data that represents that group.
learning.concept: When the population served changes, do not expand coverage based only on a random split of historical data.

A.text: Cover all newly eligible people from the outset, omit appointment status from data collection, and report only the overall average.
A.explanation: An overall average can make poor performance for the newly eligible group hard to see.

B.text: Create records for people without appointments by duplicating records for people with appointments, assign the same outcomes, and use them to validate accuracy.
B.explanation: The outcomes of an independent new group have not been observed, so actual performance remains unknown.

C.text: Resplit the historical data using different random seeds and apply the best evaluation result to all people served.
C.explanation: Repeatedly splitting the data does not add members of the newly eligible group.

D.text: Collect confirmed outcomes in a small pilot that includes the newly eligible group, evaluate performance separately by appointment status, and then decide the rollout scope.
D.explanation: This provides evaluation outcomes for people who were not represented in the historical data, so the basis for rollout can be assessed.

aib-c01-d1-006@1.title: Choose a standard for ongoing AI management
aib-c01-d1-006@1.prompt: A company has begun using AI across several departments. Leadership wants to establish organization-wide AI policies, assign responsibilities, define review procedures, and keep improving its governance after deployment. The company wants requirements for an organizational AI management system, not a method for measuring a particular model’s accuracy. Which standard is appropriate?

learning.reason: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an organizational AI management system.
learning.concept: Choose a standard based on whether the subject is an individual model or the organization’s management system.

A.text: Refer to ISO/IEC 42001 to identify requirements for an organizational AI management system.
A.explanation: It addresses the organizational management system the company wants to establish and continually improve.

B.text: Refer only to the concepts and terminology in ISO/IEC 22989, without establishing responsibilities or review procedures.
B.explanation: A common vocabulary alone does not establish the organization needed to carry out management and continual improvement.

C.text: Refer only to ISO/IEC 23053 and treat its framework for AI systems that use machine learning as requirements for organization-wide governance.
C.explanation: A framework describing AI systems that use machine learning serves a different purpose from requirements for an organizational AI management system.

D.text: Set an internal threshold for model accuracy and treat it as the requirement for organization-wide AI governance.
D.explanation: Accuracy is an individual evaluation metric; it cannot replace organizational policies and assigned responsibilities.

aib-c01-d1-007@1.title: Separate fixed rules from tasks suited to AI
aib-c01-d1-007@1.prompt: The billing department has contractually defined payment caps, and the same input must always result in the same cap. By contrast, free-form emails from suppliers do not follow a consistent format for identifying the inquiry type or the information needed. Where should AI be introduced first while keeping processing explainable?

learning.reason: A fixed cap can be applied reproducibly using a known rule. AI can help classify and extract information from free-form inputs, with uncertain decisions routed to a person.
learning.concept: Separate deterministic processing, where variation in the result is unacceptable, from processing that needs interpretation of varied inputs.

A.text: Handle only emails with a specific string in the subject line, and leave the requirement to interpret free-form emails out of scope.
A.explanation: The decision would be repeatable, but the original problem of handling inputs with varied wording would remain.

B.text: Pilot AI for classifying free-form emails and extracting information, while applying the existing deterministic rules to payment caps.
B.explanation: This automates handling varied inputs while keeping the application of contractual caps reproducible.

C.text: Have the same predictive model handle both the cap check and email classification, and treat a probability in its output as confirmation of contractual compliance.
C.explanation: A prediction probability is not evidence that a clearly specified contractual cap has been applied.

D.text: Have generative AI estimate each payment cap and follow its most plausible response without using the contract rules.
D.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to apply the clearly specified cap consistently.

aib-c01-d1-008@1.title: Choose an AI that checks availability before taking action, and limit its permissions
aib-c01-d1-008@1.prompt: In the repairs department, staff read a customer’s preferred dates and times, check availability, and register a booking if it meets the conditions. The department wants AI to assist with this process, but only staff may approve bookings that incur an additional charge. Which design meets the requirements?

learning.reason: An AI agent can retrieve current information and perform permitted actions. The business system should control actions that require designated approval independently of the agent’s response.
learning.concept: Distinguish assistance that generates text from assistance that makes actual changes in an external system; put permission controls in place for the latter.

A.text: Use a text-generation tool that does not retrieve availability to draft a confirmation saying the booking is complete, then have staff verify it after sending.
A.explanation: The message would not be based on the actual booking result and could confirm a time that was never accepted.

B.text: Use only historical booking records to predict the preferred date and time as a number, then treat the booking as registered without checking availability.
B.explanation: A prediction from a model does not show current availability or confirm that a booking was registered.

C.text: Use an agent that can check availability and register bookings only when they meet the conditions, and require staff approval in the business system for bookings that incur an additional charge.
C.explanation: The agent can act based on the schedule, while the business system can control actions that must not be taken without approval.

D.text: Give the AI a shared account that can register any booking, and rely only on the instructions in its prompt to control decisions about additional charges.
D.explanation: The business system has no control to prevent the action if the prompt is not interpreted as intended.

aib-c01-d1-009@1.title: Detect degradation while waiting for outcome data
aib-c01-d1-009@1.prompt: A model predicting the risk of shipping delays is in production. The actual number of delays is not known until deliveries are completed, but the range of products handled has expanded, and the package information supplied at prediction time is beginning to change. The operations team wants to detect changes early while avoiding misguided retraining. Choose TWO appropriate actions.

learning.reason: Changes in input distributions and missingness can be observed before outcomes are finalized. Once outcomes are available, compare predictions with actual results to assess performance and decide whether an update is warranted.
learning.concept: Use early warning indicators that are available sooner alongside business outcomes that confirm model performance.

A.text: Conclude that the model has degraded as soon as the input composition changes, and retire the model without measuring its performance.
A.explanation: A change in inputs warrants investigation, but it does not confirm how much prediction error has worsened.

B.text: Once delivery outcomes are available, match predictions with actual results and evaluate errors by category, such as product, to decide whether to update the model.
B.explanation: This can also reveal whether the impact is concentrated in particular products and provide evidence for retraining.

C.text: Continuously monitor operational metrics so the team can investigate when input composition or missingness changes relative to the baseline.
C.explanation: This can reveal data changes that warrant investigation even before the outcomes are known.

D.text: Automatically retrain the model using its recent predictions as ground truth, and do not use completed-delivery outcomes for evaluation.
D.explanation: This treats the model’s output as the actual outcome and could preserve existing errors.

E.text: Do not monitor input data until all outcomes are available, and make decisions only at the end of each quarter.
E.explanation: This could miss issues that can be detected earlier and delay operational decisions.

aib-c01-d1-010@1.title: Reduce use of unapproved AI while keeping a path open for trials
aib-c01-d1-010@1.prompt: Several departments are independently trying external AI services that seem useful for work. The information management team wants employees to be able to tell which tools are approved for business use and which are being evaluated, and to submit requests. Some tools must not receive confidential information. Which response is most appropriate?

learning.reason: An organization can clarify each tool’s status, permitted uses, data inputs, and owner, and restrict evaluation to approved test data. A process for employees to check and submit requests can reduce unofficial use.
learning.concept: Make tool availability and data conditions visible in an inventory, with a formal path for exceptions and evaluation.

A.text: Maintain an inventory showing whether each tool is approved, under evaluation, or unavailable, along with permitted data; limit evaluation to a designated test environment and data, and make the request channel clear.
A.explanation: Employees can determine what they may use now, while safe trials and formal approval remain possible.

B.text: Track approval status only in the procurement department, and make employees decide individually whenever they look for a tool.
B.explanation: Information would remain fragmented across departments, making different choices about the same tool more likely.

C.text: Prohibit use of tools under evaluation and provide no way for employees to request alternative tools.
C.explanation: This also stops trials with clearly defined conditions and does not provide the formal trial pathway the requirements call for.

D.text: Automatically approve tools that many people use, and decide on restrictions for confidential information only after use begins.
D.explanation: Popularity does not indicate whether data handling or contract terms are safe.

aib-c01-d1-011@1.title: Distinguish decisions from open items when summarizing meeting notes
aib-c01-d1-011@1.prompt: A business user wants to extract decisions and their owners from meeting notes in a consistent format. The AI must not make up plausible content for items that were not decided or that have no owner. Which prompt improvement is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Specific instructions can identify the evidence to use, the output format, and what to do when information is unknown. The expected format can also be illustrated without using real data.
learning.concept: Specify in the prompt not only the output structure but also how to handle fields that lack supporting evidence.

A.text: Specify that only information in the notes may be used, define fields for decisions and owners, and include an example in which an owner that cannot be confirmed from the notes is marked “Unknown.”
A.explanation: This clarifies the evidence and output format, and tells the AI not to guess at undecided information.

B.text: Instruct the AI to fill every field, and have it infer an owner from past performance whenever one is not explicitly named.
B.explanation: This could present an owner who was never assigned as though that information were confirmed.

C.text: Write only “Summarize the important points clearly” and let the AI choose the required fields each time.
C.explanation: The result may be readable, but its fields and the treatment of unknown information would not be consistent.

D.text: Fix the list of decisions as a verbatim example and ask the AI to return that same text every time.
D.explanation: This preserves the format but does not extract results from meeting notes that differ each time.

aib-c01-d1-012@1.title: Reserve room for the answer when working with long documents
aib-c01-d1-012@1.prompt: A team used generative AI to compare proposals, but a request was rejected only when additional documents were included. The model's input and output share the same context limit, and the input alone is already close to that limit. Excluding appendices that are not needed for the comparison is allowed. What is the appropriate approach?

learning.reason: When input and output share a context limit, both the evidence-bearing input and the answer must fit. Prioritize relevant material and reserve room for the desired answer.
learning.concept: Select the most relevant input and leave room for output within the same limit.

A.text: Resend documents of the same length repeatedly, and use the answer only if every request is accepted.
A.explanation: This does not address the cause of exceeding the limit; retrying alone will not help.

B.text: Keep all documents in the input and increase only the output limit.
B.explanation: This does not create more room within the shared limit, so the required processing may still fail.

C.text: Shorten the input by prioritizing the clauses being compared and related passages, reserve enough room for the output, and then review the result.
C.explanation: This avoids using context on unnecessary appendices while preserving both the evidence needed for comparison and sufficient room for the answer.

D.text: Mechanically remove only the end of the documents without checking whether it contains important comparison criteria.
D.explanation: Even if this brings the request under the limit, it could remove necessary evidence or conditions and lead to a wrong conclusion.

aib-c01-d1-013@1.title: Separate changing business information from output style
aib-c01-d1-013@1.prompt: An assistant for employees answers questions about internal delivery terms and exceptions. The business policy is updated every week, and employees must be able to verify the relevant policy as the source of an answer. The answer style is already satisfactory. What is the appropriate approach?

learning.reason: Retrieval-augmented generation can use approved, updated documents as evidence at answer time. Training that changes a model's writing style does not automatically ensure access to current information or its sources.
learning.concept: When facts change frequently and source verification is required, retrieve approved information at answer time.

A.text: Make the approved policies searchable and use relevant passages and their sources when answering through retrieval-augmented generation.
A.explanation: This lets the searchable information reflect current evidence and makes it possible to verify the policy behind an answer.

B.text: Show only answers for which the model expresses confidence, without providing the source policy.
B.explanation: A high confidence level is not evidence that an answer is based on an approved document.

C.text: Fine-tune once on sample answers derived from an old policy, and do not reflect later policy updates in the model.
C.explanation: The model would have no way to retrieve the information it should use when asked about updated rules.

D.text: Fine-tune on a large number of past documents to standardize the writing style, and keep the latest policy separate from both training and search.
D.explanation: Even if the style becomes consistent, there is no path for using the latest policy as evidence.

aib-c01-d1-014@1.title: Align training-label meanings across policy changes
aib-c01-d1-014@1.prompt: A logistics department is considering automated decisions about returns from retailers. Under the old policy, “return accepted” included cases placed on hold; under the new policy, it means only final approval. The column name in the historical data is the same, and no records are missing. What should be done first to train for “final approval” under the new policy?

learning.reason: Labels with the same name cannot be combined as-is when their business meanings have changed. Define the new-policy target and align only historical records supported by evidence.
learning.concept: Check whether recorded decisions retain the same meaning across policy periods, not just whether labels are missing.

A.text: Write the new model's predictions as ground truth for old cases with unknown outcomes, then measure accuracy on those same cases.
A.explanation: The actual final decisions are not known, so this treats predictions as if they were ground truth.

B.text: Define the target label under the new policy, relabel only old cases with recorded final decisions using the same definition, and distinguish cases that cannot be determined.
B.explanation: This prevents different business decisions from being combined under one label just because the column name is the same.

C.text: Keep the old, more common definition and change the new-policy target after releasing the model.
C.explanation: The training target would not match current business decisions, and the meaning of the initial evaluation would be unclear.

D.text: Treat every old label as final approval under the new policy because the column name and value type match.
D.explanation: Matching types do not distinguish an old-policy hold from final approval.

aib-c01-d1-015@1.title: Why a model can predict for a case with no exact historical match
aib-c01-d1-015@1.prompt: A logistics company predicts the likelihood of a shipment being delayed using transit distance, day of dispatch, and load factor as inputs. A new delivery route at one branch has an input combination that has never appeared before. An employee believes the model cannot make a prediction because there is no historical delivery record with an exact match. Which statement most accurately explains how the model works?

learning.reason: A trained prediction model incorporates relationships between historical features and outcomes, so it can apply them to new inputs even when no historical row matches exactly. Validate performance under unfamiliar conditions with representative validation data.
learning.concept: Inference with a trained model differs from exact-match lookup and applies learned relationships to unseen combinations of features.

A.text: An actual delivery row for the new route with the same input values must be added so the existing model can use it the next time it predicts.
A.explanation: Actual results for the new route can help with validation or later training, but they are not required for the existing model to return a prediction.

B.text: As long as each input value falls within the range recorded during training, the model will achieve the same accuracy as on existing routes regardless of the combination.
B.explanation: Even when individual values are within range, accuracy can vary with the combination and surrounding conditions.

C.text: The model can apply relationships between the features and delays learned from historical data to new inputs.
C.explanation: Unlike exact-match lookup, the model can apply learned relationships even to new inputs.

D.text: When a combination is new, replace the model's prediction by taking an equally weighted average of the effects of the individual inputs.
D.explanation: The strength of the relationships learned from data can differ across inputs, so there is no basis for replacing the existing model with a simple average.

aib-c01-d1-016@1.title: Discovering inquiry trends that existing categories cannot capture
aib-c01-d1-016@1.prompt: A manufacturing company’s service department has received tens of thousands of free-text inquiries about a new product. The team wants to discover new complaints that do not fit its existing inquiry categories, then have specialists read representative examples and define category names. No data has yet been labeled with known category names as the correct answers. Which approach is most appropriate for an initial analysis?

learning.reason: Unsupervised clustering does not require known correct categories in advance. It forms candidate groups based on shared characteristics in the text. Reviewing representative examples helps confirm whether each category reflects a meaningful business distinction.
learning.concept: Use unsupervised clustering during exploration when correct labels are not available in advance, then have people interpret the groups.

A.text: Generate a proposed reply for each inquiry and infer unknown complaints from the proportion of replies that specialists accept.
A.explanation: The acceptance rate of proposed replies can reflect factors such as how useful the replies are, so it does not organize the actual topics of the inquiries.

B.text: Forecast the total number of inquiries for each product over time and treat the difference between forecasts and actuals as new inquiry categories.
B.explanation: Differences in counts alone do not reveal the content of the inquiries or provide new categories.

C.text: Train a classifier on the existing categories and identify new complaints from changes in the number of inquiries assigned to each category.
C.explanation: Changes in counts show variation within existing categories, but they cannot distinguish the content of new complaints.

D.text: Unsupervisedly group inquiries with similar meaning, then have specialists examine representative examples from each group and define candidate categories.
D.explanation: This explores undefined categories and lets people assign labels with business meaning afterward.

aib-c01-d1-017@1.title: Aligning the meaning of a field across business event versions
aib-c01-d1-017@1.prompt: A retail chain is combining older and newer inventory events to predict stockouts. Both versions are JSON and contain a quantity field, but the older version records the quantity of transactions, including returns, while the newer version records changes in the quantity available for sale in a store. The older version still contains the return type and sale-eligibility record. What should the chain do to provide the model with quantities that have the same meaning?

learning.reason: The same JSON field name does not necessarily have the same meaning. Check how the event version handles returns, use the stored fields to convert the values into changes in the quantity available for sale, and then use them for prediction.
learning.concept: Do not combine semi-structured events with version-dependent meanings based on data type alone. Convert them to a common definition while retaining their provenance.

A.text: Assign the average quantity from stores using the newer version to comparable stores using the older version, and exclude the return-type record.
A.explanation: Replacing actual values with store averages loses real transaction changes and discards available return information.

B.text: Retain the event version, map the return type and sale eligibility to changes in the quantity available for sale, and then combine both versions.
B.explanation: The stored fields can be used to represent the same business event, and the transformation can be traced back to the event version.

C.text: Concatenate both quantities into the same field and add the version number as a model input so the model can determine the difference in meaning.
C.explanation: Adding a version number as an input does not make different business definitions of the quantity equivalent.

D.text: Convert both quantities to the same numeric type and fill missing values with zero so the existing quantity fields can be compared as they are.
D.explanation: Matching the numeric type does not align whether returns are included in the quantity.

aib-c01-d1-018@1.title: Investigating why retry records distort prediction evaluation
aib-c01-d1-018@1.prompt: A travel company is evaluating a model that predicts booking cancellations. If an outage prevents an acknowledgment from being returned, the same booking event is sent again. Each row has a unique receipt number, but retries of the same event share a booking event ID, while genuine updates have different IDs. Production accuracy is lower than accuracy measured using a split at the message level. Which data measure should be taken first?

learning.reason: If retry rows for events used in training also appear in evaluation, performance on unseen events can be overestimated. Consolidating copies of the same event using the booking event ID also prevents inappropriate weighting.
learning.concept: Identify retries from the same business event before training to prevent duplicate counting and leakage across training and evaluation.

A.text: Consolidate retries into one record using the original booking event ID, then recreate the training and evaluation sets so the same event cannot appear in both.
A.explanation: Using independent events as the unit removes the bias from multiple copies and prevents overlap between training and evaluation.

B.text: Keep only the first event received for each booking ID, deleting genuine changes in the same way.
B.explanation: Using the booking ID would discard distinct update events, so it is better to use an ID that identifies the original event.

C.text: Keep rows with different receipt times as additional observations when they have the same booking event ID, and assign more of them to the evaluation set.
C.explanation: Treating retries as separate booking events leaves the weighting bias and overestimation in place.

D.text: Confirm that every row has a unique receipt number, then split the data into training and evaluation sets with equal cancellation rates.
D.explanation: Unique receipt numbers do not show that the rows came from different original events, so retries can end up in both sets.

aib-c01-d1-019@1.title: Observing outcomes among low-priority cases
aib-c01-d1-019@1.prompt: An equipment maintenance company uses a model to prioritize reports of anomalies. Currently, specialists review only high-priority reports and record whether an anomaly was actually present. After six months, the number of recorded missed anomalies has decreased, but almost no low-priority reports have been reviewed. Which approach is best for measuring the team’s pattern of missed anomalies?

learning.reason: Because which reports are reviewed depends on the model’s decisions, reviewed cases alone cannot reveal anomalies missed among low-priority reports. Continue collecting representative observations from low-priority cases and measure their outcomes against the full population before screening.
learning.concept: When AI screening biases which outcomes are recorded, include representative reviews of low-priority cases to keep measuring false exclusions.

A.text: Reduce specialist reviews and monitor only the distribution of input values and assigned priorities in the population to quantify the missed-anomaly rate.
A.explanation: Prediction and input distributions can signal changes, but the missed-anomaly rate itself cannot be measured without actual outcomes.

B.text: Sample low-priority reports while accounting for week and equipment category, and have specialists review the outcomes to keep measuring missed anomalies.
B.explanation: Obtaining outcomes from groups the model rated low makes it possible to estimate missed anomalies without relying only on the model’s selections.

C.text: Treat reports classified as low priority as confirmed non-anomalies, then check accuracy after reclassifying them on that basis.
C.explanation: Treating the model’s output as the correct answer prevents measurement of events the model missed.

D.text: Divide the number of confirmed anomalies among high-priority reports by the total number of reports, and consider missed anomalies stable if that proportion is stable.
D.explanation: The numerator excludes low-priority anomalies that have not actually been reviewed.

aib-c01-d1-020@1.title: Compare Prompt Revisions on Untouched Examples
aib-c01-d1-020@1.prompt: A benefits team revised a generative AI prompt that drafts answers from internal policies. The developer repeatedly adjusted instructions about policy exceptions while reviewing 20 cases that were easy to misinterpret. Before others use it, the team wants to determine whether the old or new version performs better on real inquiries. Which evaluation is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Improvement on the cases used to revise the prompt does not show whether it will handle unseen inquiries. Run both versions under the same conditions on representative cases kept separate from prompt tuning, then compare them using shared criteria.
learning.concept: Separate examples used to tune a prompt from unseen examples used to decide whether to adopt it, and compare the old and new versions using the same evaluation criteria.

A.text: Evaluate the old version on routine inquiries and the new version on inquiries involving exceptions, then compare the total scores assigned by each reviewer.
A.explanation: When the inquiries differ in difficulty, the results cannot show whether the prompt revision caused the difference.

B.text: Switch to a different AI model and randomization setting from those used during development, run the new version, and compare its score with the previously reported score for the old version.
B.explanation: Because the model and execution conditions also change, the effect of the prompt revision cannot be isolated.

C.text: Apply both versions to a representative set of inquiries that was not used for tuning, and compare policy compliance and supporting evidence using the same criteria.
C.explanation: Using the same untouched cases and criteria makes it easier to judge whether the revision is likely to improve performance in operation.

D.text: Compare success rates on the 20 cases used for tuning and report the increase in successful cases as the overall operational impact.
D.explanation: Because the instructions were tailored to those 20 cases, this does not evaluate improvement on the unfamiliar inquiries the system will encounter after adoption.

aib-c01-d1-021@1.title: Adapt a Model to Apply a Consistent Editorial Policy
aib-c01-d1-021@1.prompt: A technical communications team uses generative AI to draft product announcements based on facts supplied by staff. The model produces fact-based output, but even after tuning instructions and a small number of examples, it does not meet the review standard for applying the approved editorial policy's variations in emphasis and tone. The policy is stable, and the team has several thousand approved input-and-draft pairs. What is the most appropriate next evaluation?

learning.reason: The goal is to make editorial decisions consistent when drafting from supplied facts, rather than to retrieve updated facts. Adapt the model using validated input-and-output examples, then compare it with the current approach on examples excluded from training, measuring both compliance with the editorial policy and factual fidelity.
learning.concept: When instructions and examples no longer improve results, use supervised fine-tuning to teach a stable editorial policy, then check for improvements and side effects on held-out examples.

A.text: Try retrieval-augmented generation by adding the latest product documentation to each input, and compare the accuracy of product names in the announcements.
A.explanation: The required facts are already included in the input, and product-name accuracy does not evaluate whether the model applies the editorial policy appropriately.

B.text: Train on all approved examples and decide whether to release the model based on how closely regenerated drafts match the originals for those same examples.
B.explanation: Training and evaluating on the same examples does not show the quality of first-time announcements or whether facts are preserved.

C.text: Reduce generation randomness, measure how often the same input produces the same tone, and use that as the compliance rate for the editorial policy.
C.explanation: A consistent tone does not guarantee that the tone is appropriate for the editorial policy governing each announcement.

D.text: Try supervised fine-tuning on a portion of the approved input-and-output pairs, then compare editorial-policy compliance and factual fidelity on the remaining examples.
D.explanation: The model can be adapted using examples that encode the expected editorial decisions, while its effect on unseen inputs and retention of existing capabilities are assessed.

aib-c01-d2-001@1.title: Choose an Initiative That Addresses the Returns-Processing Bottleneck
aib-c01-d2-001@1.prompt: An online retailer wants to increase the percentage of initial responses to return requests sent by the next day. Analysis shows that the main cause of delays is the time staff spend looking up the approved return policy for each product after retrieving the order information. The policies are searchable, and staff will continue to make decisions about exceptions. Which initiative should the company try first?

learning.reason: The delayed step is looking up the policy. Show staff the relevant sections and draft a response, then measure the effect using processing time, including policy lookup, and the next-day response rate.
learning.concept: Identify the workflow step affecting the key performance indicator, then connect AI capabilities and available information to that step.

A.text: Predict which orders are likely to be returned based on browsing behavior before customers submit a request, and prioritize comparing prediction accuracy.
A.explanation: Improving predictions is a separate objective from reducing the time to send an initial response to a received return request.

B.text: Show staff the relevant policy sections for each order and product, and draft a response for them. Track the next-day response rate and response quality.
B.explanation: This can shorten the step causing the delay while also checking that responses follow the policy.

C.text: Forecast the total number of returns and evaluate the initiative using monthly forecast error.
C.explanation: This could help with staffing plans, but it does not measure improvement in the identified policy lookup step.

D.text: Publish summaries of product reviews and judge the effect on returns processing based on page dwell time.
D.explanation: This might improve purchasing information, but it is not connected to the time staff spend checking the policy.

aib-c01-d2-002@1.title: Choose a Sourcing Approach That Meets the Deadline and Exit Requirements
aib-c01-d2-002@1.prompt: A wholesaler wants to support summarization of confidential contracts within five months. It has business subject-matter experts but no staff to operate models. Data must not leave a designated Region, and evaluation data and configuration must be exportable in a portable form when the contract ends. Which proposal is the best fit?

learning.reason: Among the proposals that meet the delivery deadline, choose one whose contract covers the Region, deletion, and export requirements and whose quality can be assessed with a representative pilot.
learning.concept: Treat data constraints and portability as mandatory requirements, and compare proposals based on delivery time, cost, and in-house capabilities before contracting.

A.text: Contract with a partner that can start in two months and will meet the Region requirement, but negotiate data export terms shortly before the contract expires.
A.explanation: The required end-of-contract condition is not secured before the agreement is made.

B.text: Build and operate the solution in-house to control the Region and portability requirements. Hiring and preparing the infrastructure will take eight months.
B.explanation: In-house control has advantages, but this proposal does not fit the current capabilities or delivery deadline.

C.text: Use a provider that can deliver in four months, require in the contract that processing and deletion occur in the Region and that data can be exported in a standard format, and decide whether to proceed based on a pilot.
C.explanation: This approach allows the company to evaluate the deadline, controls, and continuity requirements together.

D.text: Choose the cheapest contract that can be delivered in three months. Some data will be processed outside the designated Region, and configuration cannot be exported.
D.explanation: The timing and cost are favorable, but the proposal fails both mandatory requirements.

aib-c01-d2-003@1.title: Choose which AI initiatives to scale, defer, or stop
aib-c01-d2-003@1.prompt: A utility provider is reviewing three pilots. Maintenance planning support reduces equipment downtime, a primary objective, and operations staff are available. Payment inquiry support is expected to create significant value, but the data cannot be used until the required user consent is obtained. Image generation for communications has reduced creation time, but the business it serves is being discontinued. How should the limited budget be allocated?

learning.reason: Scale an initiative when it has demonstrated value and is operationally feasible, defer one with a resolvable prerequisite and a review point, and stop one whose target business no longer exists.
learning.concept: Allocate resources by separating initiatives to scale, defer, or stop based on outcomes, constraints, and strategic fit—not a single accuracy score or past investment.

A.text: Scale maintenance planning, defer payment inquiry support until consent can be reassessed, and stop the communications image pilot.
A.explanation: This reflects each initiative’s results, constraints, and alignment with strategy.

B.text: Scale payment inquiry support and defer maintenance planning. Continue the communications image pilot to recover what has already been spent.
B.explanation: It cannot be scaled before consent is obtained, and past spending is not evidence of future value.

C.text: Convert the accuracy metrics for all three initiatives to the same scale and concentrate next period’s budget on the initiative with the highest score.
C.explanation: Accuracy does not represent business value, data constraints, or whether the business being served will continue.

D.text: Deploy communications image generation first and defer the other two initiatives until the operational workload decreases.
D.explanation: Even if it can be deployed quickly, it is unlikely to provide lasting value for a business that is being discontinued.

aib-c01-d2-004@1.title: Choose an improvement that addresses the source of defects
aib-c01-d2-004@1.prompt: At a beverage plant, every packaging defect repeatedly occurs at a particular position on an obsolete fixture. In a controlled trial under the same conditions, a replacement fixture eliminated the defects. Replacing all the fixtures costs half as much as implementing image recognition, and the goal is to reduce defect occurrence—not the number detected before shipment. Which initiative should be recommended?

learning.reason: The cause and the effectiveness of replacement have been confirmed, and replacement acts directly on the source of the defects. Image recognition can detect defects, but under these conditions it does not eliminate their cause.
learning.concept: When a physical cause in a process has been identified, correct the process itself before using AI to detect problems sooner.

A.text: Replace the fixtures in stages and verify the result by measuring the defect rate using the same criteria as before.
A.explanation: This directly addresses the cause and checks the effect on the target metric.

B.text: Use generative AI to rewrite the visual inspection procedure, then judge manufacturing quality by the rate at which inspectors follow it.
B.explanation: Compliance with the procedure does not remove the cause of packaging defects.

C.text: Implement image classification and determine whether the goal has been met by the defect detection rate among discarded products.
C.explanation: The detection rate does not show an improvement in the defect occurrence rate.

D.text: Predict when failures will occur, keep using only the old fixtures, and increase inspection on days when the predictions are correct.
D.explanation: The cause is known, and using the old fixtures will continue to produce defects.

aib-c01-d2-005@1.title: Compare an AI platform migration without interrupting operations
aib-c01-d2-005@1.prompt: A delivery company is migrating receipt processing to a different AI platform. It cannot stop receiving receipts during peak season, and duplicate entries for the same receipt would cause incorrect payments. The company wants to evaluate the new platform’s misreads and response latency under real operating conditions before switching over. Which two preparations are appropriate?

learning.reason: Do not use the new platform’s output to finalize entries; compare quality and latency using the same permitted inputs. During a staged migration, keep one platform as the write authority and define rollback thresholds and procedures.
learning.concept: Keep a single authoritative write path, compare old and new outputs in a non-committing shadow run, and establish rollback conditions.

A.text: Migrate if the cost savings are high, and collect evidence of peak-season latency only after operations have stabilized.
A.explanation: This does not use the required peak-season performance to make the migration decision.

B.text: Process the same receipts on the new platform without allowing it to create entries, and compare errors and latency by condition with the existing platform.
B.explanation: This enables comparison using real inputs without creating duplicate entries.

C.text: At each stage of the migration, designate one platform to create entries, and rehearse a rollback in advance for cases where quality or latency falls outside the thresholds.
C.explanation: This keeps a single platform responsible for writes while limiting the impact on operations.

D.text: Write both the old and new results to production records, then review the differences at month-end and cancel any unnecessary entries.
D.explanation: This fails to prevent duplicate payment entries before they occur.

E.text: Test the new platform only with receipts that have a structure tailored to it, then compare the results with all receipts processed by the old platform using overall averages.
E.explanation: The inputs differ in difficulty, making it hard to isolate differences caused by the platforms.

aib-c01-d2-006@1.title: Measure improved first-contact resolution and safeguard resolution quality
aib-c01-d2-006@1.prompt: A public transit support team uses an AI assistant to reduce repeat contacts from riders with the same fare inquiry. It wants to avoid metrics that can appear to improve simply because chats are closed quickly. Which combination of a primary KPI and quality guardrails is appropriate?

learning.reason: Track repeat contacts about the same issue to measure first-contact resolution, and use audited incorrect-guidance rates and riders’ resolution experience to detect a decline in quality.
learning.concept: Define business outcomes using observed events, and monitor customer experience with paired KPIs that guard against deterioration.

A.text: Use the rate of inquiries with no repeat contact about the same issue within a defined period as the primary KPI, with incorrect guidance rate and resolution satisfaction as guardrails.
A.explanation: The quality measures can show whether fewer repeat contacts reflect actual resolution or merely premature closure.

B.text: Use the total number of inquiries as the primary KPI and maintaining the monthly subscription fee as a guardrail.
B.explanation: This cannot distinguish seasonal changes or reduced access to support from a genuine improvement.

C.text: Use the number of seconds until a session ends as the primary KPI and the length of generated responses as a guardrail.
C.explanation: Session duration and response length do not measure whether an inquiry was resolved correctly.

D.text: Use the number of AI assistant invocations as the primary KPI and staff adoption rate as a guardrail.
D.explanation: Both measure usage or activity, not inquiry resolution or incorrect guidance.

aib-c01-d2-007@1.title: Establish a baseline before the busy season changes
aib-c01-d2-007@1.prompt: A travel company will pilot AI assistance for booking changes in the spring. Requests will surge in the summer, and the mix of partner airlines and request types will change. A department head wants to explain improvements in processing time as an effect of the AI assistant. What should the company do before deployment?

learning.reason: To reduce the effects of seasonality and case mix, first align the definitions of processing time and the cases being measured, then establish a comparison group that continues operating under similar conditions.
learning.concept: Define comparable units of work and measurement rules in advance, and design a comparison that can account for changes in seasonality and case complexity.

A.text: Use the average processing time at the location that improved the most after deployment as the baseline, and compare all locations against it.
A.explanation: Selecting a baseline after deployment biases the comparison and does not represent the pre-deployment state.

B.text: Use processing times from another department at the same travel company as the baseline, and start adding booking-change records only after deployment.
B.explanation: This does not isolate differences in the work or measure the target process before deployment.

C.text: Use only the company-wide average before deployment and the company-wide average the following summer, treating the larger sample as a more accurate comparison.
C.explanation: The effects of seasonality and differences in case mix remain unaccounted for.

D.text: Measure case-level processing times using the same definition before deployment, and use a phased rollout to track a comparable group that has not yet deployed the AI over the same period.
D.explanation: This allows seasonality, case complexity, and baseline differences to be considered when evaluating the difference.

aib-c01-d2-008@1.title: Convert increased sales to profit to calculate ROI
aib-c01-d2-008@1.prompt: In the first year of an AI assistant for preparing business-to-business quotes, actual outsourcing savings were ¥4.2 million, additional sales were ¥8 million, and the contribution margin on those additional sales was 25%. Implementation and training cost ¥1.5 million, and operations and quality-review cost ¥2.5 million; both costs were incurred only in the first year. No items other than costs were double-counted. Given ROI = (incremental benefits − incremental costs) ÷ incremental costs, what was the ROI for the first year?

learning.reason: Incremental benefits are ¥4.2 million + ¥8 million × 25% = ¥6.2 million, and costs are ¥1.5 million + ¥2.5 million = ¥4 million. Net benefits are ¥2.2 million, so ¥2.2 million ÷ ¥4 million = 55%.
learning.concept: Convert incremental sales to contribution margin, then calculate ROI using realized labor savings and all incremental costs.

A.text: 205%. Count all ¥8 million in additional sales and ¥4.2 million in outsourcing savings as benefits, then subtract ¥4 million in costs.
A.explanation: The additional sales must be converted to contribution margin of ¥2 million.

B.text: 55%. Convert additional sales to contribution margin, add the outsourcing savings, deduct implementation and operating costs, and divide by the costs.
B.explanation: This includes all incremental benefits and costs in the specified ROI formula.

C.text: 148%. Exclude the ¥1.5 million implementation cost and count only the ¥2.5 million operating cost as the investment.
C.explanation: Implementation and training costs in the first year are also incremental costs of the initiative.

D.text: 155%. Divide ¥6.2 million in benefits by ¥4 million in costs.
D.explanation: This is a benefit-cost ratio that does not use net benefits, so it is 100 percentage points higher than the ROI defined in the question.

aib-c01-d2-009@1.title: Spot early signs of sustained adoption
aib-c01-d2-009@1.prompt: A pilot has begun for AI-assisted document search in claims adjustment. The final metric, processing days, will not be known until six weeks later, when a claim closes. The conditions for eligible claims can be recorded. During the first two weeks, which is the most appropriate leading indicator for predicting future adoption?

learning.reason: Tracking the percentage of eligible claims on which handlers use the assistant on their own after an initial use makes adoption easier to assess than a one-time training attendance or login count.
learning.concept: Before final outcomes are available, track repeat use on eligible cases as an early signal of adoption in day-to-day work.

A.text: The percentage of handlers who, after completing an initial trial on an eligible claim, use the assistant again for real work the following week.
A.explanation: This leading indicator combines an appropriate denominator with repeat use.

B.text: The percentage of handlers who logged in to their devices on the first day of training.
B.explanation: This shows attendance, but does not capture signs of actual use on cases afterward.

C.text: The total number of tokens used by the AI assistant.
C.explanation: A small number of cases with heavy usage could increase this figure, so it is a weak measure of workplace adoption.

D.text: Company-wide profit per claim as of the financial close.
D.explanation: This is a lagging business outcome and will not be available for an early assessment during the first two weeks.

aib-c01-d2-010@1.title: Reduce inference costs while maintaining quality
aib-c01-d2-010@1.prompt: In document classification for an HR department, 80% of requests are standard forms and 20% are difficult free-text requests. In a pilot, a small model met the quality threshold for standard forms only, while a large model met it for both types. Select two actions that keep difficult requests from being missed more often while controlling costs.

learning.reason: If standard and difficult cases can be identified at the entry point, route each to a model that meets its quality requirement. Compare total cost per accepted result, including retries and human corrections.
learning.concept: Choose the lowest-cost path that meets requirements on representative cases, and monitor cost per completed case including reprocessing and human effort.

A.text: Move everything to the small model and declare savings based only on the per-token price, without monitoring results.
A.explanation: The small model does not meet the quality threshold for difficult requests.

B.text: Choose the model with the lowest monthly price regardless of request type, and treat a drop in response volume as evidence of quality drift.
B.explanation: Response volume cannot identify missed requests or classification quality.

C.text: Separate standard forms from difficult requests using entry criteria, route standard forms to the small model, and send difficult or unrecognized formats to the large model.
C.explanation: This uses a lower-cost path within the quality range established by the evaluation.

D.text: Shorten every request's input to the same length, send it to the large model, and measure cost alone.
D.explanation: This could remove important parts of the text and does not confirm that quality is maintained.

E.text: Compare accepted-result quality by request type and the cost per completed case, including retries and human review.
E.explanation: This can reveal cases where rework offsets savings from a lower unit price.

aib-c01-d2-011@1.title: Compare competitors’ AI capabilities against customer selection criteria
aib-c01-d2-011@1.prompt: At a B2B delivery company, losing bids has been attributed to the fact that explaining individual delays takes several hours. A competitor advertises a generative AI chatbot but has not published its explanation accuracy or how much time customers spend verifying the explanations. Which research would best inform an investment decision?

learning.reason: What differentiates a service is not the names of competitors’ features, but how well the company can improve the outcomes customers value. Test the quality and speed of explanations in light of contract terms and real operating conditions.
learning.concept: Evaluate why customers choose a provider and the difference the company can deliver, rather than counting competitors’ product features.

A.text: Buy the model with the highest score on a general-purpose benchmark and conclude that it will also outperform competitors on bid explanations.
A.explanation: General-purpose performance does not establish an advantage in the customer’s workflow.

B.text: Count the AI features listed on competitors’ websites and conclude that matching the feature count will reduce lost bids.
B.explanation: The number of features does not show how quickly or accurately explanations are produced.

C.text: Use competitors’ advertising spend as a guide for the company’s AI development budget and defer customer validation until after deployment.
C.explanation: Advertising spend does not reveal development scale or customer evaluation.

D.text: Ask customers who chose another provider about their selection criteria, then compare the time to produce accurate explanations for representative inquiries using an internal pilot and observable competitor results.
D.explanation: This ties specific reasons for customer decisions to outcome measures.

aib-c01-d2-012@1.title: Test whether the business can shift from selling equipment to selling uptime outcomes
aib-c01-d2-012@1.prompt: A machine-tool manufacturer can now predict the risk of downtime for installed equipment earlier. Customers value uptime more than buying additional machines, and the manufacturer is considering a new source of recurring revenue. Which is the most appropriate way to validate the business model?

learning.reason: Offer a service on a small scale that uses early warnings to maintain uptime, then measure willingness to pay for the outcome, delivery costs, and scope of responsibility. Those results help determine whether the new revenue model is viable.
learning.concept: Use AI-enabled operational capabilities to validate changes to customer value, pricing, and delivery responsibilities.

A.text: Distribute prediction results to the manufacturing department and determine whether assembly time for existing machines is reduced.
A.explanation: This tests internal efficiency, not a revenue model tied to uptime outcomes.

B.text: Add failure data to promotional materials and measure views while continuing to sell equipment as before.
B.explanation: This improves the existing sales approach but does not test willingness to pay for recurring revenue.

C.text: If failure-probability predictions are accurate, apply a uniform uptime guarantee to all customers without a pilot contract.
C.explanation: This does not establish repair capacity, warranty costs, or what customers will pay.

D.text: Pilot a maintenance contract with representative customers that includes an uptime target, and measure willingness to pay, on-site response costs, warranty scope, and actual uptime.
D.explanation: This tests the value offered, pricing, and responsibilities under real conditions.

aib-c01-d2-013@1.title: Build a lasting advantage with a commercially available model
aib-c01-d2-013@1.prompt: An equipment repair provider uses a general-purpose model that competitors can also buy. The provider has authorized records linking repair causes to subsequent recurrences, review procedures used by experienced technicians, and long-term contracts that vary by region. Beyond reducing the time spent on individual jobs, which strategy can build a hard-to-copy advantage?

learning.reason: Use traceable outcomes available only to the company to improve evaluation and operations. Accumulating knowledge about the conditions for applying those practices at each deployment site can create a lasting advantage.
learning.concept: Build an advantage from company-specific operational knowledge and authorized evaluation feedback that are updated continuously.

A.text: Treat the number of answers produced in the first month as the competitive advantage, then discontinue quality records to avoid the burden of maintaining them.
A.explanation: Answer volume does not show recurrence prevention, and discontinuing records makes it impossible to track whether the advantage is maintained.

B.text: Feed authorized repair outcomes and corrections from experienced technicians into evaluation, track improvements in recurrence rates, and continue building operational practices and knowledge.
B.explanation: Proprietary data and operational capabilities can drive continuous improvement.

C.text: Freeze regional best practices once during rollout and stop all subsequent updates so there is no need to adapt them by region.
C.explanation: This prevents the provider from responding to regional differences and changing failure patterns.

D.text: Contract for the largest general-purpose model currently available and assume the performance gap will be locked in before competitors can use the same model.
D.explanation: Competitors can procure the same model, and this approach does not build distinctive operational strengths.

aib-c01-d2-014@1.title: Stage investment in a market with low maturity
aib-c01-d2-014@1.prompt: Interest in using AI is growing for an inspection service serving regional water utilities, but customer spending, fit for the equipment being inspected, and local procurement rules are still unclear. Contracts for the existing service are stable, and the results of a regulatory pilot will be available in six months. How should the company structure its AI investment?

learning.reason: Test demand, feasibility, and regulatory fit in a limited phase, and set criteria for further investment with a decision date. This supports market learning while limiting spending that would be difficult to reverse.
learning.concept: Match small, reversible investments and decision gates to uncertainty about market adoption, pricing, and regulation.

A.text: Treat the number of competitors’ promotional posts as evidence of demand and redirect the renewal budget for existing contracts to AI without validation.
A.explanation: The volume of promotional activity is not evidence of customers’ willingness to pay or actual use.

B.text: Because the existing service is profitable, do not investigate customer needs or pilot results until procurement rules are standardized across all regions.
B.explanation: This delays market learning that could be obtained with limited effort.

C.text: Run a small paid pilot with representative customers, then review the next budget only if willingness to pay, field outcomes, and procurement conditions meet defined thresholds.
C.explanation: This reduces three major uncertainties early.

D.text: Sign long-term equipment contracts for nationwide coverage to secure a first-mover advantage, and measure fit after signing.
D.explanation: This commits to potentially irreversible costs while major market and regulatory uncertainties remain.

aib-c01-d2-015@1.title: Retaining business assets in-house while supplementing specialist skills
aib-c01-d2-015@1.prompt: A logistics software company wants to deliver, within four months, a capability that interprets each customer’s complex delivery commitments. Its contract rules and evaluation data are differentiating commercial assets, and its operational capabilities are still developing. A generic product cannot be customized to change the contract rules, while a fully in-house build would miss the deadline. Which approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Use a specialist partner to fill design and implementation gaps, keep proprietary rules and evaluation assets under the company’s control, and define operational handoff conditions from the outset.
learning.concept: Choose a partnership that separates the company’s differentiating assets from variable delivery work and includes operational handoff.

A.text: Approve a plan to build everything in-house to protect business knowledge, assuming the four-month deadline can be shortened.
A.explanation: This does not fit the currently known capability and schedule constraints.

B.text: Transfer ownership of the rules and evaluation data to a partner, and discuss how to operate the capability after the partnership ends only after the first release.
B.explanation: This puts control of differentiating assets and continuity at risk.

C.text: Keep the rules and evaluation data in-house and develop the capability with a specialist partner. Include acceptance criteria for operational documentation and handoff in the contract.
C.explanation: This supplements the missing skills while retaining proprietary assets and securing an operational handoff.

D.text: Prioritize the initial deadline and adapt the customer contracts to a generic product whose rules cannot be changed.
D.explanation: This discards a core requirement for the capability to interpret customer contracts.

aib-c01-d2-016@1.title: Comparing standalone benefits with assumptions shared across initiatives
aib-c01-d2-016@1.prompt: A medical device manufacturer has proposed separate AI initiatives in three departments to search product manuals. Each department has a mix of old and new editions, cannot identify the authoritative version, and has had repeated trials that return incorrect procedures. An initiative to establish approval and distribution of authoritative versions has no AI feature directly visible to users. How should the first-year budget be prioritized?

learning.reason: Establish identification of authoritative versions, which is a prerequisite for all the initiatives, and assess it as a condition for realizing their individual benefits. Validate the reuse scope and implementation costs.
learning.concept: Prioritize investment in a shared prerequisite by its dependencies and incremental portfolio benefits, rather than by a standalone KPI alone.

A.text: Concentrate the budget in the department with the most expected users and define a shared authoritative version only after that department starts giving incorrect guidance.
A.explanation: This begins rollout before the necessary quality condition is met.

B.text: Exclude the shared initiative because consolidating manuals will not increase the number of users of customer-facing AI.
B.explanation: This ignores a prerequisite for downstream initiatives to return correct procedures.

C.text: Prioritize authoritative-version management as a shared foundation, and include avoided costs and the benefits it enables when reused across all three initiatives in the financial assessment.
C.explanation: This restores procedural correctness and accounts for avoided duplicate investment.

D.text: Allocate equal funding to each department, have each create a separate authoritative-version system, and then share them company-wide.
D.explanation: This duplicates controls for the same materials, leaving inconsistencies and costs.

aib-c01-d2-017@1.title: Connecting predictions to real dispatch decisions
aib-c01-d2-017@1.prompt: A regional home-repair company wants to reduce same-day cancellations caused by arrival delays. It can act only before dispatch is finalized in the morning, and it has one spare vehicle. It has records of past visit times and customer communications. Which AI initiative should it pilot, and how should it primarily evaluate the results?

learning.reason: Use information available in the morning to predict delays and apply the limited spare resource to dispatch decisions. Measure improvement through actual cancellations and on-time arrivals.
learning.concept: Choose a prediction use case that fits the decision time, available interventions, and customer outcomes.

A.text: Forecast monthly booking volumes quarterly and use forecast error as the primary metric.
A.explanation: This may help with staffing or budget planning, but it does not support daily priority dispatch decisions.

B.text: Predict delay risk in the morning and recommend assigning the spare vehicle to a dispatcher. Compare same-day cancellations and on-time arrivals.
B.explanation: This measures customer outcomes at a point when intervention is possible, given the resource constraint.

C.text: Automatically draft delay notifications and measure open rates only for jobs whose arrival delay has been confirmed.
C.explanation: This can measure improvements to notifications, but not the cancellations that the spare vehicle might have prevented.

D.text: Generate reasons for delays across all visits in the evening and use the review approval rate of the summaries as the primary metric.
D.explanation: This may help analyze causes, but it cannot improve that day’s dispatch decisions.

aib-c01-d2-018@1.title: Checking data and contractual continuity before replacing an AI platform
aib-c01-d2-018@1.prompt: An insurer is updating its document-classification AI. Trials on the new platform achieved higher accuracy and processing speed than the current platform, but the current contract requires processing evidence to be retained for three years. Historical outputs and references to their supporting evidence can be migrated, but the two platforms handle document identifiers differently. What should be validated before deciding whether to proceed with the update?

learning.reason: Confirm that contractual retention, evidence retrieval, and auditing can continue, and that differences in identifiers do not break evidence links. Include migration and ongoing operating costs.
learning.concept: Evaluate a platform change based not only on API responses but also on history interpretation, audit continuity, and switching costs.

A.text: Migrate only the latest results, then regenerate older evidence from sample documents if it is needed.
A.explanation: This does not meet the contractual requirement to retain the evidence supporting results at the time they were produced.

B.text: End the current contract because accuracy is higher, assuming the old platform’s evidence will remain accessible after termination.
B.explanation: This assumes, without confirmation, that evidence can still be accessed and recovered after termination.

C.text: Make the old document IDs appear to match during migration, and treat matching total counts of successful records as proof that the associations are correct.
C.explanation: Matching counts alone cannot detect incorrect links between individual histories and documents.

D.text: Migrate representative histories and reproduce evidence retrieval and audits; reconcile ID conversions and compare costs including migration, retention, and operations.
D.explanation: This verifies contractual compliance, data meaning, and continuity of costs.

aib-c01-d2-019@1.title: Measure staff time and user confidence separately
aib-c01-d2-019@1.prompt: A disaster-response office is piloting AI to summarize field reports. Executives want to reduce the total staff time spent by surge personnel. Field teams also value confidence that handoffs will not omit important information. Choose two KPIs that together can assess both goals.

learning.reason: Track a quantitative measure of the staffing burden alongside handoff recipients’ confidence and perceived workload under comparable conditions. This makes improvements of different kinds visible without conflating them.
learning.concept: Track monetary benefits and employee-experience benefits with separate measures to avoid careless double counting.

A.text: Total surge-staff time for incidents of similar scale, including time spent reviewing and correcting summaries.
A.explanation: This measures the staffing burden across the full process.

B.text: Regular survey results from staff receiving handoffs about their confidence that required information was transferred without omissions and their perceived workload.
B.explanation: This measures an experience that is difficult to quantify from the people who actually handle handoffs.

C.text: The number of summaries generated during training and the number of prompt updates.
C.explanation: These measure activity, not the workload or outcomes experienced during incidents.

D.text: The inference cost per unit multiplied by the surge staff's hourly rate.
D.explanation: Multiplying unlike units does not measure labor time or benefit.

E.text: The number of words in each summary and its compression ratio relative to the original report.
E.explanation: These describe output format but do not reveal actual work time or confidence.

aib-c01-d2-020@1.title: Establish baselines for AI and surrounding workflow steps
aib-c01-d2-020@1.prompt: A payment-inquiry team wants AI to route cases faster. By design, some requests require a separate department to perform a manual supplemental review after routing. The team currently records only the median time from intake to completion for the entire request. What should it measure now to assess the impact of introducing AI?

learning.reason: In addition to end-to-end time, distinguish routing, rework caused by misrouting, and supplemental reviews by another department. Compare cases of the same type.
learning.concept: Establish a pre-implementation baseline for the target step and the steps around it to avoid mistaking transferred work for an efficiency gain.

A.text: Record the types of cases involved and, before implementation, measure separately the time spent routing, correcting misroutes, performing supplemental reviews, and completing the case.
A.explanation: This enables comparisons under the same conditions and captures both benefits and added workload.

B.text: Keep only the completion time for all current cases, then assess impact using only the routing staff's work time.
B.explanation: The measures would not be comparable, and any review work shifted to another department could be missed.

C.text: After implementation, record only cases deemed suitable for AI and treat all other workflow steps as unrelated to the improvement.
C.explanation: There would be no pre-implementation comparison, and the impact on surrounding steps would remain unknown.

D.text: Set targets for each routing employee and use the difference from those targets in place of pre-implementation results.
D.explanation: Targets are not measured baselines, and they do not reveal workload arising in surrounding steps.

aib-c01-d2-021@1.title: Calculate the minimum volume including quality-review costs
