aib-c01-d2-021@1.prompt: AI review of export documents reliably saves ¥600 in outsourcing costs for each accepted case. Usage-based costs, including failed inference attempts, and exception-review costs are estimated at ¥200 per accepted case combined. Annual fixed costs are ¥2.4 million, and there are no other costs or benefits. What is the minimum number of accepted cases needed for the first year's net benefit to be zero or greater?

learning.reason: Net benefit per case is ¥600 − ¥200 = ¥400. Dividing the ¥2,400,000 fixed cost by ¥400 gives 6,000 cases, which is the break-even point.
learning.concept: Calculate break-even volume by separating fixed costs from net benefit per successfully processed case.

A.text: 6,000 cases. Divide fixed costs by the savings per case after subtracting usage and exception-review costs.
A.explanation: This accounts for both fixed costs and costs that vary with case volume.

B.text: 12,000 cases. Divide fixed costs by the ¥200 usage and exception-review costs.
B.explanation: The denominator must be the benefit after usage costs, not the costs alone.

C.text: 4,000 cases. Divide fixed costs by the ¥600 outsourcing savings.
C.explanation: This omits the ¥200 in usage and exception-review costs per case.

D.text: 3,000 cases. Divide fixed costs by adding the ¥200 usage and exception-review costs to the ¥600 savings.
D.explanation: Adding usage costs to the benefit overstates the net benefit from each accepted case.

aib-c01-d2-022@1.title: Test whether another team can succeed without assistance
aib-c01-d2-022@1.prompt: A search AI for contract staff reduced time in a pilot department. However, the pilot lead reset the configuration on behalf of users every day for difficult questions. Executives want to decide before the quarter whether the results can be reproduced in the next department, where they cannot add the same support staff. Which measure would be most useful?

learning.reason: Under normal day-to-day procedures, the share of cases that meet quality and time standards without the pilot lead resetting configurations shows early evidence of post-deployment workload and reproducibility.
learning.concept: Use the proportion of cases meeting standards without routine help from the pilot lead as a leading indicator of readiness to scale.

A.text: The total number of searches, including those handled by the pilot lead.
A.explanation: This does not distinguish dependence on an expert from results that meet the required standards.

B.text: The department-specific realized profit recorded at the end of the quarter after full launch.
B.explanation: This becomes known only after broad deployment, too late for the decision before rollout.

C.text: The proportion of eligible cases in which representative staff in the next department meet quality and time standards using only their normal procedures.
C.explanation: This provides an early measure of reproducible results and dependence on support during expansion.

D.text: The maximum search accuracy achievable when the lead operates the system with optimized settings.
D.explanation: This does not measure performance when the expert is not providing routine support.

aib-c01-d2-023@1.title: Control Costly Reprocessing During Peak Periods
aib-c01-d2-023@1.prompt: AI classification costs for reports spike at the beginning of each month. Even on days when the number of completed reports is the same, the total number of executions rises severalfold. Logs show that a new job is submitted as a new process every time a timeout occurs, but many of the earlier processes succeed later. What should you do first to control costs while maintaining the intake deadline and quality?

learning.reason: Check whether processing is complete before retrying, and use the processing ID to account for each report as completed once. A retry limit and exception handling near the deadline help control unbounded costs.
learning.concept: Identify the source of cost overruns and reduce duplicate jobs and retries before negotiating unit prices.

A.text: Unconditionally discard reports that are close to their deadline and keep the total number of calls at the beginning of the month equal to the previous year.
A.explanation: Reports that must be processed by the intake deadline will be lost.

B.text: Before retrying, check whether a report’s processing ID is in progress or complete; set a retry limit and a handoff process for reports near their deadline, and track cost per completed report.
B.explanation: This reduces duplicate processing while measuring both missed work and cost.

C.text: Increase every timeout and compare only monthly charges, without counting processes that complete late.
C.explanation: Changing timeout values alone does not ensure that jobs are checked against work already in progress, and the effect on deadlines remains unclear.

D.text: Increase the daily budget to match the cost spike and consider only a new contract that lowers the cost per call.
D.explanation: The main cause—unnecessary processing of the same report—remains.

aib-c01-d2-024@1.title: Choose Investments That Differentiate in a Mature Market
aib-c01-d2-024@1.prompt: In the enterprise meeting-minutes service market, transcription accuracy and price have converged across competitors. Customers now base renewal decisions on integration with internal approval workflows and the ability to meet specified retention periods. Your core transcription service already meets contractual requirements. How should you allocate a limited investment budget for next year?

learning.reason: Maintain baseline functionality that offers little differentiation at the required quality level, and validate investment in integrations and retention capabilities that affect renewals.
learning.concept: In a market where technology has become commoditized, provide general-purpose features at low cost and invest further in complementary assets customers value.

A.text: Rebuild a general-purpose model from scratch and choose investments based solely on general-purpose accuracy, separately from existing customers’ reasons for renewing.
A.explanation: There is no evidence that additional accuracy will drive renewals, and this ignores the selection criteria of integration and retention.

B.text: Stop all further development because the market is mature, and continue having employees handle approval integrations manually.
B.explanation: This gives up opportunities to improve conditions that matter to existing customers.

C.text: First decide to spend the same share of revenue on model research as competitors, then fit integration costs into the remaining budget.
C.explanation: It is more effective to base investment on the conditions that support your customers’ renewals than on competitors’ spending ratios.

D.text: Maintain transcription quality at the level required by the core service, validate approval and retention integrations with customers, and invest according to their effect on renewal rates.
D.explanation: This separates general-purpose functionality from customer-specific selection criteria and directs investment to areas that create value.

aib-c01-d3-001@1.title: Investigate differences in missed-eligibility rates hidden by averages
aib-c01-d3-001@1.prompt: A municipality uses AI to identify households to receive information about a benefits program for which they may be eligible. Overall accuracy is high, but reports indicate that many eligible households in one region are not being notified. Independently verified eligibility data is available for review. Which metric should be compared first?

learning.reason: The issue is failure to notify eligible households. Use independently verified eligible households as the denominator for each region and compare the proportion that was not notified.
learning.concept: Measure fairness in terms of the specific harm to the affected population by evaluating group-specific missed-eligibility rates among eligible people.

A.text: The proportion of all households, regardless of region, for which the notification decision was correct.
A.explanation: An overall aggregate can hide missed cases in some regions.

B.text: Compare by region the proportion of independently verified eligible households that were not notified.
B.explanation: This directly measures the relevant false negatives using eligible households as the denominator.

C.text: Compare by region the proportion of notified households that agreed with the information.
C.explanation: Households that were not notified are excluded from the denominator.

D.text: The proportion of all residents in each region who received a notification.
D.explanation: If the share of eligible residents differs by region, this cannot identify differences in missed notifications.

aib-c01-d3-002@1.title: Resolve the Conflict Between Promotional Results and Permitted Use
aib-c01-d3-002@1.prompt: A subscription provider is testing AI-generated promotional copy to improve paid subscription retention. Using free-text responses from its customer support channel increases response rates, but permission to use those records is limited to handling inquiries. The customer’s subscription status and interest categories approved for promotional use are available. What is the appropriate decision?

learning.reason: Limit inputs to those approved for the current purpose and retest whether promotional performance can improve. Obtain appropriate approval and justification before using data for a new purpose.
learning.concept: When short-term KPI gains conflict with permitted purposes of use, adapt the approach and validate value within the applicable constraints.

A.text: Reevaluate using only the approved subscription status and interest categories, and obtain approval in advance if expanding the permitted use of free-text responses.
A.explanation: This lets you evaluate an approach that complies with the current restrictions.

B.text: Have employees read the free-text responses and manually transfer them into the AI input. Do not record the source in the promotional records.
B.explanation: Adding a manual step does not change the permitted purpose of use.

C.text: Remove only names from the free-text responses and use them in promotional copy without recording that the purpose of use has changed.
C.explanation: Removing names alone neither eliminates personal information in the records nor removes the restriction on permitted purposes.

D.text: Use the original responses for a small number of customers, then request a change in the permitted purpose after response rates improve.
D.explanation: The current scope of permitted use must be respected even for a small-scale test.

aib-c01-d3-003@1.title: Build a challenge process into planning
aib-c01-d3-003@1.prompt: A training company wants to use AI to prioritize corporate training applications. Seats are limited, and applicants who are not selected may ask for a review. The data fields and pilot scope have not yet been decided. When and what should be decided so that explanations and reviews can actually be provided?

learning.reason: At the design stage, include the impact of decisions, the grounds that must be recorded, what applicants will be told, and who will review cases and by when. Without collecting the appropriate information, it may not be possible to reconstruct the grounds after launch.
learning.concept: Define decision impacts, required evidence, and the challenge process during requirements definition to prevent gaps in the evidence discovered only after launch.

A.text: During requirements definition, decide which decision grounds to record, how applicants will be notified, and who is responsible for manual reviews and by when; then verify the process in the pilot.
A.explanation: This incorporates evidence, notification, and review into both the functional and operational design.

B.text: Publish a general explanation of the AI at launch, and create a process for reviewing individual decisions only after the number of users grows.
B.explanation: A general explanation does not provide the grounds for an individual decision or a concrete review process.

C.text: After confirming that the pilot has high accuracy, add evidence retention only for applications that were accepted.
C.explanation: This fails to retain the evidence needed by rejected applicants who request a review.

D.text: Collect all data fields first, then decide what information and retention requirements are needed if complaints arise.
D.explanation: This can lead to unnecessary collection and may leave out information needed to explain decisions later.

aib-c01-d3-004@1.title: Escalate to a person when policy evidence conflicts
aib-c01-d3-004@1.prompt: An AI assistant for insurance benefit inquiries can cite a passage from a policy in its response. If the customer's plan is unknown, or multiple policies with different effective dates are retrieved, incorrect guidance could cause the customer to miss the opportunity to file a claim. Choose two measures that should be taken in practice.

learning.reason: Detect conflicting evidence or missing applicability conditions, withhold a definitive response, and hand off the candidate evidence, differences in effective dates, and points to verify to a staff member.
learning.concept: When evidence conflicts or is missing for a high-impact response, hold the answer and send the information needed for a decision to a staff member.

A.text: If the generative model gives itself a high confidence score, send the response without checking which policy applies.
A.explanation: Self-assessment alone cannot resolve conflicting evidence or missing input.

B.text: Send the policies consulted, their effective dates, the unverified plan information, and the response deadline to a staff review queue.
B.explanation: A person can resolve the missing information and prioritize the case to help protect the customer's opportunity to file a claim.

C.text: List multiple policies in the response and ask the applicant to choose which one applies to them.
C.explanation: This leaves an uncertain, high-impact decision to the applicant.

D.text: If the applicable conditions cannot be confirmed or the evidence conflicts, withhold definitive guidance and respond that confirmation is pending.
D.explanation: This reduces the chance that incorrect guidance caused by missing conditions will be sent.

E.text: Send the guidance if the response meets readability standards, even when the policies conflict.
E.explanation: Readability does not guarantee that the benefit conditions are correct.

aib-c01-d3-005@1.title: Let the committee advise and the designated approver decide
aib-c01-d3-005@1.prompt: An AI review committee at a retail group meets weekly and includes representatives from legal, privacy, technology, and operations. After an incident, no one made the decision to stop the system or notify the affected department because everyone thought they were there only to advise. What should be the top priority in the next operational change?

learning.reason: Keep expert participation in the review, while assigning an accountable business owner for each system, defining who can approve or stop it, and setting deadlines for notifications and remediation.
learning.concept: Separate cross-functional advice from specific approval and remediation responsibilities, and make the authority to stop a system during a serious incident explicit.

A.text: Designate an accountable owner and on-call authority to stop each service, and document the process for committee advice, notifications, and remediation.
A.explanation: This clarifies who decides and coordinates while still using the committee's expertise.

B.text: Increase attendance and allow the system to be stopped only when everyone agrees.
B.explanation: This does not identify a single responsible person or delegate, even when an immediate decision is needed during a serious incident.

C.text: Because the provider makes technical decisions while the service is running, have the contract management team handle questions about the company's authority to stop it.
C.explanation: The provider's technical response is separate from the company's responsibility to stop using the service and notify stakeholders.

D.text: Discuss whether to stop the service only when the AI committee meets, and let each department make its own decision until then.
D.explanation: This leaves the authority and communication path needed for immediate action undefined across the organization.

aib-c01-d3-006@1.title: Verify the controls that remain the company's responsibility after outsourcing
aib-c01-d3-006@1.prompt: A company plans to outsource summaries of payment operations to an external AI provider. Its internal policy requires processing in specified regions, deletion after a set number of days, equivalent controls at the provider's subprocessors, and evidence for audits. What should the procurement lead do before approving production use?

learning.reason: Verify that each obligation is reflected in procurement terms and the actual configuration and operations, and define how evidence covering the provider and subprocessors will be obtained and updated.
learning.concept: Turn the stated control obligations into provider contract terms, technical settings, and processes for obtaining and reviewing evidence.

A.text: Obtain the provider's general certification and skip checking whether it covers the planned service and subprocessors.
A.explanation: This does not establish whether the certification covers this processing or whether the specific control obligations are met.

B.text: Translate the obligations into contract clauses and verification criteria, validate evidence for the relevant service and subprocessors, and review them again when things change.
B.explanation: This connects the contract, actual implementation, and ongoing evidence for the decision.

C.text: If communications can be encrypted, request evidence of processing regions and deletion only during an audit.
C.explanation: Encryption does not guarantee processing regions, retention periods, or access to evidence.

D.text: Record the provider's self-attestation once, but do not recheck it when the contract is renewed or a subprocessor changes.
D.explanation: This does not verify that the controls remain in place after changes.

aib-c01-d3-007@1.title: Preserving access permissions in cross-department search
aib-c01-d3-007@1.prompt: An internal document search AI will ingest company-wide policies and documents restricted to HR staff. Sensitive information must not appear in search results or answers when an unauthorized employee asks a question. Document permissions change when employees transfer departments. Which measure should be adopted?

learning.reason: Apply the authenticated user's current document permissions on the server before search. Restricting retrieval first prevents unauthorized document content from reaching the answer-generation process.
learning.concept: Restrict search results using the authenticated user's current access rights, enforcing those rights before processing document content.

A.text: Search all materials first, then instruct the generative AI to hide HR-related content.
A.explanation: Unauthorized materials have already been passed to search and generation, leaving access enforcement dependent on instructions alone.

B.text: At search time, check the user's identity and current document permissions, and pass only authorized documents to retrieval and generation.
B.explanation: Authorization is enforced before documents are retrieved, and the controls can reflect permission changes.

C.text: Give the search account permission to view all materials, and simply omit document links from the AI's answers.
C.explanation: Hiding links does not prevent sensitive information from being disclosed in the answer itself.

D.text: Record each employee's department once at ingestion and continue using the old department's permissions after a transfer.
D.explanation: Those permissions would no longer match the employee's current work authorization.

aib-c01-d3-008@1.title: Varying the level of review by use case, even for the same model
aib-c01-d3-008@1.prompt: A transit company plans to use the same generative model to draft summaries of internal meetings and to help notify customers about alternative operating plans. For the latter use case, the company is also considering sending messages without staff approval, and an incorrect notification would directly affect passengers' travel. Which classification policy is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Evaluate each use case based on its business context, impact, human oversight, and the reversibility of errors. Apply stricter approval and stop conditions to automated external notifications.
learning.concept: Set risk classifications based on impact on affected people, reversibility of actions, and the level of oversight, rather than applying one classification to a model name.

A.text: Classify the two use cases solely by their peak accuracy at approval time, and use the same review process if their accuracy is equal.
A.explanation: Even if accuracy is equal, the consequences of an error differ.

B.text: Because the model has already been approved for internal documents, carry over the same risk classification to external notifications.
B.explanation: Internal approval did not assess the direct impact on passengers or automated sending.

C.text: Always classify the use case with the highest processing volume as the highest risk, without assessing the impact of a single error.
C.explanation: Volume alone does not capture severity or recoverability.

D.text: Assess each use case by its impact on customers and whether a person approves the action, and require stronger review for external notifications sent without approval.
D.explanation: The impact of errors and the available controls can vary by deployment, even when the model is the same.

aib-c01-d3-009@1.title: Establishing operational procedures to stop serious production issues
aib-c01-d3-009@1.prompt: An AI system that provides corporate billing guidance can cause customers to submit requests for incorrect amounts if erroneous answers spread quickly. Sample-based quality audits can be performed hourly, and a backup manual support channel is ready. Which operational measure is needed before formal production launch?

learning.reason: Set an immediate alert threshold for serious incorrect guidance and give designated staff the authority to switch channels. Rehearse the manual fallback and the criteria for recovery in advance.
learning.concept: Connect operational metrics to thresholds, on-call ownership, shutdown, and restart conditions instead of treating them as records alone.

A.text: Define a threshold for serious incorrect guidance and assign on-call staff; rehearse switching to the manual support channel and resuming service after corrective checks.
A.explanation: This connects monitoring directly to limiting customer impact and recovery.

B.text: Notify staff about serious incorrect guidance, but decide on the spot which manager to find before switching to the manual support channel.
B.explanation: Response authority is unclear, which can delay the switch.

C.text: Send alerts only if availability drops, and do not audit content while the system is responding normally.
C.explanation: Incorrect amounts can be communicated even when availability is good.

D.text: Save hourly quality records and decide on a shutdown procedure at the month-end meeting if there has been a large change.
D.explanation: Serious incorrect guidance could increase while waiting until month-end.

aib-c01-d3-010@1.title: Tracing where bias arises instead of examining only the downstream model
aib-c01-d3-010@1.prompt: A telephone support AI transcribes speech and then summarizes the conversation. The summarization model has not changed since launch, but since an update to speech processing, there have been recurring reports that reservation details are missing from summaries for customers with certain speech patterns. What is the most appropriate way to investigate the cause and its progression using support records for which use is authorized?

learning.reason: For the same call, compare staff-verified audio, the transcription, and the summary stage by stage to find where details are omitted. Continue checking for differences by customer speech characteristics and processing version, including after updates.
learning.concept: Even with the same summarization model, upstream audio preprocessing can introduce bias. Track changes in each input path and errors at each processing stage.

A.text: Exclude calls that already have omissions in the transcription from the aggregate, then have people evaluate only the remaining summaries.
A.explanation: This would exclude the suspected preprocessing impact from the evaluation.

B.text: Confirm that the summarization model version and training data have not changed, and conclude there is no bias impact if they have not.
B.explanation: If upstream speech processing changes input quality, results can change even with the same summarization model.

C.text: Track only overall summary quality and complaint rates, and do not investigate speech processing if those figures are within acceptable ranges.
C.explanation: Omissions concentrated among a small group of customers may not appear in aggregate metrics, which also do not identify where the issue occurs.

D.text: For the same calls, compare the audio content verified by staff, the transcription, and the summary to identify the stage where information is omitted. Continue monitoring differences by speech pattern and processing version.
D.explanation: This isolates the stage affecting particular customers and makes it possible to investigate recurrence after future changes.

aib-c01-d3-011@1.title: Reviewing rights and harmful content in generated promotional assets
aib-c01-d3-011@1.prompt: A manufacturer is creating generated images for a trade show. Some product photos that could be used as references are licensed for internal review only and cannot be used as production assets for external audiences. There are also concerns that generated images may contain third-party logos or derogatory content. Choose two measures to take before publication.

learning.reason: Use only materials whose permissions cover both generation and external production, then review outputs for third-party marks and harmful content.
learning.concept: Manage input permissions separately from output risks, and check for similarity and harmful content before publication.

A.text: Check only for harmful content, and treat any third-party logo as authorized at the production team's discretion.
A.explanation: This does not verify rights to the logo or the conditions for displaying it.

B.text: Review publication candidates for harmful content, third-party marks, and conspicuous similarity, and hold any questionable assets for review.
B.explanation: This can catch issues in outputs even when inputs were controlled.

C.text: Use generated results regardless of the input materials' contractual limits, as long as their pixels differ from the original photos.
C.explanation: Pixel differences do not remove contractual restrictions on the source materials.

D.text: Measure complaint volume after publication and skip asset review if there are few complaints.
D.explanation: This cannot prevent avoidable content or rights issues from being published.

E.text: Verify for each reference asset whether its rights permit use in generation and external production, and keep an approved list of usable assets.
E.explanation: This clarifies the input permissions and the basis for using each asset.

aib-c01-d3-012@1.title: Checking whether a citation actually supports a claim
aib-c01-d3-012@1.prompt: A product-support AI includes links to approved procedures in its answers, but there are repeated cases where a link leads to instructions for a different model and does not support the replacement procedure claimed in the answer. The links are not broken. Which measure would address this most directly?

learning.reason: Check whether the reference applies to the model and version and whether the cited passage supports each claim, rather than merely checking that the page exists. Route unsupported procedures for confirmation instead of presenting them as guidance.
learning.concept: Distinguish the presence of a citation from actual support for an answer's claim, and hold the answer when support cannot be found.

A.text: Shorten citation titles in standard replies and prioritize procedures with the most views.
A.explanation: View counts and title length do not verify whether a claim is correct.

B.text: Monitor HTTP responses from the linked pages and treat the answer's content as verified whenever a page is reachable.
B.explanation: A working link does not mean the page contains support for the claim.

C.text: Verify that the model and version match the procedure, and hold answers that cannot point to a supporting section.
C.explanation: This helps prevent both incorrect evidence and unsupported assertions.

D.text: Require multiple links in each answer and publish it if it meets the link-count requirement.
D.explanation: The number of sources does not guarantee that they apply or support the claim.

aib-c01-d3-013@1.title: Making explanations of decisions useful to the people affected
aib-c01-d3-013@1.prompt: An online learning service's discount recommendation AI must respond when users who are deemed ineligible ask for an explanation. The service wants to explain the review outcome, but it cannot disclose other people's contract histories used in training or internal fraud-detection details. Which information for users is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Explain the decision factors related to the person's application and how to correct inputs or make an inquiry. Do not unnecessarily disclose third-party histories or internal countermeasures.
learning.concept: Balance transparency in public explanations with protection of others' data by providing relevant factors and a path to correction.

A.text: Report the accuracy across the business and explain each individual outcome as if the same probability applied to that person.
A.explanation: Overall accuracy does not explain why a particular person received a decision.

B.text: Present other users' inputs and outcomes from similar contracts without anonymizing them, to make the explanation complete.
B.explanation: This unnecessarily discloses other people's contract information.

C.text: Provide the main reasons based on the individual's own records, how to review and correct those records, and a contact channel for requesting a reassessment.
C.explanation: This offers transparency that can lead to practical action without exposing unrelated contract histories.

D.text: Publish only the model's format name and update date, without explaining how to review individual records.
D.explanation: This gives no specific reasons or way to correct errors.

aib-c01-d3-014@1.title: Maintaining safety standards as throughput targets increase
aib-c01-d3-014@1.prompt: A facilities management department wants to double the number of inquiries it handles this quarter. The AI performs adequately for directions to facilities within the building, but in field tests it has repeatedly provided incorrect information about access restrictions during emergencies. The reception desk can distinguish routine directions from emergency-related inquiries. Which policy is most likely to balance the throughput target with safety?

learning.reason: Improve efficiency in the verified routine scope, while staff familiar with the procedures handle emergencies and cases whose type is unclear. Reassess safety before expanding into the emergency scope.
learning.concept: Expand only into lower-impact areas validated by testing, and retain human handling where serious errors are unacceptable.

A.text: Automate every inquiry and have staff check only satisfaction after the fact so that response speed does not decline.
A.explanation: Users would receive guidance already known to be seriously incorrect.

B.text: Automate only emergency-related inquiries and reassign staff who know routine directions well to increase response volume.
B.explanation: This concentrates automation in an area that failed to meet the standard in field tests.

C.text: Use AI within the verified scope of routine inquiries, route emergencies and unclear cases to staff, and track serious misinformation against a separate threshold.
C.explanation: This uses the opportunity to improve efficiency while keeping the known high-impact area separate and monitored.

D.text: Use a combined accuracy rate for routine and emergency outcomes as the operational standard, and automate all areas once the overall rate exceeds the threshold.
D.explanation: The volume of routine inquiries could conceal misinformation in emergencies.

aib-c01-d3-015@1.title: Define audit-ready records at design time
aib-c01-d3-015@1.prompt: You are designing an internal AI assistant for consultations that may contain sensitive personal information. Organizational policy requires you to determine later which model version and approved information were used if an issue arises. There is no basis for retaining the full text of sensitive consultations long term. What should you decide before receiving trial data?

learning.reason: Design records of the versions, information references, and decisions needed for an audit. Identify sensitive information and handle only the portions that are necessary. Define access and retention periods for each purpose.
learning.concept: Define the information needed for verification and investigation in advance, and avoid retaining sensitive source text indiscriminately.

A.text: Store only aggregate consultation counts and do not retain model versions or referenced information for individual cases.
A.explanation: You would not be able to investigate which version was used for a response that caused an issue.

B.text: Do not store the full text in the generation platform; instead, have staff copy it to personal storage in preparation for audit requests.
B.explanation: This creates unmanaged copies without establishing an official recordkeeping process or access controls.

C.text: Retain all conversations and user identifiers long term so you can accommodate any future audit requirements.
C.explanation: This includes data without a defined purpose or retention basis.

D.text: Identify and record the model and document versions and the necessary outcome; limit original text to the scope and duration required, and define who can access it.
D.explanation: This preserves the evidence needed for investigation while limiting exposure of sensitive information.

aib-c01-d3-016@1.title: Reduce approvals that merely ratify AI recommendations
aib-c01-d3-016@1.prompt: An AI assistant proposes payment amounts for staff handling penalties under transportation contracts. A human approves each payment, but an audit found that staff tend to select the AI's amount without reading the supporting information. What should you change to make human oversight meaningful?

learning.reason: For important cases, have staff record their judgment first based on the contract and performance history, then review the difference from the AI's recommendation with a reason. Send unusual discrepancies for another review.
learning.concept: Record human judgment before AI recommendations for high-impact decisions, and use independent review of discrepancies to reduce automation bias.

A.text: Display the AI's recommendation prominently at the top for every staff member and treat the fact that they clicked Approve as evidence of oversight.
A.explanation: The approval would remain a formality, and the first amount staff see could exert even more influence.

B.text: For high-value or unusual cases, record the staff member's initial judgment and supporting rationale first, then compare it with the AI's recommendation and send discrepancies for another review.
B.explanation: This can reduce rubber-stamping and make it a substantive step for people to check the rationale.

C.text: Close the human approval screen only when a separate model from the same provider agrees with the AI.
C.explanation: Models may make the same mistake, and this removes human oversight.

D.text: To maintain processing speed, replace all human verification with random sampling after payment.
D.explanation: Post-payment audits can help, but they cannot prevent a high-impact, unverified payment in advance.

aib-c01-d3-017@1.title: Separate new-market obligations from existing approvals
aib-c01-d3-017@1.prompt: You plan to launch the same customer support AI in another region. The departmental policy in that region adds requirements to disclose AI processing in advance, provide a process for users to switch to a human, and record fulfillment of switch requests. The current service has none of these capabilities. What should you decide before launch?

learning.reason: Map each requirement in the target region to the interface, operations, and evidence. Test the flow from request through fulfillment before enabling the service. Do not reuse the existing region's approval as is.
learning.concept: Compare obligations in a new region with current capabilities, and enable that region only after adding and satisfying any missing operational requirements.

A.text: Display the advance notice, and look for the responsible department only if a user asks to switch.
A.explanation: This lacks an available switching process and a record that the request was fulfilled.

B.text: Carry over the approval for the existing region and bundle the additional requirements into the next update after the formal release.
B.explanation: This would launch without meeting the new region's requirements.

C.text: Retain existing AI processing logs long term, and ask users to prove their switch requests using their own email records.
C.explanation: This does not record whether your organization fulfilled the request.

D.text: Add region-specific disclosure, a switching process, and fulfillment records; verify the flow from a user's request through actual service by a human before enabling it.
D.explanation: This verifies all the additional obligations through the service's actual behavior.

aib-c01-d3-018@1.title: Separate permissions for experimentation and production
aib-c01-d3-018@1.prompt: The rules for an internal AI experimentation environment permit only approved research samples. A proposal would use the same execution account for that environment and the production environment, which handles customer inquiries after launch. Select two conditions for a configuration in which the experimentation environment cannot read production data and production updates can be approved.

learning.reason: Assign permissions according to the distinct purposes of experimentation and production, and separate production data and updates. Verify approved artifacts through the designated deployment path before bringing them into production.
learning.concept: Separate data and processing permissions for different purposes using least privilege, and share only through an approved deployment path.

A.text: Automatically copy production source text to the experimentation environment every morning to increase the number of samples available for experimentation.
A.explanation: This brings customer data other than the approved samples into the experimentation environment.

B.text: Allow the production environment to receive only artifacts whose versions and approval records have been verified, through a deployment path with separate permissions.
B.explanation: This allows approved updates to be deployed while keeping operational permissions separate.

C.text: Give a single execution account permissions in both environments and hide production data from the experimentation interface.
C.explanation: Hiding data in the interface does not revoke the processing account's permissions.

D.text: Separate execution permissions by environment so that experimentation credentials cannot read production data or change its configuration.
D.explanation: This applies least privilege in practice and makes it less likely that an experiment will affect production.

E.text: Remove only production write permissions from the experimentation environment, while allowing everyone to read production data for quality comparisons.
E.explanation: This does not meet the requirement that the experimentation environment cannot read production data.

aib-c01-d3-019@1.title: Set approval based on risk after additional safeguards
aib-c01-d3-019@1.prompt: A credit union uses customer interaction records to train an employee coaching AI. Its classification policy rates the pre-mitigation risk as high for uses involving sensitive records, and requires reassessing the residual classification when anonymization and retention limits have been verified through measurement. Residual risk above medium requires additional approval from the accountable owner. In a pilot, anonymization succeeded for routine cases, but some descriptions of family circumstances still allowed individuals to be inferred. What decision should the approver make?

learning.reason: Record the pre-mitigation classification, then assess residual risk using the cases that testing found to remain. Until risk reduction is verified, the approval process for a lower residual classification cannot be applied.
learning.concept: Distinguish risk before safeguards from residual risk after verified safeguards, and determine additional approval from the residual classification.

A.text: Record the pre-mitigation classification and unresolved inference cases, then reassess residual risk. Obtain additional approval unless the risk is confirmed to be medium or lower.
A.explanation: Evaluate safeguards only to the extent verified, and follow the approval path appropriate to the remaining risk.

B.text: Exclude the anonymization failures because they are few, and use only the success rate for routine cases as the basis for approval.
B.explanation: Removing failures from the evidence prevents assessment of the disclosure risk that remains.

C.text: Keep the same classification for any use rated high before mitigation, even after safeguards are verified, and skip residual-risk assessment.
C.explanation: The policy requires a separate assessment of the risk remaining after verified safeguards.

D.text: Lower the residual classification to medium or below regardless of how often exceptions occur, because an anonymization setting is configured.
D.explanation: Installing a safeguard does not by itself show that it is effective.

aib-c01-d3-020@1.title: Address harmful content expressed in regional language
aib-c01-d3-020@1.prompt: An AI system for job listings has a mechanism to block derogatory language. In multilingual trials, it blocked prohibited terms in the primary language, but outputs containing euphemisms in other languages got through. Which measure would reduce harmful output without unnecessarily blocking legitimate inquiries?

learning.reason: Prepare harmful and legitimate examples for each language and context, and compare results with expert judgments. Route suspicious output for review and measure false positives as well.
learning.concept: Test with examples grounded in users’ languages and contexts rather than relying on simple prohibited-term matching; measure both false negatives and false positives.

A.text: While there are few normal examples in a minority language, unconditionally block all output in that language as harmful.
A.explanation: This would block legitimate inquiries more than necessary.

B.text: Use only the total number of complaints after launch, and perform no checks for languages where users have not submitted reports.
B.explanation: This fails to identify in advance the languages in which harmful expressions may be harder to detect.

C.text: Measure false negatives and false positives using representative harmful and legitimate examples for each language, then tune controls that account for context along with human review.
C.explanation: This assesses both safety and legitimate use across languages.

D.text: Machine-translate the primary language’s prohibited terms into a list, then judge quality across all languages using dictionary matching alone.
D.explanation: This does not adequately assess euphemisms or context-dependent harmfulness.

aib-c01-d4-001@1.title: Do not mistake budget approval for readiness to adopt AI
aib-c01-d4-001@1.prompt: A newspaper has secured a budget and executive sponsor for a generative AI pilot. The editorial department merely states that it can use article data, but has not recorded permission to use it. Editors have not been trained in the correction workflow, and no one has decided how inquiries will be handled at night. Which readiness assessment should be conducted first?

learning.reason: Do not treat success in one area as a proxy for overall readiness. Assign owners for each dimension and substantiate readiness with records, exercises, and actual usage conditions. Resolve blockers to the pilot first.
learning.concept: Assess leadership alignment, data, frontline teams, infrastructure, and controls together, and support self-reports with operational evidence.

A.text: Check only for executive budget approval and experimental accounts, then estimate production scale if both are in place.
A.explanation: This does not assess data rights, editorial workflows, or readiness for oversight and incident response.

B.text: Report the model’s initial accuracy as the readiness level for the entire company, without considering differences among departments.
B.explanation: Model quality does not represent organizational or process readiness.

C.text: Assess leadership, data permissions, editorial skills, infrastructure, and after-hours controls separately; identify gaps before the pilot through records and process exercises.
C.explanation: This covers the necessary dimensions and supplements self-reports with concrete evidence.

D.text: Add up employees’ self-assessments from an internal survey, allowing high scores to offset low ones.
D.explanation: This can conceal missing essentials such as data permissions or response procedures.

aib-c01-d4-002@1.title: Do not confuse successful individual pilots with enterprise maturity
aib-c01-d4-002@1.prompt: At a financial services operations company, two departments achieved time savings in separate pilots, but each uses different management practices. There is no shared usage approval, handoff, or quality monitoring, and a pilot stopped when its owner transferred. Which maturity assessment distinguishes experimentation from enterprise-wide scaling?

learning.reason: Individual pilots show signs of value, but standardization and ongoing operations are still lacking. Recognize the results at the experimentation stage while identifying the capabilities required for scaling.
learning.concept: Assess maturity based on repeatable standards and sustained operational accountability, not the most successful isolated example.

A.text: Classify the company as being at the enterprise-wide scaling stage because two departmental pilots produced good results, and leave process differences to each business unit.
A.explanation: The mechanisms for repeatability and continued operations are not yet in place.

B.text: Classify every department as being at the ideation stage because there is no formal company-wide AI policy, and exclude pilot results from the maturity assessment.
B.explanation: This ignores experience using AI and measuring its results.

C.text: Classify the company as being at the enterprise-wide scaling stage because the provider’s commercially available model is mature.
C.explanation: A product’s maturity is different from the organization’s operational capability.

D.text: Classify the company as being at the experimentation stage, where outcomes have been measured, and make usable standard procedures, owners, and shared quality monitoring prerequisites for the next stage.
D.explanation: This recognizes actual pilot results while distinguishing them from the capabilities that are still needed to scale.

aib-c01-d4-003@1.title: Identify why errors accumulate by distinguishing capability gaps
aib-c01-d4-003@1.prompt: The engineering department has staff who can assess model quality and equipment for retesting. Errors found during trials appear in weekly reports, but nothing changes no matter how often they are reported. An investigation found that no one had decided who would accept proposed fixes, whom to ask for approval, or when to release them. Which capability gap should be addressed first?

learning.reason: The gap is in the process for receiving exceptions, assigning responsibility, obtaining approval, and distributing fixes. Existing training and equipment alone do not move fixes through that process.
learning.concept: Identify missing processes and owners between issue reporting and release when technical skills and training are already available.

A.text: Provide the existing quality staff with another round of generative AI fundamentals training and continue submitting the same weekly reports.
A.explanation: The staff already have sufficient skills; a skills gap is not the cause.

B.text: Use the percentage of issues included in weekly reports as a metric, and consider the operational gap closed if every issue found is listed.
B.explanation: This does not show whether reported issues were actually fixed and released.

C.text: Establish one operating procedure for intake, prioritization, ownership, approval, and distribution of changes, then use past reports to run the process.
C.explanation: This addresses the broken workflow and gaps in accountability that are preventing changes from progressing.

D.text: Switch to a more capable generative model and investigate the backlog of fixes without changing the process from reporting through approval.
D.explanation: Changing the model does not establish how reports are accepted or approved.

aib-c01-d4-004@1.title: Sequence investments that advance strategic goals from a low level of maturity
aib-c01-d4-004@1.prompt: A specialist trading company’s strategic goal is to speed up quote responses across all branches. At present, only one location can standardize product names, and there is no budget to provide an integrated foundation and staff for every branch at once. Which first-year investment would contribute most to the long-term goal?

learning.reason: Test improvements to the quoting process at the one location with ready data, establish reusable product definitions, skills, and evaluation procedures, then expand based on results and readiness.
learning.concept: Develop team skills and a foundation that can be reused for the goal through a limited pilot suited to current readiness.

A.text: Provide the same comprehensive training to everyone this year, and defer trials involving product data and quoting workflows until next year.
A.explanation: Training alone does not show whether the data and processes needed for the strategic goal can be reused.

B.text: Prioritize generic text generation that can be completed within budget, without measuring whether it can support quoting.
B.explanation: This has little connection to the stated strategic goal.

C.text: Roll out the solution to every branch at once, then resolve inconsistent product names and staff training after deployment.
C.explanation: This takes on the challenges at less-prepared locations all at once and makes accurate quoting harder.

D.text: Pilot the quoting workflow at a prepared location, establish shared product definitions and processes for training and measurement, then select the next location based on results.
D.explanation: This can deliver results with a small investment while building capabilities that can be reused in a rollout to all branches.

aib-c01-d4-005@1.title: Distinguish data volume from the scope of cases usable in operations
aib-c01-d4-005@1.prompt: A maintenance support service for industrial equipment uses the sales department’s installation register and repair reports received from contractors. Both departments have many records, but the rate at which equipment IDs are recorded and the timing of updates vary by contractor. Which assessment directly informs whether maintenance support can start in every region?

learning.reason: Assessing successful matches, arrival delays, and permissions by region and contractor reveals gaps that company-wide record counts cannot show.
learning.concept: Measure the coverage, delays, and permissions for records that can be matched across departments; do not assess readiness by volume alone.

A.text: Measure accuracy in the region with the most complete records, then extrapolate the result to the other regions if the model is the same.
A.explanation: This ignores the stated differences in missing data and update timing across regions.

B.text: Measure, by region and contractor, the percentage of target equipment for which the latest repair information with authorized use can be correctly matched to the installation register.
B.explanation: This reveals the coverage and gaps in the data that is actually needed.

C.text: Count each department’s records separately, and consider every region ready if both counts exceed a threshold.
C.explanation: Record counts do not show whether histories for the same equipment can be matched correctly.

D.text: Centralize all histories in one place and, until more data is available, count records that cannot be matched as ready records.
D.explanation: Centralizing storage does not resolve matching or permission issues.

aib-c01-d4-006@1.title: Define the meaning of shared data and responsibility for changes
aib-c01-d4-006@1.prompt: The sales, billing, and support departments use an enterprise customer directory with AI. Each department defines an “active customer” differently in its own table, and after a change on the billing side, the support AI continued searching with the old definition. Which governance measure is most effective for sharing the data?

learning.reason: Assign an owner to maintain authoritative definitions, and agree with user departments on definitions by use case, quality, access, change notifications, and deadlines for adopting updates.
learning.concept: Make definitions, quality, conditions of use, and change notifications for core data part of an agreement between the data owner and user teams.

A.text: Synchronize each table to a single storage location and let the AI infer the authoritative definition and change notifications from the latest table.
A.explanation: Using one storage location does not resolve differences in definitions or ownership.

B.text: Have the departments share definitions verbally at the end of each month, and let each user decide individually when to apply them.
B.explanation: Definitions remain difficult to track, implementation is not assured, and ownership remains unclear.

C.text: Assign a data owner and version-control definitions, intended uses, access conditions, quality requirements, change notifications, and migration deadlines agreed with the user departments.
C.explanation: The provider and user teams can share responsibility for understanding changes and responding to them.

D.text: Have support keep using the directory it has already retrieved indefinitely to avoid changes.
D.explanation: This cannot keep up with current business definitions or customer status.

aib-c01-d4-007@1.title: Assessing whether infrastructure is field-ready through connectivity and continuity
aib-c01-d4-007@1.prompt: A logistics company is deploying an AI system to help couriers verify delivery acceptance requirements at drop-off locations. A prototype performs quickly in urban areas, but in mountainous areas with unreliable connectivity, delivery operations would be disrupted if the system cannot display an answer within 1 minute. The existing confirmed procedure for preventing misdeliveries is available offline on the device. Which infrastructure assessment should be performed before a full rollout?

learning.reason: Evaluate response and timeout behavior on the devices to be deployed and under representative connectivity conditions. Also verify that the fallback procedure fits field constraints when the system cannot be used in time.
learning.concept: Assess prototype benchmarks against field network and device conditions, latency, and fallback requirements when the system is unavailable.

A.text: Measure response times and unavailability rates using the planned devices and connectivity conditions in mountainous areas, and test switching to the existing procedure when the system does not respond within the required time.
A.explanation: This verifies the actual constraints and the path for continuing deliveries.

B.text: Plan on couriers waiting for the AI even in areas with unreliable connectivity, assuming all delivery deadlines can be extended.
B.explanation: This does not address existing operating schedules or continuity constraints.

C.text: Measure median response time over a stable headquarters connection and assume that a result under 1 minute means the target is met in every delivery area.
C.explanation: This does not assess connectivity conditions or unavailability rates in the field.

D.text: Choose the required model contract based on projected monthly usage, and check device connectivity and fallback operations after launch.
D.explanation: This does not verify infrastructure availability before launch.

aib-c01-d4-008@1.title: Giving field champions time and authority to drive adoption
aib-c01-d4-008@1.prompt: An online retailer’s customer service support initiative has been approved by the business unit director. Champions at each site know the frontline operations well, but individual performance is measured only by the number of customer interactions handled, and they have no working hours available for training or improvement. What should the sponsor do to move adoption forward?

learning.reason: Work with site managers on goals and performance evaluations, and secure time, scope of authority, and reporting paths so champions can treat training and improvement as part of their work.
learning.concept: The sponsor resolves cross-department budget and staffing conflicts and gives field champions the time and authority to carry out their roles.

A.text: Set a target only for the number of champions appointed and do not check whether they have time for training and improvement.
A.explanation: The number of appointments does not show that the champions are effective.

B.text: Align evaluation criteria with site managers, allocate working time and decision-making authority to champions, and establish a channel for escalating obstacles to executives.
B.explanation: This provides the conditions for champions to do the work and support for obstacles that cannot be resolved at the site level.

C.text: Move all champions to a central department and exclude site operations leaders from adoption decisions.
C.explanation: This weakens cross-functional leadership rooted in frontline operations and the responsibility of each department.

D.text: Resend a company-wide email expressing support and have champions continue training outside their working hours.
D.explanation: This does not resolve the constraints on performance evaluation or working time.

aib-c01-d4-009@1.title: Clarifying accountability for business outcomes in a cross-functional team
aib-c01-d4-009@1.prompt: A property management company is developing an AI system to support repair requests across three departments. The technology department understands model quality, the operations department understands intake times, and Legal understands contract terms. In previous trials, no one was accountable for overall intake outcomes, and fixes to problems were put on hold. Which team structure is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Define the responsibilities of each cross-functional specialist, then assign a role accountable for business outcomes and the launch decision, with clear processes for assessing and resolving blockers.
learning.concept: Assign a single accountable owner for business outcomes and launch decisions, while distinguishing the deliverables and decisions of technology, Legal, and operations.

A.text: Appoint an operations-side owner accountable for intake outcomes, and have the team define the assessments and handoffs for technology, Legal, and frontline operations.
A.explanation: This combines a role accountable for the overall outcome with the judgments of subject-matter experts.

B.text: Move the entire effort to the technology department and collect written input from frontline operations and Legal only after the design is complete.
B.explanation: This delays discovery of specialist constraints and leaves frontline operations out of validating business outcomes.

C.text: Assign an owner only after a request comes in, and do not involve Legal or operations before the initial launch.
C.explanation: This prevents the team from aligning on necessary conditions and frontline procedures before launch.

D.text: Split accountability for outcomes equally across the three departments and defer unresolved conflicts until the next quarterly committee meeting.
D.explanation: This leaves accountability and decision-making to move the work forward unclear.

aib-c01-d4-010@1.title: Communicating confirmed decisions and open questions separately to frontline staff
aib-c01-d4-010@1.prompt: A communications department announced a trial of generative AI for drafting copy, and a rumor spread among frontline staff that editing jobs would disappear starting next month. The only confirmed decisions are a 6-week trial and continued human approval before publication; post-trial staffing arrangements have not been decided. Which explanation from the leader is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Clearly communicate the confirmed trial scope and human roles. For undecided staffing arrangements, explain how they will be evaluated, how staff can raise concerns, and when the next decision update will be shared.
learning.concept: For an initiative that affects people, communicate confirmed timelines and roles, how open questions will be decided, and channels for two-way feedback.

A.text: Publish only the AI benchmark results and do not explain roles or the publication approval process until individual questions come in.
A.explanation: This does not directly address staff concerns or communicate operational facts.

B.text: Explain the trial period and human publication approval, state the decision criteria and next update date for unresolved staffing arrangements, and invite questions and feedback.
B.explanation: This communicates confirmed decisions, treats open questions transparently, and allows frontline staff to raise concerns.

C.text: To reassure staff, promise that no roles will ever change in the future, regardless of the trial results.
C.explanation: This presents an undecided matter as a confirmed promise.

D.text: Because staffing arrangements have not been decided, stop communicating and brief staff for the first time after the trial ends.
D.explanation: This leaves rumors uncorrected during a period of uncertainty and prevents frontline feedback from being incorporated.

aib-c01-d4-011@1.title: Creating a Safe Environment to Experiment in a Workplace with Strong Fear of Failure
aib-c01-d4-011@1.prompt: A procurement employee at a large trading company believes that finding and reporting errors in generative AI will lower their performance rating, so they avoid participating in validation. In the past, this department factored failures with new tools into individual performance evaluations. Which initial intervention would address this cultural barrier?

learning.reason: Keep trials within limits that will not affect customers or evaluations, and have managers clearly state and demonstrate that error reports will be used for improvement. Review cases together with users.
learning.concept: Avoid pressuring people to use AI through punishment or rankings. Set up reversible use cases, leadership support, and exercises where failures can be shared.

A.text: Ask the technical team to use the tool on employees’ behalf, and begin interviewing procurement staff only after time savings have been demonstrated.
A.explanation: This does not address the reason for their anxiety and reduces opportunities to learn from actual users.

B.text: After training, introduce a usage leaderboard for performance evaluations and coach employees individually if they do not participate.
B.explanation: This increases the incentive to hide errors and usage outcomes during trials.

C.text: Run trials with practice data that will not be published and in a limited business area; have managers promise that reporting errors will not lead to negative consequences, and review cases together.
C.explanation: This limits risk while demonstrating that reporting and learning will not harm performance evaluations.

D.text: Present only successful cases and accept reports of errors only after adoption reaches its target.
D.explanation: This does not create conditions in which failures can be shared safely.

aib-c01-d4-012@1.title: Designing AI Education Around Each Department’s Work
aib-c01-d4-012@1.prompt: At a manufacturing company, operators validate AI-generated inspection notes, managers approve the use cases for which AI may be used, and data stewards review the handling of sensitive information. Everyone watched the same introductory video, but judgment errors continued during trials. What should the company do next to develop these skills?

learning.reason: In addition to shared foundational knowledge, address the decisions each role actually makes in safe exercises. Use exception handling and completion criteria to assess whether people can demonstrate the required skills.
learning.concept: Separate shared foundational knowledge from role-specific decisions, and measure practical skills rather than attendance.

A.text: Hold a one-day hackathon, reward the team that generates the most content, and treat that count as evidence of everyone’s decision-making ability.
A.explanation: The number of drafts produced is separate from the skills needed to validate, approve, and manage information.

B.text: Use the same lengthy video on specialized terminology for everyone, and approve workplace use once the video completion rate reaches 100%.
B.explanation: Course completion does not demonstrate the ability to make role-specific decisions.

C.text: Create role-specific exercises and assess operators on correcting errors, managers on reviewing use cases, and data stewards on handling information through hands-on practice.
C.explanation: This checks whether learning transfers to the work for each required decision.

D.text: Have experts make every operational decision, and consider training complete once only the legal department has received it.
D.explanation: This does not develop the skills required of operators or approvers.

aib-c01-d4-013@1.title: Redistributing Work Between People and AI Based on Their Strengths
aib-c01-d4-013@1.prompt: A lodging reservation company can use AI to quickly organize rescheduling options and room availability. Cancellations due to illness or family circumstances require considerate conversation and judgment about refund exceptions. Which job redesign would reduce the burden of phone support without increasing complaints?

learning.reason: Assign information gathering and option generation to AI; have authorized people handle conversations about customers’ circumstances and decisions that require discretion. Include verified facts and unresolved points in the handoff.
learning.concept: Assign routine organization to AI and empathetic support and contractual exception decisions to people, with clear conditions for human involvement.

A.text: Have AI gather options and organize confirmed information, then hand exceptional cases to an employee to hear the customer’s circumstances and make the refund decision.
A.explanation: This reduces the burden of routine work while preserving interpersonal support and discretion.

B.text: Have employees state the refund rules first, then let AI make the final decision on exceptional cases so no person is involved.
B.explanation: This automates steps that require human discretion and conversation.

C.text: Have AI hear the customer’s circumstances and make irreversible refund denials, while employees review only weekly summaries.
C.explanation: This removes the role of hearing the customer’s circumstances and considering exceptions.

D.text: Keep all customer interactions as they are, and have AI summarize conversations only after they end.
D.explanation: Summaries are useful, but this leaves the opportunity to automate option gathering unused.

aib-c01-d4-014@1.title: Evaluating an Experiment Before Moving to the Next Stage
aib-c01-d4-014@1.prompt: A procurement department ran an experiment using AI to extract key points from instructions. Time savings for routine cases exceeded the target, but extraction of exception conditions did not meet the quality threshold set before the experiment. The business unit wants to announce at a trade show that the solution will launch next month. Which decision follows an iterative approach?

learning.reason: Prioritize the experiment’s acceptance criteria over the announced launch date. Isolate the cause of failure, revise the design and scope, and decide on the next stage after revalidation.
learning.concept: Set transition criteria for ideation, experimentation, and launch; when unexpected quality failures occur, step back, fix them, and validate again.

A.text: Treat the failures on exceptions as decisive, end the current trial, and do not carry the results from routine cases forward for evaluation as a future candidate.
A.explanation: There is an option to exclude exceptions from scope or otherwise use the value found in routine cases in the next experiment.

B.text: Launch the solution officially and assign exceptions to the team responsible for the next model. Do not change the scope communicated to customers until the fixes are ready.
B.explanation: This makes a use case available despite its failure to meet the required quality.

C.text: Since time savings exceeded the target, lower the quality threshold after the fact and officially launch for exceptions within the same scope.
C.explanation: This changes multiple success criteria after the experiment to suit the results.

D.text: Analyze why exceptions failed, adjust the design or scope of use, and validate again. Launch only within the scope that meets the agreed criteria.
D.explanation: This uses experiment results in the next iteration and advances based on explicit criteria.

aib-c01-d4-015@1.title: Determine whether a short-term pilot success can be transferred to other sites
aib-c01-d4-015@1.prompt: A warehouse company improved its same-day processing rate with an AI tool that helps reconcile applications at one site. Only that site uses standardized forms; other sites use some different forms and approval procedures. What should the company do next to turn the short-term result into a company-wide rollout?

learning.reason: Separate the reconciliation process that can be shared from the forms and approvals that need local configuration, then verify effectiveness and fit in stages at sites with both similar and different conditions.
learning.concept: Extract a reusable core from a short-term success and validate it in stages at sites with similar and different conditions.

A.text: Assume the result is not guaranteed anywhere beyond the first site, and do not use the pilot results until every site has identical forms.
A.explanation: This would forfeit the opportunity to assess a design that can accommodate regional differences in stages.

B.text: Have each site build a completely separate AI system, and share only the example from the site with the most users as a success story.
B.explanation: This prevents reuse of the successful process and does not measure how well it fits sites with different conditions.

C.text: Apply the first site's configuration to every site at once, and track only the company-wide average same-day processing rate.
C.explanation: Differences in forms and approvals could cause problems at particular sites that are hidden by the average.

D.text: Standardize the common reconciliation process, separate site-specific forms and approvals through configuration, and verify results and quality in stages at sites with different conditions.
D.explanation: This reuses the early approach while validating its constraints and effectiveness when transferred.

aib-c01-d4-016@1.title: Share company-wide rollout responsibilities between a specialist organization and local teams
aib-c01-d4-016@1.prompt: At a large wholesaler, several branches are independently building AI review forms and monitoring capabilities for the same use case. However, only inventory staff can judge the business impact of an incorrect recommendation. If the company creates a central AI specialist organization, how should responsibilities be divided?

learning.reason: The specialist organization should establish common reviews, evaluation methods, and standard components; knowledgeable local teams should own local business outcomes, exceptions, and operational decisions.
learning.concept: A center of excellence manages reusable foundations and controls, while local teams own business quality and outcomes.

A.text: Have each branch build all its own technology and controls, while the central organization collects success stories once a year.
A.explanation: This does not eliminate duplicate common reviews and monitoring.

B.text: Have the central organization provide common review procedures, evaluation components, and a platform, while branches define exceptions and own business outcomes. Both sides should share examples and improve the standards.
B.explanation: This balances reuse with local ownership of business responsibilities.

C.text: Have the central organization require the use of a particular model, without addressing reuse of review criteria or evaluation components.
C.explanation: Standardizing the model alone does not reduce duplicated review and monitoring work.

D.text: Have the central organization manage not only the shared platform but also each branch's inventory decisions, while branch staff report at month-end how many instructions they followed.
D.explanation: Local knowledge and accountability for business outcomes would not be reflected in operations.

aib-c01-d4-017@1.title: Track long-term outcomes, including for people who stop using the tool
aib-c01-d4-017@1.prompt: After a quoting assistant is introduced, an optional in-app survey shows high satisfaction. However, usage is low at one branch, and very few people there respond to the survey. What is the most appropriate way to understand long-term value and challenges?

learning.reason: Studying only current users does not reveal why people stopped adopting the tool. Gather feedback by branch and usage status, and continue tracking it alongside work completion time and quality.
learning.concept: Do not rely only on optional responses from regular users; track former users and business outcomes by group over time.

A.text: Exclude the low-usage branch from the evaluation, and calculate long-term impact only for branches where people continue using the tool.
A.explanation: This prevents analysis of the conditions that keep adoption from taking hold.

B.text: At each branch, regularly ask both continuing and former users why they use or stopped using the tool, and review their feedback alongside trends in completion time and quality for the work it supports.
B.explanation: This avoids relying only on users who are likely to respond and also tracks business outcomes.

C.text: Fix the satisfaction score from immediately after launch as the baseline, and thereafter check only the number of inference requests.
C.explanation: This does not adequately measure why people continue using the tool or how business outcomes change.

D.text: Show the in-app survey more often, and estimate value across all branches using only company-wide satisfaction totals.
D.explanation: The survey would still miss people who do not use the tool and would not reveal branch-specific issues.

aib-c01-d4-018@1.title: Choose the acceptance conditions for moving a prototype to production quality
aib-c01-d4-018@1.prompt: A prototype AI complaint classifier meets its quality threshold on representative data. Its configuration is in a developer's account, and revision history and alert recipients have not been set up. Choose two tasks required before integrating it into formal business operations.

learning.reason: Version-controlled deployment and approval that do not depend on an individual, together with monitoring owned by an on-call rotation and rehearsed incident response, are basic requirements for moving from experimentation to ongoing operations.
learning.concept: Acceptance criteria should require operational ownership, monitoring, incident-response exercises, and approval of production artifacts in addition to prototype results.

A.text: Define quality and availability monitoring, response deadlines and an on-call rotation, and fallback procedures; rehearse incident response before production launch.
A.explanation: This verifies that operators can actually monitor and maintain the service.

B.text: Appoint an owner for formal operations, and move the evaluated version and configuration to a deployment and approval path that can reproduce them.
B.explanation: This removes dependence on an individual's account or memory to keep the service running.

C.text: Because the prototype meets the accuracy threshold, keep its configuration and incident response solely in the developer's personal account.
C.explanation: This cannot ensure the ownership or access needed for ongoing operations and recovery.

D.text: To speed up formalization, let anyone apply changes directly to production, including changes outside the main business workflow.
D.explanation: Quality cannot be maintained when changes lack approval and traceability.

E.text: Wait until one month after launch to decide who should receive notifications about quality declines or incidents.
E.explanation: Problems must be detected and addressed from the first day.

aib-c01-d4-019@1.title: Assess how simultaneous enterprise-wide use affects existing operations
aib-c01-d4-019@1.prompt: Three departments in a corporate group share an AI platform. Each department meets its response-time target under its individual load, but their peaks coincide at month-end. Delays in the department that processes closings directly cause missed deadlines, while the other two departments have work that can be deferred. What should be validated before enterprise-wide rollout?
