learning.reason: Reproduce the three departments' concurrent peaks and measure delays against each department's deadlines. Reserve capacity for closing work and control work that can be deferred to demonstrate that service targets can be met.
learning.concept: Reproduce resource contention at concurrent peaks that individual department tests do not reveal, and determine priority capacity for critical work and the conditions for further rollout.

A.text: Reproduce the expected concurrent peak, reserve capacity and priority for closing work, and test department-specific targets, including controls for the departments whose work can be deferred.
A.explanation: This reveals contention caused by sharing and validates the continuity of critical operations.

B.text: Set a fixed cap based on the average daily processing volume and defer all work above the cap until the next day, regardless of its business importance.
B.explanation: This does not protect closing work whose delay would cause a missed deadline.

C.text: Arrange to scale up the platform starting at the next month-end only if the department processing closings falls behind.
C.explanation: This does not validate whether the first concurrent peak can be handled without missing deadlines.

D.text: Average the mean response times from each department's individual test. If the result meets the target, process all work at the same priority at month-end.
D.explanation: This does not assess contention for shared resources under concurrent use or deadlines that differ by department.

aib-c01-d4-020@1.title: Turn idea submissions into sustained learning in the field
aib-c01-d4-020@1.prompt: An AI showcase for branches nationwide produced many prototypes. Six months later, few locations are still improving them, and field staff cannot practice evaluation unless experts make site visits. Which initiative should be prioritized in the next workforce-development cycle?

learning.reason: Develop local coaches and provide practice materials, criteria for assessing results, and a route for consulting experts. Measure whether people in the field can continue practicing and improving autonomously.
learning.concept: Develop the field's capacity for safe, ongoing validation and review through local coaches; prototype counts alone are not evidence of workforce-development outcomes.

A.text: Enable local coaches to run exercises using safe learning materials, evaluation criteria, and a channel for consultation, and track ongoing improvement.
A.explanation: This builds learning and improvement capacity at each location without relying on experts being assigned there continuously.

B.text: Stop evaluation exercises until an expert visits each location, then launch actual use company-wide all at once.
B.explanation: This does not sustain ongoing practice in the field.

C.text: Hold a company-wide showcase every month and use the number of submitted prototypes as the sole measure of workforce-development success.
C.explanation: This does not establish whether people have learned to evaluate and improve solutions on an ongoing basis.

D.text: Distribute the top prototype unchanged for nationwide use and skip evaluation and learning at each branch.
D.explanation: Distributing technology alone does not develop the ability to assess suitability or make improvements.

aib-c01-d1-022@1.title: Choose the type of prediction needed to allocate workers
aib-c01-d1-022@1.prompt: A packaging company wants to estimate the work time required for each order and assign workers based on the day's total workload. Work times range from 15 minutes to less than 9 hours, and orders in the same “long” category can require different amounts of labor. Historical product features and actual work times are available. Which learning objective is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Regression using actual work times as target values produces numeric predictions that can be summed for each order. A category prediction cannot capture differences within the same category.
learning.concept: Distinguish classification based on a threshold from regression that predicts a continuous quantity, and choose the prediction value required by the downstream process.

A.text: Group orders by similarity in their product descriptions and generate a representative product name for each group.
A.explanation: Grouping orders does not necessarily yield the specific work time for each one.

B.text: Use regression trained on actual historical work times to estimate a numeric work time for each order, then compare the total error with the allocation results.
B.explanation: This produces the numeric values needed to assign workers.

C.text: Classify orders as long or short and count only the number classified as long each day.
C.explanation: Orders in the long category can still require different amounts of work, so a count alone is not a good way to calculate the total needed for allocation.

D.text: Generate work instructions from order notes and use text length as a substitute for work time.
D.explanation: No relationship between text length and actual work time has been learned, so there is no basis for predicting the required numeric value.

aib-c01-d1-023@1.title: Find similar reports even when they use different wording
aib-c01-d1-023@1.prompt: A service desk at an equipment sales company has a free-text field where customers describe symptoms. The desk wants to show similar past reports and the responsible department as candidates, even when the wording differs, such as “it tends to stop” and “it stops working.” Staff open the actual reports to verify the evidence for each candidate. Which approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Search for similar past reports using representations of their meaning, and return references to the original reports. There is no need to generate text about new causes of failure.
learning.concept: Choose embedding-based semantic search over generation that creates content without retrieving the correct documents or over exact-match rules.

A.text: Convert report text into semantic vectors, search for similar past reports, and display the original reports and departments.
A.explanation: This handles paraphrasing while letting staff verify results against the source reports.

B.text: Without referring to past reports, have a model generate fictional reports describing the same symptoms.
B.explanation: This cannot provide actual reports that staff can verify as candidates.

C.text: Compress the current report and return only past reports that exactly match the short summary.
C.explanation: Exact matching cannot find similar reports that use different wording.

D.text: Search for reports with a similar word count and length, and present them as reports of the same symptoms.
D.explanation: Similarity in text length does not establish similarity in symptoms.

aib-c01-d1-024@1.title: Detecting stale business data despite recent ingestion
aib-c01-d1-024@1.prompt: A cold-chain transport monitoring AI uses cargo temperatures measured within the last 30 minutes to recommend inspections. After a communications outage, old measurements from delivery devices arrive in a batch and appear recent if only ingestion time is considered. The measurement time recorded by each device is available, and clock skew is monitored separately. Which method should be used to check the quality of data used for inspection decisions?

learning.reason: Business freshness should be determined from measurement time. Do not treat delayed, out-of-order measurements as current; route vehicles that fail the freshness requirement for a fallback check.
learning.concept: Distinguish ingestion time from event time, and assess freshness for decisions using event timestamps and ordering.

A.text: If the number of records received within a fixed period matches a typical week, conclude that every vehicle meets the freshness requirement.
A.explanation: Old data arriving all at once could inflate the count, and some vehicles could have stale data even if the total count looks normal.

B.text: For each vehicle, select the latest value with a valid measurement time and route it for an operational fallback check if it is more than 30 minutes older than the decision time.
B.explanation: Using the time the measurement was actually observed and the time of the business decision prevents delayed data from being treated as current.

C.text: Subtract the estimated outage duration uniformly from the ingestion time and use that instead of the device's measurement time.
C.explanation: The actual measurement time is available. If outage durations differ by vehicle, an estimate does not represent the freshness of each vehicle's data.

D.text: Use only records ingested successfully in the last 30 minutes and treat the last temperature ingested for each vehicle as its latest value.
D.explanation: A measurement may have been taken before the outage even if it was ingested moments ago, and arrival order does not necessarily match measurement order.

aib-c01-d1-025@1.title: Preserving process state across handoffs between AI agents
aib-c01-d1-025@1.prompt: For an air cargo exception investigation, customs records and warehouse inventory must be investigated separately under different permissions. Both results are needed to decide how to resolve the case, and reprocessing the same inquiry sends duplicate notifications to staff. Select two appropriate designs for supporting this workflow with AI agents.

learning.reason: Separate investigations that require different permissions, then bring their progress and results together using state tied to the case ID. Resume only unfinished work and define when processing ends or is handed off to a person.
learning.concept: Separate independent specialist work from coordination, and use shared state to assign work and define stopping conditions.

A.text: Assign each investigation to a specialist with limited permissions, and use a coordinator that prepares a resolution only after both results are available.
A.explanation: This meets the requirements for separate permissions and for bringing the results together.

B.text: Whenever work is interrupted, always rerun every investigation from the beginning, without recording prior notifications or progress.
B.explanation: This cannot prevent duplicate operational messages and leaves the processing state unknown.

C.text: Give every specialist permission to change both ledgers so that any specialist can handle the case in the same way.
C.explanation: This violates the constraint that permissions are separated.

D.text: Do not share progress with the other specialist, and mark the case resolved as soon as either result is available.
D.explanation: This fails to use the other result required for resolution.

E.text: Record completion status and results by case ID, resume only unfinished work after an interruption, and hand off expired cases to a staff member.
E.explanation: This prevents duplicate notifications and distinguishes unfinished work from cases handed off to a person.

aib-c01-d1-026@1.title: Recognizing a changed prediction relationship despite a stable input distribution
aib-c01-d1-026@1.prompt: A subscription service predicts cancellations using usage frequency and support history. After a new “temporary pause” plan is introduced, the input distribution remains nearly the same as it was at launch. However, users who previously had low usage and then canceled as predicted are now increasingly keeping their subscriptions by using the plan. Which response should the operations team prioritize?

learning.reason: Even if the input distribution stays the same, a policy change can alter the relationship between features and observed outcomes. Evaluate that relationship and model accuracy using outcomes under the new plan, and revalidate the model or target as needed.
learning.concept: Do not treat stable input distributions as proof of stable performance; track changes in the meaning of outcomes and their relationship to the same features.

A.text: Collect confirmed cancellation and continuation outcomes under the new plan, compare actual outcomes with predictions by usage frequency, and decide whether changes are needed.
A.explanation: This evaluates whether the outcome associated with a feature has changed, in line with the business definition.

B.text: Adjust the predictions by correcting only the input distribution to match its original distribution, without using actual cancellation outcomes.
B.explanation: What has changed is how cancellation outcomes relate to the inputs.

C.text: Treat a temporary pause and an actual cancellation as the same outcome, without checking whether the business needs to distinguish them.
C.explanation: Combining outcomes that differ from the target changes what performance is being measured.

D.text: Conclude that performance has not changed because the input distribution is stable, and stop comparing predictions with actual cancellations.
D.explanation: Changes in the predicted outcome cannot be detected from the input distribution alone.

aib-c01-d1-027@1.title: Turning ambiguous priorities into an ordered workflow
aib-c01-d1-027@1.prompt: A city communications team wants to give residents a short explanation of public-facility usage requirements. When instructed to be “concise, but include everything necessary,” the team sometimes omits the application deadline and sometimes exceeds the word limit. The deadline and eligible audience must never be omitted; only background information may be left out. Which prompt change is most likely to help?

learning.reason: Specify the sequence for extracting required details, applying priorities, omitting only permitted information, and performing a final check. This makes it more likely that both the required content and word limit will be met.
learning.concept: When generating text under multiple business constraints, make the steps, priorities, and checks explicit.

A.text: Instruct the model to extract the deadline and eligible audience first as required items, reduce the background information to meet the word limit, and then verify that the required items are present.
A.explanation: This makes the relative priority of the constraints and the checking procedure explicit.

B.text: Add examples with detailed background information and treat an answer as within the word limit if it is about as long as the example.
B.explanation: This does not specify which constraint takes priority or require checking for the mandatory items.

C.text: Make the word limit stricter and leave it to the model to decide what to remove.
C.explanation: There is no mechanism to ensure the most important requirements are retained.

D.text: Repeat the same general instruction several times to meet both the word limit and the information requirements.
D.explanation: It remains unclear what to keep and in what order to make adjustments.

aib-c01-d1-028@1.title: Estimate context capacity using real documents
aib-c01-d1-028@1.prompt: A legal team sends an AI one English version, one Japanese version, and one version of the same application form with many tables. The team wants to limit document length to fit the model's limit. The proposal applies one conversion rate to the character count of the entire document, but document formats and character types differ. Which method should be used to set a reliable limit?

learning.reason: The same character count can produce different token counts depending on language, symbols, and table structure. Count the combined document and instructions with the actual model, and account for the capacity reserved for output.
learning.concept: Evaluate the largest cases using the model's token count and actual input composition instead of relying on character-count estimates.

A.text: Count representative examples of each language and table format with the intended model, and leave headroom for shared instructions and output as well.
A.explanation: This measures the input types and the full context that will actually be used in production.

B.text: Assume files with the same byte size have the same number of tokens, and use the same capacity for every model.
B.explanation: Tokenization and format handling vary by model and content.

C.text: Estimate all languages and tables using the average conversion rate for English documents, and accept inputs when the average is below the limit.
C.explanation: This does not protect against inputs in other languages or table formats that exceed the average.

D.text: Measure only the number of characters in the response, and impose no input limit if the requested response is short.
D.explanation: The input itself could still exceed the model's limit.

aib-c01-d1-029@1.title: Distinguish a predicted probability from a guarantee for an individual case
aib-c01-d1-029@1.prompt: A maintenance team plans inspections using failure probabilities. After calibrating predictions on equipment covered by its contract, the team found that about 80% of equipment predicted at around 80% failed by the deadline. When a particular machine has a predicted value of 80%, what is the appropriate explanation for the person responsible for it?

learning.reason: A well-calibrated 80% prediction refers to the event rate in a representative group with the same predicted value. It does not guarantee an outcome for a particular machine; inspection priority should also take the impact of failure into account.
learning.concept: A calibrated probability describes the frequency of an event among a group with similar predictions.

A.text: This means the proportion of all machines whose failure status is predicted correctly is 80% for each individual machine.
A.explanation: An individual predicted probability is a different measure from aggregate classification accuracy.

B.text: This means the failure will occur after 80% of the time remaining until the deadline has elapsed.
B.explanation: A probability does not specify a scheduled failure time.

C.text: This means the machine is already 80% failed, with the remaining 20% outside the prediction.
C.explanation: This is the likelihood of a defined event, not the extent of failure.

D.text: This means that about 80% of a group of machines with similar 80% predictions will fail. It does not determine whether an individual machine will fail.
D.explanation: This describes calibration as a probability frequency in the intended population.

aib-c01-d1-030@1.title: Choose input for video analysis that depends on action order
aib-c01-d1-030@1.prompt: A manufacturer wants to detect deviations from an assembly procedure. Even when the same three components and tools appear, performing two actions in the reverse order causes a defect. The site has videos, photos of finished products, and daily process summaries. Which is the most appropriate input for an initial trial?

learning.reason: The analysis must distinguish not only whether the components are present, but also the order in which actions occur. Evaluate time-ordered video segments against records confirming the procedure's order.
learning.concept: When temporal order in continuous video is needed for a decision, a single frame or aggregated values are insufficient.

A.text: Use a photo of the finished product and assume the order was correct if all components are visible.
A.explanation: The action sequence cannot be recovered from the same final state.

B.text: Preserve the continuous video and its temporal order for the work in question, and evaluate detection on segments that a person has checked as correct-order and reverse-order examples.
B.explanation: This retains both the information needed to distinguish order and the ground truth.

C.text: Use only daily work counts and component counts, and infer which tasks were performed in reverse order from the daily proportions.
C.explanation: Daily summaries do not preserve the temporal order of individual tasks.

D.text: Keep only still frames in which tools are clear, remove timestamps, and classify whether tools are present.
D.explanation: This retains some visual clues but discards timestamps and continuity.

aib-c01-d1-031@1.title: Identify a field unavailable at prediction time
aib-c01-d1-031@1.prompt: A wholesaler wants to predict at order time whether next-day delivery will be late. Historical records contain the order time, destination, and refund category assigned after delivery was completed. Including the refund category substantially improved validation accuracy. What is the first step in reevaluating the model?

learning.reason: A field that exists in historical records but becomes known only after the time of prediction can make accuracy appear higher by leaking future information. Validate again using only fields available when the order is placed.
learning.concept: Exclude from model inputs any historical values that become known only after the prediction time.

A.text: Because the refund category is related to delays, preserve the validation accuracy by having shipping staff enter a provisional value.
A.explanation: A provisional value is not the same information as the actual refund category, so the original accuracy cannot be assumed.

B.text: Remove the order time for anonymization, randomly split the historical rows, and retain the refund category.
B.explanation: A random split does not make information that is unavailable at prediction time available.

C.text: Convert the refund category to numeric codes to make it harder to identify, and remove the field name from displayed explanations.
C.explanation: Changing the values or how they are displayed does not prevent use of post-event information.

D.text: Restrict the inputs to fields available when the order is placed, exclude the refund category determined after delivery, and validate again.
D.explanation: This makes the information available during evaluation consistent with what will be available in production.

aib-c01-d1-032@1.title: Separate shared terminology from verification of certification coverage
aib-c01-d1-032@1.prompt: Two AI vendors use the terms “training,” “inference,” and “updates” differently across their documents. One vendor’s proposal says that because it uses an ISO-derived glossary, the customer’s services are also covered by third-party certification. Select TWO actions for the procurement team.

learning.reason: Define the parties’ contractual terms using shared terminology. Separately, if certification is claimed, verify the organization, service, and scope against the certificate.
learning.concept: Conformance to a terminology standard and third-party certification of a specific organization and scope require different evidence.

A.text: Because the vendor has standardized its terminology, rely only on sales materials and do not request disclosure of the certification’s scope.
A.explanation: Sales materials do not establish whether the relevant organization, product, or operations are covered.

B.text: For any service claimed to be certified, check the organization named on the certificate and its scope, and verify that the proposed work is included.
B.explanation: This checks the use of standardized terminology separately from what the certification covers.

C.text: Do not include each vendor’s terminology in the contract; treat similar terms as synonyms.
C.explanation: Interpretation can vary when the contractual assumptions or scope of work differ.

D.text: Assume that if the same terminology is used, the specific services and contract are included in the same certification scope.
D.explanation: Using a glossary does not prove what was included in the assessment.

E.text: Use a shared glossary to define terms used in the contract, and document differences in meaning between vendors.
E.explanation: This reduces mismatched expectations caused by differences in terminology.

aib-c01-d1-033@1.title: Do not rely on historical decisions when the rules are explicit
aib-c01-d1-033@1.prompt: A library wants to allocate mobile-library borrowing slots by branch. The allocation caps, priorities, and overall cap are established by ordinance and agreement, and tie-breaking rules are also defined. Past allocations mostly reflect an older agreement. What method will produce the same result for everyone in accordance with the new agreement?

learning.reason: Specify the established constraints, optimization objective, and tie-breaking rules, then calculate the allocation. There is no need to learn the old policy.
learning.concept: For an allocation determined by known constraints and objectives, consider deterministic optimization instead of learning from past decisions.

A.text: Specify the caps, priorities, and tie-breaking rules, then allocate using deterministic constrained optimization and check each condition.
A.explanation: This directly meets the new agreement’s conditions and the requirement for reproducible results.

B.text: Give the original agreement text to generative AI and choose the most readable table from several answers.
B.explanation: Readability does not establish compliance with the constraints or reproducibility under the same conditions.

C.text: Train on past allocations as the correct answers, then use agreement with past allocations to verify compliance with the new agreement.
C.explanation: Reproducing results that reflect the old agreement does not show compliance with the new conditions.

D.text: Instead of using the explicit rules, group branches by similarity and automatically assign the same number of slots to each group.
D.explanation: Similar branches are not necessarily subject to the same contractual priorities or caps.

aib-c01-d1-034@1.title: Set an expiration and transition criteria for a tool under evaluation
aib-c01-d1-034@1.prompt: The product department wants to use an external AI image-classification tool that is still under evaluation for only three weeks. Testing with public samples is permitted, but pre-commercialization product images must not be submitted. What controls should be put in place to prevent the tool from remaining in use after the evaluator changes roles?

learning.reason: Register the exception’s permitted scope and expiration date, its owner, and evaluation evidence; define automatic expiration and the conditions for moving to an approved approach.
learning.concept: Limit evaluation exceptions by purpose, data, and duration, then transition to formal approval or end use based on the review.

A.text: Grant permanent approval when the trial starts, then inspect submitted content later and revoke access only if necessary.
A.explanation: This grants an unapproved scope to a tool that is still under evaluation.

B.text: Record only the tool’s name in the company-wide AI inventory and let any department use it while the evaluation continues.
B.explanation: There are no restrictions on purpose, owner, data, or duration.

C.text: Register the evaluator and the expiration date for testing with public samples, stop access when the approval expires, and decide whether to grant formal approval or end use based on the evaluation results.
C.explanation: This makes the evaluation’s scope and what happens afterward clear.

D.text: Continue using the tool only through individual accounts on the evaluation team, then ask about usage history after the evaluator changes roles before granting formal approval.
D.explanation: This does not let the organization control continued use or the scope of submitted content.

aib-c01-d1-035@1.title: Distinguish evidence retrieval from generation failures
aib-c01-d1-035@1.prompt: A customer-facing AI gives an incorrect answer about the compatibility of a specialty part listed in an approved catalog. When the relevant passage was provided directly in the input for the question that led to a complaint, the AI answered correctly. In normal retrieval, however, the passage was not among the top candidates. What is the most appropriate next test?

learning.reason: Because the AI can answer when given the correct evidence, first measure whether that evidence can be retrieved, then improve search and the index.
learning.concept: Confirm that the AI can answer when given the correct material, then address gaps in knowledge retrieval.

A.text: Remove part numbers from the catalog so the model can answer using more general product knowledge.
A.explanation: This loses information needed to identify compatibility and makes it harder to retrieve the relevant material.

B.text: Fine-tune the model using only questions it answered correctly during testing, without examining retrieval results.
B.explanation: The retrieval problem already identified in the confirmed failure case would remain.

C.text: Configure the model to give longer answers, and treat a detailed explanation as evidence that the compatibility answer is correct.
C.explanation: The amount of explanation does not show whether the supporting evidence was retrieved.

D.text: Measure the retrieval rate of the correct passage across a set of questions, and incorporate part numbers or aliases into retrieval. After improving retrieval, reassess answer correctness.
D.explanation: This allows retrieval and generation to be evaluated separately.

aib-c01-d1-036@1.title: Why the same learning method can produce different results
aib-c01-d1-036@1.prompt: A model estimates equipment priority. It is retrained using the same learning method but with six months of new actual results added. When given the same input as before, the new version produces a different priority. The team member believes the result should be unchanged because the method was not changed. Which explanation is appropriate?

learning.reason: Even when the training procedure is unchanged, different training data can produce different coefficients or conditions. Compare the old and new models as versions and assess the business impact of the difference.
learning.concept: A learning algorithm is the procedure for producing a model; models produced from different data can make different decisions.

A.text: A difference in predictions for the same input proves that the device necessarily retrained the model while it was running.
A.explanation: Predictions can change solely because the old and new trained models differ.

B.text: If the input column names and order are the same, only the learning method determines subsequent predictions.
B.explanation: The learned values also affect the result.

C.text: Even with the same learning method, the model's internal state learned from the data can change, so the same input can produce a different prediction.
C.explanation: This correctly distinguishes the method from the model produced by training.

D.text: Once a prediction changes, the new model should be considered correct, and historical data should not be used for validation.
D.explanation: A difference does not prove improvement. The result must be checked against actual outcomes.

aib-c01-d1-037@1.title: Evaluate performance on real data when supplementing tests with generated examples
aib-c01-d1-037@1.prompt: During development of a model that routes failure reports, there are not enough training examples for rare reports. Business experts have a small number of real examples and propose using generative AI to create variations in wording. What is the most appropriate way to use synthetic examples?

learning.reason: Generative AI can expand examples of different wording, but a synthetic distribution may not represent real operations. Validate synthetic examples as supplemental data, reserve real examples independently, and measure accuracy against them.
learning.concept: Separate the use of generative AI to create synthetic examples from evaluation of a predictive model in the real environment.

A.text: Treat synthetic examples alone as the actual ground truth, and split examples created from the same generation instructions between training and testing.
A.explanation: This cannot measure differences in real-world occurrence, wording, or difficulty.

B.text: Use synthetic examples validated by experts to supplement training or robustness checks, and reserve approved real examples for an independent evaluation set.
B.explanation: This limits the role of generated data and measures performance under conditions closer to the real environment.

C.text: Assume that the number of synthetic examples matches the occurrence rate of rare reports, and set alert thresholds for predictions based on the synthetic-example ratio.
C.explanation: The number of generated examples does not indicate the occurrence frequency in the real environment.

D.text: Because evaluating real examples is difficult, use only the routing model's confidence scores as the test's pass criteria.
D.explanation: Business performance cannot be assessed without comparing results with ground truth.

aib-c01-d1-038@1.title: Keep recognized values separate from table structure
aib-c01-d1-038@1.prompt: You need to extract item-and-quantity pairs from a two-column order PDF. Text recognition can read both numbers, but concatenating the text in reading order has produced cases where a quantity from the right column is associated with an item from the left column. What should you change to preserve the item and quantity associations?

learning.reason: Text extracted from a PDF can be correct without guaranteeing that logical fields are associated correctly. Use table rows, columns, and positions to pair items and quantities from the same row, and validate them against the original.
learning.concept: Preserve and validate position and structure when extracting fields from forms where text alone can lose table row-and-column associations.

A.text: Set a character-recognition accuracy target and automatically register every order in which each character was read correctly.
A.explanation: Even with high character-recognition accuracy, errors can remain in pairing items and quantities from different rows.

B.text: Put the numbers in a separate list, sort them in ascending order, and assign them from the top of the item list.
B.explanation: Sorting loses the associations in the original document.

C.text: Preserve positions, table rows and columns, and page references when extracting pairs, then test them against the associations in the original document.
C.explanation: Extraction can be validated using both text and structural information.

D.text: Accept only orders from which signature text can be extracted with high accuracy, and do not evaluate item-and-quantity associations.
D.explanation: Signature-field quality cannot verify table associations.

aib-c01-d1-039@1.title: Evaluate forecasts of the future against historical training conditions
aib-c01-d1-039@1.prompt: You designed a model that predicts demand for the update month each month. The past three years of sales data contain seasonality within fiscal years and changes in corporate contracts. A proposal says the model can be used starting next month, based on accuracy from a random split that includes the latest data. Which validation approach is closer to real operations?

learning.reason: Train only on history that was available at each forecast point, and evaluate on the following period. Changing the origin helps assess resilience to seasonality and contract changes.
learning.concept: Prevent future information from entering time-series training splits, and use shifted evaluation origins to assess future performance.

A.text: Use only the oldest period for validation, and use a model trained on later contract changes to estimate accuracy for next month.
A.explanation: This evaluates predictions from the future into the past, which differs from the order in actual operation.

B.text: Train and validate on the latest finalized data, and pass if the same case produces a reproducible output.
B.explanation: Performance on an unknown period cannot be determined using information included in training.

C.text: Use multiple historical cutoff points as forecast origins, train only on data available before each origin, and predict the periods that follow before comparing the results.
C.explanation: This reproduces the information available at each point in time.

D.text: Randomly split the data across fiscal years, include history from after each validation row's following month in training, and compare average values.
D.explanation: This uses actual results from later dates that would not be available at prediction time.

aib-c01-d1-040@1.title: Deciding what to automate when exceptions are rare
aib-c01-d1-040@1.prompt: In the procurement process for supplies, the existing system can handle standard requests. There are only a few special-purpose requests each month, reviewers use different reasoning to decide them, and historical records contain only the final outcomes. What should be done first to align the criteria and make decisions on exceptions reproducible?

learning.reason: Define the criteria for exceptions with the reviewers, then have people record and compare the rationale and outcomes. Set up intake and recordkeeping using the existing approach, and consider automating decisions only after they can be evaluated using consistent rationale.
learning.concept: When the correct outcome and criteria are not yet established, improve recordkeeping and review before automating exception decisions.

A.text: Leave exception decisions to one experienced reviewer and add only the outcomes to the existing records.
A.explanation: This may reduce differences for now, but others cannot reproduce or verify the reasoning.

B.text: Set up a process to receive exception requests and record the rationale, then have reviewers check decisions together. Consider automating decisions once the criteria and evaluation cases are in place.
B.explanation: This starts by recording rationale that can be reviewed later, for decisions that still require human judgment.

C.text: Apply the review criteria for standard requests to special-purpose requests without modification.
C.explanation: Even if the results are reproducible, they may not be appropriate because the reasons specific to special-purpose requests are not considered.

D.text: Train a classifier using only the recorded approval outcomes and preserve each reviewer's approval rate.
D.explanation: This would reproduce variation without its rationale and would not align the criteria across reviewers.

aib-c01-d1-041@1.title: Investigating why alert volume changed
aib-c01-d1-041@1.prompt: The number of maintenance AI alerts rose on the day administrators expanded the weekly inspection capacity and lowered the decision threshold; the hit rate per alert fell. The model version is unchanged, and confirmed failure records are available after the fact. How should you determine whether the model has degraded?

learning.reason: Lowering the threshold can change the hit rate among selected cases even if the model has not changed. Compare predictions using the same threshold or ranking performance, and evaluate the effect of the operational rule separately.
learning.concept: Measure changes in prediction ranking or calibration separately from changes to operational thresholds.

A.text: Retrain the model based only on the lower hit rate, keep the new threshold, and make no other checks.
A.explanation: This does not separate the effect of the operational change from model degradation.

B.text: Restore the previous threshold and skip checking actual outcomes if the alert count returns to its previous level.
B.explanation: A matching alert count does not show that the model is correct at the same rate.

C.text: Use confirmed outcomes to compare predictions from the old and new periods at the same threshold and with the same ranking metric, separating that comparison from alert volume caused by the capacity change.
C.explanation: This lets you assess changes in model performance under the same decision conditions.

D.text: Treat the increase in alert volume as the amount of degradation, and always exclude new cases selected by the expanded inspection capacity from accuracy measurements.
D.explanation: This does not test why alert volume increased or how the model performs on the new cases.

aib-c01-d1-042@1.title: Preserving comparable evidence across split documents
aib-c01-d1-042@1.prompt: The compliance department wants to identify required procedures that are not consistently followed across 30 sites and determine which sites are involved, using lengthy reports. All the reports cannot fit into a single input, but each can be processed on its own. The final report must include policy numbers and references to the evidence for each site. What is an appropriate approach?

learning.reason: For each report, extract the required procedure items using a common structure and retain references to the supporting evidence. Compare sites using these concise, consistent records. If the extracts are insufficient, check the original text.
learning.concept: When context limits prevent processing all documents at once, extract the required fields and citations from each document, then consolidate them into a shorter input for comparison.

A.text: Infer noncompliance from the documents for just one site, then fill in the rest using general industry knowledge rather than the reports.
A.explanation: This cannot be verified across all sites, and it does not provide the sources required for the report.

B.text: Concatenate only the beginning of every report, discard later sections, and generate an explanation of the evidence.
B.explanation: This may miss evidence about procedures that appears outside the opening sections.

C.text: Write a free-form, one-sentence summary for each site and remove policy numbers and document references to reduce the length.
C.explanation: This prevents comparison across different items and does not provide the evidence required for the final report.

D.text: For each report, extract the status and references to the original text using common policy numbers, then consolidate those records for cross-site comparison and review.
D.explanation: This reduces the input size while preserving consistent comparison criteria and sources across all reports.

aib-c01-d2-025@1.title: Improving experiment prioritization in research
aib-c01-d2-025@1.prompt: The materials development department has hundreds of formulation candidates but can run durability tests on only 30 per month. Historical formulation conditions and durability test results are available, and an actual durability test is required before a product can be adopted. What is the best first AI initiative to accelerate time to market?

learning.reason: Rank candidates using predictions and measure whether the limited testing capacity can identify a passing candidate sooner. Continue the actual tests required for adoption.
learning.concept: Separate the effect of AI on candidate selection from properties that must be confirmed through physical experiments.

A.text: Use predictions to prioritize candidates, then compare the time and number of experiments needed to find passing candidates using the same testing capacity.
A.explanation: This connects AI output to business impact that can be verified through experiments.

B.text: Generate product descriptions and measure research speed by the time the research team spends creating new copy.
B.explanation: This does not improve the main constraint: durability test capacity.

C.text: Skip actual testing for the formulation with the highest predicted probability of passing, and judge the initiative by the reduction in experiments.
C.explanation: This does not verify that the product adoption requirement has been met.

D.text: Have AI summarize past tests, and consider durability verification complete if the summaries receive more views.
D.explanation: Use of summaries is different from the speed at which passing materials are found.

aib-c01-d2-026@1.title: Compare building in-house with buying while accounting for demand fluctuations in general-purpose work
aib-c01-d2-026@1.prompt: An education company wants to provide lecture transcripts within four weeks. A validated commercial service meets its quality and contract requirements and offers pay-as-you-go pricing during slow periods and reserved capacity during peak periods. Building in-house requires an operations owner at all times, but none is available. Transcription itself is not a source of unique value. Which investment decision is appropriate?

learning.reason: For a standard capability that does not differentiate the business, start by considering a purchase and estimate costs across a range of usage levels, including switching costs. Be cautious about long-term fixed commitments that assume high utilization.
learning.concept: Compare the fixed costs of building a non-differentiating standard capability in-house with the cost of purchasing capacity at different commitment levels.

A.text: If quality is the same, build a custom solution and assume no operations owner is needed in the meantime, even before hiring is complete.
A.explanation: This does not meet the deadline or ongoing operations constraints.

B.text: Because transcription is not a differentiator, launch on the assumption that a free trial tier can be used for every lecture indefinitely.
B.explanation: This does not confirm production capacity or the conditions for continued use.

C.text: Make the peak-period maximum volume the minimum purchase commitment year-round, and decide whether costs are lowest based only on the reserved-capacity rate.
C.explanation: This ignores annual costs that include unused capacity.

D.text: Revalidate quality using representative lectures, compare pay-as-you-go pricing with reserved capacity across a range of usage levels, and buy the service.
D.explanation: This fits the deadline and operational capacity while avoiding a contract that is unfavorable under fluctuating demand.

aib-c01-d2-027@1.title: Prioritize initiatives based on the processing capacity of downstream teams
aib-c01-d2-027@1.prompt: The enterprise sales team must choose one of two initiatives. Generating proposal text would triple the number of proposals, but review capacity is already at its limit, and no additional review staff can be secured. The other initiative analyzes lost-deal reasons and increases the proportion of promising opportunities among proposals using the same review capacity. The business goal is the number of deals won, not the number of proposals. Which initiative should be prioritized?

learning.reason: When review is the bottleneck, producing more proposals is unlikely to increase wins. Run a small comparison to test whether changing the mix of proposals that can be reviewed improves win outcomes.
learning.concept: Prioritize an increase in valuable outcomes that downstream teams can process over upstream generation speed.

A.text: Roll out proposal generation across the company and arrange for review capacity only after an increase in wins has been achieved.
A.explanation: This postpones capacity for a review step required before a deal can be won.

B.text: Decide based only on the number of sales users, and measure neither the review process nor wins until both initiatives are complete.
B.explanation: This leaves out the constrained step that limits value and the intended business outcome.

C.text: Test filtering for promising opportunities within current review capacity, and verify whether the same number of reviews results in more wins.
C.explanation: This accounts for the capacity constraint and ties the test to the business goal.

D.text: Choose the initiative that triples the number of generated proposals, and count unreviewed proposals toward projected wins at the same rate.
D.explanation: This assumes benefits from proposals that cannot get through the review limit.

aib-c01-d2-028@1.title: Recognize when duplicate entry is caused by a gap between systems
aib-c01-d2-028@1.prompt: Registering a business partner requires staff to re-enter a normalized company ID, already entered in the application system, into the accounting system. The value is transferred as is, approval rules are consistent, and both systems have existing integration endpoints. An AI-based solution is proposed to prevent entry errors. Which recommendation is appropriate?

learning.reason: If no interpretation or inference is needed and the cause is notification or copying between systems, use a simple integration to eliminate the extra entry.
learning.concept: After approval, transfer the confirmed company ID through an integration so it only needs to be entered once.

A.text: Use AI to predict past errors by the staff responsible for copying the data, and review re-entry only when the staff member is deemed high risk.
A.explanation: This leaves duplicate entry in place and does not directly ensure input accuracy.

B.text: Have AI infer the ID from the company name, and compare the time required for inference with the time required for copying.
B.explanation: The correct ID already exists, so inference is unnecessary and could introduce incorrect estimates.

C.text: Send the approved ID through the existing integration endpoint, and reconcile the transfer result and any retry after a failure.
C.explanation: This eliminates duplicate entry and makes integration failures traceable.

D.text: Recreate the application with generative AI, embed the company ID in the text, and have another department extract it manually.
D.explanation: This makes the process for transferring a confirmed value more complex.

aib-c01-d2-029@1.title: Evaluate a switch by including one-time migration costs and projected usage growth
aib-c01-d2-029@1.prompt: A candidate internal AI platform reduces the current inference unit price by 30%. Migration requires a three-month overlapping contract and staff retraining, and if usage doubles next year, the new platform will use a different pricing tier. Quality does not differ significantly. Which comparison is most useful before deciding whether to adopt it?

learning.reason: Using the same period and multiple usage assumptions, include migration, overlap, training, ongoing operations, and usage tiers to assess total switching costs and when savings would be realized.
learning.concept: Compare migration and parallel operations, usage-dependent pricing, and steady-state operating costs over the same period.

A.text: Ignore migration costs because they are one-time costs, and calculate the new platform's cost using only the maximum usage projected for next year.
A.explanation: The comparison period and assumptions do not match those for staying on the current platform.

B.text: Include the overlapping contract, training, operations, and pricing tiers; compare staying and switching over the same period under multiple usage scenarios.
B.explanation: This also shows whether the decision changes as usage grows.

C.text: Calculate annual costs using only the difference in current inference unit prices, and switch if the new price is lower.
C.explanation: This overlooks one-time migration costs and future pricing tiers.

D.text: Compare the projected payment for the first month of migration with the old platform's annual average.
D.explanation: This compares different conditions during startup and steady-state operations.

aib-c01-d2-030@1.title: Measure Rework Burden When Rework Items Have Different Costs
aib-c01-d2-030@1.prompt: An architecture firm observes that AI-assisted drafting leads to more formatting fixes but fewer full redesigns. Both a partial design revision and a full redesign are counted as one rework item. The goal is to reduce rework burden per delivered project. Which primary metric is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Total the actual rework time for each project and normalize it per delivery for a comparable mix of projects. This captures the different burdens of formatting changes and full redesigns.
learning.concept: To assess improvement, account for the actual burden and work volume instead of simply counting rework items.

A.text: Measure only the time spent on the initial draft and exclude the time for all subsequent revisions.
A.explanation: This leaves the rework burden the goal is intended to measure out of the metric.

B.text: Count only full redesigns in each period, without accounting for differences in the number of delivered projects or other revisions.
B.explanation: This omits both the volume of deliveries and the burden from accumulated revisions.

C.text: For a comparable mix of projects, total the actual time spent on revisions, from formatting fixes to redesigns, and compare the result per delivered project.
C.explanation: This reflects the different burdens of revision types and makes comparisons easier when delivery volumes change.

D.text: Treat minor fixes and full redesigns as one item each, and compare only the number of revisions per delivered project.
D.explanation: This overlooks the difference in burden per revision.

aib-c01-d2-031@1.title: Isolate the Effect of Process Improvements Introduced at the Same Time
aib-c01-d2-031@1.prompt: Next month, a billing team will adopt a new form template for everyone and can add AI review for some team members. The template alone is expected to reduce entry errors compared with the current form. Leadership wants to assess the additional effect of AI. Which design is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Keep the existing measurement definition and compare groups using the same new template, with and without AI. Align factors such as task complexity to separate the impact of simultaneous changes.
learning.concept: When the workflow changes for everyone, estimate AI's effect by comparing AI and non-AI groups under the same conditions.

A.text: Use the same new template for comparable teams with and without AI, and compare errors over the same period using the same evaluation criteria.
A.explanation: Keeping the template's effect common to both groups makes it possible to assess the effect of AI.

B.text: Include only low-complexity bills that AI preapproved, and compare them with all bills processed using the old form.
B.explanation: The bills differ in complexity, so the additional effect of AI cannot be determined.

C.text: Use the results of high-performing employees after AI adoption as the baseline for organization-wide reporting.
C.explanation: Selecting the comparison group based on post-adoption performance distorts the measured effect.

D.text: Compare next month's results for AI users with this month's results for everyone using only the old form.
D.explanation: The effects of the template and AI are confounded.

aib-c01-d2-032@1.title: Avoid Double-Counting Released Capacity and Reduced Cash Spending
aib-c01-d2-032@1.prompt: An administrative AI assistant saves 80 hours of work each month. Of those hours, 30 let the organization reduce a contractor engagement, saving ¥120,000 per month. The remaining 50 hours are redirected to other work by existing employees at the same salaries; incremental profit has not yet been measured. Operating costs are ¥50,000 per month. What verified net cash impact can be reported for the current month?

learning.reason: Subtract the monthly operating cost of ¥50,000 from the ¥120,000 in contractor spending actually avoided, for a net savings of ¥70,000. Report the employees' released capacity separately rather than counting it as a cash benefit.
learning.concept: Separate unused employee capacity from verified cash savings, and avoid counting the same hours in both cost and benefit calculations.

A.text: A loss of ¥50,000. Because salaries are unchanged, the contractor reduction is not a benefit either.
A.explanation: This excludes contractor spending that can actually be reduced as a separate expense.

B.text: ¥120,000. Report the reduction in contractor spending as the net impact.
B.explanation: This does not subtract the new operating cost of ¥50,000.

C.text: ¥270,000. Apply the contractor's hourly rate to all 80 hours saved, then subtract operating costs.
C.explanation: This treats employee time as reduced cash spending even though salary expenses are unchanged.

D.text: ¥70,000. Subtract the ¥50,000 operating cost from the ¥120,000 contractor savings, and report the 50 employee hours separately.
D.explanation: This distinguishes measured cash spending from the additional capacity created.

aib-c01-d2-033@1.title: Measure Early Signs of Proficiency Between Training and Pilots
aib-c01-d2-033@1.prompt: An insurance operations department wants to shorten the time it takes new hires to process applications correctly. The final assessment is several months away, but the department can score practice cases of the same difficulty every week. Which leading indicator is most useful?

learning.reason: Tracking the number of weeks until a person correctly handles cases of the same difficulty for the required number of consecutive attempts can reveal changes in proficiency before the final assessment. This should be distinguished from deciding that training is complete.
learning.concept: Use a leading KPI to track when users can repeatedly perform tasks correctly; do not equate logins with proficiency.

A.text: The number of weeks it takes a new hire to correctly complete the prescribed number of consecutive tasks of the same difficulty.
A.explanation: This can measure skill retention earlier than the final assessment.

B.text: The total number of questions a new hire sends to the AI.
B.explanation: The count can rise when someone is repeatedly uncertain, so it does not necessarily indicate successful learning.

C.text: The proportion of new hires who open the AI interface on the first day of training.
C.explanation: First-day use is distinct from acquiring job skills.

D.text: The average salary and retention rate of new hires one year later.
D.explanation: These are measured too late and do not directly measure proficiency in processing applications.

aib-c01-d2-034@1.title: Reuse processing for the same request to reduce costs
aib-c01-d2-034@1.prompt: An AI system recreates the same short summary in the same language every night for a public brochure shared across all locations. The material is updated a few times a month, and a new summary is always required on the day it is updated. Which cost measure preserves quality and update speed?

learning.reason: Reuse an approved output when the document version, language, and summary method have not changed. Regenerate it if any of them changes, and measure cost per completed request and version consistency.
learning.concept: Reuse results only for processing with stable inputs and the same approved version; do not mix results for newer versions or personal information.

A.text: Reuse an approved result for the same document version, language, and summary instructions, and regenerate it whenever any of these changes.
A.explanation: Limit reuse to each condition that can affect the result.

B.text: Generate a summary only once a month and keep displaying it until the next run, even if the material is updated.
B.explanation: This fails the requirement to provide new content on the day of an update.

C.text: Store summaries using only the document name and reuse them for requests in other languages and for newer versions.
C.explanation: This could return a summary with different content or in the wrong language.

D.text: Use a cheaper model to summarize every document every night without checking whether the quality matches the existing approach.
D.explanation: This still repeats unnecessary work and does not ensure quality.

aib-c01-d2-035@1.title: Compare competitors that do not use AI using the same outcome measures
aib-c01-d2-035@1.prompt: In a shipment-contract tracking service, customers are switching from an AI-enabled competitor to a non-AI competitor because filing a tracking notice is easier there. Your company also has an AI budget. Which analysis should you start with to identify an opportunity to improve your competitive position?

learning.reason: Compare the alternatives customers choose using the same measures, such as filing effort, outcomes, and price. Then separate the steps that create the gap from the possible ways to improve them.
learning.concept: Analyze the competitive landscape without assuming AI is required, and assess alternatives based on the quality, effort, and price customers compare.

A.text: Average the number of new customers at companies that use AI, then make the AI model faster until it reaches that number.
A.explanation: The relationship between customers' reasons for choosing a service and model speed has not been tested.

B.text: Include non-AI competitors, compare the effort to complete a filing, accuracy, and price, and identify the step where the gap arises.
B.explanation: This reveals competitive differences among the alternatives customers actually compare.

C.text: Compare only competitors that describe AI features, and prioritize products where your company can add AI.
C.explanation: This does not analyze the alternatives that are actually taking customers away.

D.text: Survey existing customers only about the number of AI features, without asking about filing experience or comparisons with competitors.
D.explanation: This does not reveal why customers choose a service or where the current process creates friction.

aib-c01-d2-036@1.title: Test a new offering unit for customers that were previously uneconomical to serve
aib-c01-d2-036@1.prompt: A construction-estimating support company could sell only annual contracts because expert document reviews had a fixed cost. AI now organizes the documents and shortens the time people spend on the final review, making a per-project offering for small customers feasible to consider. Which approach is appropriate for validating the business model?

learning.reason: Test acquisition cost, cost per project, and willingness to pay on a small scale with the new offering unit. Determine whether it is viable while existing contracts remain in place.
learning.concept: When AI lowers delivery costs, design a new contract unit for customers with lower usage volumes.

A.text: Remove the people responsible for all customer reviews before changing the contract unit, and minimize costs by relying on AI alone.
A.explanation: This evaluates profitability after removing the required quality and human final review.

B.text: Keep only annual contracts and assume the new customer segment can now be acquired because internal processing costs have fallen.
B.explanation: This does not test the offering unit customers want or their willingness to pay.

C.text: Run a paid per-project pilot with small customers and measure conversion, cost per project, and the effect on existing contracts.
C.explanation: This tests whether the new sales unit and cost structure are viable.

D.text: Offer the per-project service for free and assume that if usage increases, the same number of customers will use it when it is paid.
D.explanation: Free usage does not measure willingness to pay.

aib-c01-d2-037@1.title: Build business strengths that endure when switching to a new model
aib-c01-d2-037@1.prompt: A business purchasing-support service offers summarization using a model that competitors can also obtain. Your company can easily add connections to each customer's ordering and approval processes, but a team member wants to prioritize temporarily reaching the top of the model rankings. Which investment will help the service continue to be chosen?

learning.reason: Integrate with customers' approval workflows while keeping the architecture model-swappable, and demonstrate value through reduced rework and implementation effort.
learning.concept: Build value in customer workflow integrations, domain expertise, and operational track record rather than relying on temporary performance from a general-purpose model.

A.text: Lock customers into long-term contracts and prevent them from exporting their work so they cannot easily switch.
A.explanation: This does not create a reason to choose the service based on usability or measured outcomes.

B.text: Develop reusable connections to approval workflows and ordering systems, preserve the ability to switch models, and measure improvements in rework and implementation time.
B.explanation: This strengthens practical value that remains even as model performance changes.

C.text: Sign only a short-term, nonexclusive contract with the top-ranked model and make its capabilities the sole competitive advantage.
C.explanation: Competitors can obtain the same model, and any change in ranking can erase the difference.

D.text: Require every customer to use the same standalone screen and remove connections to their existing ordering processes.
D.explanation: This discards an existing implementation capability and does not improve customers' workflows.

aib-c01-d2-038@1.title: Separate the minimum market-entry requirement from research investment
aib-c01-d2-038@1.prompt: For document search in the public sector, competitors offer nearly the same level of search assistance, and that level will become a participation requirement in the next bid. Your company can adapt commercial components in the short term, but developing a proprietary model would miss the next deadline. What is the best level of investment?

learning.reason: Secure the capability and ongoing operation needed for the bid in the short term. Consider additional research costs only when evidence shows a difference customers will value.
learning.concept: Meet an AI capability that has become a market-entry requirement while limiting extra investment that does not differentiate the offering.

A.text: Invest in adapting and validating existing tools to meet the required level, then assess further research if evidence shows it could differentiate the offering.
A.explanation: This separates the necessary defensive investment from optional differentiation.

B.text: Skip the next bid requirement to research the highest performance of a proprietary model, and judge investment only by future market share.
B.explanation: This forfeits a near-term market participation requirement without evidence that research will create an advantage.

C.text: Pay the entire budget as a minimum usage commitment based on the reputation of one model's high performance.
C.explanation: This does not validate the bid requirement, actual demand, or additional costs.

D.text: Since the features are comparable to competitors', make no AI investment and state during the bid that the search-assistance requirement is met.
D.explanation: Compliance cannot be demonstrated without the required implementation and validation.

aib-c01-d2-039@1.title: Evaluate developer assistance by the work required to ship a release
aib-c01-d2-039@1.prompt: In the software department, work to update undocumented legacy features is stalled. AI can generate candidate diffs and test ideas, but the goal is to deliver reviewed changes sooner, not to increase lines of code. How should the trial be used and evaluated?

learning.reason: Have people validate and use candidate changes, then compare end-to-end time from creation through review, rework, and delivery, along with defects found after release.
learning.concept: Evaluate completed, usable changes, review burden, and defects rather than the volume of generated code.

A.text: Compare only review scores for the changes, without recording the extra time spent revising them or when they are delivered.
A.explanation: Review-time scores alone do not show whether the backlog has decreased.

B.text: Let the responsible developers review and adopt candidate diffs and test ideas, and measure delivery time—including review and rework—as well as defects.
B.explanation: This captures both the intended business outcome and potential side effects.

C.text: Automatically incorporate every candidate diff and count the generated lines as the amount of completed change.
C.explanation: This does not measure time to deliver reviewed changes or defects.

D.text: Generate promotional copy for new features only, and treat increased readership as an efficiency gain in legacy feature updates.
D.explanation: This does not address the workflow where the updates are stalled.

aib-c01-d2-040@1.title: Judge whether to continue a funded trial by its future impact
aib-c01-d2-040@1.prompt: An AI purchasing advisor sped up the display of recommendations, but across three branches the extra work caused by serious inventory errors exceeded the benefit. Correcting the suspected cause twice produced the same result. The department head signed an expensive contract and wants to roll it out to all remaining branches. What is the appropriate decision?

learning.reason: Money already paid does not improve future returns. Use the repeated negative business impact to stop the rollout, review the contract, and assess other initiatives or conditions for a new trial.
learning.concept: Separate past spending from future value, and stop an initiative whose adverse impact persists after realistic improvements.

A.text: Stop the evaluation because branch reports cannot be compared, and decide on the rollout based on company-wide usage rates.
A.explanation: This replaces evidence that can measure value and harm with usage rates.

B.text: Report only the improvement in recommendation display time, and exclude correction work from the investment evaluation because another department handles it.
B.explanation: This leaves out the real burden caused by the initiative.

C.text: Roll it out to all remaining branches to spread the contract cost across more cases, since the money has already been spent.
C.explanation: This uses a cost already incurred to justify a choice expected to cause further losses.

D.text: Pause the expansion and assess projected losses from further rollout and the contract termination terms. Consider another trial only if there is evidence that the adverse impact has been resolved.
D.explanation: This decision is based on future value, losses, and costs that will still be incurred.

aib-c01-d2-041@1.title: Choose procurement when an existing in-house team can meet a unique requirement
aib-c01-d2-041@1.prompt: A company that sells dispatch software needs a feature that lets customers frequently validate their own rules. External products have fixed specifications and can be configured only with the rules in place at the time of contracting. The company has the staff needed to develop and operate the feature, and validation has confirmed that implementation by the deadline is feasible. What should it do next?

learning.reason: Because custom rules shape product value and the deadline and in-house capability have been validated, consider building the core capability in-house. Compare it with procurement options, including operating costs.
learning.concept: Compare in-house development with external products when the requirement and the ability to own a differentiating capability are established.

A.text: Build the core rule-management capability in-house, and compare a validated plan with external options, including maintenance and operating costs.
A.explanation: This keeps the differentiating capability under the company's control and includes ongoing operating costs in the estimate.

B.text: Move all implementation to an external provider and sign a contract that prevents the company from making changes until the provider revises its product.
B.explanation: This makes a core competitive capability dependent on an external provider's schedule.

C.text: Approve the in-house build on the assumption that no monitoring or support costs will arise after testing.
C.explanation: Maintenance and operating costs also need to be included in the investment decision.

D.text: Substitute a product with fixed specifications and tell customers who use custom rules that they will no longer be able to change them.
D.explanation: This removes the ongoing change capability customers need.

aib-c01-d2-042@1.title: Decide whether investment in a complex AI model is justified by current performance criteria
aib-c01-d2-042@1.prompt: An internal cafeteria forecasts weekly ingredient quantities. Using the average of the most recent four weeks and adjustments for closure days, it meets its waste and stockout targets. A complex forecasting model has slightly lower historical error, but operating it requires extra work from staff. What is the best near-term choice?

learning.reason: When the existing method meets the defined business targets, check whether a small numerical improvement justifies the added cost. If there is no demonstrated need, retain the method that is easier to explain.
learning.concept: Compare incremental improvements when a transparent, low-operational-burden method already meets the business requirements for accuracy and explainability.

A.text: Move entirely to the advanced model whenever its historical forecast error is even slightly lower.
A.explanation: This does not compare the size of the measured difference with the burden on staff.

B.text: Keep using the current simple method and monitor waste and stockouts. If improvement becomes necessary, compare the additional cost with the business benefit.
B.explanation: This maintains the target performance and allows investment when a need has been demonstrated.

C.text: Produce forecasts using both the current method and AI every week, then average them. Do not measure the value of the additional work.
C.explanation: The benefit of the added burden of operating two processes remains unknown.

D.text: Stop producing forecasts and base ingredient orders each week solely on the experience of a different staff member.
D.explanation: Discarding a proven, effective baseline would reduce consistency and reproducibility.

aib-c01-d2-043@1.title: Verify that old and new results lead to the same operational decisions
aib-c01-d2-043@1.prompt: A regional care provider is replacing a system that helps plan the order of home visits. In the old version, “Top-ranked” means “reserve time first”; in the candidate new version, it means “share with another staff member before deciding the order.” The display order and integration format are the same. What should the provider do to prevent an overlooked issue during migration?

learning.reason: Map each output label to the action staff should take, decide who will interpret it and how during any parallel-running period, and test the process in practice.
learning.concept: Validate the business meaning of each output and its effect on staff decisions in addition to API compatibility.

A.text: Explain the new meaning after cutover and make individual corrections if confusion among staff increases.
A.explanation: This fails to manage a known difference in meaning at the time of release.

B.text: Switch to the new version without changing staff decision procedures because the integration format is unchanged.
B.explanation: The same display can have a different meaning, so the old procedure could lead to incorrect handling.

C.text: Consider the migration complete if the old and new versions produce the same number of top-ranked results, even if individual staff members make different decisions.
C.explanation: Matching counts do not show that the results are being handled correctly in the workflow.

D.text: Document the mapping between meanings and actions for each version, update the display and procedures, and test representative cases to confirm that staff make the right decisions after sharing.
D.explanation: This verifies compatibility through the resulting business workflow.

aib-c01-d2-044@1.title: Distinguish an apparent increase in sign-ups from actual sales
aib-c01-d2-044@1.prompt: A trial of AI-generated product descriptions increased the number of people who started checkout after viewing an offer. However, some customers later cancel because they misunderstood the terms of use. Which two metrics should be used as the primary financial KPI and the customer-focused measure?

learning.reason: Evaluate realized revenue, net of cancellations and discounts, over the same period and under comparable conditions—not just checkout starts. Separately track cancellations and complaints attributable to the descriptions.
learning.concept: When cancellations or discounts occur after sign-up, measure realized outcomes and complaints.

A.text: The cancellation rate for misunderstandings about product terms and confirmed complaints related to the descriptions.
A.explanation: These measures help show whether customers understand the offer less well despite the increase in sign-ups.

B.text: For comparable audiences, realized revenue per person reached, net of cancellations, returns, and discounts.
B.explanation: This measures the financial result achieved, rather than checkout starts alone.

C.text: The average character count of product descriptions, to make their information volume consistent.
C.explanation: Length does not show that product terms were communicated accurately.

D.text: The number of seconds from starting checkout to reaching the first input field.
D.explanation: This does not capture completed purchases or misunderstandings about the offer.

E.text: The number of product-description candidates generated.
E.explanation: This measures activity, not sales or customer understanding.

aib-c01-d2-045@1.title: Include drop-offs in the baseline for measuring outcomes
aib-c01-d2-045@1.prompt: A lender is considering AI to support online loan consultations. The lender currently records the average handling time for completed consultations but does not count consultations that users leave before completion. It wants to evaluate both time savings and consultation completion after deployment. What should it do before deployment?

learning.reason: Define the population using conditions at the start of a consultation, then record the status of every case, including incomplete ones, along with start and end times and the observation deadline. Do not infer improvement from average handling time alone.
learning.concept: Because measuring completed cases only can change the denominator after deployment, define the population at intake and track all cases.

A.text: Continue storing only completed consultations and count every reduction in long cases as a time saving attributable to AI.
A.explanation: The average will improve simply because long cases that ended early are missing from the denominator.

B.text: Record how often only people expected to use AI open the page, without comparing them with consultations handled through the existing process.
B.explanation: This does not align the pre-deployment completion criteria and population being observed.

C.text: Set targets for the new baseline first and begin measuring actual results only after deployment.
C.explanation: There would be no pre-deployment values to serve as a baseline.

D.text: Define the population at intake, track every case—including incomplete ones—for a fixed period, and use consistent definitions for completion rate and time.
D.explanation: This makes it possible to compare the effects on time and completion using the same denominator.

aib-c01-d2-046@1.title: Evaluate an investment based on when its benefits arrive
aib-c01-d2-046@1.prompt: The initial cost of an AI-enabled administrative efficiency initiative is ¥2 million. Its cash benefits, net of additional operating costs, are ¥1.21 million at the end of year 1 and ¥1.21 million at the end of year 2.
