The annual discount rate is 10%, and there are no other cash flows. What is the net benefit in present-value terms?

learning.reason: ¥1.21 million ÷ 1.1 = ¥1.1 million, and ¥1.21 million ÷ 1.1² = ¥1 million. Subtracting the current cost of ¥2 million from the ¥2.1 million total gives a net benefit of ¥100,000.
learning.concept: Discount benefits to the end of each period and subtract the initial cost to account for when the cash flows occur.

A.text: ¥2.1 million. Add the benefits for both years after discounting them.
A.explanation: Because this is a net benefit, the initial cost of ¥2 million must be subtracted.

B.text: ¥420,000. Add the two ¥1.21 million benefits and subtract ¥2 million.
B.explanation: This does not discount benefits that occur at different times.

C.text: ¥100,000. Discount each year-end benefit for the applicable number of years, then subtract the initial cost.
C.explanation: This brings cash flows from different points in time to a common present-value basis.

D.text: ¥200,000. Discount both benefits by only one year, making each worth ¥1.1 million.
D.explanation: The benefit received at the end of year 2 must be discounted for two years.

aib-c01-d2-047@1.title: Assess eligible use cases before outcome metrics become available
aib-c01-d2-047@1.prompt: AI assistance for inbound receiving can be used only when the required shipment packaging information arrives from the shipping location. Confirming cost savings takes a quarter, but the decision about expanding to the next site is due in one month. In an existing pilot, the quality of eligible cases met the required standard. Which leading indicator should be prioritized next?

learning.reason: Measure, for each site, the share of cases where the required information is available by the deadline and the case is eligible for assistance. This provides an early view of how many opportunities there are to achieve the intended outcomes.
learning.concept: Use the share of eligible cases as a leading indicator to determine whether a large number of ineligible cases could limit long-term benefits.

A.text: Count how many AI screens were prepared during site training.
A.explanation: This does not show which receiving cases meet the conditions for use in operations.

B.text: Measure, by site, the percentage of all inbound cases for which the required packaging information arrives by the specified time.
B.explanation: This gives an early measure of how many cases can benefit from the quality already established.

C.text: Measure only the site-level cost reduction confirmed at the end of the quarter.
C.explanation: This is an important outcome, but it will not be available in time for the expansion decision.

D.text: Compare the total number of cases processed by AI without accounting for total inbound volume or the conditions for assistance.
D.explanation: This does not distinguish differences in workload from differences in the share of cases eligible for use.

aib-c01-d2-048@1.title: Identify where costs are increasing on a shared platform
aib-c01-d2-048@1.prompt: Spending on a shared AI service for text analysis is increasing month over month. Calls can be identified by department, but costs are not aggregated separately by department. High-value review work and experiments whose results are rarely used run on the same platform. Choose TWO measures to control the budget while maintaining quality.

learning.reason: Tie usage and costs to the department and purpose to identify changes. Track the cost per outcome that is actually used, and set limits and accountability for low-value experiments.
learning.concept: Connect departmental usage to costs, then address low-value consumption first to avoid across-the-board cuts.

A.text: Keep the unused experiments unchanged and lower the quality evaluation standard only for high-value use cases.
A.explanation: This shifts the disadvantage to the use cases that matter most.

B.text: Reduce every use case’s budget by the same percentage without investigating departmental usage or impact.
B.explanation: This could impair important review work while leaving the causes of low-value usage unaddressed.

C.text: Attribute calls to departments and use cases, and show the responsible departments the cost per outcome and the difference from monthly targets.
C.explanation: This makes it possible to see who is using the platform, for what purpose, and where costs are increasing.

D.text: Set time limits and usage quotas for experiments with little demonstrated value, and require the responsible department to review whether to continue them.
D.explanation: This targets low-value consumption while limiting the impact on important use cases.

E.text: Calculate budget limits using only the shared service’s consolidated bill, and delete usage records by use case.
E.explanation: This prevents costs from being tied to the purpose of each use case.

aib-c01-d3-021@1.title: Provide the same service to people who cannot use the voice channel
aib-c01-d3-021@1.prompt: A municipal service center is launching an AI voice service for booking appointments. Completion rates for voice users are good, but the text channel for people who have difficulty speaking cannot confirm an appointment. Users must wait until the next day to book by phone. What should be done first?

learning.reason: Make equivalent appointment outcomes available through channels users can access, then evaluate completion rates and wait times for each channel.
learning.concept: Assess fairness through both access to a channel and the final outcome, rather than through average performance alone.

A.text: Improve the voice AI’s recognition accuracy and leave the text channel as a phone booking for a later date.
A.explanation: This leaves people who need a non-voice channel at a disadvantage.

B.text: Allow users to confirm the same appointment slots through the text channel, and track completion rates and wait times by channel.
B.explanation: This makes it possible to assess both access to the service and the outcomes it provides.

C.text: Combine completion rates for all users and skip evaluating appointment functionality in the text channel if the overall rate is high.
C.explanation: Difficulty using a less common channel could be obscured by the average.

D.text: Improve only the text channel’s instructions and do not record whether or when an appointment is confirmed.
D.explanation: Improving instructions alone does not provide equivalent booking availability or wait times.

aib-c01-d3-022@1.title: Weighing a small performance gain against confidence in the reasons for decisions
aib-c01-d3-022@1.prompt: Two approaches are being considered to screen applicants for fee waivers at a facility. Approach A detects 93% of eligible applicants, but technical validation frequently found that its individual decision explanations did not correspond to the decisions actually made. Approach B detects 91% and can record the policy criteria used for each decision. The minimum detection rate is 90%, and recording the reasons is also mandatory. Which approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Adopt an approach that meets both the minimum quality threshold and the explainability requirement. Compare it with higher-performing approaches only when their explanations can be validated.
learning.concept: Choose an approach that meets both the required explanation standard and the minimum performance threshold when explanations are mandatory for the business process.

A.text: Adopt A and have staff select policy text afterward to fill in any reasons that could not be recorded.
A.explanation: This does not resolve the problem that the explanations fail to correspond to the actual decision process.

B.text: Operate B while checking eligibility decisions and their reasons. Reassess A once its reasons can be validated.
B.explanation: This lets you start with an approach that meets both mandatory requirements.

C.text: Average the scores from A and B, then use B's recorded reasons as-is for the final decisions.
C.explanation: B's reasons do not necessarily explain decisions based on the averaged scores.

D.text: Prioritize the detection rate, relax the explanation requirement, and handle each case only if an appeal is filed afterward.
D.explanation: This fails to meet the mandatory requirement to record reasons.

aib-c01-d3-023@1.title: Designing data handling and customer support before an experiment
aib-c01-d3-023@1.prompt: A customer support AI pilot may end. After the trial, users' unresolved cases still need to be handled, and personal data collected solely for the experiment must be disposed of in accordance with the contract. When should the organization establish which policies?

learning.reason: Before the experiment, define stop conditions, customer communications, transfer of unresolved cases, data retention and deletion, and evidence that these steps were completed.
learning.concept: Set requirements for shutdown, alternative processing, and history handling before the pilot begins, then reflect them in vendor contracts and operations.

A.text: When stopping the pilot, close the related screens because customers can check their status there; do not define individual notices or case transfers.
A.explanation: Support for unresolved cases would be interrupted.

B.text: Before the experiment starts, define how cases will be transferred and users notified, as well as how returns and deletions will be verified; reflect these steps in vendor terms and intake procedures.
B.explanation: This allows case handling and data management to continue after the experiment ends.

C.text: Wait until a decision to end the pilot has been made before asking the vendor how the data will be handled.
C.explanation: There is no advance assurance that data can be retrieved or deleted within the required period.

D.text: Keep data collected solely for the experiment indefinitely so the pilot can be restarted in an emergency.
D.explanation: This prevents disposal in accordance with the contract.

aib-c01-d3-024@1.title: Separating AI recommendations from approval authority for consequential actions
aib-c01-d3-024@1.prompt: An AI system drafts a notice terminating a contract for an external recipient. This is a difficult-to-reverse action, and policy requires an approver other than the front-line manager to review the contract and facts. Choose two appropriate controls.

learning.reason: The AI may help prepare a notice, but it should not have sending authority. A separate approver should check the subject and conditions, and the organization should record who approved it and when.
learning.concept: Carry out irreversible external actions only after independent verification of the recommendation and approval by an authorized person.

A.text: If the AI's internal confidence is high, have the separate approver review the notice the day after it is sent.
A.explanation: This does not provide the required independent review before sending.

B.text: Send only cases for which an independent approver has checked the contract and current facts and recorded the basis for approval.
B.explanation: This verifies the validity of the conditions and the responsible person's accountability.

C.text: Use the front-line manager's ID so the AI and independent approver can review the case with the same credentials.
C.explanation: This does not keep the approver separate or establish accountability.

D.text: Do not grant the drafting AI permission to send externally; allow a separate workflow to send the notice only after approval.
D.explanation: An unapproved recommendation cannot become an external action.

E.text: Audit all notices in a sample at the end of each month and do not require assigned individual approvals.
E.explanation: An audit after release cannot prevent an irreversible action.

aib-c01-d3-025@1.title: Separating the department seeking an exception from the person authorizing it
aib-c01-d3-025@1.prompt: A sales director is accountable for the performance of an AI initiative and wants to make it available to some customers even while it has not met the required threshold. One proposal would let each department head approve exceptions to the standards for their own initiatives. Which accountability design provides appropriate governance?

learning.reason: The business team requests the exception, while a separate approver reviews its rationale, impact, deadline, and alternatives. Record who is responsible for approval and reassessment.
learning.concept: For exception requests with a conflict of interest, establish independent review, a time limit, reassessment, and a channel for handling objections.

A.text: The department submits its rationale and alternatives; an independent reviewer assesses the impact and duration, then assigns a date for reassessment.
A.explanation: This separates the business objective from the assessment of whether the exception is justified.

B.text: Move all requests and approvals to the vendor, leaving the organization responsible only for the model contract.
B.explanation: The organization would be unable to govern operational exceptions for its own service.

C.text: Grant exceptions without an end date, and review them only if the review committee raises an objection.
C.explanation: This omits a deadline, reassessment, and documentation of the rationale.

D.text: Let the department head approve an exception whenever they consider it important to meeting their own targets, and record the rationale only after release.
D.explanation: This does not separate the conflict of interest or create a record before release.

aib-c01-d3-026@1.title: Preserving an audit trail of past decisions after model updates
aib-c01-d3-026@1.prompt: An AI system assists with approving items, and records must make it possible to reproduce the model version and approval materials used at a later date. The provider periodically updates the model behind an API whose name does not change. What should be verified in the procedures and contract?

learning.reason: Retrieve and record the version used for each response, and link it to the versions of the configuration and approval materials. Check whether updates without notification and verification meet the requirements.
learning.concept: When recordkeeping is required at the version level, require contract terms and configuration that allow the version that actually responded to be retrieved and retained.

A.text: If users have saved the outputs, there is no need to retain the old model version or approval materials.
A.explanation: The output alone does not show which version and supporting evidence were used for the decision at the time.

B.text: Record only the date of each inquiry, then infer the model version from the provider’s published page after an audit begins.
B.explanation: This cannot establish which version actually generated the response at that time.

C.text: Record the API name each time and assume responses before and after an update came from the same version if the name is unchanged.
C.explanation: The API name does not identify the version that was actually running.

D.text: Verify that the version associated with each response can be retrieved and recorded, link it to the versions of the configuration and approval materials, and confirm the terms for update notifications.
D.explanation: This makes the evidence needed for an audit traceable even when the version changes.

aib-c01-d3-027@1.title: Revoking access to generated materials when an employee changes roles
aib-c01-d3-027@1.prompt: An internal AI system summarizes HR materials with restricted access and creates links for sharing within a team. A case has come to light in which an employee who was removed from the assignment could no longer open the source material but could still view the summary through an earlier link. What should be fixed first?

learning.reason: Apply the source material’s classification to generated outputs and check current access when they are retrieved. Include invalidation of old links and cached copies in the process for role changes.
learning.concept: Even when the source material is protected, apply the same permission changes to generated shared content and cached copies.

A.text: Apply the source material’s restrictions to generated outputs as well, check current permissions when they are retrieved, and revoke existing sharing permissions when an employee changes roles.
A.explanation: Access to information derived from the source can then reflect the employee’s current role.

B.text: Make sharing links longer and harder to guess, while continuing to let anyone who already has a link retrieve the material.
B.explanation: A link held by someone whose permissions have been revoked remains valid.

C.text: Continue protecting only the source material and treat summaries as generally shareable because they were created by a model.
C.explanation: The summaries may still contain restricted information.

D.text: Remove the sharing-link display from generated answer pages, but do not check permissions when someone accesses a URL directly.
D.explanation: People who still have an old link can continue to access the material.

aib-c01-d3-028@1.title: Keeping infrequent, high-impact risks in the review process
aib-c01-d3-028@1.prompt: The organization’s classification table requires additional review, regardless of likelihood, for hazards that could have a severe impact on an individual. A frequently disrupts display formatting but does not lose content. B rarely gives a person the wrong reason for an individual account suspension. Which prioritization is appropriate for early action?

learning.reason: Do not compare frequency alone; send B for additional review under the severity rule. Manage A separately for its impact on usability.
learning.concept: Distinguish likelihood from impact in the evaluation framework and apply mandatory review criteria for severe risks.

A.text: Exclude B from the risk register and treat it as a communications issue because addressing it involves notifying users.
A.explanation: Notification does not remove the impact of giving someone the wrong reason for an account suspension.

B.text: Review A first because it happens frequently, and merely record B until its occurrence rate is the same.
B.explanation: This conflicts with the rule requiring review of severe incidents regardless of likelihood.

C.text: Conduct an additional review of B and verify mitigations, while addressing A’s frequency and impact through routine quality management.
C.explanation: This applies the organization’s severity criteria and allows both issues to be managed.

D.text: Do not assess operational impact for either incident until complaints about each reach one per week.
D.explanation: This substitutes a complaint-count threshold for a risk review.

aib-c01-d3-029@1.title: Responding when the human review queue starts to back up
aib-c01-d3-029@1.prompt: Cases that the AI system defers must be reviewed by an operations employee on the same day. During busy periods, the AI system itself has high availability, but handoffs are carried over to the next day and users miss their deadlines. What measure should be added to monitoring?

learning.reason: Monitor the waiting time for handoffs, the number of cases nearing their deadlines, and available capacity. Prioritize urgent cases or bring in additional help before deadlines pass.
learning.concept: In addition to model-quality monitoring, observe whether handoffs to people are completed within the required time.

A.text: Record AI uptime in detail and consider handoffs successful whenever the system remains available.
A.explanation: This does not measure the step that is backing up on the human side.

B.text: Count total handoffs at the end of each month and leave same-day processing to individual discretion.
B.explanation: This cannot prompt action before a deadline is missed.

C.text: Set alerts for time remaining and the number of unprocessed cases, and prepare procedures for prioritizing near-deadline cases and getting additional help.
C.explanation: This makes it possible to monitor whether the human measures are working within the deadline.

D.text: Clear all deferred cases to reduce the number of handoffs, without checking for incorrect decisions as a result.
D.explanation: This exposes users again to the problems that human review was intended to prevent.

aib-c01-d3-030@1.title: Investigating Bias That Individual Attributes Can Hide
aib-c01-d3-030@1.prompt: An AI assistant for employment services had adequate completion rates when results were grouped by preferred language or device type separately. After launch, a concern was raised that guidance might be interrupted only for users who speak a less common language and use an older device. What is the most appropriate investigation?

learning.reason: Review the combination of the two attributes using only permitted aggregates, and assess estimates for small groups alongside additional observations rather than treating them as conclusive.
learning.concept: Evaluate reasonable combinations of groups in advance, while accounting for uncertainty in sparse data and protecting privacy.

A.text: Disclose the identities of the small number of affected users so all employees can review each case.
A.explanation: This expands access to the records and exposes identifying information beyond what the investigation requires.

B.text: Stop displaying language, group results only by device, and track whether complaints decrease.
B.explanation: This cannot test the suspected combination of attributes.

C.text: Aggregate operational outcomes by language and device together within the permitted scope, and validate further where a segment has substantial uncertainty.
C.explanation: This identifies the conditions associated with the impact while avoiding firm conclusions from sparse data.

D.text: Compare each attribute separately and continue operating without investigating combinations if there are no differences.
D.explanation: Aggregating one attribute at a time can hide an issue affecting a particular combination.

aib-c01-d3-031@1.title: Honor Attribution Requirements Even for Licensed Material
aib-c01-d3-031@1.prompt: A publisher uses generative AI to create descriptions for an exhibition. Some reference materials may be reused in public-facing content, but the agreement requires attribution of the original author and disclosure of modifications when they are quoted. What should be done before publishing AI output?

learning.reason: Map the materials used to their contractual attribution requirements and review quotations and modifications in the output. Exclude from publication any material whose attribution basis cannot be verified.
learning.concept: In addition to permission to use input materials, carry any required credit and modification terms into the published work.

A.text: Calculate the proportion reproduced across the work, and waive individual attribution requirements if it is small.
A.explanation: The amount reproduced does not remove conditions required by the original agreement.

B.text: Remove attribution to the original authors because reuse in public content is permitted.
B.explanation: Contractual attribution requirements still apply when publication is allowed.

C.text: Use the AI provider's company name as the source for everything, without retaining links to the original materials.
C.explanation: This prevents tracking the required original authors and modifications.

D.text: Record the original materials and agreement terms, review what was actually quoted or modified, and add the required attribution.
D.explanation: This carries accurate source and modification information into the published content.

aib-c01-d3-032@1.title: Validate Numeric Results Even When the Structure Looks Right
aib-c01-d3-032@1.prompt: A procurement AI extracts unit prices and quantities from purchase orders into structured fields. All output fields are present, but some examples treat the price per box as the price per item, producing totals that differ substantially from the originals. What is the most direct safeguard before automatic entry?

learning.reason: Check how units correspond to quantities, then apply approved conversions and compare totals. Isolate purchase orders whose basis is unclear or whose totals do not match.
learning.concept: Use external validation of unit, magnitude, and arithmetic invariants for results that appear structurally correct.

A.text: Recalculate using approved conversion rules that include units, and route cases outside the permitted tolerance for human review.
A.explanation: This can detect numeric inconsistencies that a schema check cannot find.

B.text: Check whether every field name is present, and do not evaluate units or values if they match.
B.explanation: This cannot detect the unit error or amount discrepancy at issue.

C.text: Adjust only the final quantity until the total matches, and do not retain the original unit.
C.explanation: This changes the quantity and its supporting evidence, losing facts that should be preserved.

D.text: If two totals generated by the model match, do not compare them with the original total.
D.explanation: The model may repeat the same incorrect conversion.

aib-c01-d3-033@1.title: Protect Individual Records While Preserving Analytical Value
aib-c01-d3-033@1.prompt: An employee counseling service uses AI to produce monthly summaries that help managers understand consultation trends. The source records contain health symptoms and family information, and even summaries for small departments could reveal individuals. Managers need only organization-wide trends by broad category. What is the appropriate disclosure policy?

learning.reason: Limit reporting to the aggregation level required, combine small groups to reduce inference risks, and exclude source records or excerpts that could identify people.
learning.concept: Separate information needed for departmental improvement from personally identifiable content, and share only at the necessary level of detail.

A.text: Aggregate by the broad categories needed and combine small groups. Do not draw examples from source records that are linked to individuals.
A.explanation: This shares trends that meet the purpose while reducing the risk of identifying individuals.

B.text: Give managers access to all source records and leave the handling of personal information to their discretion.
B.explanation: This widely shares sensitive information that is not needed for the work.

C.text: Share detailed breakdowns by department and age group regardless of the level of detail managers need.
C.explanation: Fine-grained information beyond the purpose can create a re-identification risk.

D.text: Summarize every consultation in chronological order, remove only names, and distribute the summaries by department.
D.explanation: A combination of dates, content, and small groups can still reveal individuals.

aib-c01-d3-034@1.title: Avoid forcing uncertain classifications to meet throughput targets
aib-c01-d3-034@1.prompt: An AI system classifies corporate complaints as serious or routine. Cases that teams can assess consistently are classified reliably, but reviewers disagree on borderline cases. Missing a serious complaint delays the organization’s external response, while treating every complaint as serious would overwhelm the staff handling them. Which operating approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Automate only the range shown to be reliable in advance, and route borderline cases for prioritized review. Adjust the boundary by monitoring missed cases, false alarms, and review volume.
learning.concept: Define a holdout range and a safe response rather than forcing low-confidence cases into a strict binary classification.

A.text: Use the threshold that maximizes throughput and exclude classification errors from evaluation.
A.explanation: This prevents the organization from evaluating material operational harm.

B.text: To eliminate unreviewed cases, always treat borderline cases as routine and track complaint counts afterward.
B.explanation: Review of important borderline cases could be delayed.

C.text: Treat every case, not just borderline cases, as serious and defer anything staff cannot handle until the next period.
C.explanation: This can exceed staff capacity and delay responses that are actually needed.

D.text: Automatically classify cases within the reliable range and send borderline cases to a time-limited review queue. Measure both missed cases and review volume.
D.explanation: This addresses automation, staff capacity, and safety requirements together.

aib-c01-d3-035@1.title: Help users understand AI use before they choose
aib-c01-d3-035@1.prompt: A recruiting service is considering a system in which AI summarizes interview recordings for staff to review. Users must know the purpose before recording and be able to choose not to be recorded. The screen and notice specifications have not yet been decided. What should be done first?

learning.reason: Make pre-recording notice and an alternative path explicit requirements, then test whether users understand the purpose and their options during design.
learning.concept: Treat the timing of the notice and user understanding as pilot criteria, rather than relying on wording added after the fact.

A.text: Explain the use of AI only in an email sent after recording, and use the email read rate to confirm consent.
A.explanation: Users cannot make a choice before recording.

B.text: Do not design a choice in advance, because users who want to decline recording can revoke it through the complaint channel after launch.
B.explanation: A post-event process cannot replace the user's decision before recording.

C.text: Present the purpose and options briefly before recording, then use a pilot to verify that an unrecorded interview can be conducted and that users understand the notice.
C.explanation: The information and the practical choice can be validated while requirements are being designed.

D.text: Add explanations of technical terms at the end of the terms of service, and omit any notice about recording when the interview begins.
D.explanation: This does not verify that the purpose and alternative are communicated at the point of use.

aib-c01-d3-036@1.title: Include human spot checks of automated decisions
aib-c01-d3-036@1.prompt: For approved, minor delivery-condition issues, the AI responds automatically when its decision confidence is above a set level. Staff review only cases placed on hold. The organization also wants to detect a gradual increase in errors in automated responses. What human oversight is appropriate?

learning.reason: Sample high-confidence automated responses too, considering timing and case type, and have staff independently verify their correctness using the evidence.
learning.concept: Review completed cases independently, because human review limited to held cases cannot reveal errors in automated processing.

A.text: Recheck automated responses using only the model's self-assessment, and request human judgments only after an incident occurs.
A.explanation: The same error patterns may be missed, and this provides no early oversight.

B.text: If the number of automated responses is the same every day, conclude that quality is unchanged without collecting audit results.
B.explanation: Stable volume does not mean stable accuracy.

C.text: Review held cases in detail and exclude automated responses from investigation because the model has high confidence.
C.explanation: This leaves the accuracy of the automated decisions—the part the organization most needs to understand—unobserved.

D.text: Sample automated responses as well, accounting for case type and timing, and have staff review the evidence and outcome.
D.explanation: This can detect errors in automated decisions that held cases alone would not reveal.

aib-c01-d3-037@1.title: Enable recovery while protecting backups
aib-c01-d3-037@1.prompt: Approved customer documents used by an internal AI system are encrypted. Operations staff store backups monthly, and employees outside the responsible team must not be able to read restored documents either. The documents must remain recoverable during the defined retention period, even after encryption keys are rotated. Choose two appropriate designs.

learning.reason: Encrypt copies, require separate authorization for restoration and content access, and align key handling with the retention period so required data can still be decrypted. Test restoration after rotation.
learning.concept: Include backups and older versions in encryption management, balancing confidentiality with decryption access during recovery.

A.text: Make all previous encryption unusable as soon as keys are rotated, and test restoration of old backups only when an incident occurs.
A.explanation: A required older backup could become impossible to decrypt during its retention period.

B.text: Leave backups unencrypted because they are not accessed as primary data, and check access only if the business is interrupted.
B.explanation: Copies contain the same customer information and must remain protected outside restoration as well.

C.text: Maintain the means to decrypt data for as long as it must be retained, and test whether older documents can be restored after key rotation in a restricted environment.
C.explanation: This verifies that both protection and recovery work after key rotation.

D.text: Encrypt backups too, and separately restrict permissions for approved restoration operators and for employees who can read restored documents.
D.explanation: Permission to perform a restoration should not grant unrestricted access to document contents.

E.text: To speed recovery, also grant every writer permission to read documents and manage keys.
E.explanation: This expands sensitive permissions beyond what routine operations require.

aib-c01-d3-038@1.title: Assessing business risk after combining components
aib-c01-d3-038@1.prompt: An AI that summarizes internal shipping notes and an AI that creates delivery guidance from approved conditions were each assessed as low risk for their individual use cases. A new proposal automatically passes the first AI's summary to the second AI, which then sends guidance directly to users. How should approval of the different components be handled?

learning.reason: Distinguish the approved use case for each component from the customer-facing use case after they are combined. Reassess the flow, including how missing or inconsistent information could affect notifications.
learning.concept: Do not infer the risk of a combined workflow from low-risk approvals of its individual components; assess whether errors can propagate and amplify across outputs.

A.text: Validate the combined notification end to end, assess how omissions may propagate and affect external users, and select controls again.
A.explanation: Consider both the characteristics of the components and how they are used in the actual workflow.

B.text: Apply the same conclusions to the combined process because the individual components were assessed as low risk.
B.explanation: Conditions under which errors propagate between components were not part of the individual reviews.

C.text: Use the average of the two assessment scores as the risk classification, excluding external notifications from the score.
C.explanation: This does not assess the impact of the workflow as a whole.

D.text: Because it is difficult to tell which component caused an error, revert to the assessments made before integration and investigate only after deployment.
D.explanation: This does not validate integration issues before users receive notifications.

aib-c01-d3-039@1.title: Verifying that safeguards reach the people responsible for responding
aib-c01-d3-039@1.prompt: An AI system responsible for publishing documents is configured to hold publication and notify a staff member when it finds an unapproved version. An audit finds that the notification recipient has been retired, even though the settings page appears normal. What is the appropriate ongoing control?

learning.reason: Use dedicated test documents to verify periodically that publication is held, notifications are delivered, and staff receive them. Keep the test results as evidence instead of relying only on the presence of a setting.
learning.concept: Periodically verify isolation, notification, and delivery to the responsible staff member using authorized tests, rather than relying on configuration alone.

A.text: Record when the setting was enabled and do not check it regularly as long as the configuration file exists.
A.explanation: This does not show whether notifications reach their recipient.

B.text: Periodically test with test documents to confirm that publication is held as intended, notifications reach staff, and the notifications are handled.
B.explanation: This verifies that the control and its communication path work in practice.

C.text: Monitor only complaints received after publication and use the number of emails as a substitute for notification checks.
C.explanation: This does not test the full hold, notification, and receipt workflow.

D.text: Remove the hold setting and send every document to staff's regular queue, leaving viewers to decide whether each version is approved.
D.explanation: This does not prevent unverified versions from being published.

aib-c01-d3-040@1.title: Isolating the change that reduced reliability
aib-c01-d3-040@1.prompt: Answer quality from a business support AI has suddenly declined. The document index and model version were both updated on the same day, and the cause is unknown. Evaluation data for the old configuration and the old documents are available. Which investigation method would best isolate the impact and support recovery?

learning.reason: With the same representative questions, compare combinations of old and new models and document indexes, then assess retrieved evidence and answer quality. Once the cause is identified, roll back the relevant change.
learning.concept: Compare configurations using known inputs to separate the effects of upstream data updates from model changes.

A.text: Guess which model version to roll back to, and stop evaluating if the behavior is not consistent.
A.explanation: This does not evaluate the effects of the two updates separately.

B.text: Using the same representative questions, switch one configuration element at a time and compare the retrieved evidence and answer accuracy to identify the change that caused the degradation.
B.explanation: A controlled comparison with the same inputs can isolate the cause.

C.text: Delete the old configuration and judge quality by whether the new configuration's overall response time matches the previous response time.
C.explanation: This cannot determine answer accuracy or identify the cause.

D.text: Change both elements at once to other new versions, then decide which of the two caused the problem if it goes away.
D.explanation: Adding changes prevents the effects from being isolated.

aib-c01-d4-021@1.title: Assessing readiness for each intended deployment scope
aib-c01-d4-021@1.prompt: A university's document-writing AI has usage procedures and a support contact for internal drafts reviewed by staff. For automated responses to students, there is no overnight human fallback, and no method has been defined to identify urgent requests. A meeting requests a single readiness assessment for the entire university. Which assessment is appropriate?

learning.reason: Define the requirements for each scope and impact. Assess use that meets its conditions separately from the measures needed before external-facing use is ready.
learning.concept: The operational readiness required for internal drafts differs from that required for customer-facing work, even when the technology is the same.

A.text: Because the student-facing use case is not ready, exclude the internal drafting use case that meets its conditions from assessment on the same basis.
A.explanation: This fails to use readiness evidence specific to each use case.

B.text: Assign both use cases the same readiness level and let a simple average of technical and operational scores offset unmet requirements.
B.explanation: This can hide conditions that must be met before deployment.

C.text: Assess internal drafting and automated student responses separately, and decide whether to deploy the latter only after urgent requests can be identified and a fallback response is verified.
C.explanation: This addresses readiness requirements that vary with the actual scope of use.

D.text: Because internal use has a support contact, treat overnight support for students as ready and deploy both use cases on the same day.
D.explanation: Internal operational capability does not demonstrate overnight support for students.

aib-c01-d4-022@1.title: Assessing different maturity levels across an organization
aib-c01-d4-022@1.prompt: At a financial services operations company, a shared platform allows a new team’s environment to be ready the same day. However, teams are trying out policy reviews and production staffing for the first time, and most initiatives have no accountable owner for release. What is the most appropriate way to report maturity?

learning.reason: Describe the platform’s repeatability separately from operational and governance capabilities, and establish the minimum conditions needed before scaling across the organization.
learning.concept: Assess each capability required at a maturity stage without extrapolating technical-platform maturity to frontline operations or governance.

A.text: Because each team reviews policies, rate technical maturity as conceptual, even with the shared platform.
A.explanation: This does not reflect the capabilities that actually exist in each area.

B.text: Average all areas and classify the whole organization by the highest level reached by any team.
B.explanation: This conceals variation across the organization and gaps in required capabilities.

C.text: Because the platform can be prepared quickly, record every other area as ready to scale across the organization.
C.explanation: Fast environment setup says nothing about production decisions or accountability.

D.text: Rate the platform as reusable, and record operations and governance as being in the pilot stage. Make accountable release ownership and consistent reviews prerequisites for scaling.
D.explanation: This makes differences in maturity and the next required conditions clear.

aib-c01-d4-023@1.title: Diagnosing why user provisioning is not progressing across environments
aib-c01-d4-023@1.prompt: Staff can use the AI tool for training, but access needed for operational pilots must be provisioned manually in two systems each time. Both business and security staff understand the procedure, and approvals are completed the same day. What capability should be addressed first so that approved users do not have to wait when the tool is rolled out to 10 departments?

learning.reason: The clear bottleneck is provisioning integration, not approval decisions or training. Implement identity and permission provisioning and revocation linked to approval outcomes.
learning.concept: Distinguish a skills gap from a platform-integration gap, and address the capability that is actually impeding the process.

A.text: Integrate the two environments so that permissions are provisioned and revoked based on approval outcomes, and measure how long the changes take to take effect.
A.explanation: This improves the part that is actually delayed while preserving the required approvals.

B.text: Give all employees shared permissions in both environments before approval to speed up provisioning.
B.explanation: This bypasses the valid approval process and broadens access.

C.text: Have users take basic training again and continue setting up access manually as before.
C.explanation: Retraining staff who already understand the procedure does not remove the cause of the wait.

D.text: Limit the number of approval requests to reduce wait times and continue provisioning separately in both environments as before.
D.explanation: This does not meet the goal of scaling or improve the process.

aib-c01-d4-024@1.title: Planning a development path to reduce reliance on external support
aib-c01-d4-024@1.prompt: An external specialist is needed for the initial deployment of an internal AI system, but starting next year, the company plans to evaluate quality and recover from failures in-house. Internal engineers can currently perform only basic operations. Which investment plan goes beyond simply handing over documentation?

learning.reason: Move from initial joint work to a phase where internal staff lead and external specialists provide support, then complete the handover when internal staff can independently evaluate quality and recover from failures.
learning.concept: Sequence joint work, supported operations, and independent demonstration against outcome-based milestones to build toward the target capabilities.

A.text: Have the external specialists complete the initial deployment on their own, then switch to in-house operations after receiving documentation when the contract ends.
A.explanation: This does not verify that the company can perform the required work itself.

B.text: Reject external assistance and operate the system in production from the start, learning the necessary tasks only when failures occur.
B.explanation: This ignores current capability gaps.

C.text: Treat an introductory course for everyone as the handover, and defer evaluation and recovery exercises until next year.
C.explanation: This does not verify the practical capabilities the company needs.

D.text: Progress from joint delivery to in-house-led operations, then to independent evaluation and recovery, requiring successful exercises at each stage before moving on.
D.explanation: This reduces reliance while confirming learning through demonstrated outcomes.

aib-c01-d4-025@1.title: Mapping where evaluation data is missing across business operations
aib-c01-d4-025@1.prompt: An AI system classifies reasons for returns at a wholesaler. Company-operated warehouses have detailed classification records. Contractors have a similar number of return records, but most are labeled “Other,” so damage cannot be distinguished from incorrect quantities. Can data from across the company be used for training and evaluation?

learning.reason: Assess the coverage of valid labels for the target return reasons, not just aggregate record counts. Add contractor examples that make the required reasons verifiable.
learning.concept: Map the full candidate dataset to its labeled portion and detect whether important case types are missing.

A.text: The numbers are similar across warehouses, so differences in reasons will average out across the company.
A.explanation: “Other” does not let you compare the required categories.

B.text: Remove detail from the company-operated warehouses’ classifications until the share labeled “Other” matches the contractors’ share.
B.explanation: This would discard information about categories needed across the entire scope.

C.text: Check label detail and the number of verifiable records by warehouse operating model and return reason, then improve the contractor data that is missing categories before evaluation.
C.explanation: This verifies whether the reasons needed for actual deployment can be evaluated.

D.text: Duplicate the contractors’ records more often during training to compensate for the missing labels with volume.
D.explanation: Duplicating records does not add the missing classification information.

aib-c01-d4-026@1.title: Assigning responsibility for communicating corrections and withdrawals of shared data
aib-c01-d4-026@1.prompt: A company obtains public information about multiple facilities from external partners and uses it in a search AI system. Partners cannot tell whether withdrawn materials have been removed from every place where they are used, and corrections reach only some departments. What should be the top priority in a joint operating agreement?

learning.reason: Assign responsibilities to the information owner and users, and share versions, correction and withdrawal notices, deadlines, and confirmation that the information has been removed from search.
learning.concept: Link provider corrections and changes to usage rights to an agreed notification process and confirmation that downstream systems have applied them.

A.text: Handle corrections through individual emails between staff, and start a new record from scratch whenever a staff member changes.
A.explanation: This provides no organization-wide tracking or confirmation that corrections were applied.

B.text: Assign owners and contacts on the user side, and agree on versioning, correction and withdrawal notices, deadlines for applying them, and confirmation of the results.
B.explanation: This makes it possible to track responsibility and outcomes while keeping information sharing in place.

C.text: Copy all data once a month and let each user decide whether to keep materials that have been withdrawn.
C.explanation: This cannot ensure that explicit withdrawals are applied across all users.

D.text: Have the provider share the information once, then leave all subsequent suitability checks to the search AI's self-evaluation.
D.explanation: The model is not told that material was withdrawn or when the change must be applied.

aib-c01-d4-027@1.title: Assessing a design when some data cannot be sent outside a controlled environment
aib-c01-d4-027@1.prompt: An administrative services company cannot send customer identifiers outside its controlled environment. It wants to use an external AI service to classify only the subject of an inquiry. The company can remove identifiers within the controlled environment, but has not confirmed whether doing so would also remove information needed for classification. What should it do before selecting a platform?

learning.reason: Prepare inputs with identifiers removed inside the controlled environment, then test both whether removal works correctly and whether enough information remains for classification. If the requirements cannot be met, compare processing in another location.
learning.concept: Prepare only permitted fields before external processing and validate the results and required measures under realistic data conditions.

A.text: Delete all text and send only the inquiry timestamp to the external service, then declare the approach suitable without checking actual classification quality.
A.explanation: This does not verify that the classification task still works after the required information has been removed.

B.text: Create inputs permitted for external processing within the controlled environment, then use representative cases to verify successful removal, classification quality, and required processing time before comparing candidates.
B.explanation: This allows the company to assess data constraints and whether performance and operations are viable before making a selection.

C.text: Send the original text to the external AI service and remove the identifiers after classification, assuming this meets the restriction on transmission.
C.explanation: The restriction is already violated when the original text is sent externally.

D.text: Measure accuracy only on short practice examples without sensitive information, then test preprocessing and connectivity from the controlled environment after launch.
D.explanation: This provides no evidence about quality or processing capacity for inputs that reflect production constraints.

aib-c01-d4-028@1.title: Maintaining cross-site momentum after an organizational change
aib-c01-d4-028@1.prompt: An organizational restructuring moves the executive sponsor for a promotional support AI initiative to another role. The frontline team is in place, but no one is available to coordinate across business units or approve the next budget. What should the company do to keep implementation moving?

learning.reason: Formally appoint a new business owner and transfer success criteria, budget, unresolved cross-organizational issues, and decision deadlines. Maintain a forum where the implementation team can report progress.
learning.concept: When a sponsor changes, formally hand off decision-making authority, budget, and unresolved issues.

A.text: Continue asking the former sponsor to make decisions without formally appointing them, and leave internal authority unchanged.
A.explanation: Formal authority and accountability are not transferred to the next leadership team.

B.text: Disband the frontline team for now and defer the enterprise rollout plan until the next fiscal year.
B.explanation: This unnecessarily discards frontline work and decision-making that could continue.

C.text: Formally appoint a new sponsor and transfer the budget, decision-making authority, priorities, and reporting path for the implementation team.
C.explanation: This allows decisions about cross-site obstacles and funding to continue.

D.text: Let each site continue implementation on its own, and decide who owns the next budget after rollout.
D.explanation: Cross-site decisions and funding would be interrupted.

aib-c01-d4-029@1.title: Including affected users as well as operators in validation
aib-c01-d4-029@1.prompt: An education company plans to use AI to route learning support inquiries. Development and planning are underway, but support staff are assigned to handle exceptions, and learners could not tell what to do next when using the current prototype. What should the next team design be?

learning.reason: Include development, support staff, and user representatives in validation, with each responsible department owning deliverables related to exceptions and user outcomes.
learning.concept: Add operational and user representatives to the core development team and make responsibility for each deliverable explicit.

A.text: Include support staff and learner representatives in validation: support staff own exception procedures, planning owns user completion criteria, and engineering owns fixes and retesting.
A.explanation: This fills gaps in the design and clarifies who verifies the results.

B.text: Declare the system complete based only on engineering tests, and brief support staff and learners just before launch.
B.explanation: This does not incorporate frontline exception handling or the results of user testing into the design.

C.text: Have planning decide exceptions on behalf of support staff, and assume that the provider guarantees learners' successful completion.
C.explanation: The validation team does not include people who understand operations or users' circumstances.

D.text: Do not assign individual responsibilities; have everyone take part in final testing and leave acceptance decisions and retesting after fixes to each person.
D.explanation: This does not assign accountability or confirmation after fixes.

aib-c01-d4-030@1.title: Communicate pilot conditions as well as results across the organization
aib-c01-d4-030@1.prompt: A document AI pilot at three sites showed that routine forms could be processed faster, but staff at a site with many exceptions spent more time reviewing them. Leadership wants to inform everyone about the rollout schedule and expected benefits. Which approach would best preserve trust?

learning.reason: Share what was observed for each type of work and how staff can get support, without promising the same benefit to every department. State when measurement will happen again and whom to contact.
learning.concept: Present measured results, uncertain effects, and a contact path for workplace concerns together.

A.text: Notify only the site where review time increased, and do not publish the start dates or support information for the other sites.
A.explanation: This does not share each site's readiness or the conditions behind the comparison.

B.text: Withhold the observed results to avoid differences in outcomes, and promise staff a uniform productivity improvement across the company.
B.explanation: This guarantees an uncertain outcome and raises expectations too high.

C.text: Announce the improvement rate at the fastest site as everyone's target, without mentioning the added review burden for exceptions.
C.explanation: This overgeneralizes a favorable result and does not explain what support people who need it will receive.

D.text: Share the results for routine and exception-heavy work, the planned phased start, where to raise concerns, and when the results will next be reviewed.
D.explanation: This makes both the success and the caveats useful to people doing the work.

aib-c01-d4-031@1.title: Address why frontline staff do not trust the system
aib-c01-d4-031@1.prompt: An experienced inspector feels that earlier automation disregarded their expertise. The new AI also provides little explanation, and they believe using it will take away their decision-making authority. What should the implementation lead do first?

learning.reason: Include frontline staff in evaluation and design, and use real examples to examine when recommendations fail and how decisions should be handled. Tie adoption decisions to both staff input and observed results.
learning.concept: Listen to real concerns and verify the AI's rationale through understandable evaluation and frontline participation, rather than mandating use.

A.text: Have managers compare non-use counts every week, require use, and ask no questions about the reasons.
A.explanation: This pressures people to use the system without addressing the source of their distrust.

B.text: Remove examples of errors from the rollout materials and show only representative examples that were correct in testing.
B.explanation: This removes opportunities to examine limitations and may undermine trust in real work.

C.text: Involve trusted frontline peers, compare the AI's rationale and failure cases using real examples, and jointly decide how final decisions and corrections will work.
C.explanation: This respects staff expertise and makes the AI's output verifiable.

D.text: Have a central team explain only how the features work and direct staff to a complaints channel after launch.
D.explanation: This does not allow the causes of distrust to inform the design before launch.

aib-c01-d4-032@1.title: Practice handling difficult situations in training
aib-c01-d4-032@1.prompt: A contracts team member passed a test on basic AI terminology. However, during a workplace pilot, they could not decide when to stop using the AI or whom to notify after its output included an incorrect contract clause. What should the next training cover?

learning.reason: Use authorized training examples of exceptions to rehearse checking the evidence, stopping use, escalating the issue, and documenting it. Assess participants' decisions and actions.
learning.concept: Teach responsible use with practice that goes beyond a knowledge test to identifying risky cases and stopping and escalating appropriately.

A.text: Since errors would decrease if no one used the AI, have only managers take the test and omit training for frontline staff.
A.explanation: This does not develop the judgment frontline users need.

B.text: Use exercises with an incorrect clause or missing supporting evidence, and have participants verify the basis, stop use, notify the appropriate person, and document what happened.
B.explanation: This lets the organization assess the decisions staff need to make as part of a realistic sequence of actions.

C.text: Raise the passing score for the basic terminology test and rely only on existing onboarding material for incident response.
C.explanation: Knowing terminology is different from being able to stop use and notify someone.

D.text: Practice generating only error-free text and use the number of items created during training as the passing criterion.
D.explanation: This does not teach participants to detect or respond to problems.

aib-c01-d4-033@1.title: Use time saved on routine work to improve quality
aib-c01-d4-033@1.prompt: A maintenance team used AI to streamline transferring reports into designated fields. The quality of its response depends on whether staff can identify causes from infrequent anomalies and revise procedures. Which job design should the team adopt next?

learning.reason: Use AI to support routine organization, and assign staff to analyze anomalies, explain root causes, and improve procedures that have been reviewed.
learning.concept: Allocate time saved by automating formatting and aggregation to finding exceptions and improving staff decision criteria.

A.text: Return routine work to people and let AI determine the causes of exceptions on its own.
A.explanation: This gives up the efficiency already achieved and leaves difficult decisions unverified.

B.text: Measure only the hours saved and investigate the causes of anomalies less often than before.
B.explanation: This reduces the team's ability to investigate what determines the quality of its work.

C.text: Apply AI-proposed procedures at every site without review, while staff continue entering only counts.
C.explanation: This assigns no one to assess the rationale or impact.

D.text: Use AI to assist with routine report transfers, while staff investigate anomalies, verify the reasons, and review proposed procedure changes.
D.explanation: This draws on human expertise to keep improving the quality of the work.

aib-c01-d4-034@1.title: Form testable hypotheses before deciding on an enterprise-wide rollout
aib-c01-d4-034@1.prompt: A procurement lead believes AI can speed up requests for quotations. The two candidates are document search and automated drafting, but the main cause of delays is unknown. What is the best way to experiment while keeping the existing process in place?

learning.reason: Form a hypothesis about which tasks could take less time, test the candidates separately with a limited scope, and compare quality and rework as well. Narrow down the use cases worth adopting based on the results.
learning.concept: Turn an idea into an experiment with a defined scope, measurements, and stopping criteria, and decide in advance what you want to learn.

A.text: Measure the slow steps, form hypotheses, define the scope and duration, and test each initiative. Use time, quality, and rework to decide whether to proceed.
A.explanation: This makes it possible to compare causes and effects and apply lessons from unsuccessful trials.

B.text: Keep repeating model demos and decide what to measure only after users stop making requests.
B.explanation: This does not verify improvements in actual work or provide a basis for deciding whether to proceed.

C.text: Finalize production contracts first and use price as the basis for the deployment decision.
C.explanation: This commits to a rollout before testing the hypotheses and business impact.

D.text: Deploy both initiatives company-wide at the same time and measure their impact on quotation processing.
D.explanation: It would be difficult to tell which use case produced the benefits, and the trial would have a broad impact.

aib-c01-d4-035@1.title: Set expansion budgets incrementally based on early results
aib-c01-d4-035@1.prompt: A pilot of contract-review assistance at one site produced results. Experts provided support at no charge during the pilot, but other sites will incur costs for regular training and quality checks. How should the organization build on this small success as it expands?

learning.reason: Separate the pilot results from the cost of support, then measure repeatable benefits and paid support costs in another limited group of sites. Expand the budget only for the scope that meets the criteria.
learning.concept: Reestimate exceptional support and fixed costs from early successes at the future scale, and tie the business case to the next investment.

A.text: Allow only the successful pilot site to sign a production contract, without investigating whether support can be standardized for other sites.
A.explanation: This leaves the reusable capabilities and costs at scale unknown.

B.text: Measure results, including support costs, in the next small group of sites and expand as each group meets the criteria for benefits and ongoing operations.
B.explanation: This builds on the initial results while accounting for costs that change with scale.

C.text: Purchase all production capacity before expanding, then check whether the operating conditions can reproduce the initial results.
C.explanation: This commits costs before confirming profitability and the ability to execute.

D.text: Treat the free support as the ongoing unit cost, multiply the pilot's time savings by the number of sites, and approve a full rollout.
D.explanation: This omits costs that differ between the pilot and the scaled deployment.

aib-c01-d4-036@1.title: Share information to prevent rebuilding the same capabilities
aib-c01-d4-036@1.prompt: Companies in a group have independently built AI review and generation capabilities, and some now duplicate the same functions. A specialist team exists, but the companies do not know what evaluation methods and components are already available. What should they do next?

learning.reason: The specialist organization should consolidate information about initiatives, owners, results, evaluations, and reusable components, then consult and assess reuse early in the design process.
learning.concept: Make initiatives, evaluation assets, and owners visible through a specialist organization, and assess whether to reuse them when new proposals arise.

A.text: Move all AI implementation to the specialist team to avoid duplication, and have the central team make business evaluations and exception decisions as well.
A.explanation: This removes the people who understand operational decisions and exceptions from the process.

B.text: Maintain a shared initiative register with owners, scope, evaluation materials, and reusable capabilities, and discuss what to share or build separately early in each new proposal.
B.explanation: Organizations with aligned roles can reuse evaluations and implementations.

C.text: Standardize only on the AI provider, without sharing components or evaluation results.
C.explanation: Using the same provider does not eliminate duplicated implementation or evaluation work.

D.text: Let each company finish building everything before counting the initiatives, and exclude capabilities from reuse if they have different owners.
D.explanation: This does not prevent the initial duplication or make use of other companies' work.

aib-c01-d4-037@1.title: Track whether operational feedback leads to measurable improvements
aib-c01-d4-037@1.prompt: Requests to improve an AI system are collected every week. The operations team makes revisions in response, but does not measure which concerns improved or whether they recurred. How can the organization improve its assessment of long-term value?

learning.reason: Connect each request to the conditions in which it arose and a metric, then record the release, reassessment date, and owner. Review the results with the people who reported the issue.
learning.concept: Link requests to the resulting changes and outcomes, and use the same KPI to measure whether improvements persist.

A.text: Link each request to its context and improvement metric, owner, and release, then measure the same metric again and report the results to the people in the field.
A.explanation: This makes it possible to verify ongoing changes against actual business outcomes.

B.text: Record only the implementation date and have stakeholders infer the past situation when the next request arrives.
B.explanation: There is no criterion for verifying the result of a fix afterward.

C.text: To avoid dissatisfaction with changes, change the measurement criteria every month after launch and do not compare them with the initial data.
C.explanation: This makes it impossible to distinguish sustained results from deterioration.

D.text: Add more channels for submitting requests and treat an increase in the number collected as an improvement in quality.
D.explanation: A higher count does not show whether problems were resolved or prevented from recurring.

aib-c01-d4-038@1.title: Verify that the trial contract supports production operations
aib-c01-d4-038@1.prompt: Document processing with AI passed a weekday daytime trial. In production, processing must also run on weekends, and when an outage occurs, a dependent provider must be able to investigate the issue within 2 hours. The trial contract does not guarantee weekend support or ongoing capacity. What should be done before launch?

learning.reason: Separately from trial accuracy, confirm the production dependency service and the scope of its contractual support. Secure and test a contract or alternative path that meets the required response times and capacity.
learning.concept: Confirm the terms of production dependencies, maintenance support, and capacity changes against actual business hours.

A.text: Assume that operational terms are the same for the trial and commercial use because they come from the same provider, and do not make any further checks.
A.explanation: This ignores the possibility that the contract scope and terms differ.

B.text: Add more examples for practicing the outputs, and skip the contract review if weekend outages seem unlikely.
B.explanation: Examples of output quality cannot confirm response times for outages or guaranteed capacity.

C.text: Confirm the terms for weekend support and capacity, specify the necessary contract terms or alternatives, and test that the required coordination works before launch.
C.explanation: This verifies before production that support covers business hours and dependencies during an outage.

D.text: Keep the contract as is because the trial quality was good, and negotiate the necessary support after the first weekend outage.
D.explanation: The support and continuity terms required at launch would remain unresolved.

aib-c01-d4-039@1.title: Continue the rollout around departments’ busy periods
aib-c01-d4-039@1.prompt: The enterprise document AI system has completed operational testing. Accounting is in its quarterly close this month, while Procurement is operating normally. The rollout support team can fully onboard only one department at a time, and each department can still choose its old process. Which rollout approach preserves continuity?

learning.reason: Provide support to a prepared department operating normally, and switch the busy department during a quieter period. Confirm readiness, a fallback to the old process for issues, and metrics with each department.
learning.concept: Check support capacity and each department’s change window, then enable capabilities in stages.

A.text: Require all employees to switch to the new method on the same day, and take questions only through one shared company-wide queue.
A.explanation: This combines a change during the close with inadequate support.

B.text: Require Accounting to use the full system from day one because it is the busiest department and is expected to benefit first.
B.explanation: This concentrates the impact during a period when the department is less able to absorb change.

C.text: Split support across both departments and serve them at the same time, but exclude the close completion time from operational evaluation.
C.explanation: This exceeds the available support capacity and prevents detection of delays to critical work.

D.text: Support Procurement through its migration first, then switch Accounting after the close with support capacity in place and a plan to return to the old process if needed.
D.explanation: This accounts for departmental workload and support constraints so the rollout can continue.

aib-c01-d4-040@1.title: Expand a specialist-dependent task into a team capability
aib-c01-d4-040@1.prompt: Document analysis AI is used in each department, but only one person across the company can perform the evaluation procedure. When that person is away, revisions stop. Which training plan allows the rollout to continue while maintaining quality?

learning.reason: Create a reproducible procedure for the most important evaluation and deliberately select backups from multiple departments. Confirm that they can perform it independently using representative cases.
learning.concept: Prepare for the absence of a key person by confirming that colleagues can cover the work through practice and on-the-job performance.

A.text: Standardize the evaluation procedure, have backups from multiple departments independently assess representative cases, and compare their assessments with the specialist’s rationale.
A.explanation: This verifies backup capability while maintaining quality.

B.text: Reduce the specialist’s vacation time and leave the evaluation method exclusively with that person as before.
B.explanation: This does not change the structure in which one person’s absence stops the work.

C.text: Skip all evaluation of revisions to keep the rollout moving, and review them later based only on user reports.
C.explanation: This neither addresses the staffing gap nor protects production quality.

D.text: Publish a recording of the evaluation procedure and consider training complete without checking whether anyone else can perform it.
D.explanation: Access to a recording does not demonstrate that others can reproduce the procedure independently.

aib-c01-d1-043@1.title: Do not treat categorical identifiers as quantities
aib-c01-d1-043@1.prompt: In a delivery-delay prediction model, delivery regions are stored as numbers such as 17, 18, and 90. The numbers reflect the order in which regions were opened and have no relation to distance or road conditions. An operator proposes treating regions with nearby numbers as having similar conditions. What is the appropriate approach?

learning.reason: A region number is a categorical identifier, and differences between its values do not represent geographic or delivery differences. Treat the region as a category, and obtain actual distance separately if it is needed.
learning.concept: Even when stored as numbers, identifiers should not be treated as continuous quantities; confirm their meaning when designing inputs.

A.text: Assume that a higher region number means greater demand, and provide it to the model as a ranking.
A.explanation: Numbers assigned by opening order do not indicate a demand ranking.

B.text: Treat the region numbers as categories, and represent distance and traffic conditions using separately measured or defined fields.
B.explanation: This separates identifiers from quantities and allows each feature to reflect its actual meaning.

C.text: Use the difference between region numbers as distance, and correct the prediction afterward using address information.
C.explanation: The relative size of the numbers does not represent distance, and this is not an appropriate measurement.

D.text: Normalize the numbers to a minimum-to-maximum range, and assume that regions with closer numbers are geographically nearer.
D.explanation: Transforming the numeric range does not correct the mistaken interpretation.

aib-c01-d1-044@1.title: Do not evaluate rare events by overall accuracy alone
aib-c01-d1-044@1.prompt: One in every 100 applications is urgent. A model that treats every application as routine has 99% accuracy, but it has not improved the handling of urgent cases. There is also a limit to how many additional reviews staff can handle. How should the next trained model be evaluated?

learning.reason: Compare how many urgent cases the model catches with the share of cases flagged as urgent that actually are urgent. Choose a threshold that balances workload against missed cases.
learning.concept: Check performance on the target minority class when strong results on the majority class make a model look accurate.

A.text: Count the total errors using only the records used for training, and assume the review workload will remain manageable in production if the count is low.
A.explanation: This does not evaluate performance on unseen cases or the breakdown of urgent-case decisions.

B.text: Set aside only routine cases for evaluation and estimate missed urgent cases from complaints after release.
B.explanation: This does not assess the minority class that matters to the intervention before adoption.

C.text: Measure recall and precision for urgent cases on representative data, then choose a threshold that meets the required detection level and review-volume limit.
C.explanation: This reveals both missed rare cases and the additional reviews generated.

D.text: Adopt the model as soon as overall accuracy exceeds 99%, without checking the outcomes for actual urgent cases.
D.explanation: Correct predictions on the many routine cases can hide failures on the rare cases.

aib-c01-d1-045@1.title: Describe machine learning systems using a common framework
aib-c01-d1-045@1.prompt: Several companies are jointly building a machine learning system. Each development organization documents models, training pipelines, and inference architectures differently, making it hard to identify who owns each function during technical handoffs. They need a common framework for describing AI system architecture, rather than an organizational management certification. Which reference is most appropriate?

learning.reason: ISO/IEC 23053 provides a common framework for describing AI systems that use machine learning. Distinguish the goal of describing system architecture from requirements for an organizational management system.
learning.concept: Use the ISO/IEC 23053 framework to map ML terms and components across different teams.

A.text: Use security audit results in place of architecture diagrams and leave the ownership of inference and training undefined.
A.explanation: Audit results alone cannot describe a system’s technical architecture or areas of responsibility.

B.text: Put each company’s product manuals side by side without mapping terms, even when they use different terminology for models and training.
B.explanation: This does not provide the common description needed for joint work.

C.text: Use the machine learning system framework in ISO/IEC 23053 to map each company’s functions and show how their terms and inputs and outputs correspond.
C.explanation: This fits the goal of describing different implementations using common concepts.

D.text: Obtain ISO/IEC 42001 certification on the assumption that it will standardize each company’s architecture diagrams, and prepare no technical description for the project.
D.explanation: An organization’s management system and the architecture of an individual system require separate descriptions.

aib-c01-d1-046@1.title: Do not treat a new feature as already approved with its tool
aib-c01-d1-046@1.prompt: An AI tool used to summarize published documents has been approved internally. The provider has added a new integration feature. It ingests internally shared documents and stores a search index with the provider. The team wants to enable it under the existing approval. What is the appropriate practice for ethics and data governance?
