learning.reason: The new feature processes data differently from the use covered by the existing approval. Preserve the existing use while reviewing the new processing separately, and restrict the feature until it is approved.
learning.concept: Do not automatically extend tool-level approval to the data processing of a new feature.

A.text: Because the provider is approved, classify its index storage the same way as summarization of published documents.
A.explanation: This does not assess the new ingestion scope or how the stored index will be handled.

B.text: Keep the existing permitted use, but determine how to classify the new feature only after reviewing its data scope, index deletion, and access controls.
B.explanation: This aligns the approval scope with the additional data processing.

C.text: Permanently prohibit both the new feature and all existing approved uses, without investigating what has changed.
C.explanation: This removes even assessed uses without identifying the scope of the potential issue.

D.text: Limit the number of internal documents and let people use the feature at their discretion without a feature review.
D.explanation: Even a small number of documents may be subject to unreviewed processing and retention conditions.

aib-c01-d1-047@1.title: Use prompts to clarify the boundary between similar requests
aib-c01-d1-047@1.prompt: A generative AI system that classifies facilities-management notes confuses “reschedule a follow-up appointment” with “ask about scheduling a new visit.” The field team has examples that are similarly short, resemble both categories, and include evidence for the correct category. What prompt improvement should they try first?

learning.reason: Define both categories, explain what indicates that an appointment is already scheduled, and provide contrasting boundary examples. Specify that the model should abstain when the text does not provide enough evidence to decide.
learning.concept: Clarify label boundaries with contrasting near-examples and the features needed to make the decision.

A.text: Add more ordinary correct examples for only one category, without defining the other category.
A.explanation: This does not show the boundary in both directions and may bias the classification.

B.text: Repeat the label names more often and make the explanations of the classification reasons shorter.
B.explanation: This does not address the missing decision criteria that cause the confusion.

C.text: Define the categories based on whether an appointment already exists, provide similar-looking examples with different correct labels, and say to abstain when there is not enough evidence.
C.explanation: This makes the distinction concrete and also discourages unsupported classifications.

D.text: Since both are about appointments, instruct the model to classify a request as a new inquiry whenever its wording is polite.
D.explanation: Writing style is not evidence that an appointment has already been made.

aib-c01-d1-048@1.title: Carry confirmed details forward accurately through long conversations
aib-c01-d1-048@1.prompt: A reservation assistant uses the number of companions and meal preferences that a user confirmed at the start near the end of a long exchange. To stay within the context limit, older conversation history was trimmed, and the AI changed confirmed details based on guesses. Which method is best for retaining the details?

learning.reason: Store confirmed preferences in a structured record and require the user's confirmation to update them. Add that record to the prompt when needed, rather than relying on the entire older conversation.
learning.concept: When the full history of a long conversation cannot be supplied, explicitly save the confirmed state and include it in the input when needed.

A.text: Always concatenate the entire conversation and, if it exceeds the model's limit, send it anyway, prioritizing confirmation of the reservation.
A.explanation: Because there is a limit, confirmed information cannot be passed reliably.

B.text: Send only the latest few messages and, if information is missing, fill it in using the preferences of a similar user.
B.explanation: This mixes the user's confirmed details with guesses.

C.text: Whenever older history is omitted, summarize it in free-form text without distinguishing confirmed values from values still under consideration.
C.explanation: Tentative information included in the summary could overwrite confirmed values.

D.text: Record confirmed preferences separately and reflect only updates made by the user. Provide that record when it is needed to generate a response.
D.explanation: This keeps confirmed information available even with a short context.

aib-c01-d1-049@1.title: Assign models only to tasks improved by adaptation
aib-c01-d1-049@1.prompt: A machine manufacturer adapted a generative AI model to extract product codes from maintenance requests. Extraction passed evaluation, but the adapted version performed worse on multilingual failure descriptions used by the same company; only the original version meets the quality standard for those descriptions. The two tasks are on separate screens, and it is known before submission which task a user will perform. Which deployment approach should be used?

learning.reason: An improvement from adaptation does not guarantee improvement in other capabilities. Because the task is identifiable, assign the adapted version to product-code extraction and preserve the original version's quality for multilingual descriptions.
learning.concept: When specialization causes another capability to fall below its standard, assign models by use case if the use case can be identified.

A.text: Assign the adapted version to extraction and the original version to multilingual descriptions, and track quality separately for each use case.
A.explanation: Because the use case can be identified in advance, this uses the verified improvement while preventing regression in the other use case.

B.text: Route to the original version based on the user's country, rather than the screen, only if the adapted version could not answer in multiple languages.
B.explanation: A user's country does not reliably identify the use case or preferred language, and a response that fails the standard may be shown first.

C.text: Rule out separate deployment by use case and retire the adapted version entirely, even though it improved extraction quality.
C.explanation: Because the tasks are on separate screens, the improvement for extraction can still be used.

D.text: Average the extraction and multilingual results across both tasks, and replace both screens if the adapted version has the higher overall score.
D.explanation: An average score can hide multilingual descriptions that do not meet their individual quality requirement.

aib-c01-d1-050@1.title: Use likelihood and business impact together
aib-c01-d1-050@1.prompt: The maintenance team can inspect only one machine today. Machine A has a 60% probability of failure and a loss of ¥100,000 if it fails; machine B has a 20% probability of failure and a loss of ¥800,000. Inspection costs the same for both, and assume that inspecting either machine will prevent the failure in question. Which choice reduces expected loss the most?

learning.reason: A's expected loss is ¥60,000, while B's is ¥160,000. If the same inspection cost can prevent either failure, prioritize B.
learning.concept: Multiply a predicted probability by the magnitude of the impact. When intervention costs are the same, address the case with the greater expected loss first.

A.text: Inspect B. Compare the product of each machine's failure probability and loss amount.
A.explanation: This compares likelihood and impact in the same monetary units.

B.text: Inspect A. A higher probability means a greater expected loss.
B.explanation: This does not account for the difference in loss amounts.

C.text: Choose either machine with equal probability. Probabilities do not represent certain losses, so they cannot be compared.
C.explanation: Even for uncertain events, expected loss can prioritize them when the other conditions are the same.

D.text: Inspect A. If B's failure probability is below 50%, treat its loss as zero.
D.explanation: A low probability does not make a large potential loss negligible.

aib-c01-d1-051@1.title: Choose an AI approach when failure types cannot be listed in advance
aib-c01-d1-051@1.prompt: A manufacturing line has ample sensor records from stable operation, but very few labeled examples for each type of failure. The goal is to identify behaviors for staff to investigate, including unknown anomalies. Which approach should be used first?

learning.reason: Learn the normal range and flag behavior outside it as a candidate. A candidate is not a confirmed diagnosis of failure; a person should compare it with the actual equipment.
learning.concept: Detect deviations from normal operation separately from classification that predicts the type of anomaly.

A.text: Detect deviations from normal operating patterns and present them for review.
A.explanation: This fits a situation where failure types cannot be exhaustively listed in advance.

B.text: Use only the annual average for all equipment and report no anomaly if the average has not changed.
B.explanation: Short-lived anomalies and equipment-specific behavior can be hidden by the average.

C.text: Train a supervised model to classify failure names without records of those failure names.
C.explanation: The required labeled examples are unavailable.

D.text: Have generative AI write descriptions of possible failures and use the text alone to confirm anomalies in sensor behavior.
D.explanation: There is no comparison with actual measurements.

aib-c01-d1-052@1.title: Check Measurement Units and Aggregation Intervals Even When Field Names Match
aib-c01-d1-052@1.prompt: Factory A records pressure in kilopascals every second, while Factory B stores a per-minute average in megapascals. The goal is to predict pressure spikes lasting a few seconds. Before combining the data, which TWO actions should be taken?

learning.reason: Matching units cannot restore pressure peaks lasting a few seconds that were lost through averaging. Keep data for brief events distinct and measure at Factory B at the required finer interval.
learning.concept: Check unit conversions and aggregation intervals; do not invent time information that cannot be recovered from historical data.

A.text: Reduce Factory A's data to per-minute averages and assume that minute-level observations are sufficient for brief spikes.
A.explanation: This would lose the seconds-level changes needed for the decision.

B.text: Copy each average from Factory B 60 times and treat the copies as per-second data.
B.explanation: Duplicating an average cannot reconstruct the peaks.

C.text: Distinguish the measurement intervals and add measurements at Factory B that can capture changes lasting a few seconds.
C.explanation: This makes it possible to check brief changes that cannot be observed in data already averaged over a minute.

D.text: Once the units match, assume the measurement intervals match too and join both factories' values into the same training feature.
D.explanation: The difference in time resolution would remain.

E.text: Record the original units and validate the conversion rules for expressing both sets of measurements in the same unit.
E.explanation: This allows pressure magnitudes to be compared correctly across the factories.

aib-c01-d1-053@1.title: Align Labeling Criteria Before Adding More Training Data
aib-c01-d1-053@1.prompt: You are building an AI system to classify customer inquiries. There are already enough records from staff members, but one staff member labels the same wording as “refund” while another labels it as “contract change.” The cause is an ambiguous classification guide. Which preparation should be prioritized?

learning.reason: Have multiple staff members independently label the same cases, resolve disagreements, and create a guide that reflects their agreement. Train and evaluate with cases labeled under the aligned criteria.
learning.concept: When the same case receives different training labels, measure agreement and clarify the criteria and how exceptions are handled.

A.text: Add duplicate cases as they are to increase the data volume, and evaluate only against the current records' labels.
A.explanation: This does not address the root cause of the disagreement.

B.text: Use a larger model and let it learn the differences in staff members' criteria as they are.
B.explanation: Model size does not determine which judgment is correct.

C.text: Treat the classifications from the staff member who entered the most records as correct and do not compare them with anyone else's.
C.explanation: The number of entries does not show that a judgment is valid.

D.text: Have staff members classify the same examples independently, examine the reasons for disagreements, revise the definitions, and prepare agreed-upon training labels.
D.explanation: This makes the learning objective and the criteria for correct answers consistent.

aib-c01-d1-054@1.title: Choose Which Source to Trust Before Taking Action
aib-c01-d1-054@1.prompt: A booking agent consults two sources. An internal list shows a time slot as available, but the official booking ledger reports that the same slot is already reserved. The agent can create bookings, and duplicate bookings must be avoided. Which control is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Use the official ledger to determine availability and verify the latest state before creating a booking. If the discrepancy prevents a decision, hold the action and request human review.
learning.concept: An agent that takes actions should detect conflicting source results and wait for an authoritative state or human resolution before committing.

A.text: Decide whether the slot is available by majority vote, and use the internal list if the sources are tied.
A.explanation: This does not account for differences in source authority or freshness.

B.text: Reserve the slot only after the official ledger confirms it is available, and hand the case off to a person if the discrepancy cannot be resolved.
B.explanation: The action follows an authoritative state and a verified result.

C.text: Create the booking first, then check whether the official ledger reports a duplicate booking.
C.explanation: This takes the very action that should be avoided before checking.

D.text: Tell the user the slot is available, but do not record the agent's booking result.
D.explanation: This cannot keep the booking state consistent with the promise made to the user.

aib-c01-d1-055@1.title: Correct Probability Calibration When Ranking Is Preserved
aib-c01-d1-055@1.prompt: A model estimates the probability of late payments. When cases are ranked from highest probability to lowest, its detection rate among the highest-ranked cases remains as good as before. Recently, however, cases shown at 40% have had an actual late-payment rate of about 25%, making the review capacity set using those probabilities too large. What is the appropriate response?

learning.reason: Ranking performance and probability calibration are different properties. Validate recalibration against recent finalized data and check ranking performance as well.
learning.concept: Separate ranking from probability calibration in evaluation; when only the probabilities are misaligned, try recalibration first.

A.text: Reassess probability calibration using recent finalized data, then check both probability calibration and ranking performance on separate validation data.
A.explanation: This targets the property that has actually degraded.

B.text: If ranking performance is unchanged, treat the probability discrepancy as an operational issue and leave the model unchanged.
B.explanation: The probabilities used to set review capacity no longer have the same meaning.

C.text: Completely reverse the ranking and switch the cases selected for review to account for the lower late-payment rate.
C.explanation: This would discard ranking performance that has been preserved and would not correct the probabilities.

D.text: Remove past cases that were not late from the evaluation data so the displayed probabilities match the late-payment rate.
D.explanation: This would distort the actual distribution of cases.

aib-c01-d1-056@1.title: Do not treat instructions in source documents as system instructions
aib-c01-d1-056@1.prompt: The accounting department uses AI to read free-text submissions from business partners and extract the site name and requested date. Some people write requests to the person handling the submission as commands in the text. Which improvement would ensure that commands in a document are not treated as additional instructions to the AI and that missing fields are not guessed?

learning.reason: Explicitly separate the instructions from the content to be extracted, and treat requests within that content only as source material. Specify the permitted output fields and what to return when a value is missing, then validate the result.
learning.concept: Clearly identify a supplied document as the extraction target, distinguish the source of instructions, and limit the response to the requested fields.

A.text: If a document contains even one command, discard the entire document and fill both fields using values from another document.
A.explanation: This prevents valid documents from being processed and can lead to incorrect entries based on other materials.

B.text: Append the partner’s document verbatim to the end of the instructions and give priority to the last command written.
B.explanation: A command in the source material could override the original extraction instructions.

C.text: Delimit the content to be extracted and explicitly state that instructions within it must not be followed. Return only the site name and requested date, and indicate when either is not provided.
C.explanation: This distinguishes business instructions from input data.

D.text: To respect the requester’s intent, carry out any actions described in the document before extracting the fields.
D.explanation: The sender of a document does not have authority to instruct the AI to perform actions.

aib-c01-d1-057@1.title: Choose inference execution based on when results are used
aib-c01-d1-057@1.prompt: Each branch receives a forecast of its visit count for one day before business hours. The input consists of records finalized each night and does not change during the following day’s operations. Staff at all branches open the results at the same time in the morning, so they want to avoid wait times when viewing them. Which approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Generate a batch of forecasts for all branches after the inputs are finalized, and save the forecast target date and model version. The results can then be served from storage in the morning.
learning.concept: Without changing the model, choose batch inference based on when results must be current and the required response time.

A.text: Fix the forecast using values from before the input is finalized, and do not incorporate the later finalized values until the following month.
A.explanation: This fails to use finalized data that is available for the day’s forecast.

B.text: Run inference with the same input every time someone opens the screen, and aggregate peak-time latency after displaying the results.
B.explanation: Inference would be repeated for the same input and could increase morning wait times.

C.text: After the input is finalized, generate forecasts for all branches in a batch, record the target date and model version, and display the saved results in the morning.
C.explanation: This meets both the update requirement and the response-time requirement when viewing results.

D.text: Retrain the model each time a staff member opens the screen, then generate a forecast on the spot.
D.explanation: Retraining when results are viewed is unnecessary when the inputs and conditions have been finalized by the previous day.

aib-c01-d1-058@1.title: Distinguish image classification from AI that locates objects
aib-c01-d1-058@1.prompt: During a materials inspection, a photo may show several identical cases. An inspector needs to check their positions in the image one by one and determine whether the required number is present. Showing only “case present” is not enough. Which AI approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Detect each object’s location and count it so inspectors can compare the results, including when objects are crowded or overlapping.
learning.concept: When a task requires the number and location of multiple objects, choose per-object detection rather than image labels.

A.text: Classify whether a case appears anywhere in the image and treat the value indicating its presence as the number photographed.
A.explanation: A label does not indicate a count or location.

B.text: Forecast the number of shipments from each photo’s capture time, without addressing where they are in the image.
B.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to check locations.

C.text: Generate a general caption for each photo and count the occurrences of the word “case” in the text as the number of cases.
C.explanation: The number of times a term appears in a caption does not indicate the number of objects in the image.

D.text: Use object detection to indicate the position of each case in the image, count them, and evaluate detection results even in photos with overlapping cases.
D.explanation: This approach can handle both the number and the locations of the objects.

aib-c01-d1-059@1.title: Do not discard extreme values indiscriminately
aib-c01-d1-059@1.prompt: The order history for an order forecast includes orders 20 times larger than usual. A review indicates that some were genuine results of large promotions, while others appear to be digit-entry errors. The business also wants to account for future promotions. Which data-preparation approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Check representative cases against the original records and separate verified events from entry errors. If promotion factors are known at inference time, use them as features and evaluate the model on large-scale events.
learning.concept: Confirm the cause of an outlier using source records or related metrics, and distinguish valid exceptions from recording errors.

A.text: Treat all extreme records as valid and train on them more heavily so that the model predicts more high-volume orders.
A.explanation: Entry errors can affect the model.

B.text: Use original records and promotion records to distinguish genuine large orders from entry errors, and evaluate performance under verified promotion conditions as well.
B.explanation: This preserves important business events and corrects clear errors.

C.text: Delete every row whose deviation from the mean exceeds a threshold, and consider the results representative even for months with promotions.
C.explanation: This discards actual promotions that the model should predict.

D.text: Replace every extreme value with the median and decide whether to deploy based only on whether the forecast has become easier to make.
D.explanation: This cannot handle real short-term increases in demand.

aib-c01-d1-060@1.title: Choosing where to collect additional labeled data
aib-c01-d1-060@1.prompt: In an independent evaluation of an application review system, standard applications perform well, but errors are frequent only in applications involving multiple parties, including representatives. The document formats are known, and the cause is a shortage of correctly labeled examples for this group. How should the budget for additional labeling be used?

learning.reason: Collect correctly labeled examples from the affected group. Reserve some for evaluation and check whether performance on standard applications is maintained.
learning.concept: Collect new data based on confirmed high-impact failure categories instead of gathering it indiscriminately from the population.

A.text: Treat every prediction from the current model as correct, including for the group where it is wrong, and train on those outputs.
A.explanation: This copies confirmed errors into the training data.

B.text: Exclude applications involving representatives from training and reduce the total number measured to speed up evaluation.
B.explanation: This removes the group that needs improvement from consideration.

C.text: Collect additional examples at random in the same proportions as the current data, and judge success only by improvements on standard applications.
C.explanation: Information about the group where errors are concentrated would remain insufficient.

D.text: Prioritize examples involving representatives, independently verify their correct labels, split them between training and evaluation, and reevaluate standard applications as well.
D.explanation: This targets the missing information and lets you check for side effects.

aib-c01-d1-061@1.title: Routing inquiries with varied wording
aib-c01-d1-061@1.prompt: A home-appliance support desk has three valid departments to handle inquiries. It has many historical cases with labels confirmed by staff, but similar requests are phrased in many different ways, and fixed keyword rules leave many inquiries unrouted. Which approach to using AI is appropriate?

learning.reason: Classify free-text inquiries into known departments and route uncertain cases to the staff who already handle them. Existing rules can be used when routing conditions are clear.
learning.concept: Try classification support when labels are established but hand-written rules cannot enumerate all possible wording.

A.text: Choose the next department based on each department’s past case volume, without using the inquiry text.
A.explanation: This does not take the actual reason for the inquiry into account.

B.text: Because the departments are already established, generate and adopt a new department name for each inquiry.
B.explanation: This would not route inquiries according to the existing areas of responsibility.

C.text: To avoid missing keywords, send every previously unseen word to the busiest department.
C.explanation: This increases unnecessary transfers without assessing the inquiry’s intent.

D.text: Try text classification with the confirmed examples, route uncertain cases to staff, and compare misrouting rates by department.
D.explanation: This accommodates varied wording while leaving exceptions to people.

aib-c01-d1-062@1.title: Choosing which image regions to process when full images do not fit
aib-c01-d1-062@1.prompt: A maintenance AI system identifies equipment model numbers from many high-resolution photos. Sending the photos together reaches the input limit. An approach that downsizes every image uniformly makes the small text on nameplates unreadable. How can the system preserve evidence for the model numbers while processing the images?

learning.reason: Extract the nameplate regions while preserving readable resolution. Identify each photo, process only the needed images, and send unreadable cases for review.
learning.concept: Balance image detail against context limits by selecting the regions needed for the task at sufficient resolution.

A.text: Extract the nameplate regions at a resolution that keeps the text readable, retain references to the photos, and process the required regions.
A.explanation: This reduces input size while preserving the evidence.

B.text: Downsize every image to the same minimum resolution and have the AI guess model numbers that are no longer readable.
B.explanation: This loses the text information the task requires.

C.text: Send all images, discard anything over the limit, and do not record which original images were referenced.
C.explanation: This risks omissions and makes the evidence impossible to trace.

D.text: Determine each model number from the average number of times it appears in the photos, and open the nameplate images only after a support request.
D.explanation: This does not verify the model number actually shown in the photos.

aib-c01-d1-063@1.title: Using knowledge that can be removed individually later
aib-c01-d1-063@1.prompt: An organization may use a contractor’s training materials to answer questions only while that contractor’s consent remains valid. If one contractor withdraws consent, only that contractor’s materials must be removed from answer sources within the same day. The materials contain specific information that the original model was not trained on. Which method is suitable for adding this knowledge?

learning.reason: Treat the materials as reference data with clear contractor ownership and permissions instead of training them into model weights. When consent is withdrawn, stop retrieval, remove the materials from caches and other reuse paths, and test that they no longer reach the answer path.
learning.concept: Keep documents that may need to be withdrawn out of model weights; enforce and verify their usage restrictions at retrieval time.

A.text: Fine-tune on materials from all contractors, and delete only the original training files when consent is withdrawn.
A.explanation: Deleting the source files does not establish that the influence of specific materials has been removed from the updated model.

B.text: Manage reference materials separately for each contractor, check authorization at retrieval time, and verify upon withdrawal that the materials are excluded from retrieval and reusable results.
B.explanation: This applies per-document usage restrictions without rewriting trained model weights.

C.text: Continue retrieving the withdrawn materials for a set period and add a notice at the end of generated answers that consent has been withdrawn.
C.explanation: This fails the requirement not to use the materials as a basis for answers.

D.text: Summarize each contractor’s materials into a single training dataset, then configure the system to hide only the name of a contractor who withdraws consent.
D.explanation: Hiding the name does not verify that content derived from that contractor’s materials has stopped being used.

aib-c01-d2-049@1.title: Distinguishing likely buyers from customers whose purchases a campaign can increase
aib-c01-d2-049@1.prompt: A retailer wants to increase net profit using a limited number of discount coupons. Giving them to customers who already tend to buy would add the cost of the discounts. Within the permitted scope, the retailer can also run a controlled trial in which some customers receive no coupon. Which AI initiative best fits this goal?

learning.reason: Compare purchases increased by sending a coupon with the discount cost, then test whether distributing coupons to customers whose behavior they change is worthwhile.
learning.concept: Separate predicted purchase likelihood from the incremental effect of a marketing campaign.

A.text: Estimate the purchases caused by offering a coupon by comparing customers who receive one with those who do not, then test recipients based on incremental profit after discounts.
A.explanation: This evaluates the campaign's effect and cost separately from customers' underlying likelihood to buy.

B.text: Rank recipients only by coupon redemptions, without checking purchases before or after distribution.
B.explanation: A redeemed coupon does not show whether it changed the customer's purchasing decision.

C.text: Change the coupon copy and use the version with the highest open rate for all customers.
C.explanation: Open rates do not measure the profit generated by a limited number of coupons.

D.text: Distribute coupons to customers with the highest purchase probability first, and infer that the most redemptions also mean the highest net profit.
D.explanation: This counts sales from people who would have purchased without a coupon as incremental and still incurs the discount cost.

aib-c01-d2-050@1.title: Combining purchased and in-house capabilities by function
aib-c01-d2-050@1.prompt: A railway company's customer-service AI needs both general Japanese language processing and support for decisions about the company's own rail-replacement transport rules. Commercial language-processing components meet the requirements, and the company's staff update the replacement-transport rules daily. Building everything in-house would exceed the deadline, but the replacement-rule processing alone can be built in-house. Which approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Purchase a verified component for general language processing, while the company manages its changing, domain-specific rules and their evaluation. Define the boundary and versions clearly.
learning.concept: Buy standardized foundational capabilities and manage internally the parts that provide differentiation and carry responsibility.

A.text: Move replacement-transport decisions to an external general-purpose capability and build the language processing from scratch to differentiate the company.
A.explanation: This reverses which capability needs to be built in-house and which can be replaced with a commercial one.

B.text: Leave the replacement-transport rules to a commercial answer service and wait for the provider's annual update whenever they change.
B.explanation: This does not support the company's need to update its own rules daily.

C.text: Purchase the language-processing component, while keeping the replacement-transport decisions, authorized reference materials, and evaluation under the company's control. Test how the components work together.
C.explanation: This provides the foundational capability within the deadline while preserving control over the company's unique responsibilities.

D.text: Build every capability in-house and assume no new staff are needed, even though this is known to exceed the deadline.
D.explanation: This does not satisfy the available time and staffing constraints.

aib-c01-d2-051@1.title: Avoiding double counting when initiatives target the same outcome
aib-c01-d2-051@1.prompt: In a billing department, an AI document checker and a redesigned data-entry form are both expected to reduce the same verification errors. Trials of each initiative separately showed some improvement. How should the department decide whether to fund both?

learning.reason: Because both initiatives target overlapping improvements, compare using either one alone with using both, and assess whether the additional benefit justifies the additional cost.
learning.concept: Avoid counting the same business outcome twice by comparing each initiative's standalone effect with its incremental effect when combined.

A.text: Evaluate the improvement from each initiative alone and from using them together on the same basis, then make the investment decision using the second initiative's incremental benefit and additional cost.
A.explanation: This avoids simply adding the standalone results and double counting the same improvement.

B.text: Give the AI-based initiative a higher score and exclude the form redesign from the comparison even though its improvement has been demonstrated.
B.explanation: This prioritizes an initiative based on its method rather than comparing net benefits.

C.text: Since overlap is difficult to assess, allocate the same budget to both and do not record the differences between using either one alone and using both after rollout.
C.explanation: The basis for the budget allocation and the additional results would remain unknown.

D.text: Simply add the number of errors reduced in the separate trials and assign the entire combined benefit to both budgets.
D.explanation: This counts the reduction in the same errors twice.

aib-c01-d2-052@1.title: Do not let AI decide while business rules remain in conflict
aib-c01-d2-052@1.prompt: The sales and accounting departments have conflicting official documents about how refunds should be handled, and no one has decided which takes precedence. The main cause of current processing errors is this conflict, not difficulty entering information. A proposal claims that giving both documents to a new AI will resolve the issue. What should be prioritized?

learning.reason: The responsible owners must decide which policies and exceptions apply, how they are revised, and how the changes are communicated. Do not replace unresolved organizational policy with AI output.
learning.concept: When an organization's policy is unresolved, first establish who has authority to decide the rules and how they apply.

A.text: Give both documents to the model and make whichever explanation it generates with higher probability the official policy going forward.
A.explanation: The model has no authority to reconcile or standardize policy.

B.text: Change only half of the erroneous cases based on the AI's decision, then check for consistency with the old policies afterward.
B.explanation: This changes business decisions without resolving the conflict.

C.text: Automatically prioritize the document from the department with the higher transaction volume and skip approval by the business owners.
C.explanation: Transaction volume does not determine which policy takes precedence.

D.text: Bring the policy owners together to decide which rules apply and what exceptions are allowed, then organize the obsolete versions. Reassess afterward which steps AI can support.
D.explanation: This addresses the root cause and establishes trustworthy business requirements.

aib-c01-d2-053@1.title: Assigning ownership and tracking cases across a cutover
aib-c01-d2-053@1.prompt: The organization is changing contract intake from manual handling to AI-assisted processing. Many cases will still be open on the planned cutover date, and for some, a person has already promised the customer a response deadline. The new system automatically recognizes only new submissions. Which two preparations should be made for the production cutover?

learning.reason: Inventory open cases and carry forward their owners, progress, and response deadlines. Distinguish new submissions from work already in progress to prevent cases from being overlooked or duplicated.
learning.concept: Reconcile the state of open cases during a migration and transfer ownership and deadlines for each case.

A.text: Re-enter all existing cases as new and discard their previous ownership and deadline information.
A.explanation: This can cause rework, missed deadlines, and duplicate promises.

B.text: Stop accepting new submissions and then shut down the old system. Do not check the stopped system’s case list to see what remains open.
B.explanation: The in-progress state needed for the cutover will not be carried over.

C.text: Test only the performance of new submissions and handle open cases only if users contact the organization again.
C.explanation: This can cause response deadlines promised before the cutover to be missed.

D.text: Use the existing case IDs to distinguish open cases from new submissions, and reconcile the cases during a cutover rehearsal to check for unprocessed or duplicate registrations.
D.explanation: This verifies through the actual workflow whether the migration proceeds as planned.

E.text: Reconcile the owners and deadlines for open cases, then decide which cases will be completed under the old process and which will be migrated.
E.explanation: This preserves promised responses and processing ownership through the cutover.

aib-c01-d2-054@1.title: Measuring deadline breaches that averages can hide
aib-c01-d2-054@1.prompt: With AI assistance, the average application processing time fell from 60 minutes to 30 minutes. However, cases requiring lengthy manual review remain, and reports indicate that the operational goal of processing every application within 2 hours is being missed. Which metric should be added as the next primary metric?

learning.reason: Averages can hide cases with long processing times. Measure the percentage of cases exceeding 2 hours and the exceedance by category across the same population.
learning.concept: Evaluate deadline breaches separately from average processing time.

A.text: The average processing time for the 10 fastest completed cases.
A.explanation: This excludes the cases that take the longest from the measurement.

B.text: The average number of seconds before data entry begins.
B.explanation: This does not measure whether each application was completed by the deadline.

C.text: The percentage of cases that take more than 2 hours, broken down by type and including exceptions.
C.explanation: This directly measures whether the operational goal is being met and which types of cases remain delayed.

D.text: The number of AI-generated drafts divided by the number of applications.
D.explanation: This measures volume but does not show whether deadlines were missed.

aib-c01-d2-055@1.title: Comparing sites with different starting performance
aib-c01-d2-055@1.prompt: Site A, which will adopt AI, has many experienced employees, while at site B, which will not adopt AI, half of the cases are handled by new employees. A proposal is to compare only the averages after adoption. What should be prepared before adoption?

learning.reason: Collect pre-adoption data at both sites using the same definitions, and segment by experience and case complexity. Evaluate changes under comparable conditions.
learning.concept: Measure each site’s baseline before adoption and assess changes against it.

A.text: Use the time of the best employee at site A as the company-wide benchmark and do not measure site B’s pre-adoption performance.
A.explanation: The sample is biased, and the comparison conditions are not aligned.

B.text: Do not record cases when they are less complex, and change which cases are included after adoption without documenting a reason.
B.explanation: Changes in the population being measured cannot be evaluated consistently.

C.text: Compare only the post-adoption processing times at sites A and B and attribute the entire difference to AI.
C.explanation: Differences in employee experience and case mix would be counted as an AI effect.

D.text: Measure processing time and quality at both sites before adoption using the same method, then compare before-and-after changes within groups matched for employee experience and case type.
D.explanation: This distinguishes pre-existing differences from changes after adoption.

aib-c01-d2-056@1.title: Accounting for losses that average estimates can hide
aib-c01-d2-056@1.prompt: The estimated net benefit of AI assistance in its first year is 1.5 million yen under the typical scenario and minus 2 million yen under low adoption. Management will accept a first-year loss of no more than 1 million yen. The provider offers a fixed contract for the first year and a contract with a lower base fee but a higher per-unit rate as usage increases. Which evaluation should be performed before approval?

learning.reason: In the presented low-usage estimate, the loss amount exceeds the acceptable limit. Compare each contract's net benefit from low to high usage, and check separately whether the loss amount in each case stays within the limit and how the contract terms affect the benefit in the typical scenario.
learning.concept: Do not decide based only on a positive baseline ROI; test conservative scenarios against the loss limit.

A.text: Compare usage and net benefit across multiple scenarios for each contract, and check the loss limit under low adoption as well as the typical-case benefit.
A.explanation: This evaluates both typical value and financially acceptable downside for each contract.

B.text: Assume that the contract with the lower base fee will always keep the maximum first-year loss within the limit, without checking usage charges or the contract term.
B.explanation: Usage-based charges and financial outcomes also need to be evaluated, even when the base fee is low.

C.text: Take the simple average of the net benefits under low adoption and the typical scenario, and choose a contract based only on whether the result is positive.
C.explanation: A positive average does not establish that the loss limit is met in each individual scenario.

D.text: Choose the fixed contract because the typical scenario is profitable, without considering the financial constraint under low adoption.
D.explanation: A profit under the typical scenario does not show that the low-adoption loss limit will be met.

aib-c01-d2-057@1.title: Measure progress toward a long-term contract renewal
aib-c01-d2-057@1.prompt: The renewal of an enterprise service contract will be finalized in six months. AI organizes the contract details to help the account manager reach agreement with the customer on a renewal proposal. Which leading indicator should inform next month's operating decisions?

learning.reason: Track the share of target customers who have progressed to an inquiry or an agreed next step, rather than simple views or document-generation counts. Compare that measure with actual renewals later.
learning.concept: Track progress in user decision-making before a later outcome is finalized.

A.text: The total number of emails between the account manager and the customer.
A.explanation: More exchanges do not necessarily lead to agreement or contract renewal.

B.text: Only the company's total renewal revenue, which will be known in six months.
B.explanation: This is an important lagging outcome, but it will not be available in time for next month's decision.

C.text: The share of target customers who agree on a next step, such as a time to review the renewal proposal or topics to consider.
C.explanation: This shows whether renewal discussions are progressing before the final renewal outcome.

D.text: The number of characters in the contract summary generated by AI.
D.explanation: This measures the format of the output, not progress toward renewal.

aib-c01-d2-058@1.title: Manage operating costs by separating retention purposes
aib-c01-d2-058@1.prompt: Costs for an AI tool that supports approval requests have risen. Analysis shows that the cause is the indefinite retention of intermediate draft files that can be recreated, rather than long-term retention of the approval rationale. The official rationale must be retained for a prescribed period. Which cost-control measure is appropriate?

learning.reason: Classify official evidence separately from temporary files, and set a purpose-appropriate expiration period for intermediate files. Before deletion, check for dependencies related to audits.
learning.concept: Reduce incremental costs by setting expiration periods for reproducible temporary artifacts while retaining audit records.

A.text: Change the model used to generate drafts, without comparing the volume of temporary files already accumulated.
A.explanation: This does not address the identified source of the cost increase.

B.text: Keep the official evidence for the required period, set expiration dates for intermediate files confirmed to be reproducible, and check costs and retention of necessary data.
B.explanation: This controls the source of the cost while preserving the retention obligation.

C.text: Delete the largest items without checking their purpose, and apply the same retention period to the rationale supporting approved requests.
C.explanation: This could violate the requirement to retain necessary records long term.

D.text: Move all data to a cheaper storage destination without assessing restoration conditions or the continuing growth in volume.
D.explanation: This does not control the indefinite accumulation of temporary materials.

aib-c01-d2-059@1.title: Identify an unmet usage requirement among competitors
aib-c01-d2-059@1.prompt: For meeting-assistance services aimed at municipalities, a major competitor has high general transcription accuracy. However, several small municipalities prioritize being able to create records without access to their internal network and send them later. What is the best initial research to assess a market gap?

learning.reason: Identify the target customers' important requirements, determine whether candidate services actually meet them, and investigate willingness to pay if they do not.
learning.concept: Compare customer-segment requirements with existing services instead of relying only on average feature performance.

A.text: Compare the target customers' requirements for offline operation with competitors' actual behavior, and investigate the value of addressing any shortfall.
A.explanation: This identifies a condition that may influence customers' choices beyond overall accuracy.

B.text: Rank services only by general recognition accuracy across all customers, without evaluating use outside the network.
B.explanation: This excludes a decision criterion that may distinguish the alternatives.

C.text: Offer lower prices than competitors to all municipalities without researching how the requirements are used.
C.explanation: This does not establish whether customers can perform the work they need to do.

D.text: Conclude that internal-network constraints have no competitive significance because the competitor has high market share.
D.explanation: This infers the needs of a specific segment from a market-wide average.

aib-c01-d2-060@1.title: Validate a new offering using existing data
aib-c01-d2-060@1.prompt: A distributor owns historical data used for its internal demand forecasts. Its contract permits external sharing only of sufficiently aggregated results that cannot identify individual transactions. Suppliers are interested in regional demand trends. What is the most appropriate proof of a new revenue model?

learning.reason: Run a small paid service based on aggregations permitted by the contract. Check how often customers use it, the price they will pay, and the costs of selling and maintaining it.
learning.concept: Go beyond improving existing operations by testing an analytics offering against licensing limits and new customers' willingness to pay.

A.text: Improve only the accuracy of internal ordering, without validating whether suppliers would pay for it.
A.explanation: Internal improvement and willingness to pay for a new business offering are separate questions.

B.text: Build a nationwide service based only on expressions of interest in demand data, and set subscription fees based on inquiries after launch.
B.explanation: This does not validate pricing or intent to use before making the upfront investment.

C.text: Offer the raw historical data for a fee without aggregation, on the grounds that it allows more flexible analysis.
C.explanation: This exceeds the scope of external sharing permitted by the contract.

D.text: Run a paid trial that provides regional trends using permitted aggregations, and measure update frequency, willingness to pay, and maintenance costs.
D.explanation: This tests both the revenue and costs of the new offering.

aib-c01-d2-061@1.title: Build a system that increases the value contributed by partners
aib-c01-d2-061@1.prompt: A company offering AI for inspection work has won more business when customers can use it without replacing their existing specialist providers. Those providers do not have time to build custom integrations. Which investment would create a long-term advantage?

learning.reason: Establishing standard integration methods and contractual requirements makes it easier for specialist providers to participate. Measure the breadth of expertise available and its effect on customer retention.
learning.concept: Design for compatibility and lower integration costs so value grows through participation rather than through a single model.

A.text: Require every specialist provider to build a custom connection, preserving the long implementation time as a barrier to entry.
A.explanation: This does not increase the number of integrations available and limits customer choice.

B.text: Provide a common integration specification and vetted information exchange, then measure the breadth of participating specialties and the effect on customer retention.
B.explanation: Participation can continuously expand the value available to customers.

C.text: Improve only the performance of the latest model and leave operational integrations with specialist providers to individual requests.
C.explanation: This does not improve the factor already shown to increase sales.

D.text: Replace all specialist-provider work with an in-house AI system and remove customers’ ability to designate approved providers.
D.explanation: This removes value for customers who want to keep their existing providers.

aib-c01-d2-062@1.title: Do not apply the same investment ratio to markets at different stages of maturity
aib-c01-d2-062@1.prompt: In Market A, the customer base and operating model for AI maintenance support are established, and competitors are strengthening local support. In Market B, the types of equipment data permitted and customer demand are still unclear, and it is not yet known whether the existing AI can be offered there as is. What is the most appropriate investment allocation for the next fiscal year?

learning.reason: In Market A, invest in operations based on proven customer value and competitive conditions. In Market B, validate usage conditions and willingness to pay before deciding on further investment, rather than deploying at scale.
learning.concept: Even when the underlying technology is shared, reflect local competitive pace and adoption requirements in incremental investment.

A.text: Stop investing in customer support in Market A until research in Market B is complete, then address competition in both markets at once.
A.explanation: This would delay the response to proven demand and competition in Market A.

B.text: In Market A, strengthen local operations in light of demonstrated value and competition; in Market B, limit investment to validating usage conditions and paying demand.
B.explanation: This treats funding needs and decision criteria differently for an established market and an unvalidated one.

C.text: Because there are few competitors in Market B, roll out across the entire market ahead of Market A before the data usage conditions are known.
C.explanation: This commits to long-term costs despite uncertain demand and implementation conditions.

D.text: Because the model is shared, allocate the same budget percentage to both markets based only on their existing revenue.
D.explanation: This ignores differences in competition and adoption conditions across regions.

aib-c01-d2-063@1.title: Get experience that would be lost during a handoff to the people who need it
aib-c01-d2-063@1.prompt: During overnight equipment maintenance, recovery is delayed because the night-shift technician has to rediscover the symptoms observed by the day-shift technician and the checks that were not completed. The work details are in authorized handoff records. Which initiative and evaluation approach are appropriate?

learning.reason: Bring forward the supporting evidence and open follow-up items, then evaluate missed checks and repeat investigation time during handoffs.
learning.concept: Connect the diagnostic information needed during a departmental handoff to outcome measures that show whether it helped.

A.text: Have AI generate the night shift’s schedule and treat the number of schedules created as a business outcome.
A.explanation: This does not measure whether the diagnostic information needed for recovery is handed over.

B.text: Forecast future equipment replacement costs and measure whether the difference from the quarterly budget decreases.
B.explanation: This does not address the time spent searching for information during the overnight handoff.

C.text: Present symptoms, completed and outstanding checks, and references to the source records in a handoff summary; measure repeat investigation time and missed items.
C.explanation: This directly improves the handoff that is causing delays.

D.text: Rank cases resolved before the shift change and do not measure repeat investigation after the handoff.
D.explanation: This cannot assess value for cases that require a handoff.

aib-c01-d2-064@1.title: Separate benefits that depend on changes to an external party’s process
aib-c01-d2-064@1.prompt: AI in a transportation department could greatly shorten delivery times if an external carrier temporarily increased pickups from twice a day. Another initiative, detecting incorrect shipping labels in advance, has a smaller benefit but can be implemented by your company alone. Negotiations with the carrier will not conclude for six months. What should the next-period plan be?

learning.reason: Confirm the conditions required to realize each benefit and start with an improvement the company can measure itself. Keep the effect dependent on an external party conditional until agreement is reached.
learning.concept: Separate benefits that depend on another party’s unconfirmed actions and prioritize improvements within the business’s control.

A.text: Pilot the incorrect-label initiative and plan and estimate the pickup initiative separately, contingent on agreement with the external carrier.
A.explanation: This realizes benefits available to your company while distinguishing those that remain uncertain.

B.text: Since there is no agreement with the external carrier, treat the benefits of both initiatives as zero and do not evaluate the improvement that can be piloted independently.
B.explanation: This discards an initiative that can be implemented independently.

C.text: Book the maximum benefit from both initiatives in full for this fiscal year and spend the budget even if the external contract is not finalized.
C.explanation: This treats an unconfirmed dependency as though it had already been resolved.

D.text: Keep the number of contracted pickups unchanged and assume that improving AI performance alone will produce the same delivery-time benefit for every shipment.
D.explanation: This does not change the physical constraint on pickup capacity.

aib-c01-d2-065@1.title: Evaluate usage rights as a separate adoption condition from purchase price
aib-c01-d2-065@1.prompt: A public relations firm uses generative AI to create regional customer announcements. The lowest-cost provider reuses the drafts in shared data and cannot offer the usage rights required for commercial deliverables. Another provider agrees in writing to both conditions and is within budget. Their capabilities tested equally. Which adoption policy should the firm choose?

learning.reason: Treat the prohibition on data reuse and commercial usage rights as pass-or-fail conditions first, then compare cost, quality, and operational responsibility among options that meet them.
learning.concept: Check business rights and provider dependencies before comparing required capabilities and cost.

A.text: Assume the firm can operate without checking the rights terms if it limits the amount of input.
A.explanation: Using a small amount of input does not change the applicable usage terms.

B.text: Evaluate providers whose contracts can confirm the usage rights and treatment of input, then compare the contract with actual trials.
B.explanation: This addresses rights and operating conditions that must be met before comparing prices.

C.text: Choose the lowest-cost provider if the trial results are equivalent, and check for secondary use of data at contract renewal.
C.explanation: This does not meet the customer's required conditions before publication.

D.text: Treat an internal edit of the deliverable as creating contractual usage rights.
D.explanation: The fact that the firm edited the content does not establish contractual rights.

aib-c01-d2-066@1.title: Decide whether direct measurement is cheaper and more reliable than estimation
aib-c01-d2-066@1.prompt: A warehouse is considering using AI to estimate its loading rate from daily photos. Cargo hidden in the back cannot be seen in the photos. A simple counter added to existing loading equipment can directly measure the number of cargo items with the required accuracy and cost. Which approach should the warehouse choose?

learning.reason: If the required value can be observed directly at the agreed cost, trial the counter instead of estimating cargo that cannot be seen, and validate its operating procedure and accuracy.
learning.concept: Compare AI with required accuracy and operating burden when a field measurement is inexpensive and feasible.

A.text: Skip accuracy validation and evaluate counting improvements by the number of departments that adopt AI.
A.explanation: This does not measure the value the warehouse needs.

B.text: Deploy both complex AI and a counter, and let each team decide how to handle differences after operations begin.
B.explanation: This leaves an unnecessarily complex system and inconsistent decisions.

C.text: Estimate the total from only the visible parts of the photos and exclude the number of hidden cargo items from the evaluation.
C.explanation: Errors in the unobservable portion remain.

D.text: Validate the counter with representative inbound and outbound operations, and choose direct counting if it meets the required accuracy and operating cost.
D.explanation: It provides data closer to the underlying cause within the required conditions.

aib-c01-d2-067@1.title: Identify an existing check that could be lost when introducing AI
aib-c01-d2-067@1.prompt: An approver used to mark by hand any line on a paper application whose price exceeded a threshold. After switching to AI assistance, the price list is shorter, so readers can proceed without marking it. Checking high-priced items is still required. What should be done before accepting the transition?

learning.reason: Carry forward the purpose of the former mark: identify items over the threshold and verify the criteria and evidence for determining which cases require human review.
learning.concept: Inventory the business controls embedded in the old workflow and ensure the same purpose can be verified after migration.

A.text: Show an image of the mark from the paper form on the screen, without recording who checked the relevant line.
A.explanation: A visual cue alone does not show that the required check was performed.

B.text: Identify prices above the threshold and require a check; test whether the approver's review result and the item reviewed can be verified later.
B.explanation: This reproduces the existing business control in the actual new workflow.

C.text: Approve the shorter display first and treat the previous marking requirement as specific to paper forms.
C.explanation: The review obligation represented by the mark is not replaced.

D.text: Accept the change based only on reduced preparation time, and address missed high-priced items if an audit finding occurs.
D.explanation: This postpones a control that can be verified before operations begin.

aib-c01-d2-068@1.title: Measure whether internal time savings have shifted work to customers
aib-c01-d2-068@1.prompt: An application assistance AI has shortened internal review time. In return, customers must manually fill in additional forms required by the AI. The goal is to reduce the burden on customers through completion of their applications, not just to save internal time. Which KPI is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Measure customer work, additional requests, corrections due to errors, and completion outcomes to determine whether the burden was merely shifted elsewhere.
learning.concept: Measure total burden, including customer input and rework, in addition to the responsible team's processing time.

A.text: Track customer time spent entering and correcting information, the number of resubmissions, and the final completion rate for the same applications.
A.explanation: This measures the added burden together with the final outcome.

B.text: Measure the generation time for AI-provided drafts only for applications with short completion times.
B.explanation: This excludes difficult applications and does not capture the actual burden on customers.

C.text: Count the types of forms provided to customers and assume that more options mean greater convenience.
C.explanation: The number of options does not measure the burden of data entry or rework.

D.text: Measure only reviewers' time savings as a monetary amount.
D.explanation: This does not measure the impact on customers.

aib-c01-d2-069@1.title: Do not count a change in review criteria as an AI benefit
aib-c01-d2-069@1.prompt: Before AI was introduced, internal summaries were judged verbally as good or poor. After introduction, a different reviewer plans to score them against a five-point rubric. What should be done first to make the quality change comparable?

learning.reason: Define a shared scoring rubric and evaluate representative outputs from before and after introduction using the same method. Calibrate reviewers by aligning their judgments on examples.
learning.concept: Use the same quality criteria and a calibrated review method from the outset to avoid differences caused by the rubric.

A.text: Start evaluating only after introduction and treat the average score on the start date as the prior state.
A.explanation: There is no pre-introduction baseline for comparison.

B.text: Create a shared rubric, calibrate the reviewers, and compare representative summaries from before and after introduction under the same conditions.
B.explanation: This distinguishes a change in evaluation method from a change in quality.

C.text: Use text length before introduction and accuracy scores afterward, then compare the changes as if they were on the same scale.
C.explanation: These measure different properties.

D.text: Mechanically convert the pre-introduction good/poor judgments to scores of 5/1 and assume they correspond to the new rubric.
D.explanation: This does not establish that the actual quality and scoring conditions are equivalent.

aib-c01-d2-070@1.title: Calculate the payback time when benefits start later
aib-c01-d2-070@1.prompt: An AI-assisted service costs ¥900,000 to introduce. Its net benefit after operating costs is ¥0 in each of months 1 and 2, then ¥150,000 per month starting in month 3. Benefits are recorded at month-end, and there are no other cash flows. At the end of which month is the initial cost first recovered?

learning.reason: The required positive benefits total ¥900,000, or 6 months at ¥150,000 per month. Since there are no benefits in the first two months, payback occurs at the end of month 8.
learning.concept: Include the period before net benefits become steady, and find the month when cumulative benefits reach the initial cost.

A.text: At the end of month 9. Wait until the month after benefits first equal the initial cost.
A.explanation: The initial cost is first recovered at the end of month 8, when cumulative benefits equal the cost.

B.text: At the end of month 6. Use only the price and the steady-state monthly benefit.
B.explanation: This omits the first two months, when there are no benefits.

C.text: At the end of month 8. Six monthly benefits from month 3 through month 8 total ¥900,000.
C.explanation: This reflects the actual benefit start date and cumulative amount.

D.text: At the end of month 7. Assume benefits begin in month 2.
D.explanation: The benefit in month 2 is ¥0.

aib-c01-d2-071@1.title: Use recommendation follow-through as a leading indicator
aib-c01-d2-071@1.prompt: A maintenance support AI suggests inspection candidates, but an inspection cannot actually be performed if the required parts are unavailable. It will take several months to determine whether failures have decreased. Which leading indicator should be used to improve operations next month?

learning.reason: Track how many reviewed recommendations can be acted on within the allowed period, as well as reasons—such as unavailable parts—that prevent action.
learning.concept: Observe follow-through and reasons for inaction early; simply viewing a recommendation does not show whether it was carried out.

A.text: Only the readability rating of the recommendation text.
A.explanation: It does not measure physical constraints that can prevent an inspection.

B.text: The total disposal cost of all equipment next year.
B.explanation: It will not be available in time for next month's operational decisions.

C.text: The share of recommendations judged valid that are acted on by the specified deadline, along with reasons they were not acted on.
C.explanation: It measures the action needed after a recommendation.

D.text: The total number of times recommendations are displayed in a day.
D.explanation: It does not measure whether they are acted on.

aib-c01-d2-072@1.title: Reduce costs for queued requests that no longer deliver value
aib-c01-d2-072@1.prompt: Sales copy is generated sequentially after requests are received. While waiting, a sales representative may cancel a request, but the current system continues generating copy for every request. Validation found that canceled jobs accounted for 20% of usage-based costs. What is the appropriate action?

learning.reason: Check each request’s status when processing is about to begin, and exclude canceled or expired requests. Measure latency and cost for work that is still needed.
learning.concept: Recheck a request’s status before processing to prevent work that has been withdrawn or whose deadline has passed.

A.text: Move all requests to a larger model to improve the accuracy of the generated copy, and leave cancellation handling unchanged.
A.explanation: This does not reduce usage-based costs that deliver no value.

B.text: Remove the cancel button from the interface and continue counting the monthly number of generated items as before.
B.explanation: There would be no way to stop jobs that are no longer needed.

C.text: Process only half of all requests and leave the rest unrecorded to reduce the monthly budget by the same proportion.
C.explanation: This would also eliminate necessary work and make it unclear which costs were reduced.

D.text: Check for cancellation or expiration immediately before processing, exclude those requests, and monitor the turnaround time and cost per completed valid request.
D.explanation: This reduces wasteful generation while tracking the quality of the work that proceeds.

aib-c01-d3-041@1.title: Restrict the use of information needed for fairness testing
aib-c01-d3-041@1.prompt: The contact information provided by a consultation AI does not need to use a user's age band. Auditors, however, need to check whether incorrect guidance is disproportionately distributed across age bands. Collection is approved solely for auditing, and access to personally identifiable information can be restricted. Which design is appropriate?

learning.reason: Do not add an attribute that is unnecessary for ordinary inference. Link it to the audit only under the approved time limits and access controls, and report aggregated results.
learning.concept: Separate protected attributes from inference inputs and handle them only for an approved fairness audit.

A.text: Keep the data separate from inference, let a limited number of audit staff use it within a defined scope for evaluation, and report aggregated results.
A.explanation: This makes it possible to check group-specific errors while limiting unnecessary use of the data.

B.text: Because age bands are used for fairness testing, send them with every inference request and let the provider reuse them freely.
B.explanation: Approval for auditing does not authorize use for inference or secondary purposes.

C.text: Remove age bands from all operations and assume that incorrect guidance is equally distributed across groups.
C.explanation: This eliminates a direct way to check fairness.

D.text: Keep age bands only for users who received correct guidance, and exclude records of incorrect guidance from the audit.
D.explanation: This removes the failure cases needed to detect bias.

aib-c01-d3-042@1.title: Assess whether a cost-saving measure could lead to unfair decisions
aib-c01-d3-042@1.prompt: An internal AI system has compiled response times for individual employees. To reduce the work involved in performance reviews, management proposes automatically placing slower employees in a coaching program. In practice, more experienced employees handle more complex cases, and the relationship between response time and capability has not been validated. Which decision is appropriate?

learning.reason: Response time can inform process improvement, but its validity as a basis for individual evaluation has not been established. Reassess it using evidence that includes case difficulty and quality, with human review.
learning.concept: Before using a workload metric as a measure of individual capability, check differences in work conditions and the validity of the decision.

A.text: Put the proposal to automatically assess individuals by response time on hold; compare case difficulty, quality, and the purpose of the assessment, then define the appropriate scope of use and human review.
A.explanation: This considers both the efficiency gains and the validity of decisions that could disadvantage individuals.

B.text: Hide employees' names in the initial review, then automatically determine who needs coaching based on response time alone.
B.explanation: Anonymization does not make the metric more valid.

C.text: Treat evaluation against the same time threshold for everyone as fair, and exclude case difficulty.
C.explanation: Even an apparently uniform standard can produce results affected by differences in work assignments.

D.text: Because meeting operational targets takes priority, start evaluations and assess validity afterward based only on the number of appeals.
D.explanation: This makes potentially incorrect individual assessments before validating the metric.

aib-c01-d3-043@1.title: Identify affected people before finalizing requirements
aib-c01-d3-043@1.prompt: A proposal would use AI for phone guidance after a branch closes. Management and development have drafted the request, but the requirements of people who speak other languages, family members who complete procedures on someone else's behalf, and staff who take over when a call is handed off to a person have not been confirmed. What should happen before the design review?

learning.reason: Investigate the circumstances of affected people and operators, then include conditions that make the system unusable and safe alternatives in the requirements and acceptance criteria.
learning.concept: Early in design, distinguish the impacts on direct users, people affected by decisions, and operators, then use those impacts to set failure criteria.

A.text: During the pilot, consult only people who are most likely to use automated responses; study other users after the official launch.
A.explanation: This leaves conditions that could disadvantage some users untested.

B.text: Treat management's call-volume target as the requirement of all stakeholders, and exclude staff needs from the pilot.
B.explanation: This fails to identify the needs of people directly affected and those responsible for handling alternatives.

C.text: Identify stakeholder representatives and the effects of failures, then include alternative paths and evaluation criteria in the requirements and pilot.
C.explanation: This allows user difficulties to shape the design before selecting a model or delivery method.

D.text: Recruit participants after development is complete, and consider alternatives for people who cannot use the system during maintenance.
D.explanation: This fails to incorporate impacts and needs into the initial design.

aib-c01-d3-044@1.title: Verify that approvers have the skills needed to make a decision
aib-c01-d3-044@1.prompt: AI generates guidance about loan terms in multiple languages. The current approval screen allows staff to send the guidance even if they cannot understand the source language. In a pilot, a repayment term was mistranslated into another language, and general staff did not notice. Choose two measures that would make human oversight effective.

learning.reason: Assign cases to staff who can check both the language and the subject matter. If qualified staff are unavailable, hold the message and route the case to a verified channel.
learning.concept: An approval setting is not effective oversight unless the reviewer has the relevant language and subject-matter skills.

A.text: To avoid the time needed to find a fluent reviewer, send the guidance after checking only formal conditions such as numbers and terminology.
A.explanation: The meaning may be mistranslated even when the numbers are correct.

B.text: If a staff member clicked Approve in the screen, do not record whether they understood the language.
B.explanation: Counting approval actions does not establish that the content can be reviewed.

C.text: Route the guidance to a staff member who can review its language and repayment terms, and assign them responsibility for judging and approving mistranslations.
C.explanation: This provides the language proficiency and subject-matter knowledge needed to evaluate the result.

D.text: If no staff member with the required skills is available, hold the unverified translation and route the customer to a confirmed human guidance channel or another verified option.
D.explanation: Even when qualified staff are unavailable, customers can receive support without being shown unverified content.

E.text: Translate the guidance again with the same AI that produced it, and treat matching text as equivalent to human approval.
E.explanation: The same model may repeat the mistranslation, so this does not replace expert judgment.

aib-c01-d3-045@1.title: Clarifying central standards and local accountability for use
aib-c01-d3-045@1.prompt: The group’s AI committee sets common prohibitions. Each company knows its users and operations best. The companies plan to use the same AI for different business purposes, and each assumes that if the model is approved centrally, the business decisions are also the central team’s responsibility. How should responsibilities be organized?

learning.reason: The central team owns minimum standards and reviews of high-impact cases; each company’s business owner oversees its own use and residual risk. Make the boundaries and escalation criteria clear.
learning.concept: Do not mistake central review for the final business decision. Separate common standards from responsibility for specific business risks.

A.text: Do not assign operational responsibility within the organization; if a problem occurs, convene whoever paid for the deployment.
A.explanation: This delays incident decisions and corrective action.

B.text: Prioritize each company’s discretion and do not apply common prohibitions or exception reporting.
B.explanation: The group’s minimum standards would not be consistent.

C.text: Set central minimum standards and review criteria, while the business owner for each use case takes responsibility for acceptable business use, oversight, and remediation.
C.explanation: This balances common controls with accountability for actual operations.

D.text: Treat a centrally approved model as approved for every use across all companies, and make the provider responsible for operational problems.
D.explanation: This leaves out use-case decisions and local accountability.

aib-c01-d3-046@1.title: Reflecting changed obligations in products and operations
