aib-c01-d3-046@1.prompt: An internal advertising operations policy now requires disclosure and an approval record whenever an AI-generated image is released externally. The existing generation feature can be published without checking either requirement. What is needed to implement the change?

learning.reason: Identify the affected business processes and exceptions, assign responsibility for disclosure and approval, and verify that compliance is recorded and retained before enabling the change.
learning.concept: Go beyond maintaining a static approval document: translate new requirements into owners, checks, and evidence of compliance.

A.text: Identify the affected uses, require disclosure and approval before release, and assign an owner to verify and record compliance.
A.explanation: This connects the policy to actual operations and evidence.

B.text: Share a link to the new policy and leave the release process and evidence to each individual.
B.explanation: There would be no reliable way to confirm that the obligation was consistently met.

C.text: Change only the contract for using the generation model and exempt the existing release feature from the formal procedure.
C.explanation: The new requirement would not apply to the affected release path.

D.text: Measure image-generation accuracy periodically and check the site disclosure and approval record only if accuracy declines.
D.explanation: The policy requirements and image quality are separate matters.

aib-c01-d3-047@1.title: Varying action permissions by user responsibilities, even with the same AI
aib-c01-d3-047@1.prompt: An internal facilities AI can look up past repair information, but only administrators can confirm a repair date. Requests are submitted through the same interface. A regular employee must not be able to update a record just by writing “I am an administrator” in a message. Choose TWO measures.

learning.reason: Handle lookup and updates with separate permissions, and check the authenticated user’s role and target before processing an update. Do not derive roles from input text.
learning.concept: Separate read access from record changes and enforce access on the server based on the authenticated user’s role.

A.text: Give every user the same update permissions and merely hide the administrator icon in the interface.
A.explanation: The interface cannot restrict backend action permissions.

B.text: Separate lookup and update operations, and limit update permissions and the facilities they apply to by role.
B.explanation: This lets you manage the impact of reads and state changes separately.

C.text: Allow an update if a regular employee claims to be an administrator, then check it in the next day’s report.
C.explanation: A self-assertion cannot establish authorization.

D.text: Before confirming an update, have the receiving process check the authenticated user’s current role and permission for the target.
D.explanation: This keeps the model’s input text separate from authorization of the action.

E.text: Instruct the model to “allow administrators only” and do not check authorization in the system that performs the action.
E.explanation: This relies on generated text to make an authorization decision.

aib-c01-d3-048@1.title: Reassessing risk when scale and operational dependence change
aib-c01-d3-048@1.prompt: An administrative summarization AI was classified as low risk because only a small number of volunteers used it optionally. There is now a proposal to require it for case handoffs by all employees and eliminate the alternative procedure. The generation feature would not change. What should be evaluated when reviewing its classification?

learning.reason: A broader rollout and loss of an alternative can increase the impact of errors or outages. Reconsider the classification and controls using scale, dependent processes, and recovery capability.
learning.concept: Do not extrapolate the low impact of a pilot to a company-wide deployment. Reassess outage and recovery risks as dependence increases.

A.text: Determine risk only by comparing with the original pilot group size, without examining dependence on critical business processes.
A.explanation: User count alone does not capture the severity of business disruption.

B.text: Reassess risk by considering the number of users, alternative paths, dependence on critical handoffs, and recovery conditions, then add controls as needed.
B.explanation: This reflects the impact of the proposed expansion in the risk assessment.

C.text: Assume that increasing the number of users will improve model accuracy, and keep the low-risk classification.
C.explanation: Usage volume is not the same as improved accuracy, and this does not address the impact of an outage.

D.text: Assume that user count and operational dependence do not affect risk as long as the feature remains the same.
D.explanation: The impact of an outage and users’ ability to choose another process would change.

aib-c01-d3-049@1.title: Alert when the monitoring data itself stops
aib-c01-d3-049@1.prompt: Critical AI misguidance is aggregated hourly. One day, the quality metric showed zero incidents, but the records had not actually reached the monitoring aggregation pipeline. What should be monitored alongside critical misguidance?

learning.reason: Independently monitor the difference between business-side processing counts and the number of records received for monitoring, the last-arrival time, and the missing-data rate, and alert when data has not been observed.
learning.concept: Distinguish zero incidents from an inability to observe them, and independently verify that monitoring inputs arrive and remain fresh.

A.text: Replace the metric with a rate that excludes periods with no records, and omit those periods from reports.
A.explanation: This hides the time during which risk could not be assessed.

B.text: Add no monitoring; if there are zero misguidance incidents, report that processing was correct.
B.explanation: This confuses lack of observation with an actual zero.

C.text: Periodically check only whether the monitoring dashboard responds.
C.explanation: The dashboard can open even when measurement data is not arriving.

D.text: Reconcile processing activity with the monitoring-side arrival count and freshness, and alert on missing or delayed data separately from zero quality incidents.
D.explanation: This detects a monitoring outage so the actual situation can be checked.

aib-c01-d3-050@1.title: Check whether an attribute used indirectly appears in another feature
aib-c01-d3-050@1.prompt: A job-recommendation ranking model does not take applicants’ origin information as input. After training, however, a concern is raised that applicants with the same qualifications and track record receive different rankings depending on the ZIP code used. How should the cause of this bias be investigated during operation?

learning.reason: Use records or test cases with the same business conditions, such as qualifications and track record, to assess whether rankings depend excessively on changes in ZIP code.
learning.concept: Measure differences under the same business conditions for features that may represent attributes unrelated to the decision.

A.text: Conclude that proxy features cannot have an effect because origin information is not an input.
A.explanation: Other features may correlate with differences between groups.

B.text: Investigate the effect of ZIP code using comparisons and test cases that hold business conditions constant; if the dependency is unnecessary, revise the inputs and track the change.
B.explanation: This makes it possible to assess both the proxy feature and the effect of correcting it.

C.text: Give all applicants with different ZIP codes the same ranking, without evaluating valid differences in qualifications.
C.explanation: This loses necessary selection information without identifying the cause of the problem.

D.text: Compare only applicant counts across all users to assess the relationship between ZIP code and outcomes, without controlling for qualifications or track record.
D.explanation: This makes it difficult to separate the effects of different business conditions and features.

aib-c01-d3-051@1.title: Separate review of harmful source text from its redistribution
aib-c01-d3-051@1.prompt: Moderation staff use AI to summarize the key points of reported conversations. Investigators need the original text, but a company-wide report needs only the circumstances and classifications. The AI carelessly reproduces derogatory language in reports. What is the best change?

learning.reason: Preserve evidence for investigators with access restricted by authorization and purpose, and use classifications and necessary key points in reports. Before publication, check that harmful source text has not been reproduced.
learning.concept: Restrict access as needed for investigations while reducing the re-exposure of harmful content in outputs.

A.text: Show the original text only to authorized investigators; limit the company-wide version to classifications and necessary key points, and review the output.
A.explanation: This preserves evidence while preventing unnecessary re-exposure.

B.text: Add a warning to the company-wide text, but leave its content and audience unchanged.
B.explanation: A warning alone does not prevent unnecessary redistribution.

C.text: Permanently delete words classified as harmful from the original records and prevent auditors from reviewing them.
C.explanation: This loses necessary evidence and makes it impossible to check whether the classification was correct.

D.text: Include every reported case in company-wide reports using the original wording, and remove only personal names.
D.explanation: Removing names does not stop harmful language from being redistributed.

aib-c01-d3-052@1.title: Prevent out-of-scope inputs from becoming processing errors
aib-c01-d3-052@1.prompt: An expense-statement AI processes predefined formats accurately, but it has been found to be unable to distinguish taxes from discounts in a new format from an overseas subsidiary. The interface accepts both as valid numeric inputs. Choose two measures to prevent incorrect entries in production.

learning.reason: Identify evaluated input conditions at the entry point and route out-of-scope cases to a manual or otherwise validated path. Measure how often new formats occur and how they are corrected, then expand coverage after independent evaluation.
learning.concept: Make out-of-scope conditions explicit, validate whether they can be processed, and route them appropriately.

A.text: Set all taxes and discounts to zero for unknown formats to reduce incorrect entries.
A.explanation: This produces amounts that are wrong even for valid documents.

B.text: Permanently exclude all overseas locations, and do not add formats or reassess quality.
B.explanation: This eliminates any path to reassess the problematic scope through validation.

C.text: Collect the results of manual reviews and data on how often the format occurs; add it to the supported scope only after it passes independent testing for overseas formats.
C.explanation: This bases changes to the scope on evidence from the operating environment.

D.text: Register the output regardless of format as long as it has a numeric data type.
D.explanation: A structural check alone cannot reveal a misunderstanding of meaning.

E.text: Identify supported formats at the entry point, and hold automatic registration for new or indeterminate formats.
E.explanation: This keeps unevaluated inputs out of the production workflow.

aib-c01-d3-053@1.title: Make limitations visible where people use AI decisions
aib-c01-d3-053@1.prompt: An AI system that helps adjust facility temperatures has been validated in equipment used under normal conditions. It has not been evaluated for specialized equipment, but the difference in conditions is described only in a lengthy design document on a separate page. Which change would improve transparency?

learning.reason: When a recommendation is used, briefly show the applicable conditions, examples outside the evaluated scope, and the steps for human review. Check in actual workflows whether users can understand the information and make an informed decision.
learning.concept: Communicate the intended use, uses to avoid, and validation steps where decisions are made instead of leaving them buried in technical documentation.

A.text: Display only the generation probability and do not state the conditions under which the system can be used.
A.explanation: A number alone does not show the scope of the evaluation.

B.text: Show the applicable conditions, note that specialized equipment requires review, and provide an alternative procedure next to the recommendation.
B.explanation: Users can see the limitations they need to make a decision at the point of use.

C.text: Because the information has already been published, remove the link from the user interface to the design document as well.
C.explanation: Users would have difficulty understanding the limitations when making a decision.

D.text: Include examples involving specialized equipment in the instructions for normal operation without distinguishing whether they were evaluated.
D.explanation: Users could mistake the scope that was actually evaluated.

aib-c01-d3-054@1.title: Reconcile routine deletion with a case-specific preservation hold
aib-c01-d3-054@1.prompt: Records from a consultation AI are normally deleted after 90 days. An auditor has formally directed that one specific record be preserved until the investigation is complete. All other records must remain subject to the normal deletion conditions. How should the records be managed?

learning.reason: Specify the record, duration, and responsible person, preserve that record, and continue deleting routine records as scheduled. Record the release and handling decision when the hold ends.
learning.concept: When an exception to retention is needed, limit it to the specified records and document decisions about normal retention periods and evidence preservation.

A.text: Delete all records as scheduled, then have the AI regenerate the content of the record for the audit.
A.explanation: This does not preserve the actual record from the time of the consultation.

B.text: Copy the preserved record into shared meeting materials without defining who can access the copy or how it will be deleted.
B.explanation: Access and handling after preservation are not controlled.

C.text: Because an audit has been scheduled, permanently retain all records for all users as an exception.
C.explanation: This exceeds the scope of the specific instruction and conflicts with the normal retention conditions.

D.text: Preserve only the specified record and document the authorization, reason, and release decision. Continue managing the retention period for all other records as usual.
D.explanation: This preserves the necessary evidence while maintaining normal handling of other data.

aib-c01-d3-055@1.title: Do not require unnecessary personal data as a condition of applying
aib-c01-d3-055@1.prompt: An application guide for members can provide accurate basic guidance using only eligibility and region. To increase click-through rates, a staff member wants to make details about family and health mandatory. The rules require basic guidance to remain available to people who do not opt into optional personalization. Which policy is appropriate?

learning.reason: Provide basic guidance using a small set of necessary information. If additional information is used, make its purpose and optional nature clear, and verify that the basic path remains available.
learning.concept: Separate business goals for recommendation accuracy from whether data is mandatory, and preserve the basic service for people who decline optional personalization.

A.text: Require detailed information from everyone if it increases click-through rates, and withhold guidance from people who do not respond.
A.explanation: This fails to meet the requirements for providing basic guidance and collecting only necessary information.

B.text: Assume that detailed fields may be required of everyone if responses are anonymous, and do not distinguish basic guidance from optional personalization.
B.explanation: This does not consider whether the information is necessary or whether users have a choice.

C.text: Provide basic guidance using the minimum necessary fields, and make personalization using additional information an optional choice with a clear purpose.
C.explanation: This preserves users' choice while allowing the benefits of personalization to be evaluated.

D.text: First collect detailed information from everyone, and review unnecessary fields only if users later ask for them to be deleted.
D.explanation: This collects unnecessary data up front and obstructs users' choice when applying.

aib-c01-d3-056@1.title: Enable operators to stop an incorrect plan
aib-c01-d3-056@1.prompt: An internal AI automatically updates a maintenance schedule. A supervisor can review the plan, but if work is assigned to equipment that is already scheduled for construction, the assignment cannot be changed until the next day. Which human-oversight capability is missing?

learning.reason: A supervisor must be able to immediately hold an incorrect assignment and switch to human planning. Record the action and its basis so the original decision can also be reviewed.
learning.concept: Human oversight must allow authorized operators to stop a process after an incorrect decision and switch to an alternative, not merely observe it.

A.text: Display a lengthy explanation for the assignment, but let the schedule be finalized automatically even when it violates a constraint.
A.explanation: Displaying a reason is different from having the authority to change the assignment.

B.text: Allow an authorized operator to immediately hold or correct the assignment and return to manual planning, while recording the reason.
B.explanation: This enables intervention and explanation before the schedule is carried out.

C.text: Share the number of incorrect assignments in a weekly report and let operators only submit feedback about the AI.
C.explanation: People cannot actually stop or correct the plan.

D.text: Show the schedule earlier, but wait until the next batch run to change an incorrect assignment.
D.explanation: Even if people can review it, they cannot make the correction needed that day.

aib-c01-d3-057@1.title: Preventing Cross-Customer Mixing of Derived Information in a Shared AI Platform
aib-c01-d3-057@1.prompt: Multiple customer organizations use the same AI platform. Their source materials are separated by customer, but the storage key for a shared area that reuses past answers consists only of the question text. Choose two measures to prevent one customer’s data from being returned to another customer.

learning.reason: Scope reused results by customer and permission. Check current permissions for stored results and exports, and stop the corresponding reuse if the source material becomes unavailable.
learning.concept: Separate the storage locations for generated results and each company’s access permissions, in addition to separating source materials.

A.text: Separate reused results by customer organization and permitted scope, and do not retrieve results belonging to another customer.
A.explanation: This prevents another organization’s result from being used by mistake when the question text is the same.

B.text: Check current permissions when retrieving answers or exports, and handle invalidation if permission to the source information is withdrawn.
B.explanation: This preserves the same controls when conditions change after data has been stored.

C.text: When two companies ask the same question, distribute the answer created first regardless of the company.
C.explanation: This does not preserve company-specific materials and permissions.

D.text: Because the companies were separated when materials were ingested, allow stored answers to be returned without identifying the company.
D.explanation: Reuse or output can bypass the separation applied to the source materials.

E.text: Share question reuse across all companies and redact only company names in the answers.
E.explanation: Information about another company may remain in the body of the answer.

aib-c01-d3-058@1.title: Making AI Operations Independently Verifiable
aib-c01-d3-058@1.prompt: The department operating an AI system reports each period that its controls are working. The executive committee requires another person to verify that the reported procedures were carried out in practice. Which accountability design is appropriate?

learning.reason: Keep operational responsibility with the business unit, and give the independent assurance role access to review the necessary evidence and authority to report the results to executives.
learning.concept: Separate the operational role that builds and runs the system from the independent role that reviews evidence and reports findings.

A.text: Have operators approve their own review results and use verbal reports to their manager instead of evidence.
A.explanation: There is no independent verification or traceable evidence.

B.text: Have an independent reviewer change the model each month and then have the person who made the changes review the process.
B.explanation: The reviewer makes changes directly and cannot avoid self-assessment.

C.text: Receive a report from the business owner only when a control has failed.
C.explanation: This does not independently verify the claim that controls are working.

D.text: Leave operations to the business unit, while an independent reviewer with limited access samples evidence and reports to executives with remediation deadlines.
D.explanation: This combines separation of duties with verification of actual operations.

aib-c01-d3-059@1.title: Preventing Excessive Reproduction Even When Reference Is Permitted
aib-c01-d3-059@1.prompt: A training assistant AI may search course materials under a contract and direct users to relevant chapters. Redistributing the body text to users is prohibited, but a prototype returned long, continuous passages in response to questions. Choose two measures to prevent recurrence.

learning.reason: Define the output scope for directing users to sources, and detect and reject or review long, continuous extractions. Leave delivery of the original text to an existing authorized channel.
learning.concept: When reference and redistribution rights differ, set quotation limits for outputs and review suspicious examples.

A.text: Because searching is permitted, remove restrictions on the extent of quotations in answers.
A.explanation: Permission to search is different from permission to redistribute the body text.

B.text: Assume that returning the text to users is not redistribution if the generated result is first stored in a separate internal file.
B.explanation: Changing where it is stored does not change the fact that it is distributed to users.

C.text: Assume that unlimited reproduction is allowed if the author is credited, without checking length or terms of use.
C.explanation: Attribution does not remove a prohibition on redistribution.

D.text: During pre-release testing and operation, detect long matches, hold suspicious results, and check the scope of the contract.
D.explanation: This verifies whether the design that withholds such content works in practice.

E.text: Direct users to references for relevant passages, and limit requests to return continuous body text to the permitted scope.
E.explanation: This provides the necessary guidance within the terms of the contract.

aib-c01-d3-060@1.title: Investigating Reliability Issues When Rephrasing Changes the Conclusion
aib-c01-d3-060@1.prompt: An AI assistant that explains membership rules sometimes gives contradictory conclusions for the same application eligibility when asked, “Can I use this?” versus “Would I be ineligible?” The source document version was the same. Which response is appropriate?

learning.reason: Compare conclusions across different phrasings of the same conditions. When they do not align with one another or the evidence, route the case for review and test again.
learning.concept: Evaluate contradictions caused by wording differences when equivalent inputs use the same evidence.

A.text: Treat the policy conclusions as consistent as long as response times are the same for every question.
A.explanation: Response time and consistency of conclusions are separate matters.

B.text: Make every response the same length and conclude that the conclusions will therefore be the same.
B.explanation: Equalizing length does not guarantee consistency of content.

C.text: Create paraphrases that ask about the same business conditions, evaluate consistency of evidence and conclusions, and test how to hold inconsistent results for review.
C.explanation: This measures whether changes in input phrasing alone produce different decisions.

D.text: Test only the first question phrasing as a standard example and exclude errors from other phrasings from the metrics.
D.explanation: This removes the reported issue from the scope of testing.

aib-c01-d4-041@1.title: Assessing operational readiness under actual working conditions
aib-c01-d4-041@1.prompt: The delivery AI meets the required accuracy and budget, but staffing shifts are planned at two sites around the launch date. The department that helps configure user permissions also has limited availability. Leadership wants to determine which sites can go live. What is the most appropriate way to assess readiness?

learning.reason: Use actual work schedules to check staffing, shift coverage, skills, permissions, and communication at each site, and address any essential gaps first.
learning.concept: Compare working hours, responsibilities, technical dependencies, and management decisions against the actual plan.

A.text: Make going live without support a completion criterion, then investigate departments that run into problems after launch.
A.explanation: This does not address known readiness gaps before launch.

B.text: At each site, compare actual schedules and shift coverage, skills, permissions, and support-department availability, then determine which sites are ready to operate.
B.explanation: This assesses the trial’s success alongside the conditions needed to sustain operations.

C.text: Decide based on average accuracy and the company-wide budget, without checking the staffing needs of individual sites.
C.explanation: This does not confirm the conditions each department needs for operations.

D.text: Assume every site can begin operations based only on the number of users who have already opened the AI interface.
D.explanation: This does not measure day-to-day staffing or access readiness.

aib-c01-d4-042@1.title: Separating user count from production operating maturity
aib-c01-d4-042@1.prompt: Company A has 500 participants in a free trial, but has not defined operating standards or formal owners. Company B has 40 intended users, but has assigned owners and monitoring as part of its workflow and operates a process for handling issues. Which description is appropriate when comparing their maturity?

learning.reason: Do not determine a stage by user count. Evidence of production launch is that routine service delivery, ownership, and monitoring are in place.
learning.concept: A large experiment does not reach the operational stage without responsibility and controls for day-to-day service delivery.

A.text: Place both companies at the same stage because both can use AI, regardless of whether they have formal operational responsibilities.
A.explanation: This does not reflect differences in their ability to sustain the actual service.

B.text: Consider A more mature in all cases because B needed to handle issues, even though A has not launched a production service.
B.explanation: This mistakes the presence of incident-handling capability for lower maturity.

C.text: Treat A as a large-scale experiment and B as a limited production launch; separately verify evidence of shared operations before deciding whether B can scale company-wide.
C.explanation: This distinguishes the scale of an experiment, formal service delivery, and organization-wide expansion.

D.text: Consider A ready for company-wide deployment based on its user count, and classify B as an experiment because it has fewer users.
D.explanation: This uses headcount to judge operational capability.

aib-c01-d4-043@1.title: Identifying a gap in expertise for evaluating specialist judgments
aib-c01-d4-043@1.prompt: AI classifies reports of equipment accidents. Engineers can calculate metrics, and the operating procedures and infrastructure are in place, but the trial team has no safety specialist who can evaluate the grounds for classifying an accident as serious. Which capability should be added first?

learning.reason: Improved metrics alone do not establish that the classifications are valid. Include specialists in the evaluation and create reproducible criteria and examples.
learning.concept: Even when model capabilities and monitoring are in place, a separate skill set is needed to validate the correctness of business judgments.

A.text: Because accidents are infrequent, remove severity assessment and determine whether the system passes based only on screen responsiveness.
A.explanation: This fails to test an important business objective.

B.text: Increase the infrastructure’s processing capacity and rely on existing evaluation metrics to establish that the labels are valid.
B.explanation: Processing speed cannot establish whether a business judgment is sound.

C.text: Train engineers only to increase the number of classifications, and involve specialists after the service is formally launched.
C.explanation: This cannot establish the required correctness before launch.

D.text: Assign someone qualified to assess severity, and have the specialist and engineers establish criteria and evaluation examples.
D.explanation: This fills the missing capability for business validation.

aib-c01-d4-044@1.title: Prioritizing the capabilities needed for the next expansion
aib-c01-d4-044@1.prompt: A tourism company’s inquiry AI is in production for domestic users. Its next business goal is to support two foreign languages. Approved translation materials and staff who can evaluate correctness in both languages are lacking, while the inference infrastructure has spare capacity. Which investment priority is appropriate?

learning.reason: Develop materials and evaluation capability for the languages in scope, verify operational capability with the priority languages, and then proceed. Do not invest further in infrastructure that already has spare capacity before demand is established.
learning.concept: Identify the dependencies that constrain future expansion and invest in stages while retaining capabilities that are already useful.

A.text: Prioritize a technical upgrade by doubling infrastructure capacity, then check the materials’ accuracy through translation logs after launch.
A.explanation: This does not directly address the current gap.

B.text: Enable all languages at once and have customers report errors until staff can be hired.
B.explanation: This provides neither evaluation nor ownership before external release.

C.text: First prepare approved materials and evaluation capabilities for the priority languages, then verify quality and operations in a limited scope before moving on to the next language.
C.explanation: This allocates budget to the actual dependencies.

D.text: Stop domestic operations before planning language expansion, and do not carry forward the existing quality standards.
D.explanation: This discards existing strengths and does not prepare the additional languages.

aib-c01-d4-045@1.title: Check whether data is available to verify outcomes, even when input data is available
aib-c01-d4-045@1.prompt: A company plans to predict contract renewals. Contract details and support inquiry histories are available, but confirmed renewal records are controlled by a reseller, and it has not been agreed whether they can be used for training or evaluation. Which is the appropriate way to assess data readiness for the pilot?

learning.reason: Separate the conditions for using inputs from those for using confirmed outcomes. Check what may be used for each purpose and determine the scope in which the model can be evaluated against verified outcomes.
learning.concept: Assess access to features separately from legal and contractual access to outcome records for evaluation.

A.text: Confirm the permitted uses of the outcome records and how they can be linked with the reseller, then determine whether representative authorized examples can be used for training and evaluation.
A.explanation: This separates the availability of inputs from the conditions for matching them to outcomes.

B.text: Assume that confirmed outcomes for retained customers are available because there are enough inquiry records.
B.explanation: The number of input records does not substantiate contract renewal outcomes.

C.text: Put a model into operation without training and request permission for the first time after contracts expire.
C.explanation: There would be no basis for evaluating performance before deployment.

D.text: Assume that customers with long inquiries ended their contracts, and treat confirmed renewal records as unnecessary.
D.explanation: Inquiry length does not necessarily match the actual outcome.

aib-c01-d4-046@1.title: Agree with data providers on data freshness
aib-c01-d4-046@1.prompt: Several warehouses send shipment records for next-day forecasts. Previously, there was no agreed cutoff time, and one warehouse sent its data after the next day's forecast had already been produced. What should be added to the data-sharing agreement instead of blaming the people responsible?

learning.reason: Clarify the relevant time period, arrival deadline, response to delays or missing data, and each party's authority and responsibility with both the provider and the user.
learning.concept: Agree on data-sharing frequency, arrival times, and notifications for missing data rather than leaving quality solely to the consuming team.

A.text: Agree with the warehouses on each data cutoff, arrival deadline, owner, and the communication and actions required when data is late or missing.
A.explanation: This establishes a shared process for the required data freshness.

B.text: Rewrite the arrival time as the shipment event time and stop tracking the time provided by the source.
B.explanation: This distorts the event timeline and makes the cause impossible to trace.

C.text: Have the forecasting team infer when shared data is late without agreeing on handoff times with the providers.
C.explanation: This does not establish a process that ensures data arrives when needed.

D.text: Standardize only the names used by all warehouses, leaving differences in cutoff times unresolved.
D.explanation: Matching names does not ensure the data arrives in time for the next-day forecast.

aib-c01-d4-047@1.title: Assess whether the platform lets multiple teams experiment safely
aib-c01-d4-047@1.prompt: Twenty teams will experiment with AI at the same time inside the company. Sample data is available for the experiments, but production customer settings and data must not be touched. Inference capacity is shared, and in the past one department's experiment prevented other departments from using it. Choose two platform acceptance criteria.

learning.reason: Separate permissions and data for production and experiments, and set quotas and impact boundaries for each team. Verify that isolation works and the platform supports the required scale under concurrent use.
learning.concept: Validate isolation of experimental resources, peak load, and access to approved data.

A.text: Set quotas for each team and test with representative concurrent workloads that other teams and production are unaffected.
A.explanation: This checks resource controls and actual experimental capacity together.

B.text: Give every team unlimited quotas and administrative privileges for production preparation, and specify usage order in a document.
B.explanation: This does not provide effective isolation or resource controls.

C.text: Measure only the first team's processing speed and assume the same results will hold for all 20 teams.
C.explanation: This does not measure contention from concurrent use of shared capacity.

D.text: Share production to simplify experiment setup and rely on each person's memory to distinguish sample data from customer data.
D.explanation: This creates a risk of inadvertently changing production.

E.text: Create an area for experiments and use permissions to separate approved samples from operations on production settings and data.
E.explanation: This isolates the impact of experiments from production.

aib-c01-d4-048@1.title: Escalate unresolved adoption criteria between departments for an executive decision
aib-c01-d4-048@1.prompt: For an AI system that supports operational reviews, Sales wants cases received quickly, while Compliance wants every case to receive additional review. The on-the-ground champion has no authority to change either department's evaluation criteria, and the pilot has been stalled for three weeks. What should the sponsor do?

learning.reason: Organize the competing interests and requirements, then set criteria that balance quality and speed in line with business goals, define departmental responsibilities, and decide how exceptions will be handled. The champion can run the pilot on the ground.
learning.concept: A sponsor with shared goals and decision-making authority should resolve competing interests that the operational champion cannot.

A.text: Remove either Sales or Compliance from the pilot and assume the results can be reproduced across the organization.
A.explanation: This does not meet the original workflow requirement for both departments to work together.

B.text: Measure the model's quality score again and deploy it without setting departmental criteria if the score is high.
B.explanation: This does not resolve the conflict over business objectives and acceptable limits.

C.text: Have the champion schedule more meetings and wait for one department to voluntarily give up its goals.
C.explanation: This does not address the lack of authority to resolve competing interests.

D.text: Reconcile both departments' requirements, approve agreed pilot criteria, and communicate responsibilities and exception decisions to the teams.
D.explanation: This enables a cross-department decision and clarifies who is responsible for execution.

aib-c01-d4-049@1.title: Include outsourced operations in the cross-functional team’s responsibilities
aib-c01-d4-049@1.prompt: During a trial of an AI system for incident notifications, alerts from the field are sent to an external call center. Because the operations team was not consulted, it was unclear which company was responsible for alerts that went unnoticed. Which change should the cross-functional team make?

learning.reason: Include business, contract management, technical, and outsourced operations staff; define and exercise the handoff, who decides when an alert is not received, and each company’s responsibilities.
learning.concept: Do not make decisions based only on an internal design. Define roles for coordinating outsourced operations, contracts, and quality assessments.

A.text: Keep the contractor out of the design and ask them to include only the responsible person’s name in a report after an incident.
A.explanation: This does not define handoff conditions or responsibility for handling exceptions in advance.

B.text: Include leaders, contract managers, and technical staff from both companies in the trial of notification and receipt, and decide who will make decisions and by when if an alert is not received.
B.explanation: This design helps prevent responses from stalling at departmental or company boundaries.

C.text: Remove contract management and let each company’s operations staff decide the notification content and deadlines on the day.
C.explanation: This cannot maintain consistent responsibility assignments and deadlines.

D.text: Have in-house engineers check only that alerts are delivered, and exclude everything after receipt from the trial.
D.explanation: A process step that affects business outcomes would go untested.

aib-c01-d4-050@1.title: Communicate the work process and next review date when pausing a trial
aib-c01-d4-050@1.prompt: An AI-assisted data entry tool has produced unexpected errors, so the trial will be paused for one week for some cases. Staff must use another method to meet deadlines, and the restart date has not yet been decided. What is the appropriate way to communicate this?

learning.reason: State which cases are affected and when, provide the alternative procedure and a contact, and communicate the restart conditions and the date of the next update. Gather feedback from staff as well.
learning.concept: Change communications to staff should include the reason, scope of impact, alternative procedure, a way to provide feedback, and the next planned decision or update.

A.text: Identify the affected cases, the previous procedure, and who to contact, and communicate the restart conditions and the date of the next update.
A.explanation: This lets staff act immediately without promising that the trial will restart.

B.text: Do not explain why the trial is paused, and promise that it will definitely restart in one week.
B.explanation: This presents an undecided restart as certain.

C.text: Do not announce the change until users open the application screen; explain it individually only to those who run into trouble.
C.explanation: Staff cannot prepare an alternative procedure in advance.

D.text: Wait until the technical investigation is complete before notifying anyone, and leave each person to handle cases that cannot use the tool.
D.explanation: Staff would not have the information they need to keep deadline-driven work moving.

aib-c01-d4-051@1.title: Find out why staff are returning to informal procedures
aib-c01-d4-051@1.prompt: Use of an approved AI tool is low at a branch. In interviews, staff said that the tool cannot print forms they need at the start of a shift, so experienced employees have returned to an informal spreadsheet. What should be the first step to increase adoption?

learning.reason: Do not conclude that staff are resistant based only on usage. Find out what the spreadsheet actually enables them to do. Work with staff to prototype a printing workflow, then assess workload and safety.
learning.concept: Understand apparent resistance in terms of specific work constraints, then improve the functionality or procedure together with staff.

A.text: Exclude employees who are comfortable with spreadsheets from the study and report the usage rate only for the remaining employees.
A.explanation: This removes affected users from the figures without improving the conditions that are causing the problem.

B.text: Examine the printing workflow with staff, try an improvement that produces the same outcome through an approved procedure, and measure its impact on workload and adoption.
B.explanation: This addresses a specific reason staff are returning to an informal workaround.

C.text: Give a uniform warning to anyone who used the informal procedure, and do not investigate the obstacles with the approved method.
C.explanation: This does not provide an alternative that staff can continue to use.

D.text: Require employees to sign in to the AI tool at the start of each shift, and do not add printing functionality until usage increases.
D.explanation: The problem of being unable to produce the forms staff need would remain.

aib-c01-d4-052@1.title: Maintain skills needed to continue working when automation stops
aib-c01-d4-052@1.prompt: AI assistance with intake processing has left new employees with almost no opportunity to practice reviewing cases correctly by hand. Work agreements require the work to continue manually within two hours when the AI is unavailable. Which training plan should be used?

learning.reason: Regularly practice a fallback procedure using realistic examples, and verify that new employees can process cases independently within the required time.
learning.concept: Keep practicing and assessing steps that must continue during exceptions, even if they are no longer part of normal operations.

A.text: Train staff only to operate the AI buttons; have colleagues learn the manual procedure from one another after an outage occurs.
A.explanation: This does not show in advance that staff can process cases correctly within the required time.

B.text: Put manual procedure materials in a shared location, but do not practice finding or carrying out the procedure.
B.explanation: Having a procedure is not the same as being able to carry it out on time.

C.text: Regularly practice switching to the fallback procedure, and assess review accuracy, completion time, and the skills of backup staff.
C.explanation: This helps maintain the capabilities and continuity conditions that are actually required.

D.text: Because the AI has high availability, exclude the manual continuity requirement from the evaluation.
D.explanation: Availability does not satisfy the requirement to continue working during an outage.

aib-c01-d4-053@1.title: Design policy maintenance and routine search as separate capabilities
aib-c01-d4-053@1.prompt: In the contracts department, staff spend much of their time searching for approved materials. When contradictions are found between policies, Legal and Sales also need to discuss and resolve them. How should roles be designed after AI is introduced?

learning.reason: Use AI to search approved materials and provide supporting evidence. People should assess the impact of contradictions and formally update policies once agreement is reached.
learning.concept: Use AI to assist with finding authoritative materials, while people handle conflicting business policies and their formal updates.

A.text: Have people continue searching all materials as before, while AI changes only the wording of policies without referring to the discussion outcomes.
A.explanation: The search burden remains, and the agreed outcomes cannot be incorporated.

B.text: Have AI search for materials and then resolve contradictions and rewrite official policies on its own.
B.explanation: This makes organizational decisions and changes policy without review.

C.text: Have AI automatically prioritize whichever policy gets the most correct answers, and skip discussions between Legal and Sales.
C.explanation: Policy priority cannot be determined by usage frequency or answer accuracy.

D.text: Use AI to assist with routine searches for materials, while people reconcile contradictions across departments, approve changes, and revise policies.
D.explanation: This frees people to focus on policy decisions that require human judgment.

aib-c01-d4-054@1.title: Form the next hypothesis when a pilot produces unexpected results
aib-c01-d4-054@1.prompt: In a procurement AI pilot, errors increased with full automation. In the condition where the system only suggested candidates, staff maintained their accuracy while spending less time making decisions. The initial proposal assumed full automation. Which next step is appropriate?

learning.reason: Record that the automation hypothesis did not hold, then retest the impact of decision support in representative business tasks. Proceed toward launch only for the scope supported by sufficient evidence and conditions.
learning.concept: Revise the initial hypothesis based on observed results and design the next experiment around the benefits that have been demonstrated.

A.text: In response to the failure of full automation, discard all results from decision support too and do not record the cause.
A.explanation: This fails to learn from the range in which the pilot succeeded.

B.text: To stick to the original plan, treat full automation as having met the criteria and launch it.
B.explanation: This ignores the significant degradation observed in the experiment.

C.text: Launch both approaches at once based only on the time savings, and exclude differences in errors from evaluation.
C.explanation: This prevents quality from being assessed for two approaches with different assumptions.

D.text: Refocus the use case on decision support, set usage conditions and success criteria, and run a broader experiment.
D.explanation: This tests a different hypothesis derived from observed results.

aib-c01-d4-055@1.title: Choose what can be carried over from early results to another department
aib-c01-d4-055@1.prompt: Finance achieved early results with AI-generated document descriptions. HR wants similar assistance, but the intended uses, access needs, and consequences of errors for HR documents differ from those in Finance. How should the organization expand while building on its short-term results?

learning.reason: Carry over the evaluation, rollout, and training procedures from Finance’s success, while validating the intended use, data, and criteria for HR. Start with a small scope.
learning.concept: Reuse the evaluation methods and operations behind an early success, while checking the suitability of the business data and criteria in the new department.

A.text: Use the evaluation and operating methods that worked in Finance, and run a small pilot using HR’s approved materials, permissions, and business-specific acceptance criteria.
A.explanation: This reuses capabilities that can be carried over while testing the impact on the new business function.

B.text: Build everything independently for HR and do not share Finance’s evaluation materials or intermediate failures.
B.explanation: This discards reusable knowledge gained from early results.

C.text: Expand without testing correctness if HR reaches about the same usage volume as Finance.
C.explanation: Usage volume cannot demonstrate the quality and controls HR needs.

D.text: Copy the documents and access settings used in Finance to HR and launch on the assumption that quality will be the same.
D.explanation: This does not account for differences in use and permissions, so the success criteria cannot be carried over.

aib-c01-d4-056@1.title: Turn lessons from failures in each department into shared evaluation practices
aib-c01-d4-056@1.prompt: AI operations teams in each business unit correct errors independently. The same kinds of failures recur in other departments, but sensitive original records cannot be shared. What should the central specialist organization do?

learning.reason: Work with each department to use approved anonymized cases or synthesized representative examples, and define common failure patterns and checks. Share the results in a form that the relevant departments can reuse.
learning.concept: Have a specialist organization analyze cases across teams, generalize the lessons, and develop tests and decision criteria that other departments can use.

A.text: Distribute original records unchanged to all employees and ask each person to investigate what they want to find.
A.explanation: This discloses information that cannot be shared and does not establish an evaluation process.

B.text: Hold cross-functional reviews using approved representative cases, then make the shared causes, reproduction conditions, and checks available in a shareable form.
B.explanation: This enables other departments to prevent the same problems without broadly distributing sensitive records.

C.text: Keep corrections within each department and have the central team track only the total number of reports.
C.explanation: Other departments cannot learn from the same failures.

D.text: Assume errors will be resolved if every department uses the same provider, and do not investigate cases or run checks.
D.explanation: Standardizing the provider does not necessarily prevent similar errors in business processes.

aib-c01-d4-057@1.title: Check whether early gains continue
aib-c01-d4-057@1.prompt: During the first month of using an AI writing assistant, the enablement team provided daily support and work got faster. Support will decrease in month three. The owner wants to determine whether the improvement will last under normal working conditions. Which check is appropriate?

learning.reason: Track support levels, business outcomes, quality, and user challenges against the same criteria at multiple points after launch to assess results under normal operations.
learning.concept: Continue tracking outcomes and constraints after operations shift from a heavily supported launch period to normal operations.

A.text: Check only how many requests the support team handled, and stop measuring quality and task time after the first month.
A.explanation: This cannot assess work outcomes after support decreases.

B.text: Lock in the first month’s time savings and budget for later costs and outcomes at the same rate.
B.explanation: This confuses the effects of short-term support with steady-state results.

C.text: Continue measuring the same quality and task time after moving to normal operations, and also track usage, support levels, and adoption challenges.
C.explanation: This helps determine whether the results depend on the initial level of support.

D.text: In month three, ask only new users about satisfaction and exclude first-month users from the analysis.
D.explanation: This prevents comparison of continued improvement across the same group.

aib-c01-d4-058@1.title: Enable safe production updates to a prototype
aib-c01-d4-058@1.prompt: A prototype lets users change inference and search settings on the same screen. Its trial met quality criteria, but the settings used at the time were not saved, and there is no plan for where to revert if quality degrades. Select two conditions required to move to production operations.

learning.reason: Keep the evaluated model, materials, and settings as a version so the approved configuration can be reproduced. Also test in advance that the restored configuration can handle the business state.
learning.concept: Make reproducibility of the same version and the ability to restore a change while continuing business operations acceptance criteria.

A.text: Treat rollback as unnecessary, and do not save the latest settings if the average response is good that day.
A.explanation: This leaves the team unable to address performance degradation or inconsistencies.

B.text: Have operators make changes directly after launch, and reconstruct changes from memory only if a discrepancy occurs.
B.explanation: This does not track production changes or the previous state.

C.text: Rehearse rollback when criteria are not met, and verify that the restored version can handle existing business records.
C.explanation: This demonstrates both configuration recovery and business continuity.

D.text: Document the procedure, but wait until an incident occurs to check whether the old configuration can run.
D.explanation: This does not verify recovery capability before launch.

E.text: Save the model, index, prompt, and settings together as an evaluated version so the same configuration can be reproduced.
E.explanation: This makes it possible to identify and deploy an approved configuration.

aib-c01-d4-059@1.title: Check that the fallback path does not share the primary path’s failure
aib-c01-d4-059@1.prompt: Sales offices in three regions plan to rely on AI search. A backup screen is available, but its search and identity verification use exactly the same dependencies as the primary screen. They want to continue critical business operations even if the provider has an outage. What should they check before rollout?

learning.reason: Identify dependencies shared by the primary and backup paths, and rehearse whether the fallback can operate independently of those failures. Provide a manual path or a different dependency where needed.
learning.concept: Before rolling out to multiple departments, validate shared dependencies between primary and backup paths and verify that the fallback is effective.

A.text: Assume a failure of the primary path and test conditions in which the same dependencies are unavailable to the backup. Confirm an independent fallback that can keep the business operating.
A.explanation: A different screen alone does not protect against failures that affect both paths.

B.text: Measure only response time on the backup screen under normal conditions, without testing outage conditions.
B.explanation: This does not show whether operations can continue when the backup is needed.

C.text: Certify it as a backup because it opens at a different URL, without investigating dependencies for search or identity verification.
C.explanation: Even on a different screen, processing cannot continue if shared functions fail.

D.text: Verify only that the AI provider issues outage notifications, without creating a path for users to continue processing.
D.explanation: A notification is not a fallback that keeps business operations running.

aib-c01-d4-060@1.title: Verify the lineage of derived fields before adoption
aib-c01-d4-060@1.prompt: A proposal would use a department-created job classification table for an AI assistant that supports payroll inquiries. There are no missing values, but the rules mapping the table to the original HR data are undocumented, and departments created it differently. Which assessment of its readiness for use is appropriate?

learning.reason: Trace the data’s origin and transformation, and confirm its meaning and scope. Reconstruct from approved data any portion that cannot be checked against source materials or its creator.
learning.concept: Even when all values are populated, definitions and errors cannot be verified if it is unclear where and how the data was produced.

A.text: Have the AI infer how job titles were classified, and let no one verify whether the inferred process is correct.
A.explanation: A generated explanation does not prove the actual origin of the data.

B.text: Trace the source data and transformation rules, and compare classifications in a sample. Rebuild unsupported portions from approved materials.
B.explanation: This makes it possible to examine the actual definitions and identify errors.

C.text: Consider the data ready because there are no missing values, and copy the same field names across all tables.
C.explanation: This does not establish whether the intended meanings are consistent.

D.text: Treat the largest department’s method as authoritative and investigate differences from other departments only after launch.
D.explanation: The number of records does not determine whether a business definition is valid.

aib-c01-d1-064@1.title: Compare probabilities only over the same time period
aib-c01-d1-064@1.prompt: Equipment A at a company is predicted to have a 40% probability of failure within 30 days, while equipment B has a 25% probability within 7 days. The same maintenance team wants to choose which equipment to inspect first to prevent failures this week. How should they interpret these predictions?

learning.reason: Predictions with different time horizons cannot be compared as measures of risk over the same period. Align both predictions to the definition of this week before comparing them.
learning.concept: Align the event and time horizon when comparing probabilities.

A.text: Because 40% is greater than 25%, conclude that A is also more likely to fail this week.
A.explanation: The probabilities cover different periods: 30 days and 7 days.

B.text: Divide A's 40% into four equal parts and treat the result as this week's probability, without any other information.
B.explanation: The prompt does not say that failures are equally likely in each week.

C.text: Find the failure probability for the same 7-day period for both items, and also consider how much an inspection could mitigate the impact.
C.explanation: This makes the predictions comparable over the same period.

D.text: Treat model A's figure as a daily result and multiply it by 7 to compare the two.
D.explanation: This incorrectly treats a probability within 30 days as a per-day probability.

aib-c01-d1-065@1.title: Distinguish items found in documents from AI-generated inferences
aib-c01-d1-065@1.prompt: The general affairs department wants to record equipment IDs and expiration dates from contracts in a register. A different employee will review blank fields, so they must not be filled in by inference. Before recording a value, the employee must be able to open the source text at the location of the selected number. Which capability is appropriate?

learning.reason: Extract the requested fields from the source text and return them with their locations. Send missing or uncertain values for review.
learning.concept: Use extraction to map identifiers found in existing documents; do not generate information that is absent.

A.text: Extract the specified fields from the source text, retain their locations, and send fields with no match for human review.
A.explanation: The required values can be verified against their supporting text.

B.text: Summarize each contract by field and add a link to the entire document, without saving where each value was found.
B.explanation: This does not provide a reference to the specific passage needed to verify a value directly.

C.text: Learn from contract periods in the past, infer expiration dates, and treat the inferred values as if they appeared in the source text.
C.explanation: This fails to distinguish an inference from an extracted fact.

D.text: Classify documents into equipment or contract-period categories, then have an employee search a register for a value in a nearby category.
D.explanation: This provides neither the value stated in the contract nor a way to verify where it appears.

aib-c01-d1-066@1.title: Check combinations even when individual values are valid
aib-c01-d1-066@1.prompt: Records used to predict booking cancellations had valid dates for the booking date, cancellation confirmation date, and service start date. However, some cancellation confirmation dates were earlier than the booking dates, an order that is not possible in this business process. What should be corrected first?

learning.reason: Validate each date against business chronology as well as checking that the date itself is valid. Compare violations with the source records, and manage separately any records that cannot be corrected reliably.
learning.concept: Check relationships that are valid in practice in addition to the type of each individual field.

A.text: Add a chronological relationship to the data quality rules, then compare violations with the source records and correct or exclude them.
A.explanation: This addresses contradictions among values that type checks do not detect.

B.text: Convert every value to the same date format, and skip checking the order once the formats match.
B.explanation: Matching formats do not make the chronological order correct.

C.text: Sort the dates used as input without regard to their meanings, and save the earlier date as the booking date.
C.explanation: This changes the meaning without first checking which record is wrong.

D.text: Add the contradictory rows as correct training examples and measure only whether the deployed model can handle the anomalous order.
D.explanation: The quality of the business facts used for training is not established.

aib-c01-d1-067@1.title: Do not let existing customer history bias predictions for new customers
aib-c01-d1-067@1.prompt: A company wants to predict inquiries submitted just after a new contract begins. Its history contains similar initial records every time a company adds a branch. A random row split would leave the same companies in both the training and evaluation sets. The hiring decision is based on performance for a company the model has never seen. Which evaluation method is appropriate?

learning.reason: Split by company and evaluate on the initial records of companies excluded from training. Splitting rows by branch leaves the effects of company-specific patterns the model may have learned.
learning.concept: When assessing generalization to new customers, keep related history from the same customer out of both training and evaluation.

A.text: Split the data by company, and evaluate using only information available at the start for companies that were not in the training data.
A.explanation: This matches the conditions for generalization to new companies.

B.text: Remove company names and assume it is acceptable for branch data from the same company to appear in both sets.
B.explanation: Even without names, records can share company-specific patterns.

C.text: Validate using only companies included in training and assume the same accuracy will apply to unseen companies in the same industry.
C.explanation: This does not establish validity for companies the model has not seen before.

D.text: Split the branch rows into even smaller groups, ensuring that each set contains an equal share of rows from the same companies.
D.explanation: This does not reproduce evaluation on companies the model has not seen.

aib-c01-d1-068@1.title: Investigate whether the monitoring anomaly lies in the execution path rather than the model
aib-c01-d1-068@1.prompt: An AI scheduling assistant has seen an increase in failures per completed case. Accuracy is unchanged for cases that receive a response, but the dependent lookup function is taking longer. What should be done first?

learning.reason: Distinguish a change in quality from service unavailability. Investigate lookup latency and the cause of timeouts, then measure both metrics after recovery.
learning.concept: Separate timeouts from the quality of predictions that were returned correctly, and choose an update that addresses the cause.

A.text: Move all responses to a new model without comparing lookup latency before and after the change.
A.explanation: The problematic dependency would remain, so the effectiveness of the change could not be verified.

B.text: Separate cases with no response from incorrect answers, and investigate lookup latency and its dependencies. After recovery, check the completion rate and accuracy.
B.explanation: This distinguishes execution problems from prediction problems.

C.text: Since accuracy is unchanged, stop recording the issue without referring the change in completion rate to another team.
C.explanation: This leaves an increase in operational failures unaddressed.

D.text: Attribute the failure rate to insufficient training data and retrain the model without investigating the lookup process.
D.explanation: This would not resolve the cause of missing responses.

aib-c01-d1-069@1.title: Specify terminology for the intended audience
aib-c01-d1-069@1.prompt: Create a short guide to remote building inspections for residents using the service for the first time. Keep the official names of the installed devices accurate, and explain technical terms in plain language. A general request to “make it easy to understand” also leads to the official names being rephrased. What would improve the instructions?

learning.reason: State the audience and purpose, keep official names fixed, and briefly explain other technical terms. Include a good output example and conditions for checking terminology.
learning.concept: Along with general instructions, specify the audience, terms that need definitions, and official terminology that must not change.

A.text: Keep all wording as is and instruct the model only to reduce the word count.
A.explanation: This would not add the explanations first-time users need.

B.text: Rephrase every difficult term to the same degree, with no exceptions for official names.
B.explanation: This would replace names that must be preserved.

C.text: Specify that the guide is for first-time residents, identify the official names to preserve and the terms to explain, and include a short example.
C.explanation: This distinguishes what may be rephrased from the names that must remain unchanged.

D.text: Specify only that the guide should be in Japanese, and leave the audience and treatment of technical terms to the model.
D.explanation: The language alone does not convey the desired level of vocabulary or the names to preserve.

aib-c01-d1-070@1.title: Use an authoritative source for current values and generate explanations separately
aib-c01-d1-070@1.prompt: An AI assistant for employees must provide current inventory counts and explain what to consider when choosing an equivalent item. Inventory counts change frequently in an approved ledger, and the exact value must be displayed separately from the explanation. Which approach to adapting the model is appropriate?

learning.reason: Retrieve the authoritative value for the correct item ID from the inventory ledger and show it separately. Use the language model to help explain the information to users, not to estimate the number.
learning.concept: For exact numbers that change frequently, retrieve the current value each time instead of having a generative model estimate it.

A.text: Check only the number of digits and format of generated values, without comparing them with the ledger.
A.explanation: Even a correctly formatted value may not be an accurate inventory count.

B.text: Infer inventory counts from explanations previously written by staff and reduce access to the ledger.
B.explanation: This does not consult an authoritative source for frequently changing, exact values.

C.text: Retrieve and display the value for each item ID from the approved ledger, and generate the explanation of considerations from approved information.
C.explanation: Separating retrieval of authoritative values from text generation helps maintain quality.

D.text: Adapt the model using last month's inventory and output the learned values as current inventory.
D.explanation: Past training results alone cannot keep up with changing values.

aib-c01-d1-071@1.title: Evaluate cases where operational costs differ by the direction of prediction error
aib-c01-d1-071@1.prompt: A theater uses attendance forecasts to schedule its entrance staff for the day. Underestimates cause entry delays and refunds, while an overestimate by the same number of people can be handled by adjusting staff assignments. The two forecasts have the same mean absolute error. How should the theater choose which one is more suitable for operations?

learning.reason: Even when error magnitudes are equal, the costs differ by direction. Convert underestimates and overestimates across representative events into costs, then compare operational losses, including refunds and staff adjustments.
learning.concept: Compare two forecasts with the same mean absolute error using costs associated with underestimates and overestimates separately.

A.text: Separate underestimates from overestimates and compare them using the actual costs of refunds and staff adjustments.
A.explanation: This reflects the fact that errors of the same size can have different costs.

B.text: Conclude that the operational costs are equal because the mean absolute error is the same.
B.explanation: Mean absolute error does not account for error direction or differences in cost.

C.text: Treat every overestimate as correct and every underestimate as incorrect, and exclude the cost of overestimates from the totals.
C.explanation: Staffing and assignment adjustments also have costs.

D.text: Compare only the performance for the event with the highest attendance and exclude costs for all other events.
D.explanation: This cannot support a decision under representative operating conditions that include typical events.

aib-c01-d1-072@1.title: Check whether general performance extends to your organization’s specialized terminology
aib-c01-d1-072@1.prompt: You are evaluating AI to explain specialized maintenance documentation. A candidate foundation model scores highly on general writing evaluations, but there is no test that uses component abbreviations understood only within your organization. Which evaluation should guide the adoption decision?

learning.reason: Use general metrics as a reference, but have specialists evaluate representative examples containing the abbreviations and context found in the work. Also verify that the explanations include the information needed to be accurate.
learning.concept: Assess usability under real work conditions by separating a general-purpose model’s training coverage from quality for a specific use case.

A.text: Compare only the number of terms each model references, and conclude that the model with the largest vocabulary fits the specialty.
A.explanation: A large vocabulary does not demonstrate that the model can use internal abbreviations correctly.

B.text: Prepare unseen examples containing the actual abbreviations and maintenance scenarios, then have subject-matter staff compare the accuracy of the explanations and their supporting evidence.
B.explanation: This distinguishes general scores from suitability for the actual use case.

C.text: Automatically convert internal abbreviations into common words before providing them to the model, without checking whether the conversions or original terms are correct.
C.explanation: Misinterpreting an abbreviation can lead to a different explanation.

D.text: Choose the model with the highest general writing score and assume it will be equally accurate when abbreviations appear.
D.explanation: Performance on general tasks does not show whether the model understands the meanings of specific abbreviations.

aib-c01-d1-073@1.title: Choose an input that retains signals lost in a transcript
aib-c01-d1-073@1.prompt: During equipment inspections, you want to detect bearing faults from changes in sound frequency. You have recordings, but their transcripts contain only the technicians’ conversations. Which input and evaluation approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: The needed information is a feature of the sound wave. Use acoustic information from the recordings and evaluate with examples whose anomaly times and normal operation have been verified.
learning.concept: Handle recordings and verified timestamps when acoustic information is lost by converting speech to text.

A.text: Summarize the transcripts in detail and classify every interval with no mention of a fault in the conversation as normal.
A.explanation: Changes in sound are not necessarily mentioned in the conversation.

B.text: Infer fault categories only from recording length and file names, without evaluating frequency.
B.explanation: The input does not include the feature the task depends on.

C.text: Use the recordings’ acoustic features as well as the conversations, and evaluate against records that let you match inspection findings to the times of anomalies.
C.explanation: This connects the signal needed for the decision with the ground-truth outcomes.

D.text: Use the technicians’ job roles and number of times they speak as substitutes for frequency changes in each recording.
D.explanation: Information about the speakers cannot represent the equipment’s acoustic signal.

aib-c01-d1-074@1.title: Do not use values capped at the measurement limit as-is
aib-c01-d1-074@1.prompt: An AI system for equipment predicts the maximum vibration during operation. Some sensors record their upper limit whenever the actual vibration exceeds it, even when the vibration is much stronger. The value is within the valid range, so it passes the current type check. How should the training data be improved?

learning.reason: Distinguish records capped at the limit from accurate maximum values. Identify affected examples using equipment settings or status, and verify them with measurements capable of capturing the required intensity.
learning.concept: Distinguish a true maximum from a value capped by a measuring device, even when the value appears to be within range.

A.text: Add a fixed amount to every capped value and treat the adjusted value as the true maximum.
A.explanation: The record does not establish how far the actual value exceeded the limit.

B.text: Delete all data from sensors that record the limit and omit evaluation under strong-vibration conditions.
B.explanation: This would leave performance under extreme conditions that matter in operation unmeasured.

C.text: If a measured value is within the valid range, treat a value at the limit as the actual measured maximum.
C.explanation: The true vibration above the limit was not recorded.

D.text: Use equipment limits and operating records to identify capped examples, then add an evaluation of extreme values using equipment that can measure the required range.
D.explanation: This accounts for information lost because of equipment limits and makes it possible to evaluate maximum-value predictions.

aib-c01-d1-075@1.title: Investigate why adding more of the same history does not improve results
aib-c01-d1-075@1.prompt: A demand model for event venues still has similarly large errors on both the training and evaluation sets after the training history is increased fourfold. An investigation finds that the inputs do not include the size and type of the events that drive demand. These are known at prediction time. What should you try next?

learning.reason: Adding more examples alone cannot provide information that is absent from the inputs. Link event size and type, which are available at prediction time, to the historical records, then compare performance under the same evaluation conditions.
learning.concept: When adding training examples does not reduce error and useful explanatory information is missing, investigate the required inputs and model conditions.

A.text: Duplicate the existing history, which contains the same information, and treat an increase in the number of records as evidence that the error has improved.
A.explanation: Duplication adds no missing information, and record count alone does not demonstrate improvement.

B.text: Add event size and type, which are known at prediction time, as inputs, then compare errors with the previous model under the same representative conditions.
B.explanation: This addresses the identified information gap and tests the effect of the added features.

C.text: Use the final attendance count, which is known only after the event, to improve accuracy and report that it can also be used before the event.
C.explanation: This uses information unavailable at the time the prediction is made.

D.text: Exclude large events from evaluation and deploy to all venues if the remaining conditions meet the target.
D.explanation: This does not verify performance under the business conditions causing the errors.

aib-c01-d1-076@1.title: When a tool-using agent is unnecessary
aib-c01-d1-076@1.prompt: The purchasing team copies only approved rows into three ledgers in a fixed order. It is also predetermined that processing stops and a standard notification is sent if an error occurs. No external research or decisions to change the order are needed. Which design is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Set the known processing order and stop condition in a fixed workflow. The mere presence of tool calls does not require an agent that plans freely.
