learning.concept: When the call order and conditions are known, choose a defined, trackable process instead of open-ended planning.

A.text: Have an agent inspect each ledger and change the copy order every time, recording the result only when processing is complete.
A.explanation: This does not preserve the specified order or record intermediate decisions.

B.text: Rely on document generation alone to produce instructions for each ledger, without checking whether a person carries them out.
B.explanation: This does not automate the actual copying or the standard error handling.

C.text: Use a fixed workflow to verify approval, copy the rows in the prescribed order, and stop and send a notification on failure.
C.explanation: A fixed workflow is easy to track when the procedure is fully defined.

D.text: Set up three agents to begin copying at the same time and have an operator correct discrepancies later.
D.explanation: This does not meet the requirements for order and stopping.

aib-c01-d1-077@1.title: Distinguishing seasonal changes from unexpected degradation
aib-c01-d1-077@1.prompt: A travel inquiry classification AI receives more family-travel inputs in summer. This June, the distribution of input sources changed substantially compared with May, but it is similar to the same period last year. The system was trained on typical summer conditions, and performance on representative examples has not yet declined. What is the appropriate response?

learning.reason: Set baselines for expected seasonal patterns and compare them with the same period last year and current quality. Do not decide to update solely based on the magnitude of a change.
learning.concept: Assess seasonal changes in input data against same-season baselines and confirmed performance to avoid unnecessary updates.

A.text: Retrain immediately using only records outside the summer because the distribution changed from the previous month.
A.explanation: This narrows the training scope without distinguishing expected seasonal changes from performance degradation.

B.text: Track the distribution and confirmed performance against same-season baselines and operating conditions, and assess causes and updates if performance degrades beyond the baseline.
B.explanation: This distinguishes expected changes from changes that require action.

C.text: Exclude family-travel inputs from evaluation to bring the distribution closer to May and preserve overall accuracy.
C.explanation: This removes an important condition that has become more common in actual operations from the evaluation.

D.text: Make no comparisons because the distribution changes every year, and exclude summer results from quality reporting.
D.explanation: This can miss degradation beyond the seasonal range or issues with new inputs.

aib-c01-d1-078@1.title: Incorporating AI-specific considerations into existing risk management
aib-c01-d1-078@1.prompt: A development company already has an enterprise risk management process. It wants to incorporate guidance for identifying, assessing, and treating risks associated with developing and using AI systems without replacing that process with a separate one. Organizational third-party certification and standardization of technical architecture diagrams are outside the scope of this objective. Which reference is the most direct fit?

learning.reason: ISO/IEC 23894 provides guidance for managing AI-specific risks throughout the lifecycle and integrating risk management into existing activities.
learning.concept: Choose between AI risk management guidance and requirements for an organizational management system based on the objective.

A.text: Refer to ISO/IEC 23053 to standardize how the technical architecture of machine learning systems is described.
A.explanation: This standard addresses a common format for describing architectures, which is different from the risk management guidance sought here.

B.text: First decide to obtain certification to ISO/IEC 42001, and organize the risk process after that assessment is complete.
B.explanation: Requirements for an organizational management system and guidance on specific methods serve different purposes.

C.text: Use ISO/IEC 22989 to align AI terminology and concepts across the company.
C.explanation: A shared vocabulary is useful, but the objective is guidance for managing AI-specific risks.

D.text: Refer to ISO/IEC 23894 to incorporate methods for identifying, assessing, and treating AI risks into existing activities.
D.explanation: This directly fits the goal of integrating AI risk management into an existing process.

aib-c01-d1-079@1.title: Changing the work sequence in response to unexpected findings
aib-c01-d1-079@1.prompt: An internal research AI investigates the cause of a discrepancy reported by a user. If the first ledger it consults is unavailable, it must choose different related documents or a different scope. It is limited to read-only queries and a maximum number of processing steps. Select two capabilities the agent needs.

learning.reason: Plan the next query based on observed results. Stop when the permitted scope or processing limit is reached, and hand off the information gathered.
learning.concept: Rearrange information gathering within fixed action permissions and a processing budget, then stop and hand off work that exceeds those limits.

A.text: Record unresolved questions and the documents already investigated when the limit is reached, then hand the work over to an operator.
A.explanation: This respects the stopping condition and leaves the work in a state a person can continue.

B.text: When information is insufficient, invent plausible supporting content and report the investigation as complete.
B.explanation: This fills gaps that require verification with fabricated results.

C.text: Modify documents that could not be queried successfully to achieve the research objective.
C.explanation: This exceeds the permitted read-only scope.

D.text: Keep the original plan and repeat only the first failed query without limit.
D.explanation: This makes no progress and violates the processing limit.

E.text: Use the information obtained and the remaining gaps to select other permitted documents and change the research sequence.
E.explanation: This adapts the procedure to the situation.

aib-c01-d1-080@1.title: Inform users of the approved scope before a contract changes
aib-c01-d1-080@1.prompt: The conditions under which a sales AI tool was approved include an old contract that says the provider does not retain the materials entered. The renewal would change the terms to allow retention, so the contract review is still underway. Which policy should govern usage while keeping users' work moving?

learning.reason: When the old contract expires, keep processing under the new terms pending approval. Show users the prohibited scope, the start date, and approved alternatives.
learning.concept: Even when a tool keeps the same name, tie its approved conditions to an end date and update its availability and alternative paths.

A.text: Update the inventory with the changeover date and the approval status of the new terms, pause processing that is under review, and point users to an approved alternative.
A.explanation: This communicates the restriction and a way to continue transparently.

B.text: Have each individual user read the retention terms and decide the product's usage classification for themselves.
B.explanation: The standard and permitted scope would vary across departments.

C.text: Leave the inventory unchanged because the product name is the same, and tell users about the retention terms after they have selected it.
C.explanation: Users could already start processing under terms that are still under review.

D.text: Prohibit every approved alternative that could serve the same work until the retention setting is finalized.
D.explanation: This would also remove safe alternatives that are already approved.

aib-c01-d1-081@1.title: Improve output consistency and factual accuracy separately
aib-c01-d1-081@1.prompt: The wording varies considerably each time you generate a standard notice from the same approved materials. The headings and fields must stay fixed, and the date must match the materials. Choose two things to do in configuration and validation.

learning.reason: Try sampling settings and format instructions to reduce variation. Since settings do not guarantee factual accuracy, compare the date and fields against the materials.
learning.concept: Use sampling to control variation in wording, and verify factual values against their sources separately.

A.text: Increase diversity to generate several notices, then register the most frequently occurring date as correct.
A.explanation: Frequency alone does not confirm that the date matches the materials.

B.text: Lower the temperature, assume the date will then always be correct, and end the evaluation.
B.explanation: Reducing variation in wording and factual accuracy are different concerns.

C.text: Specify the format, try a lower temperature, and compare wording variation for the same input.
C.explanation: This lets you evaluate the effect on the desired reproducibility.

D.text: Check the output fields and date individually against a fixed field list and the approved materials.
D.explanation: This detects errors that may remain even in consistent output.

E.text: Remove the approved materials from the input and use only the result with standardized wording as the official answer.
E.explanation: This removes the evidence needed to verify facts.

aib-c01-d1-082@1.title: Do not treat a polished partial output as a completed run
aib-c01-d1-082@1.prompt: You generate descriptions for products in a consistent format. When you submit 100 items together, only 50 are returned, and they appear to be correctly formatted; the run is recorded as having reached its output limit. Which method lets you verify the descriptions for all 100 items?

learning.reason: Reconcile the input list and output by ID, and split the work into runs shorter than the limit. Check each batch's completion reason and count to detect omissions.
learning.concept: Check for termination caused by output limits and confirm the required item count; preserve completeness by splitting and reconciling the work.

A.text: Send the same 100 items every time and use only the output's character count to determine whether anything was added.
A.explanation: This cannot identify input limits, duplicates, or IDs that were not output.

B.text: Split the processing into smaller batches, check each batch's completion reason and product IDs, and reconcile them against the full list.
B.explanation: This makes missing or duplicate outputs detectable.

C.text: If the first 50 returned descriptions are correctly formatted, register the remaining descriptions as generated too.
C.explanation: Correct formatting does not verify the required item count.

D.text: Remove the product IDs to shorten the output, then fill in the missing count based on sequence.
D.explanation: This cannot guarantee which description corresponds to which item.

aib-c01-d1-083@1.title: Improve retrieval quality first when the question and source use different languages
aib-c01-d1-083@1.prompt: The internal AI uses current equipment documentation as a reference. The documents are in English, but questions in Portuguese retrieve the wrong types of documents. Equivalent questions in English retrieve appropriate evidence, and the approval scope for using the documents is the same. Which improvement should be tested first?

learning.reason: Compare multilingual search methods and query transformations that preserve intent across languages. Check the rate of retrieving the correct sections and the answer evidence in both languages.
learning.concept: Evaluate whether the system can reach the relevant source text across languages, separately from changes to generation.

A.text: Tune the model to answer all exceptional questions from general knowledge and avoid accessing the current documents.
A.explanation: This would not meet the requirement to answer based on approved materials.

B.text: Change the answer model's writing to English only and do not investigate which documents were retrieved.
B.explanation: The problem of retrieving the wrong evidence based on the input language would remain.

C.text: Since searches in English work correctly, change only the answer's style for Portuguese.
C.explanation: Changing the style does not make the wrong documents valid evidence.

D.text: Try multilingual search or query transformation that preserves the supporting evidence, and measure whether the correct sections are retrieved in both languages.
D.explanation: This evaluates the confirmed retrieval gap between languages.

aib-c01-d1-084@1.title: Match delayed outcomes to the predictions they belong to
aib-c01-d1-084@1.prompt: A delivery-delay AI makes predictions when shipments are dispatched. Results for short-haul shipments are known the same day, while results for long-haul shipments are confirmed several days later. The report measures performance by combining that day's predictions with the actual results of different shipments that arrived that day. What would improve the report?

learning.reason: Link each prediction and actual outcome using the same shipment identifier, then compare them for each shipment with a confirmed outcome. Report shipments whose outcomes are not yet confirmed separately.
learning.concept: Do not compare aggregates from different periods; match predictions to confirmed outcomes for the same subjects and time points.

A.text: Calculate performance only for shipments with quick results, and assume the same applies to long-haul shipments whose results are not yet known.
A.explanation: This does not measure performance for shipments with different transit times.

B.text: Compare aggregates for different shipments by matching only the day of the week, and exclude days with high variability.
B.explanation: Matching the day of the week still does not compare the same subjects.

C.text: Record every shipment that has not arrived as delayed, and compare it with that day's predictions.
C.explanation: Shipments that eventually arrive on schedule would also be treated as delayed.

D.text: Match predictions with outcomes by shipment ID, measure performance for shipments whose outcomes are confirmed, and report the number of unconfirmed shipments separately.
D.explanation: This evaluates predictions and outcomes for the same shipments and periods.

aib-c01-d2-073@1.title: Help customers complete the process, not just reduce inquiries
aib-c01-d2-073@1.prompt: At an electric utility, customers contact the service desk because they cannot find the identity-verification documents required to change their address. The requirements are approved, and customers complete verification and registration through the existing process. Which pilot is appropriate for reducing the service desk's workload?

learning.reason: Provide approved guidance at the point where it is needed, then track whether customers complete the process and whether they contact the service desk again.
learning.concept: Tie a use case intended to reduce service desk workload to a business process customers can complete.

A.text: Have AI infer the address and register it before the existing identity checks, then evaluate only the number of lines on the screen.
A.explanation: This skips required checks and does not measure registration errors.

B.text: Summarize trends across all past inquiries and use report views as the pilot's measure of success.
B.explanation: This does not measure whether customers completed the required process.

C.text: Remove the service desk's contact information from the AI screen and treat fewer inquiries as more completed transactions.
C.explanation: Inquiry volume can fall simply because it has become harder to ask for help.

D.text: Show approved instructions that fit the customer's situation, and measure completed address changes and repeat inquiries after the guidance is shown.
D.explanation: This addresses why customers contact the service desk and measures the intended service outcome.

aib-c01-d2-074@1.title: Distinguish planned vendor capabilities from capabilities available today
aib-c01-d2-074@1.prompt: A delivery company uses AI for sorting every morning from 2:00 to 4:00. A lower-priced purchase option has support for the required time window on its roadmap, but no delivery date is confirmed. A partnership option can provide an on-call night shift from day one, and the cost of transferring operations to the company's own team is within budget. What should be considered in the selection?

learning.reason: Treat staffing and recovery during the required hours separately from price. Do not count a planned capability as confirmed; verify its date and a fallback.
learning.concept: Reflect the risk of delays to future capabilities without a formal commitment or proof of delivery in the sourcing approach and continuity plan.

A.text: Prioritize the price difference and purchase without confirming an official date for the capability.
A.explanation: Nighttime support required at launch is not assured.

B.text: Assume both options provide the same nighttime support from day one because it appears on the roadmap.
B.explanation: This treats a future plan as equivalent to an available contractual commitment.

C.text: Skip validation of the delivery model and assume that moving operations in-house will always make it possible to staff an on-call night shift.
C.explanation: There is no evidence of hiring or operational capacity.

D.text: Verify launch-time support, a fallback if the requirement is not met, and the handover using schedules or contracts, then compare costs and risks.
D.explanation: This compares required operating conditions and costs using evidence that they can be met.

aib-c01-d2-075@1.title: Allocate scarce specialist capacity even when funding is available
aib-c01-d2-075@1.prompt: There is funding for two AI pilots, but the technical specialist responsible for approvals has only 20 hours per month available. Initiative A has high value but uses all 20 hours every month, leaving no time to review existing safety inspections. Initiative B can run with the remaining hours while preserving those inspections. How should the organization decide?

learning.reason: First reserve the capacity needed for required inspections, then assess the benefits that can be realized with the remaining time. Reassess A if its review burden can be changed.
learning.concept: Choose based on value that can be realized per unit of specialist review time and the impact on required work when review time is constrained.

A.text: Make the implementation cost of B equal to A's so the decision is fair, even if their value differs.
A.explanation: The benefits achieved and the specialist time used are not considered.

B.text: Reserve time for required inspections and evaluate B with the remaining capacity. Reconsider A if its review burden can be reduced or a reviewer can be secured.
B.explanation: This accounts for constraints beyond funding and selects work whose benefits can actually be realized.

C.text: Expand A because funding is available, and perform required inspections only after AI has produced results.
C.explanation: This affects work that is already required.

D.text: Divide review time equally between the two pilots, drop the safety inspections, and put A into operation even if its review is incomplete.
D.explanation: Allocating time alone does not satisfy a required condition.

aib-c01-d2-076@1.title: Remove input ambiguity before adding an estimation step
aib-c01-d2-076@1.prompt: There are three purchasing categories for supply requests. Users know which category they need, but the current form accepts only free text, so Finance has to infer the category later and errors occur. A short selection field can be added to the existing system. What is the best first improvement?

learning.reason: If users can select a category they already know, the system has less need to infer it later. Test how easy the selection and exception path are to use.
learning.concept: Compare the cost of obtaining the correct field at the source with the cost of correcting it later with AI.

A.text: Let users select the category when they submit a request, provide a way to clarify cases they are unsure about, and track errors and time.
A.explanation: This captures the information when the decision is known and reduces downstream guesswork.

B.text: Make everyone's instructions to the AI longer without improving the input process.
B.explanation: This does not record a category that users can reliably identify at the point of input.

C.text: Automatically assign whichever category most closely resembles the entered text, even when it is unclear whether the category is correct.
C.explanation: The system still guesses without confirming the user's judgment.

D.text: Keep free-text input and create a large training set by copying past inferred results.
D.explanation: This preserves unnecessary inference and could treat past errors as labels.

aib-c01-d2-077@1.title: A new system does not necessarily eliminate the old costs
aib-c01-d2-077@1.prompt: Moving to a new AI platform can reduce inference costs. Finance calculated the savings on the assumption that the old contract would be terminated in the month after the cutover. An assessment found that a monthly process in another department depends on one feature of the old platform, and the contract also has a notice period. Which plan should be revised?

learning.reason: Check dependencies on the old platform and the contractual exit date, and include the necessary migration and parallel-running costs. Count savings from when the contract's termination conditions are met.
learning.concept: Include dependency readiness and retirement costs when deciding whether a platform switch can realize its planned savings.

A.text: Immediately stop the other department's use to reduce costs and check later whether that is compatible with its monthly process.
A.explanation: This would interrupt the old process before it has been migrated.

B.text: Remove the old contract costs as soon as the new platform passes quality checks, and investigate the other department's feature after launch.
B.explanation: The contract cannot actually be terminated until its dependencies and terms are addressed.

C.text: Keep both old contracts indefinitely and report savings from the cutover starting in the month it goes live.
C.explanation: This treats costs from contracts that have not been terminated as savings.

D.text: Check dependencies on the old feature, acceptance of its replacement, the notice period, and parallel-running costs, then recalculate net benefits based on the earliest feasible termination date.
D.explanation: This accounts for both business continuity and the costs that will actually go away.

aib-c01-d2-078@1.title: Measure both excess and insufficient inventory
aib-c01-d2-078@1.prompt: A retailer wants to reduce excess inventory using demand forecasts. At some stores, cutting inventory across the board lowers the value of excess stock, but leaves needed products unavailable on the shelves. Choose two objective and quality metrics.

learning.reason: Track both the holding burden of excess inventory and the supply impact of stockouts. Align comparison conditions for stores with different product ranges.
learning.concept: Combine the value of inventory reduced with service-level measures to identify excessive inventory cuts.

A.text: For the same product group, measure the cost of excess inventory, including waste and storage.
A.explanation: This measures the inventory-reduction objective.

B.text: Track the stockout rate during periods of demand or the share of orders that could be supplied.
B.explanation: This checks whether service levels have worsened even as excess inventory falls.

C.text: Evaluate only the proportion of stores that reduced the variety of products they carry.
C.explanation: This does not distinguish a reduction in excess inventory caused by changes in the range carried.

D.text: Measure only the number of delivery notifications and exclude periods when inventory ran out.
D.explanation: This does not capture the effect on supplying customers.

E.text: Use the number of inventory forecast requests as a proxy for how much inventory improved.
E.explanation: Request volume does not represent holding costs or stockouts.

aib-c01-d2-079@1.title: Use existing records to assess a baseline that was not measured before launch
aib-c01-d2-079@1.prompt: After AI-based maintenance intake began, the team discovered that it had not measured the time spent on work before launch. Some sites have historical processing records that show the date and time and the process step involved; other sites have only monthly counts. What is the appropriate approach for evaluating outcomes?

learning.reason: Reconstruct the pre-launch baseline only where the process step and timing are comparable. Do not count sites without verifiable measurements as proven impact; improve comparisons going forward.
learning.concept: When reconstructing a comparison value from historical records, check definitions, scope, and confidence, and disclose missing data.

A.text: Compare definitions and calculate historical processing time only for sites where the same process step can be tracked, and document what was not measured and the scope of the evaluation.
A.explanation: This makes clear both the evidence available and the areas where no reliable conclusion can be made.

B.text: Treat the average from a few sites with time records as the pre-launch time for every site, without checking.
B.explanation: This does not verify whether the work definitions or sites are comparable.

C.text: Multiply monthly counts by the current average processing time and attribute the entire historical-to-current difference to AI.
C.explanation: This does not use observed historical processing times.

D.text: Save all records from the launch month under a pre-launch label and report the difference from that result as the outcome.
D.explanation: The post-launch state does not measure the earlier baseline.

aib-c01-d2-080@1.title: Calculating the profit impact of a change in churn rate
aib-c01-d2-080@1.prompt: There are 2,000 target customers. In a comparative trial, the annual churn rate fell from 12% without AI assistance to 10% with it. Assuming the same effect for the defined target population, the additional marginal profit from each retained contract is ¥30,000, and the annual cost of AI is ¥800,000. What is the net incremental profit?

learning.reason: The churn-rate difference is 2 percentage points, or 40 customers. 40 × ¥30,000 = ¥1,200,000; subtracting the annual AI cost of ¥800,000 leaves ¥400,000.
learning.concept: Distinguish a relative change from a percentage-point difference, and use the number of additional customers retained and their marginal profit.

A.text: ¥400,000. Subtract the annual cost from the ¥1,200,000 in additional marginal profit for 40 customers.
A.explanation: This correctly uses the absolute difference in churn rates, the number of customers retained, and the cost.

B.text: ¥1,200,000. Treat the full profit from the retained contracts as incremental profit.
B.explanation: This does not subtract the annual cost of AI.

C.text: ¥5,200,000. Assume that 200 customers, corresponding to 10%, continue their contracts additionally, and subtract the cost from the profit.
C.explanation: 10% is the churn rate with AI, not the share of contracts additionally retained because of the measure.

D.text: −¥740,000. Treat the 2 percentage-point difference as 2 customers and multiply by ¥30,000.
D.explanation: This does not apply the rate difference to the target population.

aib-c01-d2-081@1.title: Measuring the review action that precedes a long-term reduction in defects
aib-c01-d2-081@1.prompt: A contract-review AI displays items that need review to reduce missed clauses. Whether it actually reduces contractual issues will not be known until the renewal date. Which metric can provide an early indication of whether the alerts are being acted on, rather than merely displayed?

learning.reason: Track the percentage of cases requiring review in which the person responsible checks the supporting evidence and records the result by the deadline. This can later be linked to the number of issues confirmed.
learning.concept: Before the outcome is known, measure the share of cases that complete the required review and proceed to the next step.

A.text: The number of times users close the review screen.
A.explanation: Closing the screen alone does not show whether a review was completed.

B.text: The annual rate of contractual issues confirmed at renewal.
B.explanation: This is a final outcome and does not inform early decisions in time.

C.text: The percentage of cases flagged for review in which the person responsible verifies the supporting evidence and records it by the deadline.
C.explanation: This shows whether the required action was taken after an alert was issued.

D.text: The total number of characters in the generated alerts.
D.explanation: This does not measure whether the required review was completed.

aib-c01-d2-082@1.title: Reviewing costs incurred even during periods of low utilization
aib-c01-d2-082@1.prompt: Eighty percent of decisions occur during the last two days of each month, while activity is low on other days. A proposal would purchase dedicated capacity for the entire year. The maximum wait time must be maintained. Which cost plan should be evaluated?

learning.reason: Use normal-period and peak demand to compare the cost of usage-based capacity and short-term additional capacity with fixed capacity. Also measure whether the wait-time requirement is actually met at peak times.
learning.concept: Compare fixed and usage-based capacity using the actual demand pattern, and validate peak service levels and annual costs.

A.text: Measure the capacity needed during normal periods and at month-end, then compare the costs of usage-based capacity combined with additional peak capacity against those of fixed capacity.
A.explanation: This accounts for both variable demand and the required service level.

B.text: Use only inexpensive capacity and defer work that cannot be processed at month-end until the following month without notifying anyone of the delay.
B.explanation: This fails to meet the operational wait-time requirement.

C.text: Exclude days with low activity and estimate the cost of the last two days of the month as the annual cost.
C.explanation: This omits recurring base costs and spending on other days.

D.text: Keep the maximum dedicated capacity fixed even on days with no activity and judge it to be inexpensive based only on the unit price.
D.explanation: This does not evaluate the total cost, including unused capacity.

aib-c01-d2-083@1.title: Investigating why customers reject an option with comparable capabilities
aib-c01-d2-083@1.prompt: A candidate administrative AI performs at a speed and accuracy comparable to its competitors. Several customers said they chose a competitor because it could show records of control testing performed before deployment. Which research should guide the next improvement?

learning.reason: Ask what evidence customer review teams require and when they need it. Then assess the difference between the materials available from your organization and competitors, and whether closing that gap would affect contract decisions.
learning.concept: When comparing competitors, examine review readiness and the evidence customers require in addition to performance.

A.text: Lower the price to match competitors and provide the information needed for control reviews only after customers complete their reviews.
A.explanation: This does not meet review requirements before adoption.

B.text: Ask customers’ review teams what evidence they require and by when, compare available materials with those of competitors, and measure the effect on contract decisions.
B.explanation: This identifies the difference that actually influenced adoption.

C.text: Study only the cost of doubling the model’s speed and disregard the control-testing documentation requested by customers.
C.explanation: This does not investigate the difference that was actually a condition of adoption.

D.text: Compare competitors’ brand names and do not research customers who declined to sign.
D.explanation: This relies on guesses instead of investigating the conditions behind the decision not to adopt.

aib-c01-d2-084@1.title: Testing a different sales channel after selling directly to existing customers
aib-c01-d2-084@1.prompt: A company has sold its meeting-minutes assistance feature only on its own. Direct sales to small customers who use a meeting system are costly, so the system provider has offered to resell the feature within its own product. Which approach should the company use to test this new business model?

learning.reason: Test embedded distribution with a small group of customers, then validate revenue sharing for the channel, customer usage, support costs, and unit economics.
learning.concept: Embed an AI-enabled feature in an existing product and validate who bears the costs and support responsibilities.

A.text: Lower only the direct-sale price, without measuring the revenue and costs from sales through the reseller.
A.explanation: This does not evaluate whether the new sales channel is viable.

B.text: Offer the provider unlimited free distribution and assume that profits will rise as the number of users grows.
B.explanation: This does not allow the company to compare revenue with costs.

C.text: Run a small resale pilot with the provider and measure revenue sharing, customer usage, and the costs of operations and handling inquiries.
C.explanation: This lets the company test the channel and the structure of revenue and responsibilities in practice.

D.text: Assume that resale will be profitable if the company’s inference accuracy is high, and decide who is responsible for support after launch.
D.explanation: Product performance and the profitability of a business model are separate.

aib-c01-d2-085@1.title: Achieving a sustainably lower delivery cost with a general-purpose model
aib-c01-d2-085@1.prompt: An AI system for reviewing business documents uses the same model as its competitors, but its costs are high because the same tests and operating settings are rebuilt for each customer. The company can standardize industry-wide review work itself and handle customer-specific checks separately. Which investment would sustainably improve its competitive position?

learning.reason: Standardize checks and operating processes that can be reused across customers while maintaining quality for customer-specific requirements. Track whether implementation costs and costs per verified completion continue to fall.
learning.concept: Protect quality by standardizing validation and operational setup for similar work instead of relying on lower feature prices.

A.text: Wait for competitors to raise their prices and continue rebuilding all tests and settings for each customer.
A.explanation: This does not improve the time and costs the company can control.

B.text: Keep costs unchanged and increase the number of contracts at prices that produce no profit in the first year.
B.explanation: This may temporarily increase the customer base, but it does not create a lasting delivery-cost advantage.

C.text: Switch to the least expensive model and eliminate all checks for customer-specific requirements.
C.explanation: Even if the model’s unit price falls, quality may decline and rework may increase costs.

D.text: Reuse common checks and operating settings while retaining customer-specific checks. Track implementation costs, cost per completed review, and quality.
D.explanation: This reduces the cost of repeating the same work while allowing the company to measure operational quality.

aib-c01-d2-086@1.title: Investing further once demand and business viability are proven
aib-c01-d2-086@1.prompt: In the safety inspection assistance market, several paid pilots have been renewed, and the economics—including pricing and support costs—are within the required range. Industry standards and sales processes are established, and competition is increasing. Which AI investment is appropriate this quarter?

learning.reason: Because payment and operating conditions have been validated, invest in capacity and quality within the range of confirmed demand, then adjust using retention and unit-cost data.
learning.concept: Assess proven demand and delivery maturity together instead of changing investment solely in response to competitors.

A.text: Make no investment in the mature market because competitors are present, and end the paid pilots.
A.explanation: This disregards proven customer value and business viability.

B.text: Increase the budget uniformly, including for overseas markets, by an amount tied to the rise in competitors, without examining pilot results.
B.explanation: This does not account for the markets that can be served or their costs.

C.text: Invest in supply capacity and quality control in stages, within the scope where demand has been confirmed, and use renewal rates and costs to decide on further expansion.
C.explanation: This lets the company reflect the level of market validation in its funding decisions.

D.text: Stop measuring operating costs because renewed pilots prove that profitability will always be maintained.
D.explanation: This would leave the company unable to track costs that change with deployment scale and competition.

aib-c01-d2-087@1.title: Reducing the causes of returns instead of only processing them
aib-c01-d2-087@1.prompt: A retailer already processes return requests quickly enough. Its business goal is to reduce repeat returns of the same product. It can match orders with reasons written by customers, and its product team can fix parts or instructions suspected of causing the returns. Which initiative is appropriate?

learning.reason: Link written reasons to products and versions to find candidate causes, have the product team verify and correct them, and then measure returns for the same reasons.
learning.concept: Use item details and written reasons to understand recurring causes, improve products, and measure the effect.

A.text: Shorten the return response and further reduce the average time from receiving a request to sending a reply.
A.explanation: This is unrelated to the goal of removing the causes of returns.

B.text: Link products and versions to customers’ written reasons to identify trends, fix confirmed causes, and measure the return rate for the same reason.
B.explanation: This connects AI analysis to actionable improvements and their effects.

C.text: Offer coupons to frequent buyers and use redemption counts to assess product improvements.
C.explanation: This does not address the reasons for returns by product.

D.text: Use the total number of historical returns to estimate next month’s staffing needs, without examining differences by product or reason.
D.explanation: This may help with staffing plans, but it does not identify the causes to reduce.

aib-c01-d2-088@1.title: Align budget priorities with the outcomes that matter
aib-c01-d2-088@1.prompt: An AI solution that assembles records needed for contract reviews would mainly reduce audit findings, with little time savings. Another proposal would shorten the drafting of public relations materials, but correcting review quality is the top priority for the next strategy cycle. The budget cannot cover both. What is the appropriate way to prioritize?

learning.reason: Assess the business priorities and the actual effect on review quality rather than comparing value only in terms of time savings. Prioritize review improvements that meet the required standard.
learning.concept: Evaluate important business outcomes and avoidable harm, not just direct cost savings.

A.text: Assess how much the solution would improve review evidence and findings, then invest first in the proposal that meets the strategic quality goal.
A.explanation: It addresses an outcome the company values, even if it is not closely tied to profit.

B.text: Give both proposals equal priority because they use AI, and defer decisions about validation scope until next year.
B.explanation: This does not connect strategic goals to the current budget.

C.text: Count only audit findings and, if expectations are high, roll out the solution company-wide even if the data is unavailable.
C.explanation: This considers value without checking feasibility and may fail to deliver the needed outcome.

D.text: Choose the proposal with the greatest time savings and exclude audit deadlines and review quality from the investment assessment.
D.explanation: This ignores the quality the business must protect and the impact of doing so.

aib-c01-d2-089@1.title: Borrow external expertise while transferring evaluation capability in-house
aib-c01-d2-089@1.prompt: A food manufacturer wants to use inspection support in its production processes. An off-the-shelf product cannot provide the required evidence for some equipment categories. The company has in-house operational knowledge but no experience evaluating AI. A potential partner can develop the evaluation jointly with the operations team and transfer the process. Which choice is best?

learning.reason: Compare partners based on their ability to support joint evaluation and make test cases, evaluation procedures, and the ability to repeat the evaluation independently acceptance conditions.
learning.concept: Make evaluation gaps that an off-the-shelf product cannot fill, and the ability to transfer those skills, part of partner selection and acceptance criteria.

A.text: Ignore the equipment-category limitations, adopt the lower-priced off-the-shelf product, and have operations explain the evidence.
A.explanation: Some categories would still lack the evidence needed for inspection.

B.text: Choose an expert partner that can develop the evaluation jointly with operations, and make the ability to repeat the evaluation independently a condition for accepting the transfer.
B.explanation: This fills the skills gap and enables the company to maintain quality after launch.

C.text: Delegate all evaluation to the partner, accept only the resulting scores, and do not share test cases or acceptance criteria.
C.explanation: The company would be unable to manage changes in the work or reevaluate the solution.

D.text: Commission an evaluation without sharing operational knowledge, and request evidence for monitoring the model only after implementation.
D.explanation: This prevents validation that reflects actual operating conditions and a transfer into operations.

aib-c01-d2-090@1.title: Reconsider an initiative if a prediction arrives too late to act on
aib-c01-d2-090@1.prompt: A retailer wants to use AI to detect stockouts for the current day and change the morning shipment quantity. In testing, the only effective signal was the result of the midday receiving inspection, and the shipment quantity cannot be changed that morning. Data available in the morning did not improve on the current decision. Which policy should be prioritized next?

learning.reason: A model using a midday signal cannot change the morning shipment quantity in the current process. Test options that change the signal or adjustment time, and for now consider later workflows where action is still possible.
learning.concept: Distinguish prediction accuracy from the point in the workflow when results can actually be used.

A.text: Do not adopt it for the current morning adjustment; consider information available earlier or actions that can be taken in the afternoon, such as replenishment or customer notifications.
A.explanation: This first checks whether the prediction can be connected to work that can actually be changed.

B.text: Every morning, display the previous day's model output based on midday results and report that this alone can prevent stockouts that day.
B.explanation: Displaying the previous day's result does not provide a signal for the current day, and the improvement has not been validated.

C.text: Keep the unchangeable cutoff time, increase only the number of model training runs, and continue improving midday accuracy.
C.explanation: Improving accuracy against the existing test results does not remove the timing constraint.

D.text: If the midday signal has high accuracy, deploy it to prevent morning stockouts even though the shipment quantity cannot be changed.
D.explanation: The intended action cannot be taken when accurate information becomes available.

aib-c01-d2-091@1.title: Clarify when and how customers can use each channel before the transition
aib-c01-d2-091@1.prompt: An AI intake service for payment inquiries is being introduced. Routine inquiries can receive immediate guidance, but inquiries made through representatives will continue to be handled through existing phone appointments for the time being. The pre-transition notice says, “All inquiries can be completed on screen.” What should be done to keep the business running?

learning.reason: Accurately communicate eligibility and preserve the entry point and responsible team for phone appointments. Test whether users can actually start and complete work through both channels.
learning.concept: Make the new scope, alternative channel, and user communications part of the transition requirements.

A.text: Keep the notice claiming all inquiries can be completed, and decide internally where to route them only when inquiries arrive.
A.explanation: This misstates the available service and leaves the alternative route undefined.

B.text: Explain the eligible inquiries, start date, and out-of-scope phone appointments, then test both channels with participants from intake through completion.
B.explanation: This keeps the work available to people who need each channel during the transition.

C.text: Switch over without sending a notice, assuming existing users already know about the phone appointments.
C.explanation: New users and people affected by the change may not know how to proceed.

D.text: Remove guidance to the old appointment process to increase use of the new channel, and let out-of-scope customers find help after an error.
D.explanation: This makes it harder for out-of-scope customers to get support.

aib-c01-d2-092@1.title: Measure how much operational capacity was gained from the time saved
aib-c01-d2-092@1.prompt: An inspection AI cut inspectors’ drafting time in half. The organization’s goal is to approve more inspections within the same working hours. The number of drafts increased, but many records remain unapproved because they need corrections. What is the most appropriate primary metric?

learning.reason: Measure inspections that have formally completed quality review under the same staffing and working-hour conditions. Track unapproved drafts and the burden of corrections separately.
learning.concept: Measure valid output and quality achieved with the same staff, distinguishing them from time savings on paper.

A.text: Increase working hours and compare the number completed, excluding the additional hours from the measurement.
A.explanation: This does not show the increase achieved under the same staffing conditions.

B.text: Measure only the average number of seconds to generate a draft, and do not assess correction time.
B.explanation: This does not show how much work was completed end to end.

C.text: Determine productivity solely by the number of drafts created.
C.explanation: This does not represent the number of inspections available for use after approval.

D.text: Measure the number of inspections that complete quality review for comparable staff hours, and also track the burden of unapproved records and corrections.
D.explanation: This measures the increase in usable operational capacity.

aib-c01-d2-093@1.title: Establish the normal range of variation before assessing a trial’s impact
aib-c01-d2-093@1.prompt: The difficulty of document-processing cases varies substantially from one operating day to the next. The person responsible for an AI experiment wants to use the previous day, when processing happened to be slow, as the baseline and announce an improvement rate. What measurement should be established before the experiment begins?

learning.reason: Choose representative periods and case categories, then examine both typical processing performance and its variation. Track equivalent conditions during the experiment and account for normal variation.
learning.concept: Record normal variation across multiple pre-rollout periods; do not infer results from a single day’s difference.

A.text: First select only the week in which the AI improved, then use the first day of that week as the historical baseline.
A.explanation: Selecting the measurement period after seeing the rollout results distorts the assessment.

B.text: Measure representative periods using the same categories and definitions so normal variation can be compared with changes after the experiment.
B.explanation: This makes it less likely that an incidental difference from a single day will be mistaken for an effect.

C.text: Assume case difficulty is the same if company-wide utilization is unchanged, and complete the baseline using only the previous day’s measurement.
C.explanation: This does not account for changes in the mix of cases.

D.text: Fix the slowest day as the baseline and exclude days when improvement cannot be measured.
D.explanation: This selectively uses the most favorable part of normal variation.

aib-c01-d2-094@1.title: Do not count benefits you already receive as gains from additional investment
aib-c01-d2-094@1.prompt: The current AI-assisted service provides ¥4 million in annual benefits and costs ¥2.2 million. The upgraded version would provide ¥5.2 million in benefits and cost ¥3.6 million. All other conditions, such as quality, are the same. What is the increase in annual net benefit from switching to the upgraded version?

learning.reason: The current net benefit is ¥1.8 million, while the upgraded version’s is ¥1.6 million. Benefits increase by ¥1.2 million and costs increase by ¥1.4 million, so the difference is −¥200,000.
learning.concept: Assess a change’s economics using only the incremental benefits and costs of the additional features.

A.text: ¥1.8 million. Compare the current benefits with the current costs.
A.explanation: This is the current net benefit; it does not show the effect of the change.

B.text: ¥1.6 million. Subtract the upgraded version’s costs from its benefits.
B.explanation: This is the upgraded version’s net benefit alone, not the difference from the current version.

C.text: −¥200,000. Compare the net benefits of the new and current versions.
C.explanation: This measures the difference from switching, excluding benefits already being received.

D.text: ¥1.2 million. Use only the difference between the ¥5.2 million in benefits and the current benefits.
D.explanation: This does not subtract the ¥1.4 million increase in annual costs.

aib-c01-d2-095@1.title: Measure implementation readiness before post-launch usage
aib-c01-d2-095@1.prompt: The value of the organization’s AI initiatives can be assessed only after six months. In the past, many ideas stalled during reviews of the data and accountable owners required for production, even when there were many proposals. Which leading indicator would show the likelihood of deployment next month?

learning.reason: Track the proportion of cases that have completed the required approvals and preparation and have advanced to a trial or delivery, along with reasons for delays. Keep this separate from the assessment of economic impact.
learning.concept: Measure cases that pass key reviews and become ready to operate, rather than counting proposals alone.

A.text: The total number of AI ideas submitted in meetings.
A.explanation: This does not show whether proposals meet the required conditions.

B.text: The combined profits of all AI initiatives six months later.
B.explanation: This is an important final outcome, but it will not be available for next month’s assessment.

C.text: The proportion of ideas under consideration that have secured data approval and a production owner and meet the conditions for the next trial.
C.explanation: This captures the number of cases ready to advance and where they are getting stuck.

D.text: The number of newly introduced model types divided by the number of departments.
D.explanation: This does not measure readiness to deliver business value.

aib-c01-d2-096@1.title: Reduce the cost of repeatedly sending irrelevant documents
aib-c01-d2-096@1.prompt: Costs for a maintenance support AI have increased. Every request includes manuals for all products, even though most are unrelated. The response-time target and requirement to provide supporting evidence must still be met. Select TWO measures.

learning.reason: Select documents needed for the product and inquiry to reduce input volume. Compare evidence coverage and quality as well as actual processing costs.
learning.concept: Examine the cost breakdown and identify which parts of the large volume of documents sent each time are needed to meet requirements and provide evidence.

A.text: Always switch to the highest-performance model and leave the input configuration unchanged.
A.explanation: This does not change the processing volume causing the increase.

B.text: Send every document in full and evaluate only the months with the lowest bills.
B.explanation: This neither reduces the input nor provides a representative comparison.

C.text: Remove all supporting documents and assume answer quality is maintained if costs fall.
C.explanation: This removes necessary evidence and does not validate quality.

D.text: Use representative questions to check evidence retrieval and accuracy, and compare latency and cost per completed request.
D.explanation: This verifies whether costs can be reduced while preserving the business requirements.

E.text: First filter for approved documents relevant to the product and inquiry, then provide only the necessary sections.
E.explanation: This reduces the irrelevant input sent with every request.

aib-c01-d3-061@1.title: Measure whether the system handles natural variation in user input
aib-c01-d3-061@1.prompt: An equipment application AI is highly accurate on clean originals. In the field, however, staff sometimes photograph folded paper forms or submit them in dim lighting. The required business outcome does not change. Which validation should be prioritized from a responsible AI perspective?

learning.reason: Create representative examples of conditions that actually occur, then examine errors for each input condition and what happens when the system cannot recognize the input.
learning.concept: Test common variations in advance and verify that important business outcomes can still be achieved.

A.text: Measure the accuracy of key fields using representative examples with dim lighting and folds, and check whether users can resubmit when the image cannot be read.
A.explanation: This validates quality under field conditions and the recovery path.

B.text: Exclude hard-to-read images from evaluation and move to production without telling users what to do under conditions that produce poor results.
B.explanation: This hides both problematic conditions and the available alternatives.

C.text: Measure accuracy only on the most legible originals and apply that value to all usage conditions.
C.explanation: This does not validate the business outcome under conditions that occur in use.

D.text: Assign only a brightness score to each image and do not evaluate the application results.
D.explanation: Input characteristics alone cannot measure business errors.

aib-c01-d3-062@1.title: Meet the publication date without making unsupported advertising claims
aib-c01-d3-062@1.prompt: The product copy generated by AI is compelling, but it asserts benefits that have not completed internal review. The team wants to publish tomorrow, but policy prohibits claims about benefits without supporting evidence. What is the appropriate response?

learning.reason: Remove unverified claims and prepare a version that can be published using approved facts alone. Add claims only after checking the evidence.
learning.concept: Balance business timing with accurate representations by limiting the publication to approved information.

A.text: Keep the publication date fixed and publish the AI-generated benefits as written, then look for evidence.
A.explanation: This tells users unverified claims before they have been checked.

B.text: Use another generative AI system and treat similar claims in both outputs as sufficient evidence of product performance.
B.explanation: Agreement between two outputs is not evidence of product benefits.

C.text: Add a small disclaimer to every benefit and present the claims as established facts without checking for evidence.
C.explanation: A disclaimer does not provide supporting evidence.

D.text: Publish only copy verified against approved facts, and consider asserting benefits only after the evidence has been confirmed.
D.explanation: This preserves the goal of publishing while meeting the accuracy requirement.

aib-c01-d3-063@1.title: Design so users can disable and correct AI suggestions across partner channels
aib-c01-d3-063@1.prompt: An AI suggestion feature is being embedded in a partner's reservation service. Suggestions also appear on screens that the original provider cannot see, so it is unclear who can disable or correct them if an error spreads. What should the design include?

learning.reason: Before providing the feature, decide who can disable and correct suggestions, which company will notify the other, and what evidence will confirm the correction was applied.
learning.concept: For deployments spanning multiple organizations, define and rehearse notification, authority, disabling, and correction procedures before activation.

A.text: Standardize only the descriptive text shown on each screen and discuss disabling and correction after an incident.
A.explanation: Responsibilities and actions are not defined when a problem occurs.

B.text: Include in the contract and acceptance tests conditions under which both companies can report an issue, disable the feature within the agreed scope, and correct an erroneous suggestion.
B.explanation: This verifies that the full response can work even on external screens.

C.text: If the provider can disable the feature on its own screens, do not test whether it may continue appearing on the partner's screens.
C.explanation: This does not establish that the response will be effective on the partner's side.

D.text: Ask whoever receives an error report to contact the partner company, but do not track whether the correction is completed.
D.explanation: This does not verify that the issue was corrected for users.

aib-c01-d3-064@1.title: Do not mistake a timeout for human approval
aib-c01-d3-064@1.prompt: A payment assistance AI drafts a payment and asks an employee to review it. Company policy allows a payment above the limit to be finalized only after an approval action. In a prototype, the payment was finalized when the employee did nothing before the request timed out. What is the appropriate improvement?

learning.reason: Do not treat a lack of response as approval. Keep the payment on hold and notify a backup employee. Record the approval outcome and the condition for finalization, and test both normal responses and nonresponses.
learning.concept: When an action requires explicit approval, treat no response as a reason to keep it on hold, just as you would a denial.

A.text: If the employee does not respond, use the AI's confidence score to approve the action on the employee's behalf.
A.explanation: The human approval required by policy is not obtained.

B.text: Record a nominal approval when there is no response because the employee may be able to reverse the payment afterward.
B.explanation: The payment is finalized based on approval that was never actually given.

C.text: Treat a read receipt for the review request as sufficient, without requiring explicit approval of the payment details.
C.explanation: A read receipt does not authorize a specific action.

D.text: If there is no explicit approval, keep the payment on hold and contact a backup employee. Finalize it only after the approval is recorded.
D.explanation: This preserves the required approval even when there is no response.

aib-c01-d3-065@1.title: Assign an owner to resolve conflicts over AI acceptance criteria
aib-c01-d3-065@1.prompt: During an AI release review, the business team evaluates the schedule, Legal reviews the contract, and Operations assesses quality. There is no rule for cases where one group approves a release while another puts the same case on hold. How should the governance structure be improved?

learning.reason: Define each team's review areas and approval conditions, and assign owners for resolving conflicts and conducting re-reviews. Do not authorize release until mandatory conditions are met.
learning.concept: Separate the business, security, and Legal review decisions, and assign responsibility for reconciling conflicting conditions.

A.text: Consolidate everyone into a single approval account and do not retain who made each decision.
A.explanation: This makes it impossible to track responsibility, outcomes, or unresolved items.

B.text: Define each team's decision scope and mandatory conditions, and specify the escalation path, deadlines, and re-review process for unresolved issues.
B.explanation: This clarifies who makes each decision and how conflicts are resolved.

C.text: Release the system even if the teams disagree, and revisit the review structure at the next annual audit.
C.explanation: The system would be released without checking a mandatory condition that remains on hold.

D.text: Accept the decision of whichever team responds first, and do not contact other teams that have put the case on hold.
D.explanation: This leaves mandatory conditions from teams reviewing different aspects unaddressed.

aib-c01-d3-066@1.title: Respond correctly to a request for a copy of records
aib-c01-d3-066@1.prompt: A company's usage policy requires it to provide a person with their saved AI consultation records within a specified period after verifying their identity. The records include both the original records and saved AI summaries used by employees. Before launching the service, which TWO measures should be taken?

learning.reason: Establish a process with identity verification and response deadlines, and test whether the original records and related saved summaries can be retrieved. Keep a record of fulfillment.
learning.concept: Map a hypothetical disclosure request to identity verification, search scope, deadlines, and evidence of completion.

A.text: Regenerate some records with AI and provide them as if they were the saved records from the time of the original consultation.
A.explanation: The records would not reflect what was actually saved at the time.

B.text: Test whether the original records and saved summaries can be retrieved using the subject's ID, and record the scope covered and the date and time.
B.explanation: This helps ensure that all requested records are covered and provides evidence of fulfillment.

C.text: To respond quickly, do not check whether the person making the request is the person whose records are being requested.
C.explanation: This could disclose someone else's records.

D.text: Set up an owner and process for receiving requests from people whose identities have been verified, along with a response deadline.
D.explanation: This supports request handling and deadline management in accordance with the requirement.

E.text: Because summaries are generated automatically, do not check where they are stored; cover only the original records.
E.explanation: This does not comply with the policy, which also covers saved summaries.

aib-c01-d3-067@1.title: Move from shared credentials to least-privilege access
aib-c01-d3-067@1.prompt: During an internal AI pilot, three departments use a single long-lived service credential. Each department uses different libraries and accesses different data, and if a compromise is suspected, it is not possible to distinguish whose access should be disabled. What should be prioritized?

learning.reason: Move to purpose-specific identities and least-privilege permissions, and track changes and usage. Disable the old credential after migration.
learning.concept: Retire shared, long-lived credentials and limit the impact of a compromise through service-specific execution roles and auditing.

A.text: Change only the names of the credentials used by department contacts, while continuing to share the same authorization behind the scenes.
A.explanation: Changing the displayed names does not change the scope of access.

B.text: Create a separate execution identity for each purpose, limit permissions to what is required, enable auditing of use, and retire the shared credential.
B.explanation: This limits the impact of a compromise and makes it possible to trace which identity was used.

C.text: To reduce the impact, give the same credential to external support staff as well as all departmental applications.
C.explanation: This expands the sharing of sensitive permissions.

D.text: Rotate the shared credential regularly, but keep its permissions across all departments and all data unchanged.
D.explanation: Rotation alone does not resolve the problems of broad access and indistinguishable users.

aib-c01-d3-068@1.title: Reassess the data classification before moving from synthetic data to real records
aib-c01-d3-068@1.prompt: An internal inquiry summarization workflow was tested with synthetic data and classified as low risk. In the next trial, the team wants to include actual user inquiries. The operation and model are unchanged, but the inquiries contain records linked to individuals. How should the review handle this change?

learning.reason: Compare the assumptions behind the prototype data with the real records, then establish the intended use, access, storage, deletion, and validation controls before introducing real data.
learning.concept: Even when the purpose and functionality remain the same, controls must change if the sensitivity of the information or the impact of a disclosure changes.

A.text: Allow anyone to use the records as long as only a small number of real records are involved, and decide on storage conditions later.
A.explanation: Reducing the number of records does not eliminate the need to define access and storage conditions.

B.text: Reuse the approval for synthetic data because the output format is unchanged.
B.explanation: The review did not account for the impact of handling sensitive real records.

C.text: Instruct the model not to output information linked to individuals and exclude input handling from the classification.
C.explanation: Risks related to receiving, storing, and viewing sensitive information remain.

D.text: Reassess the sensitivity of the real records and their intended use, and confirm access, storage, and deletion conditions before expanding the scope.
D.explanation: This makes it possible to put approvals and operating controls in place that fit the new information scope.

aib-c01-d3-069@1.title: Assess material incident counts in light of usage and monitoring coverage
aib-c01-d3-069@1.prompt: An operations team monitors incorrect contract guidance weekly. Recently, traffic doubled, and the number of incorrect responses also doubled. However, the policy requires immediate action for even one material incorrect response. Which monitoring change is appropriate?

learning.reason: Measure overall trends using a consistent denominator and monitoring scope. Keep material incidents as a separate condition for immediate action.
learning.concept: Distinguish low sample counts from increases in counts, and manage material incidents with a single-incident trigger as well.

A.text: Record only the weekly count without recording the denominator, and report the doubled count as a 50% decline in model performance.
A.explanation: This does not distinguish the effect of a change in usage volume.

B.text: Exclude every low-usage week and report material incidents only in a month-end summary.
B.explanation: This fails the requirement to act when an incident is found and can hide deterioration during periods of low usage.

C.text: Record the number of responses reviewed and the categories covered, and compare the usual error rate. Notify the team and investigate even a single material incident.
C.explanation: This preserves both trend monitoring and urgent action for material incidents.

D.text: Use rates only, and do not begin investigating a material incident unless the overall rate increases.
D.explanation: This cannot address material incidents that require action even when there is only one.

aib-c01-d3-070@1.title: Do not treat past inequitable decisions as ground truth for training
aib-c01-d3-070@1.prompt: A prioritization model for employment counseling is trained on records of people whom staff previously selected for assistance. An audit found that some offices excluded users with a particular work arrangement even when their circumstances were otherwise the same. Select two measures to take before training the model on those records.

learning.reason: Separate past decisions from the intended criteria, then independently reassess representative cases. After deployment, continue monitoring errors, including in the affected categories.
learning.concept: Do not assume past outcomes were valid; evaluate them against independent criteria and continue monitoring.

A.text: Remove the category from the decision records and consider the bias in the training labels eliminated.
A.explanation: Bias may remain in the original selection outcomes.

B.text: After release, continue comparing the model with verified operational decisions and track whether errors recur in the categories where problems were reported.
B.explanation: This helps detect a recurrence of inequities in post-training operations.

C.text: Use appropriate criteria to reassess representative cases and prepare verified training data rather than relying solely on past selections.
C.explanation: This reduces the risk of reproducing biased decisions as ground truth.

D.text: Leave past decisions unchanged because they reflect actual outcomes, and treat agreement with them as sufficient evidence of fairness.
D.explanation: A model can achieve high agreement even when it learns inequities that occurred in the past.

E.text: Evaluate only the largest office and exclude the categories where problems were reported from monitoring.
E.explanation: This prevents evaluation of the conditions that need improvement.

aib-c01-d3-071@1.title: Check whether generated output is subject to external license terms
aib-c01-d3-071@1.prompt: AI generated a short code routine for a product intended for distribution. A developer pointed out that a specific part closely resembles material unique to a third-party project. Company policy requires confirming permission to use external code before distribution. What should be done next?

learning.reason: Keep the suspicious content out of the distribution while its provenance and terms are checked. If those terms cannot be accepted, replace it with an approach that can be approved.
learning.concept: Before distributing work, have a person review recognizable externally derived content and the terms that apply to it.

A.text: Hold the suspicious part and review its provenance and terms of use. If the terms cannot be confirmed, do not use it; replace it with an approach that can be approved.
A.explanation: This allows rights requirements to be checked before distribution.

B.text: Change only the variable names and conclude that there is no need to check the terms that apply to the original material.
B.explanation: Changing names alone does not establish the material's provenance or applicable terms.

C.text: Disclose only the name of the generation tool and do not check whether use of the third-party project is permitted.
C.explanation: Identifying the generation tool does not establish permission to use external code.

D.text: Treat the code as meeting distribution requirements as long as it runs correctly.
D.explanation: Functional correctness and the terms for using external material are separate matters.

aib-c01-d3-072@1.title: Safely withholding an answer when supporting evidence is unavailable
aib-c01-d3-072@1.prompt: An AI assistant provides guidance on eligibility requirements. When its ability to retrieve approved materials goes down, it has been sending definitive answers based only on the model’s knowledge. The team wants to keep intake open, but it cannot send an answer whose requirements have not been verified in writing. What is an appropriate response?

learning.reason: If supporting evidence is unavailable, do not assert facts; route the case for confirmation or human review. Test outage behavior and verify that trustworthy evidence is available again before resuming normal responses.
learning.concept: Detect when required evidence becomes unavailable during a temporary disruption, and do not switch the affected workflow to unverified generation.

A.text: Keep displaying a normal response during the outage, then check after recovery whether users need corrections.
A.explanation: This sends unsupported information during the outage.

B.text: Always finalize the answer, because shortening it makes its supporting evidence clearer.
B.explanation: Changing the length does not provide evidence.

C.text: When an outage is detected, withhold any definitive statement about the requirements, acknowledge receipt, and route the case to someone who can verify it. Validate the behavior after recovery as well.
C.explanation: This keeps intake open while avoiding unsupported guidance.

D.text: Send an answer the model is likely to have generated in the past, even without consulting the supporting materials.
D.explanation: The answer has not been checked against the required materials.

aib-c01-d3-073@1.title: Helping users distinguish verified information from unverified guidance
aib-c01-d3-073@1.prompt: An AI assistant helps correct addresses. It displays the confirmed current address and an estimate of the delivery areas available at a new address in the same way. A user interpreted the estimate as confirmed. How should the display be improved?

learning.reason: Distinguish confirmed information from unverified suggestions, and tell users who can confirm a value and how. Test whether users understand the display.
learning.concept: Present which parts of an output are confirmed and where a person can verify the rest in a way users can understand.

A.text: Show the verification status of each value and how to check it next, then test whether users can distinguish suggestions from confirmed information.
A.explanation: This connects uncertainty to an actionable next step.

B.text: Mark everything as confirmed to keep the display consistent, and send a correction notice if one is needed later.
B.explanation: This increases the risk that users mistake an estimate for a confirmed fact.

C.text: Add general information about the model to the instructions, but do not show whether each value on screen has been verified.
C.explanation: Users still cannot distinguish the values where they need to make a decision.

D.text: Show only the estimate’s baseline next to the current address, without saying which information was actually verified.
D.explanation: The number does not show the status or what action the user should take.

aib-c01-d3-074@1.title: Designing an effective way to reach people who need a correction
aib-c01-d3-074@1.prompt: An AI assistant providing guidance on benefits applications will be accessible even to anonymous users. If it occasionally displays requirements from before a policy update, affected users must be able to find the correction without collecting additional personal information. What should the design include?

learning.reason: Show the policy version or effective date without increasing the collection of personally identifying information, and provide a correction history and a way to review it. Test that users can reach the correction.
learning.concept: Design a way to identify which guidance needs correction and notify affected users, instead of leaving them impossible to reach after the fact.

A.text: Let users check the version and date of the information they saw, provide corrections and a way to review them, and test this in advance.
A.explanation: Users can verify which information they saw and find any needed correction.

B.text: Display only a general disclaimer, and do not record the version or scope of the correction.
B.explanation: It is not possible to verify which guidance was corrected.

C.text: Require every user to provide their name and detailed personal records before viewing the guidance so delivery of explanations can be guaranteed.
C.explanation: This collects excessive identifying information for providing a correction.

D.text: Remove the old screen when a problem is found, without providing a correction path for people who already saw it.
D.explanation: People who saw the earlier guidance have no way to learn that it was wrong.

aib-c01-d3-075@1.title: Letting a person correct an outcome after a user reports an error
aib-c01-d3-075@1.prompt: An AI classifies an equipment application as ineligible. A staff member can receive an inquiry but cannot change the ineligible status, and the user can receive only the result of another assessment by the same AI. What change is needed for effective human oversight?

learning.reason: Let designated staff examine the evidence, correct an erroneous decision, and reopen the case. Keep a record of the correction and notification.
learning.concept: In addition to accepting appeals, enable reviewers to re-examine existing information and correct the operational status.

A.text: Allow all users to update application statuses, and do not perform human review.
A.explanation: This grants more access than needed and does not verify the basis for a correction.

B.text: Allow only another AI run, and treat an objection as invalid if the result is the same.
B.explanation: The same omission or error could be repeated.

C.text: Give designated staff authority to review the evidence again and reopen or correct the case, and record the basis for the decision and the notice sent to the user.
C.explanation: The outcome of human review can be applied to the actual process.

D.text: Have staff explain the reason, but prevent them from changing the application status or subsequent process.
D.explanation: An incorrect status cannot be corrected even when the user’s report is valid.

aib-c01-d3-076@1.title: Determine which workflows are subject to recordkeeping requirements
