aib-c01-d3-076@1.prompt: Internally, searches for general information do not need to be recorded, but when users agree to contract terms, the content and time of that agreement must be recorded. The same AI interface is expected to handle both. What is the most appropriate control to put in place before launch?

learning.reason: Clearly separate general information from agreements, and reliably record the required fields only when a user proceeds to an agreement. Test the transition and exception paths.
learning.concept: Map the business process and its recordkeeping requirements to the user workflow, rather than relying only on the AI feature’s name.

A.text: Handle general information and agreement through separate workflows, and verify that the agreement’s content and time are recorded and can be retrieved later.
A.explanation: This captures the evidence required for each business process.

B.text: Record general information in detail and infer the actual agreement from aggregate data provided by the service provider.
B.explanation: This does not identify what the individual agreed to.

C.text: Because both use the same interface, omit recordkeeping for agreements as though they were search requests.
C.explanation: The agreement’s content and time would not be retained.

D.text: Record the monthly number of agreements and treat that as sufficient to verify each individual agreement.
D.explanation: Aggregate counts and evidence of an individual agreement serve different purposes.

aib-c01-d3-077@1.title: Restrict where outputs can be sent using approval data
aib-c01-d3-077@1.prompt: An AI system summarizes sensitive materials and sends them to a designated administrative contact. An employee proposes using an address generated by the AI from the company name the user entered as the recipient. Which design ensures that messages are sent only to authorized recipients?

learning.reason: Use only recipients matched against the approved registry. Route mismatches and changes for verification, and record the authorization and sending outcome.
learning.concept: Enforce authorized destinations and roles on the service side instead of trusting generated recipient strings.

A.text: Display the recipient clearly, but let the send operation trust the AI’s input text.
A.explanation: The sending process cannot prevent delivery to an unauthorized recipient.

B.text: Have the send operation compare the recipient and permissions with an approved registry; if they do not match, hold the message and ask an employee to verify.
B.explanation: This prevents unconditional forwarding to an AI-generated address.

C.text: Provide a way to undo a misdirected message, but do not verify the address before sending.
C.explanation: Content delivered externally cannot always be retrieved.

D.text: Because the AI can distinguish similar company names, send whenever the output contains an email-formatted address.
D.explanation: An address’s format does not verify sending permission or whether it belongs to the actual administrative contact.

aib-c01-d3-078@1.title: Recognize that an effective control for one risk leaves other risks
aib-c01-d3-078@1.prompt: For a customer-facing AI system, a change was made so that facility information is retrieved from the latest version, and incorrect opening hours no longer appear. However, inquiries include personal records, and employees without a business need can also view the logs. What should be updated in the assessment?

learning.reason: Separate controls for information accuracy from controls for access to information. Even if accuracy improves, the risk from who can view the logs still needs to be assessed and addressed.
learning.concept: Assign controls and evidence to the specific risks they address; do not classify all risks as low based on a single control.

A.text: Use a single combined score and offset the access issue with the improvement in accuracy.
A.explanation: This does not resolve unauthorized access to personal records.

B.text: Record the log access risk as low because the accuracy tests passed.
B.explanation: An accuracy control does not restrict who can view the logs.

C.text: Because the access risk remains, delete the test records that established the accuracy improvement and mark everything as unassessed.
C.explanation: This discards evidence of a control’s demonstrated effectiveness.

D.text: Mark the accuracy control as verified, and assess and address log access separately as a residual risk.
D.explanation: This clarifies which risk each control changed.

aib-c01-d3-079@1.title: Stop harmful generated content from being distributed from its copies
aib-c01-d3-079@1.prompt: One asset created by an advertising AI has been found to demean people with a particular attribute. The same asset has been copied to several regions, and some copies are scheduled for distribution the next morning. After disabling future generation, what should be done first?

learning.reason: Check destinations and schedules, and cancel distribution before the affected asset is delivered. Preserve necessary evidence and investigate where it may already have been published.
learning.concept: Do not stop at disabling generation; track stored assets and scheduled distributions to prevent further impact.

A.text: Defer action until the next model test, and stop the next morning’s distribution only if a customer requests removal.
A.explanation: This leaves the risk that the confirmed harmful content will be distributed first.

B.text: Use the asset version to identify copies and scheduled distributions, put distribution on hold, and have an employee verify the scope of anything already published and the response evidence.
B.explanation: This stops current spread and enables impact assessment and any necessary corrections.

C.text: Delete only the original generated file, without checking shared locations in other regions or the schedule.
C.explanation: Deleting the original does not remove copied assets or scheduled distributions.

D.text: Stop only new generation, and allow all already approved scheduled distributions to proceed as planned.
D.explanation: The problematic asset will spread through the scheduled channels.

aib-c01-d3-080@1.title: Validate fluent notices against existing records
aib-c01-d3-080@1.prompt: An AI system drafts product recall notices using product versions in an existing registry. In testing, the format and quantities were correct, but one example described an in-scope product as out of scope and vice versa. The existing registry contains the definitive list of affected products. Which safeguard is needed?

learning.reason: Compare the product versions covered by each notice with the definitive registry. Hold discrepancies for review and retain enough information to determine which data and result were used.
learning.concept: Even when generated content looks correct, compare it with business records that establish definitive values or states before sending it to the next step.

A.text: Reconcile the notices only after they have been sent automatically so affected customers can be notified first.
A.explanation: A notice for the wrong product could be sent before the check.

B.text: Send only notices that read naturally, and skip validation of which product versions are affected.
B.explanation: Writing style does not show whether the notice identifies the right products.

C.text: Before sending a notice, compare its product versions against the definitive registry and hold any discrepancies for review.
C.explanation: This can catch a reversal in meaning that formatting checks alone would miss.

D.text: Accept notices if their total count is similar to previous runs, even if affected and unaffected products are switched.
D.explanation: The count does not reveal which product versions were described incorrectly.

aib-c01-d4-061@1.title: Verify individual readiness claims through a real handoff
aib-c01-d4-061@1.prompt: In a readiness review for AI-assisted equipment intake, the operations team, data team, and approval group each say their own work is ready. However, they have not processed a representative case through the entire workflow, and it is not yet clear whether an intake delay or a switch to manual handling will be communicated. What evidence should be obtained before deciding to launch?

learning.reason: Run a representative case and exception through the relevant teams to verify that the required inputs, decisions, handoffs, and fallback can be completed on time.
learning.concept: Do not rely only on readiness claims from individual teams; verify that data delivery, approvals, and exception handling work together on a representative case.

A.text: Decide which teams to contact only after production begins, and treat an announced launch date as evidence of readiness.
A.explanation: This leaves responsibility undefined until an exception occurs and may disrupt business continuity.

B.text: Measure model accuracy and availability again, but exclude handoffs during data delays from the readiness assessment.
B.explanation: This does not verify the cross-team operations needed to complete the work.

C.text: Have the relevant teams rehearse a representative case and a switch triggered by a data delay, then verify the owners, handoff times, and final outcome.
C.explanation: This provides operational evidence that the teams' assumptions align and the workflow succeeds.

D.text: Score each team's self-assessment and conclude that handoffs will succeed if the average exceeds a threshold.
D.explanation: Teams can each report readiness without proving that the workflow works under conditions requiring coordination.

aib-c01-d4-062@1.title: Check whether multi-team operations can be scaled repeatably
aib-c01-d4-062@1.prompt: A company operates AI systems independently in production across six departments. Each new department rebuilds its own approvals, incident response, and monitoring, and the previous department's owner cannot move on each time another system launches. What is the most useful evidence for judging the maturity of enterprise-wide rollout?

learning.reason: Measure whether subsequent departments can use shared foundations, support mechanisms, and controls to deploy repeatably while maintaining quality.
learning.concept: Judge maturity by evidence that later departments can sustain operations under common standards, not just by the number of deployments.

A.text: Check only whether the number of production screens doubled over six months.
A.explanation: That does not show that repeatability improved or operational dependence decreased.

B.text: Identify the department with the highest usage among the six and treat its usage as the company's maturity level.
B.explanation: One department's usage does not show whether other departments can launch independently.

C.text: Demonstrate that subsequent departments can launch using common approvals, monitoring, and support while sustaining ownership and quality.
C.explanation: This measures the capability to scale, rather than just the number of deployments or people.

D.text: Allow a new department to launch only while the previous owner continues to help, and do not assess operations after that owner leaves.
D.explanation: This leaves the staffing constraint that will worsen as the rollout expands.

aib-c01-d4-063@1.title: Find why cases remain open despite success in each department
aib-c01-d4-063@1.prompt: Three departments each test AI-assisted intake, approval, and notification, and each system behaves as required. However, the criteria for closing a case differ by department, so some cases remain incomplete even after a notification has been sent. Which capability should be strengthened?

learning.reason: Establish an owner for the end-to-end workflow, shared states from start to finish, and handoffs between departments.
learning.concept: Separate the successful completion of individual steps from the missing ownership and shared status needed to complete the entire workflow.

A.text: Repeat training in each department to improve generation accuracy, while leaving the status criteria unchanged.
A.explanation: This does not address the lack of a shared completion state.

B.text: Keep completion criteria specific to each department and do not count cases that have stalled.
B.explanation: This does not align workflow states across departments.

C.text: Assign ownership for the end-to-end case and define shared states and completion criteria that every department can verify.
C.explanation: Clear ownership and handoffs can prevent cases from being left unresolved.

D.text: Have the department handling the most cases mark them all complete without checking the statuses in other departments.
D.explanation: This does not verify whether the work required for each case is finished.

aib-c01-d4-064@1.title: Fund repeatable capabilities instead of adding more pilots
aib-c01-d4-064@1.prompt: Across a group of companies, pilots for nearly identical document-search use cases have succeeded repeatedly. However, few departments have moved them into production because each new department has to create its own measurement approach from scratch. Which policy would allocate the next budget most effectively?

learning.reason: Instead of increasing the number of pilots based on the same hypothesis, establish common evaluation and operating practices and confirm that representative departments can run them as part of routine operations.
learning.concept: Once effectiveness has already been demonstrated, invest in the shared operational capabilities that are limiting current maturity.

A.text: Run additional pilots based on the same hypothesis in every department, prioritizing the number of reported successes.
A.explanation: This does not establish shared operations or evaluation.

B.text: Eliminate individual quality checks to increase the number of deployments to production.
B.explanation: This does not build the capability to scale while maintaining quality.

C.text: Replace the platform with a higher-performance version and treat it as production even if operational ownership and measurement methods have not been identified.
C.explanation: This does not change the business capabilities that are currently holding progress back.

D.text: Allocate budget to common evaluation practices and staff development, then measure whether rollout teams can verify quality and operate the solution using the same process.
D.explanation: This addresses the capabilities that are slowing the transition from pilots to production.

aib-c01-d4-065@1.title: Verify the authoritative version, not the document count
aib-c01-d4-065@1.prompt: You are preparing product warranty guidance. The sales department has a communications draft, Legal has an approved version, and Support still has a procedure that points to an old version. You want to make PDFs from all three departments searchable, but documents with the same title have different terms and effective dates. Which data preparation approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Verify who owns the authoritative material and when it applies, and assemble information that distinguishes the current version from any history that must be retained. Use representative examples to confirm the correct document and effective period.
learning.concept: Check document versions and effective periods across departments to verify that materials are prepared as usable evidence.

A.text: Verify the owner, authoritative version, and effective period, then validate version references using an inventory and representative warranty guidance.
A.explanation: This assembles the information needed to identify evidence that can be used in business operations.

B.text: Treat a larger searchable corpus as evidence of greater readiness, and defer comparisons for cases where an outdated document is returned.
B.explanation: A larger number of documents does not resolve conflicting terms.

C.text: Automatically adopt the document with the most recent creation date without checking formal approval or effective date.
C.explanation: A recently created document may still be unapproved or intended to take effect in the future.

D.text: Ingest every file and treat the first document with a matching title as the current version.
D.explanation: This cannot distinguish the terms and expiration dates of documents with the same title.

aib-c01-d4-066@1.title: Establish approval before using shared data for a new purpose
aib-c01-d4-066@1.prompt: Three departments that manage facilities share maintenance records. Their original agreement permits use only to support incident investigations. A new department also wants to use the records to evaluate employees' work performance. What is the appropriate approach to the shared data?

learning.reason: Review the new purpose, required fields, and conditions of use with the data owner. Share only within the authorized scope and distinguish the new use from existing access.
learning.concept: Distinguish technical access from permission to use data for a business purpose, and agree on the purpose and scope with the provider.

A.text: Remove only the users' names, then permit use without regard to the original purpose of the sharing.
A.explanation: Removing names does not change the purpose limitation.

B.text: Keep the existing agreement unchanged and have each evaluator make and manage an individual copy of all the data.
B.explanation: This does not govern authorization for the new purpose or the scope of sharing.

C.text: Treat the data as available for unrestricted reuse in any business function because it can already be viewed in the shared location.
C.explanation: This exceeds the purpose for which use was authorized.

D.text: Review the new purpose and reuse conditions with the data owner, then document purpose-specific permissions and responsibilities.
D.explanation: This allows the authorized scope of sharing to be checked against the new business use.

aib-c01-d4-067@1.title: Assess platform prerequisites for future traceability
aib-c01-d4-067@1.prompt: You are selecting a platform for a support AI assistant. For each inquiry, staff must be able to later identify which model and policy version were used and which business workflow received the handoff. The feature list includes operational monitoring, but it has not been confirmed whether the platform can support this kind of linkage. Which platform evaluation is appropriate?

learning.reason: Test representative inquiries to see whether reference IDs can link the required versions and actions across each processing stage. Also verify access permissions and retention conditions for the records.
learning.concept: Verify that the platform can link not only the model but also ingestion, configuration, reference data, and business outcomes.

A.text: Check only whether administrators can view a breakdown in the console, and configure policy-version logging after launch.
A.explanation: This does not verify during platform selection that the requirements can be met.

B.text: Use representative cases to trace from an inquiry ID to the model, policy, and processing destination, and validate access and retention as well.
B.explanation: This determines whether the requirements can be met in actual operations.

C.text: Assume that if the platform displays inference usage counts, the provenance of each individual case can be determined later.
C.explanation: Aggregate counts do not show the configuration and business outcome of each case.

D.text: Store only the full text of each inquiry, without retaining the versions used or the staff responsible for processing it.
D.explanation: This does not make it possible to reconstruct what informed a business decision.

aib-c01-d4-068@1.title: Connecting frontline evidence from champions to executive decisions
aib-c01-d4-068@1.prompt: Company-wide AI champions raise issues several times a month, but the executive committee looks only at the number of users when approving the next rollout. Two departments still have unresolved quality issues. What operating practice should the sponsor change first?

learning.reason: The sponsor should consider user numbers alongside business outcomes and quality when deciding on investment. They should receive reports of obstacles from champions, authorize the necessary support and owners, and communicate the resulting decisions.
learning.concept: Executives own outcomes and decisions, while frontline champions need a way to report actual improvements and obstacles.

A.text: As long as user numbers are increasing, have champions report only positive examples after launch.
A.explanation: Quality issues and obstacles will not reach funding decisions.

B.text: Bring quality and impact evidence from champions into decision-making, and have executives assign owners and deadlines and revisit rollout criteria.
B.explanation: This lets executives use their authority to provide support and decide on expansion instead of leaving the causes entirely to frontline teams.

C.text: Let each champion decide whether to expand using separate quality criteria, then combine the results in one table later.
C.explanation: Outcomes and constraints cannot be compared across departments using a common standard.

D.text: Have executives announce results without assigning owners to problems that span multiple departments.
D.explanation: The decisions needed for coordination will not be made.

aib-c01-d4-069@1.title: Defining acceptance responsibility for the handoff from development to operations
aib-c01-d4-069@1.prompt: The team that developed an equipment-support AI will move to another project next month. The operations team will own quality and exceptions after go-live, but has not seen the trial decision rationale or recovery procedures. What is needed when transitioning across teams?

learning.reason: Development hands over the reproduction procedures and the rationale for acceptance criteria. Operations rehearses the practical procedures and recovery before accepting the handoff. Assign an owner and deadline to any remaining items.
learning.concept: The technical team hands over procedures and change information, and both teams verify that operations can respond.

A.text: Development shares the criteria and reproduction procedures, and operations rehearses exception handling and recovery. Together, they decide whether the handoff is accepted and assign owners to remaining items.
A.explanation: Knowledge is transferred, and the next operations team can confirm its ability to respond.

B.text: Development sends documentation and transfers ownership; operations checks after launch whether it can restore the service in practice.
B.explanation: The required capabilities are not verified before the handoff.

C.text: Operations assigns on-call staff but leaves the configuration, quality decision criteria, and recovery destination information with development.
C.explanation: Operations staff cannot access the information they need when responding.

D.text: To remove friction from the handoff, give everyone the same administrative permissions as development and leave ownership unassigned.
D.explanation: Responsibilities and least-privilege access become unclear.

aib-c01-d4-070@1.title: Explaining to employees how AI usage records will be used
aib-c01-d4-070@1.prompt: A company records user actions and errors to improve the usability of its AI. Employees worry that the content of what they say may be routinely sent to HR for performance reviews. Under the policy, access is limited to authorized viewers and the records will not be used for performance reviews. What should the company explain?

learning.reason: Explain the data collected, its purpose, access and retention, and the restriction against other uses. Also provide a channel for raising concerns or requesting corrections.
learning.concept: Explain the purpose of usage data, what it will not be used for, who can view it, and where employees can ask questions to reduce misunderstandings.

A.text: Do not disclose that records are collected; share only the improvements after rollout.
A.explanation: This omits information people need to understand and trust the practice.

B.text: To remove concerns, say that no error records are collected at all.
B.explanation: That would not match the actual usage and the explanation.

C.text: Notify employees only that the purpose is improvement, and let administrators decide later what can be viewed based on their requests.
C.explanation: This does not address questions about the scope of collection or access.

D.text: Explain what is collected, why, who can use it, and how long it is retained. Point to the policy that excludes performance reviews and provide a contact for questions.
D.explanation: Being clear about actual data handling can reduce mismatches with employees' expectations.

aib-c01-d4-071@1.title: Checking whether usage-count awards encourage inappropriate AI use
aib-c01-d4-071@1.prompt: A business unit has started giving awards based on the number of AI interactions, and employees now use AI even for work that is not suited to it. People who report errors spend more time stopping use, which lowers their ranking. Which intervention will establish responsible use?

learning.reason: Evaluate appropriate use, quality, and learning from errors instead of rewarding interaction counts alone. Managers should support employees who decide to stop using AI when appropriate.
learning.concept: Revise evaluation criteria and managerial responses when practices that reward usage volume discourage careful use.

A.text: Revisit the usage-count competition and reward quality, appropriate use, and issue reporting. Have managers support decisions to stop using AI.
A.explanation: The organization can reinforce desirable work practices and outcomes.

B.text: Eliminate all usage records and set no measures for quality or whether the use case is appropriate.
B.explanation: There will be no way to assess responsible use or improvement.

C.text: Reprimand individuals who use AI dangerously, but keep the usage-count competition in place.
C.explanation: This does not change the organizational incentives that produced the behavior.

D.text: Raise the usage target further and make error reporting additional work for individuals, without tracking the time it takes.
D.explanation: This puts more emphasis on usage counts and increases the incentive to hide problems.

aib-c01-d4-072@1.title: Keep training current as workflows change
aib-c01-d4-072@1.prompt: Everyone completed the initial training. Since then, the requirements for documents that can be submitted and the procedure for handing a case to a person when the AI holds a result have changed. Staff are still practicing the old procedure. Which training approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Help staff who use the changed procedure practice the permitted scope and handoff with updated examples. Identify any skill gaps and provide additional support.
learning.concept: Use practice to confirm that staff can follow the latest procedures required for their roles, and update their knowledge when operating conditions change.

A.text: Because the initial training is complete, provide no training on the new requirements and measure no impact until next year.
A.explanation: This does not establish whether staff can perform the newly required tasks.

B.text: Have staff rehearse the updated workflow using examples of the changed document requirements and handoff procedure, then confirm they can follow it.
B.explanation: This assesses whether their skills match the work that has actually changed.

C.text: Tell only managers about the new procedure and let users continue handling cases under the old version.
C.explanation: Errors in submissions and handoffs will persist.

D.text: Have everyone repeat all introductory lectures unchanged and measure only how many terms they remember.
D.explanation: This does not give staff practice with the updated work.

aib-c01-d4-073@1.title: Use AI to streamline preparation while people negotiate and decide
aib-c01-d4-073@1.prompt: Procurement staff spend a great deal of time organizing historical prices and contract terms. Contract renewals also require negotiating terms with external parties and deciding which conditions are non-negotiable. Which division of work is appropriate after introducing AI?

learning.reason: AI can organize approved records. Staff verify the evidence, listen to the other party's needs, negotiate terms, and approve the outcome.
learning.concept: Use AI to organize options and assign people to understand conflicting interests and reach agreement.

A.text: Rank every contract using only future prices and prevent staff from reviewing other terms.
A.explanation: This leaves out the conditions that need to be negotiated.

B.text: Have AI prepare comparison materials, then have staff review them, negotiate, and make the final decision.
B.explanation: This streamlines routine preparation while preserving human dialogue and discretion.

C.text: Have people collect all the materials and AI negotiate with the other party and finalize the contract.
C.explanation: This retains the labor-intensive routine work while transferring important decisions to a machine.

D.text: Evaluate how much time AI was used, without assigning responsibility for discussions with suppliers or outcomes.
D.explanation: This does not redesign the actual work.

aib-c01-d4-074@1.title: Test the operational hypothesis even after validating accuracy
aib-c01-d4-074@1.prompt: Document classification passed testing on historical materials, but no one has checked whether staff in the next stage can look at the AI's output and quickly determine the priority order. The company plans to introduce it to reduce intake time. What should happen next?

learning.reason: Record the technical result while also testing the display, decision time, and quality in a setting close to actual operations. Use the findings to choose the conditions for rollout.
learning.concept: Test technical and operational hypotheses separately during an experiment, gather evidence, and use it to choose the next stage.

A.text: Run a limited trial in which staff use the classifications, measure both processing time and decision accuracy, and use the results to decide the next stage.
A.explanation: This tests the operational hypothesis before proceeding safely.

B.text: Move to production based only on passing the technical accuracy test, and measure staff decision time for the first time later.
B.explanation: The capability that serves the business objective remains unverified.

C.text: Skip a real-world trial and have the development team estimate processing time in seconds and report that as a reduction.
C.explanation: Neither actual effort nor work quality has been verified.

D.text: Exclude the staff who do the work from the trial and treat adding more historical classification data as the only new validation.
D.explanation: This cannot measure whether the output helps people make decisions.

aib-c01-d4-075@1.title: Turn a shared short-term win into a common capability
aib-c01-d4-075@1.prompt: One department achieved a short-term win with a system that separates signed documents from drafts. Other departments have different approval procedures, but they also need to distinguish these document types. How should the rollout continue?

learning.reason: Provide the validated classification as a shared capability, with clear ownership for its version, quality, and support. Each department can retain its own approval procedure and validate the integration.
learning.concept: Turn a proven shared capability into a maintained offering with clear service conditions and ownership, separate from department-specific workflows.

A.text: Turn the validated classification into a shared capability with a clear version and owner, then test how it connects to each department's approvals and assess quality in practice.
A.explanation: This extends the short-term win to multiple departments while preserving their distinct workflows.

B.text: Only include each department's results in a presentation, and have everyone build the same classification separately.
B.explanation: This does not maintain a shared capability or reuse what was learned.

C.text: Transfer the successful department's entire approval process to the others and uniformly replace their existing responsibilities and procedures.
C.explanation: This changes more of the workflow than the reusable capability requires.

D.text: Without defining the capability or an owner, make every department request each operation from the original staff member as needed.
D.explanation: The rollout would continue to depend on the same person each time.

aib-c01-d4-076@1.title: Capturing field exceptions to shared operating standards
aib-c01-d4-076@1.prompt: An AI center of excellence has established company-wide pilot procedures. Recently, three exception requests came from departments using the same data environment, saying that the common tests cannot validate important formats. What should the center of excellence do?

learning.reason: Assess whether the center of excellence can handle the rationale, safeguards, and duration of each exception individually, and incorporate recurring issues into common tests or applicability conditions.
learning.concept: The center of excellence handles exceptions and uses issues shared across departments to improve standards.

A.text: Grant every exception permanently and never update the original standards or records of how the exceptions were handled.
A.explanation: The common requirements would become ineffective, and the same exceptions would continue.

B.text: Prioritize the wording of the common standards and do not investigate the conditions under which the tests cannot be performed appropriately.
B.explanation: The organization would remain unable to assess the quality needed in practice.

C.text: Verify the quality required under the exceptions and feed the results back into the common standards. Make reproducible tests available to other departments as well.
C.explanation: This incorporates field constraints and improves the common standards while maintaining them.

D.text: Take evaluation work away from the departments that requested exceptions and have the center of excellence declare the results correct on its own.
D.explanation: This does not check the field conditions or whether the results meet requirements.

aib-c01-d4-077@1.title: Reconnecting evaluation to changing business priorities
aib-c01-d4-077@1.prompt: The initial goal of AI assistance was to reduce intake time. In the following year, reducing inquiries that do not lead to formal procedures became more important, and time-only metrics could no longer explain the value to the teams doing the work. Which measurement approach would improve operations?

learning.reason: Keep the time metric for historical comparison and define new metrics for completion and drop-offs. Combine them with reports from the teams doing the work to understand which objectives improved.
learning.concept: Keep measurements from the outset while explicitly tracking new business goals and revised metrics to guide continuation decisions.

A.text: Do not begin measuring new metrics while the time reduction continues, even if the top priority has changed.
A.explanation: This would delay identifying the new business challenge.

B.text: To simplify reporting, discard historical time records and apply only the number of completed cases to results for prior periods.
B.explanation: This would make it impossible to distinguish progress toward the old goal from changes in the new outcome.

C.text: Preserve the existing time-reduction trend, add completion rates and reasons for dropping out, and evaluate the continuation criteria alongside feedback from the teams doing the work.
C.explanation: This allows the organization to observe both the changed strategy and the operational outcomes it still wants to maintain.

D.text: Make the metric that improved the most each month the top priority, without recording changes to the criteria or the reasons for them.
D.explanation: This would not support tracking stable, long-term value.

aib-c01-d4-078@1.title: Keeping prototype exceptions out of production
aib-c01-d4-078@1.prompt: In the AI prototype, a temporary setting allowed a small team to view samples from all cases. In production, each person must be able to view only cases belonging to their department. The prototype passed its accuracy criteria. Choose two production acceptance criteria.

learning.reason: Replace the prototype's temporary access with formal permissions and test cross-department allow and deny cases in the acceptance environment. Remove prototype exceptions and define ownership and review of formal access.
learning.concept: Inventory temporary access and data-handling arrangements used for experiments, then replace them with formal permissions and operations.

A.text: Use least privilege for production and verify that permitted cases and cases from other departments are handled as specified.
A.explanation: This confirms before operation that formal access controls work.

B.text: Because the trial had no problems, carry the exception allowing access to all cases over to the formal assignment.
B.explanation: This conflicts with the department-specific restrictions required in production.

C.text: Change the trial interface to a different color and do not make matching access settings an acceptance criterion.
C.explanation: Changing the interface does not change permissions.

D.text: Disable the exception path and designate the department responsible for granting, changing, and reviewing formal permissions.
D.explanation: This removes temporary access and assigns responsibility for ongoing operations.

E.text: Tell the model, “Do not view other departments’ cases,” and proceed to production without adding access controls to the data itself.
E.explanation: This relies on generated text to enforce a restriction that must be enforced by the system.

aib-c01-d4-079@1.title: Enabling handoffs for unresolved issues across regions
aib-c01-d4-079@1.prompt: An AI service is shared across three regions, but support is provided only during the daytime by the team in one existing region. The pilot's processing speed is normal, but an issue that occurs overnight in another region remains unattended until the next day. What should be put in place before rollout to all regions?

learning.reason: Check regional business hours and response deadlines, then provide support that maintains clear ownership. Exercise handoffs across time zones and the activation of backup coverage.
learning.concept: When expanding a shared service, plan not only for availability but also for support hours, ownership, and transfer of unresolved cases.

A.text: Keep separate response histories in each region and do not share unresolved issues with other regions.
A.explanation: Ownership of decisions and responses would be lost during handoffs.

B.text: Centralize incident intake, but assign responders only when daytime begins in the existing region.
B.explanation: Some regions would still have issues that cannot be addressed within their required time.

C.text: Assume that each region's response deadlines are met as long as everyone worldwide can open the same screen.
C.explanation: Technical access and the hours during which support is actually available are different.

D.text: Define on-call coverage and handoffs that meet each region's deadlines, then test whether issue status and ownership carry over to the next coverage period.
D.explanation: This validates operational continuity before expanding to all regions.

aib-c01-d4-080@1.title: Keep generated labels distinct from labels that have been verified
aib-c01-d4-080@1.prompt: Several departments share records of inquiries. From now on, the same field will store both classifications assigned by staff and classifications provisionally entered by AI. Another department will use that field to obtain ground truth for the next model. What should the shared rules require?

learning.reason: Record staff verification and AI’s provisional output as distinct states. The owner defines permitted uses and enforces the requirement that training data be verified.
learning.concept: In a shared-use framework, make clear which values come from source data, which come from AI, whether they have been verified, and what they may be used for.

A.text: The team entering records does not record whether a classification was verified, and the other department later guesses the accuracy of every record.
A.explanation: Information about how the data was created and judged is lost when it is needed.

B.text: Keep the value’s provenance separate from its verification status, and state in the shared specification that only records verified by staff may be used as training data.
B.explanation: Users can select records that are suitable as ground truth for their purpose.

C.text: If the text of a record is the same, provide it as training ground truth regardless of who entered it or whether it was verified.
C.explanation: An unverified prediction becomes ground truth for the next model, carrying its errors forward.

D.text: Delete only some AI-classified examples and do not tell the other department which fields it may use.
D.explanation: The meaning of shared use and verification status cannot be managed consistently.

aib-c01-d1-085@1.title: Check whether prediction ranges can support staffing plans
aib-c01-d1-085@1.prompt: A service desk demand model provides an estimate of the next day’s visitor count and an 80% prediction range each day. Staff want to use the range to decide how many people to bring in for extra coverage. Which evaluation should they use to find out whether the range is useful?

learning.reason: For representative days, calculate the proportion of actual visitor counts that fall within the range. Also check its width and differences across conditions, because a range that is too wide may not help with staffing.
learning.concept: Validate a prediction range against actual coverage and useful width, in addition to point-forecast error.

A.text: Conclude that the 80% range is meaningless if actual demand falls outside it on even one day.
A.explanation: An 80% range is not expected to include every day.

B.text: Measure only the average difference between the point forecast and actual demand, and do not examine the range.
B.explanation: Point-forecast accuracy does not reveal the proportion of observations that fell within the range.

C.text: Measure how often actual demand falls within the range on representative days and how wide the range is, then check whether it supports staffing plans even on busy days.
C.explanation: This evaluates both coverage against actual demand and whether the range is useful for decisions.

D.text: Widen the range until it includes every day, without interpreting which weekdays require staffing.
D.explanation: Coverage alone does not show whether the range is narrow enough to help with planning.

aib-c01-d1-086@1.title: Choose a feature that ranks existing options for recommendations
aib-c01-d1-086@1.prompt: A corporate learning portal wants to recommend an order for existing courses that learners can take, based on their experience. Course content and prerequisites must not change. There is also no need to generate courses that are not available. What is the most appropriate approach?

learning.reason: Constrain the candidates using eligibility rules, then rank them by fit with the learner’s experience and intended outcomes. If needed, generate only an explanation for the recommendation.
learning.concept: Distinguish ranking existing candidates by relative priority from generating new content.

A.text: Freely generate titles for new courses from requested content and display them as if they existed in the portal.
A.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to return only courses that are currently available.

B.text: Without checking which courses are available, show everyone only the course that has been opened most often overall.
B.explanation: This does not account for learners’ experience or course prerequisites.

C.text: Filter for courses the learner is eligible to take, rank them by fit with the learner’s experience and learning outcomes, and return the IDs of real courses.
C.explanation: The goal is to rank approved candidates, not create fictional courses.

D.text: Sort courses by the date they were first created and treat the oldest ones as the best learning recommendations.
D.explanation: Creation date does not indicate how well a course suits a learner.

aib-c01-d1-087@1.title: Do not determine service-area eligibility from an address string alone
aib-c01-d1-087@1.prompt: An inspection service’s visitable area changes at road boundaries, even within the same postal code. The service has registered address strings and map data representing its official service boundary. Before AI generates an explanation, which data processing step should determine whether a location is eligible?

learning.reason: Convert the address to a location that can be checked, then compare it with the validated boundary using the same coordinate conditions. If the location is ambiguous, defer the decision.
learning.concept: Treat address formatting and coordinate data for comparing against a region’s boundary as separate things.

A.text: Decide based only on the proportion of past visitors, and keep previous eligibility decisions even if the official boundary changes.
A.explanation: This may not match the official service area.

B.text: Convert the address to a verifiable location and compare it with the official boundary; if the location cannot be identified, request verification.
B.explanation: This separates variations in address formatting from the business’s geographic requirements.

C.text: Classify the location using the first words in the address and the postal code, ignoring differences across roads.
C.explanation: This cannot handle eligibility that varies within the same postal code.

D.text: Summarize an image of the map in text and declare the location eligible if the address resembles the description.
D.explanation: This does not verify the boundary against the location.

aib-c01-d1-088@1.title: Learn to distinguish administrative closure from actual resolution
aib-c01-d1-088@1.prompt: You want to use AI to estimate whether an inquiry is likely to be resolved. The ledger marks an inquiry as “closed” not only when the customer’s issue is resolved, but also when the customer leaves without waiting for a response. Closure is predicted accurately, but it is unclear whether this helps improve the service. How should you change the training setup?

learning.reason: Administrative closure is not the same as actual resolution. Use confirmed resolution outcomes or independently verified cases as training labels, and distinguish them from abandonment.
learning.concept: Use confirmed outcomes that represent the business objective as labels, rather than an easy-to-measure proxy.

A.text: Predict closure, then convert the regression output into a long explanatory text and treat it as resolution.
A.explanation: Changing the output format does not change what the model was supervised to predict.

B.text: Distinguish resolution, abandonment, and indeterminate cases using independent evidence, and evaluate the model with resolution as the target.
B.explanation: This aligns the training objective with the business outcome you want to achieve.

C.text: Because the closure records are clear, treat every case as resolved by the user.
C.explanation: Cases that were abandoned would also be learned as successes.

D.text: Because closure prediction remains accurate, do not seek separate records of resolution.
D.explanation: The predicted outcome does not match the service outcome you want.

aib-c01-d1-089@1.title: Compare an agent’s report with the actual operation results
aib-c01-d1-089@1.prompt: In a test equipment ledger, an agent handles the process for returning borrowed equipment. Its response says “Return complete,” but it may have updated the status of a different item during the process. What should you evaluate to determine whether the agent is ready for business use?

learning.reason: The response alone does not reveal which item the agent operated on or the final result. Compare the executed operations, their targets, the intended outcome, and changes to other items against the test ledger.
learning.concept: Because agents choose and execute multiple operations, validate conversational correctness separately from the final ledger state and side effects.

A.text: Check only that the response exactly matches “Return complete,” and do not score changes to the ledger.
A.explanation: Even if the wording is correct, that does not show that a different item was left unchanged.

B.text: If the total number of returned items increases by one, do not check which individual item was affected.
B.explanation: The total can be correct even when the wrong item was updated.

C.text: Measure how many operations the agent performed, and treat a lower count as evidence that it handled the correct item.
C.explanation: The agent can act on the wrong item even when it uses fewer operations.

D.text: Compare the operation history with the final ledger, verifying that the specified item is marked as returned and unrelated items were not changed.
D.explanation: This separately verifies the intended result and unauthorized side effects.

aib-c01-d1-090@1.title: Do not judge by counts alone when model use changes
aib-c01-d1-090@1.prompt: An AI that extracts product codes was used on repair forms that met the required criteria. Recently, staff have also started using it on attached photos with little text, and the overall accuracy has fallen. What should you do to investigate the cause while maintaining the existing workflow for repair forms?

learning.reason: Measure usage volume and quality for each input path to determine whether the existing use has degraded or an unexpected use has been added. Use the results to update the permitted scope or evaluation.
learning.concept: A shift in the mix of new use cases can change a simple average, so measure quality separately for the original and new uses.

A.text: Compare performance and volume separately for repair forms and photos, then determine whether the unexpected photo inputs need a separate route or tests.
A.explanation: This lets you address unexpected use separately from the existing quality requirements.

B.text: Delete photo records until the volume is about the same as before, and report that there was no decline.
B.explanation: This hides the actual increase in use and the resulting errors.

C.text: Without checking accuracy, allow photo use as long as the AI responds quickly.
C.explanation: A short response time does not guarantee that the extracted values are correct.

D.text: Because overall accuracy has fallen, rebuild the model used for repair forms without investigating the use cases.
D.explanation: This does not establish whether quality has also declined for the existing use.

aib-c01-d1-091@1.title: Test a stable output format with a small number of examples
aib-c01-d1-091@1.prompt: An internal AI can correctly extract approved values, but the order of the fields does not match a custom handoff specification. You have only a few correct input-output examples, and there is no need to incorporate new business knowledge. Choose two appropriate measures.

learning.reason: State the format explicitly, provide a few representative examples, and mechanically check the format on separate evaluation examples. There is no need to adjust model weights immediately with only a few examples.
learning.concept: When the goal is a stable output format and only a few examples are available, specify the format with a small number of examples before considering fine-tuning.

A.text: Test whether the order and values match the specification using a field arrangement not used in the examples.
A.explanation: This checks whether the format generalizes beyond memorizing the examples.

B.text: Add the ordering rules and a small number of correct input-output examples to the prompt.
B.explanation: This communicates the desired format to the existing model.

C.text: Assume that the receiving team will re-enter the displayed order every time, and do not record the format mismatch.
C.explanation: The rework caused by the specification mismatch would remain.

D.text: To update the trained weights, duplicate a few examples many times and use the same examples to judge whether the model passes.
D.explanation: There are neither diverse examples nor an independent performance check.

E.text: Keep adding large volumes of unchanged reference documents through retrieval until the field order becomes consistent.
E.explanation: More reference material will not clarify the desired format.

aib-c01-d1-092@1.title: Do Not Present a Ranking Score as a Probability
aib-c01-d1-092@1.prompt: A sales opportunity ranking model assigns priorities on a scale of 0 to 100. It is validated by the ordering of the top 10 selections, but the meaning of its scores as probabilities has not been checked. A representative wants to display “a priority of 75 means a 75% chance of closing this month.” Which explanation is appropriate?

learning.reason: A number designed to rank opportunities cannot be interpreted as a probability of an outcome. To use it as a probability, define the time period and evaluate whether observed outcomes match the predictions for groups of opportunities with similar scores.
learning.concept: Treat an output designed for ranking as a probability only when there is evidence that it has been validated for individual event rates.

A.text: Use the priority score only for ranking. To display it as a probability, validate it separately against actual outcomes over a defined time period.
A.explanation: This distinguishes what has been validated from what still requires additional validation.

B.text: Because the score is between 0 and 100, treat a priority of 75 as a 75% probability of closing this month.
B.explanation: The numeric range does not guarantee what the output means.

C.text: Subtract the average score across all opportunities from each priority score; the resulting value will be the actual probability of closing.
C.explanation: Transforming scores using the average does not establish a relationship with observed event rates.

D.text: If the top 10 opportunities are ranked correctly, treat every score across all opportunities as a correct probability.
D.explanation: Correct rankings do not guarantee that individual probabilities are accurate.

aib-c01-d1-093@1.title: Choose Translation When Transcription Alone Is Not Enough
aib-c01-d1-093@1.prompt: A company's consultation desk wants to create Japanese records from audio received in other languages without omitting numbers or dates. Accurate transcripts in the original language are already available. Which AI capability is most needed next?

learning.reason: Use translation that preserves the meaning of the original-language text, then verify that numbers, dates, negation, and other business-critical details have not changed.
learning.concept: Distinguish what transcription, translation, and summarization each change, and evaluate whether required information is preserved.

A.text: Translate the accurate transcripts into Japanese while preserving their meaning, and verify that numbers, dates, and negation are consistent.
A.explanation: This checks both that the record is in Japanese and that the required information is preserved.

B.text: Summarize each interaction in one Japanese sentence and freely choose which numbers and dates to include.
B.explanation: Required details could be omitted.

C.text: Produce transcripts in the original language more quickly without evaluating whether the text can be read in Japanese.
C.explanation: Transcribing audio does not convert it into the requested language.

D.text: Classify the audio as urgent or routine and treat the classification label as the Japanese record.
D.explanation: This does not preserve the content of what was said.

aib-c01-d1-094@1.title: Do Not Count Orders and Line Items as the Same Unit of Analysis
aib-c01-d1-094@1.prompt: Returns are being predicted at the order level. The order header has one row per order, while product line items have one or more rows per order. A simple join followed by counting rows counts orders with more products repeatedly. Which data preparation approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Make the order—the unit being predicted—explicit, and aggregate line-item fields for each order. Reconcile the order and observation counts to prevent duplicate counting.
learning.concept: Recognize one-to-many relationships, distinguish the count of prediction units from the aggregation of line-item information, and preserve the unit of analysis.

A.text: Join order headers and line items using column names alone, without matching by order ID.
A.explanation: You cannot verify that the information corresponds to the right order.

B.text: Assign a different order ID to each joined row and treat the total number of rows as the actual number of orders.
B.explanation: The problem of one order becoming multiple observations remains.

C.text: Keep only the highest-value product for each order so that each order has one line, without recording why it was selected.
C.explanation: This discards usable information about product mix unnecessarily and leaves the aggregation unclear.

D.text: Aggregate line-item information for each order, then verify the counts and matching so each order is one observation.
D.explanation: This preserves the prediction unit while still using line-item information.

aib-c01-d1-095@1.title: Prevent Local-Time Differences from Creating Errors in Daily Data
aib-c01-d1-095@1.prompt: A shipping forecast is trained using each warehouse's business days. Each warehouse records local time and also stores the offset from UTC in the input data. However, the data is currently aggregated by date alone, ignoring time-zone differences. Which data quality measure is appropriate?

learning.reason: Preserve the original time and offset to normalize points in time, then assign events to business days using each warehouse's cutoff. Validate examples at the boundary.
learning.concept: Align recorded times with the definition of a business day so that events are aggregated under the correct day.

A.text: Use the headquarters date for every warehouse and include shipments after each warehouse's cutoff on that same date.
A.explanation: This changes the warehouse-specific business day that the forecast is meant to use.

B.text: Add 12 hours uniformly for every warehouse and aggregate only the cases where the date changes.
B.explanation: This cannot account for each warehouse's time-zone offset and actual cutoff.

C.text: Use the recorded offsets to align points in time, assign business days according to each warehouse's cutoff, and reconcile boundary cases.
C.explanation: This correctly handles both when an event occurred and the operational definition of the day.

D.text: Put every time value in the same format and remove time-zone information.
D.explanation: Consistent formatting alone does not make it possible to compare the points in time represented by events.

aib-c01-d1-096@1.title: Do not use organization-level aggregates as individual labels
aib-c01-d1-096@1.prompt: A training company wants to predict whether individual learners will resubmit an assignment. Its available history contains only resubmission rates by course and does not show who resubmitted. Which learning decision is appropriate?

learning.reason: A course-level rate cannot be treated as an individual outcome. Obtain data that can be matched to individual outcomes, or change the use case to a course-level one that can be evaluated with aggregates.
learning.concept: Check whether ground-truth outcomes exist at the granularity required by the business, and do not reuse aggregate results for individuals.

A.text: For courses with a resubmission rate above half, label everyone as having resubmitted and ignore differences among learners.
A.explanation: This treats a group frequency as an individual fact.

B.text: Obtain history that can be linked to individual outcomes. If only aggregates are available, separately evaluate a course-level prediction.
B.explanation: The granularity of the learning target should match that of the outcomes that can actually be verified.

C.text: Record each course's resubmission rate as the individual outcome for everyone enrolled, and measure accuracy by agreement with that value.
C.explanation: There is no ground truth showing whether each individual resubmitted.

D.text: Assume that adding more individual attributes makes it possible to validate each person's resubmission rate without ground-truth outcomes.
D.explanation: More inputs do not provide the correct outcomes needed for comparison.

aib-c01-d1-097@1.title: Automate only the parts with fixed decision rules
aib-c01-d1-097@1.prompt: In a returns process, the purchase date can be looked up and whether the deadline has passed can be calculated using fixed rules. Even after the deadline, a staff member may grant an exception only when a disaster has halted delivery, after reviewing evidence. Which approach is appropriate?

learning.reason: Use the established process for looking up dates and calculating the deadline. If the request falls outside the deadline, do not automatically infer an exception; route it to an authorized staff member.
learning.concept: Keep the prediction accuracy required by the business separate from arithmetic rules that must be followed strictly and from human discretion.

A.text: Train AI on past exceptions and have it make a definitive decision about whether a request is within the deadline even when the purchase date cannot be retrieved.
A.explanation: This makes a definitive decision despite missing facts.

B.text: Determine the deadline using the specified calculation, and route disaster-related exceptions to a staff member with the supporting evidence.
B.explanation: This separates work that can be handled deterministically from work requiring human judgment.

C.text: Close every request made after the deadline in the same way, even though the policy provides for exceptions.
C.explanation: This fails to handle exceptions that must be reviewed.

D.text: To reduce staff workload, delegate both date calculations and discretionary decisions to a single exception-decision model.
D.explanation: This fails to distinguish fixed rules from the management of discretionary decisions.

aib-c01-d1-098@1.title: Split long policies without separating clauses from their exceptions
aib-c01-d1-098@1.prompt: A long policy includes return conditions and must be split to meet a length limit. Splitting only at headings can retrieve a main clause without its immediately following exception, resulting in incorrect guidance. The full text cannot fit in a single input. Choose two measures.

learning.reason: Link exceptions to the rules they qualify, split the material while preserving that relationship, and include the relevant sections together. Check the outcome and supporting evidence using cases that require an exception.
learning.concept: When dividing content into smaller units, keep following conditions and referenced clauses together in the same evaluation unit.

A.text: Answer as soon as a sentence matching the main clause is found, without checking other clauses.
A.explanation: If an applicable exception exists, this can lead to incorrectly stating the normal condition.

B.text: Reduce all exception text to one generic sentence without recording which main clause each exception qualifies.
B.explanation: It will no longer be possible to determine which conditions an exception applies to.

C.text: Link each main clause to references for its applicable exceptions so the clauses needed to answer a question can be retrieved together.
C.explanation: This makes it possible to handle the sections needed for a decision together without including the entire long policy.

D.text: Create cases where the outcome differs between the main clause and an exception, then evaluate whether evidence for both is retrieved and the correct conclusion is reached.
D.explanation: This verifies changes to splitting and retrieval against actual decisions.

E.text: Stop splitting the text and unconditionally truncate the last part whenever the full text sent each time exceeds the limit.
E.explanation: There is no guarantee that the necessary exceptions or references to other sections will remain.

aib-c01-d1-099@1.title: Distinguish a valid not-applicable blank from an omission
aib-c01-d1-099@1.prompt: In repair-request records, a warranty number is required only for requests covered by the warranty. Treating every blank as a data defect led to many valid requests outside warranty coverage being deleted. Which improvement is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Determine whether the warranty number applies based on an earlier field, then distinguish a not-applicable value from a required value that was not entered and assess data quality accordingly.
learning.concept: Use form branches and applicability conditions to treat valid blanks separately from missing data.

A.text: Remove the warranty-number column and stop evaluating whether required information was captured for covered requests.
A.explanation: This hides missing data that the business needs.

B.text: Remove every row with a blank in the column and estimate overall performance using only the remaining warranty-covered requests.
B.explanation: Requests outside warranty coverage are also handled in operations, so the data would no longer be representative.

C.text: Fill every blank with the latest warranty number and use the number of populated records as the quality measure.
C.explanation: This assigns an incorrect number to multiple cases, including those where the field does not apply.

D.text: Record whether the warranty number is not applicable or missing according to warranty coverage, and review cases that lack a required number.
D.explanation: This preserves the meaning of the data and makes it possible to check for genuinely missing information.

aib-c01-d1-100@1.title: Clarify system boundaries using shared AI terminology
aib-c01-d1-100@1.prompt: In procurement documents, one department uses “AI system” to mean only the model files, while another uses it to mean the entire deliverable, including data inputs and operations. You want to reread both departments’ specifications using the same concepts. Which reference and approach are appropriate?

learning.reason: Align AI terminology and concepts with ISO/IEC 22989, then document the components and responsibilities included in the procurement scope.
learning.concept: Map technical concepts and contractual responsibilities to shared definitions so ambiguous terms do not remain in discussions.

A.text: Refer to ISO/IEC 22989 to align AI terms and concepts, then state the procurement boundary explicitly in the specification.
A.explanation: A shared vocabulary can resolve differences in what is included.

B.text: Replace the word “system” with “model” in every document and use that wording even where the original specification included operations.
B.explanation: This narrows the original requirements without checking their scope.

C.text: Make ISO/IEC 42001 certification a requirement and assume that it automatically defines the contractual scope of “AI system.”
C.explanation: Management-system certification alone does not define the work included in the contract.

D.text: Choose component names for the model using only ISO/IEC 23894, without aligning the meaning used by each department.
D.explanation: Risk-management guidance alone does not resolve the shared-terminology and contractual-scope issue.

aib-c01-d1-101@1.title: Keep two tasks for the same person separate
aib-c01-d1-101@1.prompt: An equipment-booking agent handles multiple requests that one person is working on at the same time. An example occurred in which the “Confirm” action was applied to a different piece of equipment that had been opened earlier. Select TWO measures to prevent this.

learning.reason: Use an explicit ID and current state to identify the request being acted on instead of relying only on conversation order. If the target is ambiguous, ask before confirming.
learning.concept: Validate the target request and its latest state for each agent action.

A.text: Immediately before confirming, check the target and its latest state; if anything is ambiguous, ask the person to choose.
A.explanation: This helps prevent confirming the wrong request or acting on stale information.

B.text: Include the equipment name in the response after confirmation, without checking it against the booking record beforehand.
B.explanation: Naming the equipment in the report does not prevent the wrong action from happening.

C.text: Automatically confirm every request the person is handling concurrently to reduce mistakes.
C.explanation: This also changes requests other than the one specified.

D.text: Give each request a separate case ID and state, and pass the required ID to the tool when performing an action.
D.explanation: This distinguishes the target without relying on conversation order.

E.text: Remember the last piece of equipment the person used and apply every confirmation with an omitted target to that equipment.
E.explanation: When requests are handled concurrently, this can select the wrong target.

aib-c01-d1-102@1.title: Make approval categories useful for employees’ day-to-day decisions
aib-c01-d1-102@1.prompt: A company’s AI inventory marks tools as “Approved,” “Under review,” or “Not permitted.” However, employees think that approval means they can enter confidential information, and when a tool is unavailable, they search for unregistered services. What should the company do?

learning.reason: Specify the scope of approval by use case and information type. For an unapproved tool, explain how to request review; for an out-of-scope task, point to an approved alternative.
learning.concept: Explain each category and the review process so users can choose a tool that fits their purpose and data.

A.text: Treat “Under review” and “Not permitted” as meaning the same thing until an employee asks for help, and provide no other options.
A.explanation: This does not show employees how to continue their work safely or how to proceed with a review.

B.text: For each tool, list its use cases, the materials it can handle, its restrictions, how to request a review, and alternatives; then check understanding with concrete examples.
B.explanation: Employees can choose an option suited to their task and submit a review request when needed.

C.text: Shorten only the category names, without listing which data employees may enter.
C.explanation: Employees still cannot determine the conditions required to choose a tool.

D.text: Allow every approved product to be used uniformly with any feature and any material.
D.explanation: This mistakes registration status for unrestricted scope of use.

aib-c01-d1-103@1.title: Keep values in examples out of the current data
aib-c01-d1-103@1.prompt: An office AI creates invoice records. A format example contains a fictitious department code, and the AI output that fictitious code when the actual document did not include a department code. Which instruction should improve the result?

learning.reason: State that the example shows only the format and that current values must be extracted only from the document being processed. Test the condition that an example value must not be used for an unknown field.
learning.concept: Separate format examples from the current document in the prompt, and tell the model not to treat example values as evidence.

A.text: Distinguish the format example from the current document, take values only from the current document, and leave fields unfilled when information is not present.
A.explanation: This clarifies the role of the example and prevents reuse of fictitious information.

B.text: Add more examples containing the same fictitious code and prioritize whichever code appears most often in the examples.
B.explanation: This reinforces the cause of the copying.

C.text: Make the fictitious code look like a real code and require every missing field to be filled with something.
C.explanation: This causes the AI to assert a value that does not actually exist.

D.text: Do not distinguish the example from the current values, and allow the AI to use whichever code has fewer characters.
D.explanation: The output would no longer be grounded in the actual document.

aib-c01-d1-104@1.title: Find out why usage limits can be reached even when a user’s message is short
aib-c01-d1-104@1.prompt: A support AI can hit its limit even when a question is short. For frequent users, many past interactions and ledger lookup results are added. Limiting only the user’s text did not solve the problem. What should be measured next?

learning.reason: Measure the capacity of everything sent to the model and the required output, by type of added information. Reduce history or lookup results that are not needed for the task.
learning.concept: A context budget includes instructions, prior conversation, retrieval and tool results, and generated output.

A.text: Ledger lookups run outside the model, so the returned results do not count toward its capacity.
A.explanation: Lookup results added to the model’s input use capacity.

B.text: Measure only the character count of the user’s question again and assume there is no problem if it is short.
B.explanation: This does not account for the other information the model receives.

C.text: Measure the instructions, history, lookup results, and response budget actually sent, and provide only the information needed.
C.explanation: This captures the context limit, including material beyond the question itself.

D.text: Assume shorter answers will let the system accept every request, and do not measure the input limit.
D.explanation: This does not prevent cases where the input alone is too large.

aib-c01-d1-105@1.title: Match the applicable old or new policy version to the date in question
aib-c01-d1-105@1.prompt: A contract-process AI can search the latest and previous versions. Users sometimes ask about earlier applications, and the AI must answer using the conditions that applied at the time. Semantic search often selects the latest policy. Which improvement is appropriate?

learning.reason: Confirm the date the question concerns and use each document’s effective period as a retrieval condition. Cite the applicable version as evidence, and ask for clarification if the date is unknown.
learning.concept: Use explicit applicability conditions in retrieval; do not select a policy version based only on semantic similarity.

A.text: Combine past and current policies in one answer and leave it to the user to determine the differences.
A.explanation: This does not clarify which conditions apply and can lead to inaccurate guidance.

B.text: Increase the number of semantic-search candidates and use the longest document without checking its version.
B.explanation: Even if an older version is among the candidates, this does not select it based on applicability.

C.text: Delete all older versions and answer questions about past applications using only current conditions.
C.explanation: The version that applied to the earlier application would no longer be available.

D.text: Compare each document’s effective start and end dates with the date in question, then retrieve and cite the applicable version.
D.explanation: This selects evidence that matches both the content and the applicable period.

aib-c01-d2-097@1.title: Use AI to address why information becomes outdated
aib-c01-d2-097@1.prompt: Product support teams create different procedures for the same failure, leading to repeat visits. Repair histories and versions of approved procedures can be tracked. Which measure would reduce repeat visits?

learning.reason: Identify conflicting descriptions of the same failure and their applicable versions, then have the responsible teams approve corrections. Compare repeat visits after staff use the corrected procedures.
learning.concept: Choose a use of AI that connects business losses to a maintenance process and lets responsible staff correct the underlying information.

A.text: Briefly summarize the latest repair reports and measure only how many times the summaries are viewed.
A.explanation: This does not assess conflicting procedures or repeat visits.

B.text: Predict which customers are likely to need another visit and use that to staff support desks, without reviewing conflicting procedures.
B.explanation: Staffing can be planned, but the underlying guidance remains unchanged.

C.text: Align versions and failure categories to identify potential conflicts, have staff correct the procedures, and measure repeat visits after the corrected procedures are used.
C.explanation: This connects an actionable improvement to the cause of the problem and its outcome.

D.text: Have AI automatically designate the most fluent procedure as authoritative, without considering approved versions.
D.explanation: Fluency cannot identify whether a procedure is current and correct.

aib-c01-d2-098@1.title: Compare procurement proposals under real operating conditions, not sales claims
aib-c01-d2-098@1.prompt: A company wants to buy AI-based application intake. Two vendors report the same average speed and accuracy, but large applications arrive in a rush just before the deadline. Late applications cannot be reviewed that day. Which comparison should be made before signing a contract?

learning.reason: Recreate large applications arriving together, then compare completion rates, slow cases, quality, and contractual guarantees under the same conditions for both vendors.
learning.concept: In addition to published average performance, validate vendor capacity with representative inputs under business-critical peak loads.

A.text: Compare only the highest speed reported by each vendor and assume it will be sustained for every application.
A.explanation: Peak speed does not show slower cases or deadline performance.

B.text: Measure only in departments with small submissions and apply those speeds company-wide.
B.explanation: This does not reflect the sizes and workload that cause the actual problem.

C.text: Choose the least expensive option because the overall averages are the same, and collect deadline results after deployment.
C.explanation: This does not verify capacity at the busiest time.

D.text: Process representative applications under deadline-time arrival conditions, measure slow cases, completion rate, and quality, and verify the contractual guarantees.
D.explanation: This enables a like-for-like comparison under realistic constraints.

aib-c01-d2-099@1.title: Compare the value of existing capabilities before starting a new initiative
aib-c01-d2-099@1.prompt: The sales department wants to invest in a new AI system that classifies headings in customer documents.
