Another department already has a classification capability that meets the same goal and quality requirements; it could be used by adding the sales department’s permissions and terminology. No additional benefit from the new proposal has been demonstrated yet. What is the most appropriate decision?

learning.reason: Compare adapting the existing capability with developing a new one, and verify the new proposal’s additional benefits and maintenance costs. Allocate resources first to the scope that meets the conditions for shared use.
learning.concept: Prioritize based on whether business value beyond the existing capability is established, including the cost of adding another offering.

A.text: Check whether the existing capability can be used under the sales department’s requirements and what additional costs would apply; hold off on development until the new proposal demonstrates incremental value.
A.explanation: This avoids unnecessary development and operating costs while maintaining the required quality.

B.text: Add the trial count for the new proposal to the usage count for the existing capability and treat the total as company-wide impact, without accounting for overlap.
B.explanation: This fails to distinguish additional value from different initiatives.

C.text: Disable the existing capability first, then trial the solution for sales after the operating costs of both options are known.
C.explanation: This discards a reusable shared asset before comparing costs.

D.text: Prioritize the new proposal on the grounds that a separate product has value when departments differ, even if the outcomes are the same.
D.explanation: This does not compare reuse of the existing capability with the additional burden.

aib-c01-d2-100@1.title: Determine whether to add predictions to a process where decisions cannot change
aib-c01-d2-100@1.prompt: Equipment must be inspected on a fixed schedule every 90 days after its last inspection. Even if failure predictions become highly accurate, the inspection scope, schedule, and procedure cannot change. Which is the most appropriate operational improvement for this term?

learning.reason: Do not prioritize investment in predictions that do not change business decisions. Improve current work through schedule management based on known dates and tracking incomplete work.
learning.concept: Avoid adding complexity when prediction results change neither actions nor outcomes.

A.text: Improve the system for calculating due dates and tracking incomplete work, and do not add failure predictions to this fixed process.
A.explanation: This improves the parts that can change while meeting the scheduled inspection requirements.

B.text: Add predictions for all equipment and report predictive accuracy as an amount of maintenance improvement, even if the predictions are not used for scheduling.
B.explanation: No business improvement has occurred.

C.text: Discontinue all current procedures regardless of the prediction results and keep only a manual schedule.
C.explanation: This discards a usable system and does not address the actual problem.

D.text: Inspect items predicted to be high risk early and skip some scheduled inspections for equipment predicted to be low risk.
D.explanation: This violates the requirement that the inspection scope and schedule cannot change.

aib-c01-d2-101@1.title: Check that reported metrics retain the same meaning after a process changes
aib-c01-d2-101@1.prompt: When AI is introduced into maintenance intake, a single request will be split into multiple tasks. Current management reports show the on-time completion rate at the request level, and those reports are also used in customer contracts. The new system can provide completion counts at the task level. What should be verified before migration?

learning.reason: Reconstruct request completion appropriately from task status, then compare the aggregation against the contract definition and baseline over a representative period.
learning.concept: When AI changes how items are counted, test a migration that connects downstream aggregation to the previous baseline.

A.text: Map tasks back to their original requests and recalculate results using the contractual definition of completion. Before migration, validate the conditions under which the results match the old calculation.
A.explanation: This allows downstream reporting obligations to be maintained with the new process.

B.text: Treat the increased task count as a quality improvement and do not record how tasks map to their original requests.
B.explanation: The reason for the change in reported values and contractual progress cannot be tracked.

C.text: Announce only that the reporting method is changing, without reconstructing the existing contract definitions.
C.explanation: Results can no longer be evaluated against the established calculation criteria.

D.text: Compare the task-level completion rate directly with the previous request-level metric.
D.explanation: The denominator and completion criteria have changed, so the same outcome is not being measured.

aib-c01-d2-102@1.title: Measure whether audit-ready evidence can actually be retrieved
aib-c01-d2-102@1.prompt: AI is being used to organize evidence for purchase reviews. The goal is for an auditor to reconstruct the reason for a transaction and the policy that applied within a specified time. The system stores many documents. Which is the most appropriate success metric?

learning.reason: For sampled transactions, test whether the approval rationale, policy version in effect at the time, and review record can be retrieved completely. Measure the share of successful retrievals within the specified time.
learning.concept: Evaluate whether records are sufficient to reconstruct a review and can be produced in the required time, rather than counting records generated.

A.text: The number of times the latest policy can be found.
A.explanation: This does not show whether the reason for a past transaction and the policy version in effect at the time can be reconstructed.

B.text: The total number of documents stored by the system.
B.explanation: This does not verify that the required evidence is complete for each case.

C.text: For a random sample of transactions, the percentage for which the required approval rationale and policy version in effect at the time can be retrieved completely within the specified time.
C.explanation: This measures both completeness and retrieval time needed for an audit.

D.text: The median time until the first relevant document is displayed.
D.explanation: The time to reach one document does not measure retrieval of all required evidence.

aib-c01-d2-103@1.title: Compare time to reach the same quality level
aib-c01-d2-103@1.prompt: You are introducing AI to prepare research reports. Under the current process, work is complete only after a person has finished reviewing everything. The pilot proposes treating the work as complete as soon as the AI produces a first draft. What baseline is needed to compare the impact?

learning.reason: Apply the same approval criteria to both the old process and the pilot, and measure from start until a reviewed output is complete. Record difficulty and rework as well.
learning.concept: Set the completion criteria before the pilot and do not stop measuring at the draft stage.

A.text: Compare the time for AI to produce a first draft with the current time through approval.
A.explanation: The completion criteria differ, as do the steps included.

B.text: Use the same definition of completion—a quality-checked report—and measure start, finish, and review time for both approaches.
B.explanation: This compares the time required to reach an output of the same quality.

C.text: For the old process, rely only on employees’ recollections of the time taken, while recording the new process to the nearest second.
C.explanation: Differences in measurement can affect the measured improvement rate.

D.text: Exclude reports that were difficult to review only from the AI results, because they will not show the benefits of replacement.
D.explanation: This omits the review burden found in real work.

aib-c01-d2-104@1.title: Include incremental costs when calculating the benefit of expansion
aib-c01-d2-104@1.prompt: AI use at two additional sites is expected to deliver $1.6 million in verified benefits per site per year, with $900,000 in additional operating costs per site per year. Shared training for both sites will cost $600,000 in the first year only. The financial results at the current sites will not change. What is the incremental net benefit of the expansion in its first year?

learning.reason: The two sites produce $3.2 million in benefits. Subtract $1.8 million in costs and $600,000 for shared training to get $800,000.
learning.concept: Do not scale a pilot’s net benefit by site count without accounting for expansion costs.

A.text: $800,000. Subtract the additional operating costs and shared training cost from the benefits at both sites.
A.explanation: Include each incremental cost once.

B.text: $2.6 million. Subtract only the shared training cost from the benefits and assume operating costs will not change.
B.explanation: This omits the additional operating costs at each site.

C.text: $200,000. Account for the $600,000 training cost separately at each site.
C.explanation: This counts the one-time shared cost twice.

D.text: $1.4 million. Count only the difference between the benefits and operating costs at both sites.
D.explanation: This omits the shared training cost in the first year.

aib-c01-d2-105@1.title: Estimate capacity for expansion from the review burden immediately after launch
aib-c01-d2-105@1.prompt: AI generates drafts of inspection documents. The cost of formal inspections will be known at the end of the quarter, but you want to decide before expansion whether work can continue within the available expert review capacity. Which leading indicator is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Measure correction rates and the distribution of review times for the relevant cases early. Estimate the expert capacity required for the expected volume, then reconcile it against final costs later.
learning.concept: While waiting for final results, track corrections and expert time to identify future bottlenecks.

A.text: Count only the number of generated documents, without distinguishing those that needed corrections.
A.explanation: This does not reveal how much review capacity expansion will require.

B.text: Measure the correction rate and expert review time by difficulty level, then estimate the capacity needed for the expected volume.
B.explanation: This captures conditions that could halt processing before the impact is known.

C.text: Wait only for the cost of formal inspections, which will be finalized at the end of the quarter.
C.explanation: This reveals the final impact, but provides no information for the expansion decision.

D.text: Measure only expert training time and do not track review of individual inspections.
D.explanation: Training time is not a leading indicator of workload or correction burden.

aib-c01-d2-106@1.title: Identify processing costs beyond inference charges
aib-c01-d2-106@1.prompt: Half the cost of image classification came from copying and converting full-resolution images from storage before sending them to the AI. Only some regions of each image need to be classified, and those regions can be extracted in an approved environment. Which cost measure preserves quality?

learning.reason: Track data transfer and preprocessing costs separately, then compare the quality and cost per completed classification for extracting only the necessary regions within the permitted boundary.
learning.concept: Compare total cost per completion when data movement and conversion are significant, even if the model has a low unit price.

A.text: Because the service recipient asked for lower costs, use the same minimum image quality for all images without measuring classification quality.
A.explanation: This does not compare the loss of necessary information against the cost reduction.

B.text: Create the required image regions in an approved location, then compare classification quality and costs—including transfer and conversion—with the original approach.
B.explanation: This addresses an identified cost driver and lets you verify that the required quality is maintained.

C.text: Compare only the monthly inference-model charges and ignore data transfer and conversion costs because another department incurs them.
C.explanation: This overlooks the total cost of processing the request.

D.text: Keep full copies of the images in multiple environments and do not measure the traffic between them.
D.explanation: This could further increase processing and storage costs.

aib-c01-d2-107@1.title: Assess the impact of a price cut using customers’ actual choices by segment
aib-c01-d2-107@1.prompt: A competitor has sharply reduced the price of its document AI. Smaller customers are considering switching because of the price difference, while larger customers care about whether they can continue processing the same documents. What analysis should your company conduct before applying the same price cut to all customers?

learning.reason: For each customer segment, assess willingness to pay, usage requirements, and the burden of switching. Evaluate why contracts may be lost and what it costs to retain them.
learning.concept: Assess the market by segment, including the features customers use, the burden of switching, and price sensitivity, rather than relying on competitor pricing alone.

A.text: Apply the competitor’s price reduction to every customer without considering differences in value or contract renewal.
A.explanation: This could reduce profits even in segments with little need for a price cut.

B.text: Assess price sensitivity and switching requirements by customer segment, then choose a response based on actual reasons for renewal and cancellation.
B.explanation: This allows the company to evaluate the competitive threat and effective responses for each customer segment.

C.text: Match the number of features and assume all customers want the same price and quality.
C.explanation: This does not account for differences in customers’ actual reasons for choosing a product.

D.text: Assume large customers will not change their contracts, and judge other factors only from the competitor’s advertising.
D.explanation: This does not verify customer behavior or business requirements.

aib-c01-d2-108@1.title: Test transaction intermediation using AI as a new source of revenue
aib-c01-d2-108@1.prompt: A tool shop uses inventory recommendation AI to identify surplus stock. An outside construction company has also asked to borrow tools left over at another company. How should the shop test an intermediary service that requires participation from specialist businesses?

learning.reason: Use a small-scale transaction involving both sides to assess completion rates, willingness to pay fees, and the costs of verification and dispute handling.
learning.concept: Distinguish internal efficiency gains from the revenue and responsibilities of transactions that connect users.

A.text: Estimate fee revenue from the number of inventory recommendation operations, without measuring whether other companies are willing to pay.
A.explanation: This confuses internal processing volume with the number of revenue-generating intermediary transactions.

B.text: Assume that more registrations will guarantee fee revenue, and consider contracts and loan verification after launch.
B.explanation: Registration counts do not show whether transactions will be completed or what responsibilities each party will have.

C.text: Improve inventory forecasting for internal use only, without examining users’ requirements for lending and borrowing.
C.explanation: This does not validate the conditions required for both sides of the transaction to participate.

D.text: Run a small-scale pilot connecting lenders and borrowers, and measure completed transactions, fees, and the costs of identity verification and dispute resolution.
D.explanation: This can validate the new revenue unit and the operations it requires.

aib-c01-d2-109@1.title: Make operational recovery capability a reason for customers to stay
aib-c01-d2-109@1.prompt: Several companies offer parts lookup AI of the same quality. Because an outage would disrupt customers’ inspections, their contract renewals take alternative procedures and recovery track records into account. Which investment can create a long-term advantage?

learning.reason: Standardize alternative paths and support, and measure exercises, actual recovery times, and the business operations that continued. Keep improving based on the results.
learning.concept: For customers whose operations cannot stop, build an advantage by accumulating the capability to recover safely from incidents.

A.text: Buy another contract for the same model only when an outage occurs, without checking whether the contracts share a common point of impact.
A.explanation: This does not guarantee a recovery capability that can be reproduced reliably.

B.text: Promote the model’s high evaluation ranking alone and leave outage response to external users.
B.explanation: This does not improve the operations that customers value when renewing contracts.

C.text: Adopt a policy of not reporting recovery times and tell customers only whether an outage occurred.
C.explanation: This makes recovery capability and improvement difficult to assess.

D.text: Establish independent alternatives and response procedures, then improve them through exercises and track records of continuity and recovery in operation.
D.explanation: Building the system and people’s capabilities can sustain value for customers.

aib-c01-d2-110@1.title: Limit fixed investment until standards are finalized
aib-c01-d2-110@1.prompt: The logistics AI market is growing, but evidence submitted to customers must follow one of two industry specifications. A decision on a unified standard is expected next year. Demand for an aggregation feature that works with either specification has been confirmed. Which investment approach should the company take?

learning.reason: Build the shared feature with confirmed demand and isolate changes specific to each specification. Adjust investment using contracts and implementation choices that can accommodate either outcome.
learning.concept: Even in a growing market, when specifications are competing, invest in the shared parts and separate the parts that are difficult to change.

A.text: Stop validating and offering features that work with either specification until the specifications are finalized.
A.explanation: This forfeits an option to deliver value that has already been confirmed.

B.text: Commit all costs to one specification upfront, without assessing the cost of changing course or the impact on customers if a different specification is chosen.
B.explanation: This removes the flexibility to respond to the market’s decision.

C.text: Build the shared feature with confirmed demand and keep specification-specific work separate. Decide on additional investment based on the finalized standard and demonstrated demand.
C.explanation: This separates the value that is already clear from the work that depends on the pending decision.

D.text: Adopt the format chosen by a competitor without considering customer requirements or the cost of changing later.
D.explanation: This substitutes a competitor’s actions for an assessment of the company’s own demand and risks.

aib-c01-d2-111@1.title: Match multilingual support to the cause of abandonment, not request volume
aib-c01-d2-111@1.prompt: At a travel service desk, requests for information in foreign languages are few, but many customers abandon the process because they do not understand the cancellation-fee explanation. The terms have been approved, and language specialists are available to review the wording. Which initiative should be piloted?

learning.reason: Provide an explanation of the terms that is stopping customers, consistent with the approved terms, then compare completion and misleading guidance by language.
learning.concept: Apply AI language capabilities to a task that customers are unable to complete in practice.

A.text: Remove the fee explanation and report only the increase in completion rate as the outcome.
A.explanation: Customers would lose information they need to understand the terms.

B.text: Shorten all high-volume domestic guidance and exclude foreign-language users’ completions from evaluation.
B.explanation: This does not address the cause of the abandonment that needs to be reduced.

C.text: Increase the total word count translated by machine and do not measure what customers are struggling with.
C.explanation: The volume of translated text does not show that more customers completed the process.

D.text: Present the fee in the relevant languages with supporting details, have the translations reviewed, and measure completion and misunderstanding by language.
D.explanation: This addresses both the specific cause of abandonment and translation quality.

aib-c01-d2-112@1.title: Separate parts of a bundled proposal when their value and feasibility differ
aib-c01-d2-112@1.prompt: A proposal would use AI to support all recurring reports. Approved data is available for weekly sales reports, and preparing them could take substantially less time. For investment reports, use of external evidence has not been approved, and the anticipated benefits are not well supported. How should funds be allocated today?

learning.reason: Assess deployment readiness and benefits separately for each department. Pilot where the evidence is ready, and clarify the conditions for expanding to other areas.
learning.concept: Evaluate a proposal with the same name by scope, and allocate funds to the parts whose benefits can be established under available conditions.

A.text: Because it is one proposal, deploy it for all reports at the same time and obtain approval for external evidence after launch.
A.explanation: This extends approval for one prepared area to all of the work.

B.text: If any part is uncertain, never reconsider any of the work, including areas for which evidence is ready.
B.explanation: This prevents the organization from using the parts that are useful and feasible.

C.text: Validate costs and outcomes for weekly sales reports, and reassess investment reports after reviewing approval for use and supporting evidence of their benefits.
C.explanation: This sets priorities realistically in light of the different assumptions.

D.text: Treat shorter reports as equivalent in value, and do not include approval or user outcomes in prioritization.
D.explanation: This does not assess the initiative’s impact or implementation conditions.

aib-c01-d2-113@1.title: Compare definitions of billable successful outcomes
aib-c01-d2-113@1.prompt: There are two proposals for document-classification support. The first charges for each successful processing attempt, including retries for the same document. The second has a monthly fee and includes only documents accepted by the business in its usage-based charges. Accuracy is equivalent, and difficult documents often require retries. Which procurement evaluation is appropriate?

learning.reason: Distinguish processing success, retries, and business acceptance in the contract definitions, then compare the cost per accepted document using representative documents.
learning.concept: Align the unit paid for in a purchase or partnership contract with the actual business outcome.

A.text: Compare only the first proposal's initial execution fee with the second proposal's usage-based charge, excluding the monthly fee and exceptions.
A.explanation: This excludes important components of total cost.

B.text: Select the contract based only on the price difference, then estimate unknown costs later and add them to the budget.
B.explanation: Cost drivers needed for the selection have not been validated.

C.text: Because the first proposal uses the word “success,” assume it does not charge for results that the business does not accept.
C.explanation: The definition of success and the conditions for charging for retries differ.

D.text: Confirm the contract's billing unit and use representative data that includes retries to compare the cost per document accepted by the business.
D.explanation: This aligns the required outcome with charges based on actual conditions.

aib-c01-d2-114@1.title: Decide whether to build a system requiring ongoing operations for a one-time task
aib-c01-d2-114@1.prompt: A branch needs to convert 12 contract appendices to a standard format just once. The input fields and current values are fixed, and a person can prepare and review them in half a day. Preparing an AI-assisted process would require several weeks of review and environment setup. Which recommendation is appropriate?

learning.reason: For a routine task that will not recur, use an existing template and review process to deliver the required result. Do not prioritize AI adoption without a reason to incur its implementation and maintenance costs.
learning.concept: Limit costs by considering frequency, flexibility, and the minimum quality needed, and use a routine process when it is sufficient.

A.text: Use the existing format and field checks, and have a staff member review the results. Reassess if this work becomes recurring in the future.
A.explanation: This can be done within the current volume and timeline, and quality can be checked.

B.text: Assume AI will be faster and enter contract data before approval is complete.
B.explanation: This does not meet the conditions for implementation, and the presumed cost has not been measured.

C.text: Set up AI permissions and an environment first, then leave ongoing subscription costs out of the evaluation even after the task is complete.
C.explanation: This does not assess whether the one-time benefit justifies setup and ongoing costs.

D.text: Even though all conditions for applying the format are clear, defer the work to the next period on the grounds that nothing can be prepared without AI.
D.explanation: The required outcome can be produced using the existing process.

aib-c01-d2-115@1.title: Preserve prepaid usage allowances after switching AI platforms
aib-c01-d2-115@1.prompt: A business AI service is moving to a new platform. Under the old contracts, customers could use their prepaid remaining allowances until they expired, and some customers had term-specific provisions. The new platform was configured to start with its standard monthly allowance. What should be done before launch?

learning.reason: Convert and reconcile each contract’s remaining allowance, expiration date, and special provisions in the new platform. Check representative cases to ensure customers are neither charged twice nor unable to use what they purchased.
learning.concept: Reconcile contract entitlements and usage allowances as well as the technical transition to the new platform.

A.text: Set the same remaining allowance for every customer and ignore special provisions in favor of the number of records imported.
A.explanation: This does not accommodate differences in individual contract terms.

B.text: Map each remaining allowance to its expiration date and special provisions, reconcile usable amounts and charges against representative contracts, and define what to do if migration fails.
B.explanation: This preserves the operational requirements of the transition and customers’ pricing terms.

C.text: Delete all remaining allowances as soon as use of the old platform is stopped, and communicate only the new charges.
C.explanation: This does not meet the terms of existing contracts that allow use until expiration.

D.text: Confirm that the new platform starts up, and restore remaining allowances only if customers complain.
D.explanation: This does not preserve purchased entitlements at launch.

aib-c01-d2-116@1.title: Measure the impact of reprioritization on both urgent and routine cases
aib-c01-d2-116@1.prompt: AI will assign priority to requests for assistance. The goal is to handle urgent requests faster, but routine cases are also promised a response by the following day. Select two key metrics.

learning.reason: Measure how long independently confirmed urgent cases take to receive an initial response, and track the proportion of routine cases that miss their promised deadline. An overall average alone cannot distinguish the two.
learning.concept: Use separate metrics for improvement on urgent cases and the harm caused when routine cases wait too long.

A.text: The proportion of routine cases that exceed the response deadline of the following day.
A.explanation: This shows whether prioritization is harming service to routine cases.

B.text: Measure only the average time across all departments, without recording whether cases are urgent or routine.
B.explanation: Faster urgent-case handling could hide delays for routine cases.

C.text: Rank cases by the length of their guidance text.
C.explanation: This is unrelated to service commitments or the time customers actually wait.

D.text: The proportion of cases independently confirmed as urgent for which handling begins within the specified time.
D.explanation: This measures the urgent-case response that the initiative is intended to improve most.

E.text: The total number of cases that the AI labels as urgent.
E.explanation: The number of labels does not show which cases are truly urgent or how long they wait.

aib-c01-d2-117@1.title: Do not treat results from eager volunteers as the impact of organization-wide adoption
aib-c01-d2-117@1.prompt: Employees who already use new technologies regularly volunteered for an AI trial. Management wants to measure the impact of adopting AI across all employees. Operationally, a phased rollout by experience level is possible. Which evaluation design is appropriate?

learning.reason: Measure employees by experience level before rollout and include both early-adoption and usual-process groups in each stratum. Do not estimate organization-wide impact from only highly motivated volunteers.
learning.concept: Set the baseline, comparison groups, and assignment approach in advance, taking volunteer selection and employee skill into account.

A.text: Measure only the post-rollout results of employees who volunteered and treat those results as the impact for all employees.
A.explanation: Participants’ knowledge and motivation can affect the results.

B.text: Measure results before rollout by experience level, form groups in each stratum that adopt at different times, and compare them using the same definitions.
B.explanation: This makes it easier to distinguish participant-selection bias from the effect of adoption.

C.text: Deploy to all employees on the same day, then use the best-performing participant in the first week as the pre-rollout benchmark.
C.explanation: This uses a benchmark from a different condition than the pre-rollout state.

D.text: Compare post-rollout averages for volunteers and nonparticipants without examining each person’s experience or pre-rollout results.
D.explanation: This cannot distinguish preexisting differences from changes caused by AI.

aib-c01-d2-118@1.title: Compare first-year costs using included volume and overage charges
aib-c01-d2-118@1.prompt: Assume 10,000 requests are processed in a year. Plan A costs ¥1.8 million per year and includes 8,000 requests; each additional request costs ¥150. Training costs ¥200,000. Plan B costs ¥600,000 per year plus ¥140 per request for all requests, and training costs ¥500,000. All other conditions, including quality, are the same. Which comparison of first-year costs is correct?

learning.reason: Plan A costs ¥1.8 million + ¥300,000 for 2,000 overage requests + ¥200,000 for training = ¥2.3 million. Plan B costs ¥600,000 + ¥1.4 million for 10,000 requests + ¥500,000 for training = ¥2.5 million. Plan A is ¥200,000 less.
learning.concept: Compare included usage, additional usage, fixed fees, and training costs according to each contract instead of assuming a uniform per-request price.

A.text: Plan A costs ¥300,000 less. Consider only the difference in training costs and assume all other costs are the same.
A.explanation: The base fees and per-request terms are not the same.

B.text: Plan B costs ¥1.3 million less. Apply the ¥150 overage charge to all 10,000 requests under Plan A and exclude training costs for both plans.
B.explanation: Plan A includes 8,000 requests in its fixed fee, and training costs also apply.

C.text: Plan A costs ¥200,000 less. Include the 2,000 overage requests under Plan A and the training costs for both plans.
C.explanation: This applies the contract’s charging terms to the actual processing volume.

D.text: Plan B costs ¥1.2 million less. Compare only the annual base fees for both plans.
D.explanation: This excludes per-request charges and training costs.

aib-c01-d2-119@1.title: Check first whether the range of processable exception types has expanded
aib-c01-d2-119@1.prompt: The AI-assisted delivery process initially handled only routine documents. The ultimate outcome of the improvement will be the cost of reprocessing next quarter, but a decision is needed this month on whether to continue investing in broader exception handling. Which leading indicator would be useful?

learning.reason: Create an exception taxonomy that captures frequency and impact, then track the share of target cases represented by types that meet the criteria in independent tests.
learning.concept: Measure whether coverage of important use cases is expanding by using validated examples before the final outcomes are known.

A.text: Classify exceptions by frequency and impact, then track how much of the actual workload is covered by types that meet the criteria in representative tests.
A.explanation: This reveals the scope of the improvement before the investment decision is due.

B.text: Measure only how often routine documents are submitted to the AI.
B.explanation: This does not show how much of the exception workload can be handled.

C.text: Wait only for the total reprocessing cost, which will be confirmed next quarter.
C.explanation: This shows the ultimate outcome, but too late to inform this month's decision.

D.text: Measure only the number of exception cases prepared for evaluation, without checking whether they were handled correctly.
D.explanation: Creating examples is different from expanding the range that can be handled in production.

aib-c01-d2-120@1.title: Stop paying for urgent processing when the work can wait
aib-c01-d2-120@1.prompt: Document review assistance and monthly archival of historical materials use the same expensive, immediate-processing capacity. Review assistance needs a response within minutes, but the historical materials can be processed by the next morning. Choose two cost-saving measures.

learning.reason: Keep urgent work on the fast path and move deferrable work to a less expensive batch path. Track deadlines, quality, and cost per successful item.
learning.concept: Separate work with different deadlines, use a lower-cost path, and maintain service quality and timeliness.

A.text: Use separate processing paths, verify their deadlines and quality, and measure cost per completed item, including retries.
A.explanation: This measures actual costs and service quality for both use cases.

B.text: Move historical-material processing to a lower-cost batch path that meets its deadline.
B.explanation: This avoids using expensive capacity for work that does not need an immediate response.

C.text: Exclude failed candidate runs from billed usage so that costs appear stable.
C.explanation: This prevents an accurate comparison of actual costs and processing success.

D.text: Move everything to slow processing and compare only monthly costs, even if review assistance misses its deadline.
D.explanation: This fails to support a business process that requires an immediate response.

E.text: Discontinue historical-material processing without checking whether the next day's work depends on it.
E.explanation: This reduces costs by dropping a potentially necessary outcome.

aib-c01-d3-081@1.title: Protect the privacy of responses on a shared AI kiosk
aib-c01-d3-081@1.prompt: At a shared reception kiosk, users can review the details of their consultations. It was discovered that responses remained on the screen after users walked away, making them visible from the waiting line. Which improvement protects privacy while still allowing users to review the details?

learning.reason: Make detailed information available through a private channel for the authenticated user. Reduce sensitive information on the shared screen, then clear the display and session when the interaction ends.
learning.concept: Limit exposure to bystanders and clear information left on screen after use, in addition to authenticating the user.

A.text: Make consultation histories available through a shared QR code that anyone can use, and close only the display on the kiosk.
A.explanation: Sensitive content would still be exposed through the shared access path.

B.text: Keep all details on screen and force the display to close only when the next user starts.
B.explanation: People waiting nearby can read the previous user's information.

C.text: Show only the minimum information needed for reception on the shared screen, and provide the details through a private channel for the user. Clear the display and session at the end.
C.explanation: This lets users access their information while reducing exposure to bystanders and the next user.

D.text: Display a confidentiality warning, but leave the content visible from the waiting line and unchanged after the session ends.
D.explanation: A warning alone cannot prevent people nearby from seeing the information.

aib-c01-d3-082@1.title: Preserve users' notification choices while improving engagement
aib-c01-d3-082@1.prompt: A learning service uses AI to create notifications that encourage learners to continue. A trial that sent many notifications increased click-through rates, but learners who had chosen to opt out continued to receive repeated messages through other channels. How can the service balance business impact with user choice?

learning.reason: Apply opt-out choices across notification channels and set a frequency cap even for users who have opted in. Within those limits, evaluate both effective learning behaviors and complaints.
learning.concept: Manage user choice and the impact of repeated notifications even when personalization increases business engagement.

A.text: Make the notifications less prominent, but leave the sending volume and the propagation of opt-out settings unchanged.
A.explanation: Changing the presentation does not address why unwanted notifications are still sent.

B.text: Honor opt-outs across all notification channels, set a frequency cap for users who opt in, and compare continued learning with complaints.
B.explanation: This evaluates the effect on learning behavior that matters to the business while preserving user choice.

C.text: Use click-through rate as the only success criterion and defer channel-specific opt-out settings to the next operating cycle.
C.explanation: Even if click-through rates improve, users' choices about receiving notifications are not honored across channels.

D.text: Because every channel can increase engagement, allow one initial notification to be sent even to users who opted out.
D.explanation: This does not honor users' stated choice to opt out.

aib-c01-d3-083@1.title: Define the requirements for when the system must abstain
aib-c01-d3-083@1.prompt: An internal AI system is planned to present sales representatives with the terms under which a contract applies, but only standard contracts are available for the prototype. Staff handling special contracts are also expected to use the same screen, and an incorrect decision could lead to a promise not found in the contract. What should be done first during requirements definition?

learning.reason: Define what contracts will be tested and which are out of scope. Make abstaining and routing the case to a specialist an acceptance condition for situations where the terms are unclear.
learning.concept: Specify out-of-scope conditions and where to route abstentions during design so they can be included in the trial.

A.text: Specify the supported scope, how to identify special contracts, and when to abstain and hand off; then test both standard and out-of-scope cases in the trial.
A.explanation: This makes it possible to verify during design that the system does not present incorrect contract terms.

B.text: Treat special contracts as having terms similar to standard contracts, without deciding how to indicate that they are out of scope.
B.explanation: This could make users believe an answer is correct even in situations that have not been tested.

C.text: If the prototype has a high average score, release it to everyone without assigning staff to handle special contracts.
C.explanation: A high average score cannot guarantee performance on work outside the test scope.

D.text: Test only standard contracts, and add an abstention feature after incorrect guidance on a special contract occurs.
D.explanation: This leaves a known design risk untested before release.

aib-c01-d3-084@1.title: Escalate when small errors accumulate for the same user
aib-c01-d3-084@1.prompt: A support AI notifies users about missing information, one item at a time. Over several days, it repeatedly sends the same user notifications about different documents, and the process makes no progress. Each notification is minor on its own and does not trigger human review. What is the appropriate oversight?

learning.reason: Review repeat notifications and progress at the user level, and route cases for an end-to-end human review when repetition or stagnation meets defined conditions.
learning.concept: Do not continue automated processing based only on the severity of each individual item; include cumulative impact in oversight criteria.

A.text: For users with an incomplete process, stop all further automated processing and wait for them to make an inquiry.
A.explanation: This provides no oversight to help recover from a stalled process.

B.text: Monitor repeat notifications and stalled progress for each user, and have a staff member review and correct the full history when defined conditions are met.
B.explanation: This allows intervention when impacts accumulate, even if each individual item is minor.

C.text: Because each notification is minor, continue the AI's processing without reviewing the cumulative notifications.
C.explanation: This fails to recognize the accumulating impact on the user.

D.text: Make the notification wording more concise and send more notifications, even if they remain inconsistent with prior notices.
D.explanation: This does not address the cause preventing the process from moving forward.

aib-c01-d3-085@1.title: Maintain responsible decision-making when a reviewer is unavailable
aib-c01-d3-085@1.prompt: The business team and the risk owner decide whether to temporarily suspend an AI service. During the weekend when an incident occurred, the risk owner was unavailable, and nobody could assume authority to suspend the service. What change is needed as an organizational control?

learning.reason: Designate a primary owner and qualified delegates, and define the scope of their decisions, escalation conditions, handoffs, and records.
learning.concept: Clarify the responsible owner first, then define the delegate's authority, scope, and documentation.

A.text: Formally appoint a delegate, document suspension criteria and escalation contacts, and rehearse weekend decisions and handoffs.
A.explanation: This preserves accountability while enabling action during the required hours.

B.text: Give every operator the authority to suspend the service and eliminate the defined scope of delegation and decision records.
B.explanation: This addresses unavailability but does not control accountability and authority.

C.text: Continue providing the service without investigating the cause or external impact until the risk owner returns.
C.explanation: This delays decisions needed to address serious impacts.

D.text: Do not appoint an internal delegate because the provider's AI will assess risk on its own.
D.explanation: This does not establish business accountability or authority to suspend the service.

aib-c01-d3-086@1.title: Keep processing-location requirements in place on the failover path
aib-c01-d3-086@1.prompt: An AI system processes contract drafts. The contract requires processing and storage to remain in a specified region. The primary path meets this requirement, but the provider automatically selects the failover path, and its processing region has not been verified. What should be done before operations begin?

learning.reason: Verify the actual processing and storage locations on both the primary and failover paths. Allow only paths that meet the requirement, and test suspending the service safely as well.
learning.concept: In addition to approving the normal path, verify the actual region used for processing and storage on the failover path.

A.text: Because the primary path meets the requirement, treat processing outside the region during a failure as an audit exception.
A.explanation: The contractual requirement also applies during failures.

B.text: Finish validation by displaying the regional requirement on screen, without verifying which processing destination is selected.
B.explanation: Displaying the requirement does not control where processing actually takes place.

C.text: Record only normal processing and storage, and rely on the region listed in recovery documentation without checking the failover path in operation.
C.explanation: This cannot prove that the specified requirement is maintained during an actual failover.

D.text: Verify the actual processing and storage destinations on both the primary and failover paths, and restrict them to the specified region. Test suspension when safe operation cannot continue.
D.explanation: This applies the essential requirement through failover operations as well.

aib-c01-d3-087@1.title: Send the AI only the fields it needs, even when the full record is accessible
aib-c01-d3-087@1.prompt: An accounting AI checks payment due dates and amounts. People are authorized to open all information in a record, but the model should receive only the fields needed for the payment, and staff members’ personal notes must not be used. Choose three measures.

learning.reason: Check access in an AI-specific retrieval process and pass only authorized fields. Verify that personal notes are absent from the input and related records.
learning.concept: Do not stop at record-level access authorization; limit the fields passed to AI and how they are used.

A.text: Send every field and rely only on instructions to the model to keep it from using personal notes.
A.explanation: The data sent to the model exceeds what is needed.

B.text: Even when payment processing is discontinued, collect unrelated personal notes for evaluation.
B.explanation: This expands the requested purpose and scope of use.

C.text: Specify which fields the AI uses at the data retrieval layer and return only what is needed, such as the amount and due date.
C.explanation: Unneeded fields can be excluded before they are sent to the model.

D.text: Test that unneeded fields are absent from the model input and records of its processing.
D.explanation: This verifies actual retrieval and processing, not just the configuration.

E.text: Check the requester’s authorization against the case before retrieving it.
E.explanation: This prevents unauthorized use of the target record.

aib-c01-d3-088@1.title: Assess whether a human review requirement can actually be carried out
aib-c01-d3-088@1.prompt: A benefits guidance AI was classified as medium risk on the condition that “a staff member reviews each item before it is sent.” In a proposed expansion, daily volume will increase tenfold, and the department plans to send most items without review and without adding staff. How should the risk be handled?

learning.reason: The review that supported the previous classification will not be carried out, so reassess the incident impact and remaining controls before expansion. Test the effectiveness of any new review or scope limits.
learning.concept: Classify risk by checking whether assumed controls can really be carried out at the planned workload.

A.text: Deploy it to everyone first, and investigate whether there are too few reviewers only if incidents increase.
A.explanation: This does not assess the impact of insufficient review in advance.

B.text: Reclassify the system based on the number of items that can be reviewed and the impact of sending unreviewed items, then revise the review scope or operating procedures before expanding.
B.explanation: This checks the original assessment’s assumptions against the oversight that can actually be carried out.

C.text: The model and guidance text are unchanged, so the actual review rate should not affect the risk classification.
C.explanation: The assumption that supported the lower classification has changed.

D.text: If an approval screen is displayed, record that the previous level of oversight is maintained even if staff do not review the items.
D.explanation: The presence of a screen does not show that the required review actually took place.

aib-c01-d3-089@1.title: Ensure monitoring covers new processing paths
aib-c01-d3-089@1.prompt: Results from AI-assisted inquiries through an established interface are audited regularly. After a separate intake application was added, its responses were not included in the audit, even though it uses the same underlying platform. What is the appropriate improvement?

learning.reason: Compare audit coverage and actual results for each processing path. Apply controls from the start of a new path and alert when unaudited paths increase.
learning.concept: Continuously verify that quality monitoring reflects every production path.

A.text: Compare audit scope and volume for each production path, and alert on new paths and the number of unaudited cases.
A.explanation: This shows where audit coverage is missing across the platform.

B.text: Measure only the new application’s availability, and assess response errors only when they occur through the established interface.
B.explanation: This confuses availability with response quality.

C.text: Save results from the new path only after they are published, and check whether it was added to the audit only if a user asks.
C.explanation: This does not incorporate operational scope changes into the controls.

D.text: Assume that auditing only the established interface also evaluates the separate application’s operations because both use the same platform.
D.explanation: This overlooks inputs and settings specific to the separate interface.

aib-c01-d3-090@1.title: Check whether gaps in recorded outcomes distort fairness measurements
aib-c01-d3-090@1.prompt: An audit of an admissions guidance AI compares satisfaction recorded at the end of a consultation across groups. People who leave early because the guidance is difficult to follow have no recorded result, and the rate of early departure differs by language. What is the appropriate monitoring improvement?

learning.reason: Do not treat respondents’ satisfaction as representative of all users. Measure early departures and guidance quality by language, and conduct additional checks within the permitted scope.
learning.concept: Do not rule out bias based only on observations from users whose outcomes are easy to record; also examine departures after a decision.

A.text: Determine that there can be no group bias if the language used is not recorded.
A.explanation: Making the information invisible does not remove barriers to use.

B.text: Because there are few responses in minority-language groups, fill in their results with the scores for majority-language groups.
B.explanation: This replaces direct measurement needed to identify disparities.

C.text: Judge fairness for everyone using only the users who received a score, and exclude users who left early.
C.explanation: Users who could not use the service are omitted from the analysis.

D.text: Compare early departures by language and the conditions under which scores are recorded, and, where permitted, also collect reasons for early departure or an independent quality assessment.
D.explanation: This reveals whose outcomes are missing from the available data.

aib-c01-d3-091@1.title: Separate permission to use the source material from permission to create a person's likeness
aib-c01-d3-091@1.prompt: An advertising team is creating a product explainer video from an authorized photograph. The AI also created material that makes a person in the photo appear to say an endorsement they did not agree to. Company policy requires the person to approve both the use and the content of such a portrayal. What should the team do?

learning.reason: Check permission to use the photograph separately from approval of the generated endorsement. Hold the unapproved material and replace it with an approved portrayal.
learning.concept: Access to the original photograph does not by itself authorize generating and publishing an endorsement or statement by the person.

A.text: Hold any material for which the person's approval of the intended use and spoken content cannot be confirmed, and use an approved portrayal.
A.explanation: This distinguishes permission to use the photograph from approval of a newly generated endorsement by the person.

B.text: Treat an AI-generated label alone as satisfying the person's approval requirement.
B.explanation: Identifying generated content does not replace the rights holder's consent.

C.text: Because permission was granted for the photograph, publish the material without telling the person that speech was generated for them.
C.explanation: The required approval for the new use and content is missing.

D.text: Generate a different person who resembles the person in the existing photograph, then publish it so it appears to be an endorsement by the same person.
D.explanation: This could mislead viewers into believing the person endorsed something they did not.

aib-c01-d3-092@1.title: Compare stale reused results with current evidence
aib-c01-d3-092@1.prompt: A product-information AI search can retrieve a revised version immediately. However, questions that were answered previously return saved older answers. The investigation found that the document version is not checked before an older answer is reused. Which improvement is appropriate?

learning.reason: Associate reused results with their evidence version and applicability, and make them unusable when current information changes. Test both newly asked questions and previously asked questions.
learning.concept: After search results are updated, examine paths that use prior answers and verify version linkage and invalidation.

A.text: Link reused results to the evidence version and invalidate them when revisions or applicability changes occur. When the question is asked again, verify that the answer is generated from new evidence.
A.explanation: This directly improves and verifies the execution path that returns old answers.

B.text: Change only the display date of every answer to today, without recording which document the content was based on.
B.explanation: This merely makes outdated evidence appear to have been updated.

C.text: Test only that the search can retrieve the current version, and assume that saved answers are unaffected.
C.explanation: An old state can be returned through a path that does not run the search.

D.text: Give highest priority to returning identical wording for a question, and retain past answers even when documents are revised.
D.explanation: This cannot maintain the current information that users need.

aib-c01-d3-093@1.title: Let users choose what to share with AI for each task
aib-c01-d3-093@1.prompt: A document guidance feature works when users select only part of a document to send to AI. Currently, pressing Start automatically sends every page, and an explanation appears only after the data has been sent. What change is needed to protect personal information?

learning.reason: Make the information to be handled and its destination clear before assistance begins, and make it possible to select the smallest necessary scope. Set this as the default, and allow users to continue without sending anything if they do not need the feature.
learning.concept: Before assistance begins, explain where information will be sent and how it will be handled, then let users choose the minimum scope.

A.text: Show what was sent after the process starts, and remove the option to change the scope before sending.
A.explanation: Users cannot make a selection before their data is sent.

B.text: Show only the document name and treat sending every page as if users had a choice about what to share.
B.explanation: Users cannot understand what will be sent or choose its scope.

C.text: Remove personal information from the summary, and conclude that the scope of what is sent does not need to be controlled.
C.explanation: Handling the result does not limit what is sent from the original data.

D.text: Show the scope before sending, let users select only the necessary parts, and offer an option not to use the feature.
D.explanation: This enables data minimization and user choice.

aib-c01-d3-094@1.title: Work backward from the organization's incident-reporting deadline to the vendor notification process
aib-c01-d3-094@1.prompt: An organization's policy for outsourced AI processing requires an initial report within 24 hours after it becomes aware of a breach involving in-scope data, even if the scope has not yet been confirmed. The vendor proposes reporting incidents in a weekly summary. What should the organization do before adopting the service?

learning.reason: Define how promptly the vendor must notify the organization, who owns the organization's initial report, and how incident details and timestamps are recorded. Exercise whether the deadline can be met without waiting for a scheduled update.
learning.concept: When the incident detector and the organization responsible for reporting are different, clarify how notification starts, what evidence is needed, and who is responsible.

A.text: Keep the weekly notification and accept reports without requiring the time the vendor detected the incident.
A.explanation: This cannot reliably establish the incident timeline or meet the deadline for an initial report.

B.text: Set an availability target in the contract and assume that this automatically satisfies breach notification requirements as well.
B.explanation: Service availability and incident notification and reporting are different requirements.

C.text: Define prompt vendor notification and the organization's reporting owner, record timestamps and known facts, and exercise whether an initial report can be made before the scope is confirmed.
C.explanation: This translates the deadline and the requirement to report preliminary information into operational roles.

D.text: Have neither the organization nor the vendor begin notifying anyone until all affected data has been identified.
D.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to make an initial report even when the scope is not yet confirmed.

aib-c01-d3-095@1.title: Do not offset harm to some users with overall performance
aib-c01-d3-095@1.prompt: One candidate for service-counter guidance saves substantial time overall, but the proportion of users who need the feature and can complete the procedure falls below the established minimum threshold. Another candidate provides less time savings but meets the quality standard and the minimum threshold for every group. Which decision is appropriate?

learning.reason: First choose an approach that satisfies the mandatory requirements for every group. Reevaluate the higher-saving candidate only if its impact can be reduced and it can be verified to meet the minimum thresholds.
learning.concept: Compare candidates using both pre-established group-specific minimum thresholds and operational efficiency.

A.text: Because the time savings are substantial, lower the group-specific requirements after evaluation and then approve the candidate.
A.explanation: This changes a mandatory criterion after harm has been identified.

B.text: Release the candidate with the greatest overall time savings, and exclude the group that could not complete the procedure when reporting overall performance.
B.explanation: This fails to protect that group's minimum requirement and makes improvement harder to see.

C.text: Choose the candidate that meets the baseline requirements, and reconsider the higher-saving candidate only after addressing group-specific harm and confirming that it again meets the minimum thresholds.
C.explanation: This preserves the required service level while still pursuing operational time savings.

D.text: Combine the overall performance of one candidate with the completion rate for the disadvantaged group achieved by the other candidate, and treat one candidate as having achieved both results.
D.explanation: Results achieved by different approaches cannot be combined as evidence that one approach has been proven to achieve both.

aib-c01-d3-096@1.title: Plan for evaluation data disposal from the start
aib-c01-d3-096@1.prompt: A company plans to ingest approved materials for one month to evaluate the quality of a support AI. The evaluation will take place in multiple environments, and after the purpose ends, copies of the originals and temporary files must also be disposed of. Which requirement is most appropriate?

learning.reason: Before collection, record destinations and copies, and decide how to verify deadlines, ownership, and deletion.
learning.concept: Design purpose, retention limits, decommissioning—including copies—and evidence before collecting data.

A.text: Search for storage locations after testing, and assume any materials that cannot be found have been deleted.
A.explanation: This does not prepare evidence that the data was located and disposed of comprehensively within the deadline.

B.text: Set an expiration date only for the original materials, and leave copies in evaluation environments to staff who are no longer involved in the system.
B.explanation: This cannot ensure that materials are disposed of regardless of where they were ingested.

C.text: Keep copies indefinitely so the evaluation can be repeated, without checking whether the purpose of use is still the same.
C.explanation: This does not meet the one-month use condition.

D.text: Before collection, make it possible to record all destinations, copies, purposes, deadlines, and deletion responsibilities, and design a way to verify disposal at the end.
D.explanation: This makes it possible to track what was used and confirm that disposal is complete.

aib-c01-d3-097@1.title: Remove unnecessary user data from incident support materials
aib-c01-d3-097@1.prompt: An AI service returned an error, and you want to share investigation materials with an external support engineer. The required details are the time of occurrence, error type, and model version, but the original logs contain the full text and user names. What is the most appropriate way to handle the materials?

learning.reason: Prepare materials containing only the details required for the investigation, and use an authorized support channel. Confirm the shared content and recipient scope.
learning.concept: Even when external support is needed, limit the information shared and access rights to the investigation’s purpose.

A.text: Share all operational logs without a retention limit, but mark the file name as confidential.
A.explanation: A label does not limit the information shared or who receives it.

B.text: Extract only the required details, and confirm access and the expiration period before sharing them with an approved support channel.
B.explanation: This limits the information and recipients to what is needed for the purpose.

C.text: Remove the time and version before sharing, and send only the full input text.
C.explanation: This omits details needed for the investigation while disclosing unnecessary information.

D.text: Copy the full text and ask the recipient to remove anything unnecessary.
D.explanation: This discloses information unrelated to the purpose at the time of sending.

aib-c01-d3-098@1.title: Apply different risk controls to different actions in one interface
aib-c01-d3-098@1.prompt: An internal purchasing AI can display suggestions, create drafts visible only to the employee handling them, and send confirmed orders to suppliers. An incorrect confirmed order incurs cancellation costs. Which classification is appropriate?

learning.reason: Classify actions by their outcomes, impact, and reversibility, and apply stronger approval and tracking to confirmed order submission.
learning.concept: Separate classifications and controls when actions by the same user have different confirmation and execution impacts.

A.text: Because the AI is used by the purchasing department, treat suggestions and confirmed orders as one category and keep no action-specific records.
A.explanation: This does not allow controls and verification suited to each action.

B.text: Classify the fastest operation as low risk and the slowest as high risk.
B.explanation: Execution time does not measure the impact of an incorrect action.

C.text: Assess suggestions, drafts, and confirmed orders separately, and require stronger approval and records for actions that send orders externally.
C.explanation: This aligns controls with the business impact of each action, even within one feature.

D.text: Classify everything as suggestion display because all actions are available through the same input field.
D.explanation: This ignores the impact of sending confirmed orders externally.

aib-c01-d3-099@1.title: Verify that user choices still work after configuration changes
aib-c01-d3-099@1.prompt: Requests from people who opt out of AI use are routed to a human contact. After a configuration change, the choice still appears on screen, but some requests from people who opted out proceeded to automated processing. What operational control should be put in place?

learning.reason: Detect mismatches between a user’s choice and the actual processing route. Test representative cases before and after configuration changes, and establish a procedure for stopping misrouted requests.
learning.concept: Include ongoing verification that operational processes honor commitments made to users in operational monitoring.

A.text: Treat a higher share of automated processing as better quality, and exclude use of the human route from measurement.
A.explanation: This does not assess whether users’ choices are being honored.

B.text: Compare choice records with processing routes, alert on mismatches, and check before and after configuration changes.
B.explanation: This verifies that user choices are reflected in the workflow.

C.text: Monitor only whether the choice is displayed on screen, without checking the route actually taken.
C.explanation: The choice may not be honored even when it is displayed correctly.

D.text: If each user receives a result, do not check whether it followed the requested route.
D.explanation: This confuses delivering a result with honoring the user’s choice.

aib-c01-d3-100@1.title: Do not finalize an overall result just because one inquiry completed
aib-c01-d3-100@1.prompt: An AI system checks both inventory and quality approval to determine whether a product can be shipped. When one inquiry times out, it answered that shipment was allowed based on the other inquiry alone. The result and completion status of each inquiry are available. Which approach would improve operational reliability?

learning.reason: Finalize only when both inquiries succeed and their results concern the same product. Deliberately test failures and timeouts, and route cases with missing results to a person for review.
learning.concept: When all concurrently retrieved inputs are required, define the completion criteria and safely hold the decision instead of inferring missing results.

A.text: Substitute a previous answer for the timed-out inquiry without checking the product or the update time.
A.explanation: This could use a result for a different product or an outdated state.

B.text: Shorten the wording of the decision and do not record the completion status of each inquiry.
B.explanation: This cannot distinguish a decision made with all required results from behavior when an inquiry fails.

C.text: Finalize the decision only after confirming both inquiries succeeded and concern the same product; test holding the decision and handing it off when either result is missing.
C.explanation: This reduces the risk of incorrectly deciding that shipment is allowed when a required result is missing.

D.text: Decide based on the first successful response, without checking whether the other inquiry has completed.
D.explanation: This finalizes the decision based on only part of a required shipping condition.

aib-c01-d4-081@1.title: Update the readiness decision when an assumption changes
aib-c01-d4-081@1.prompt: A job-seeking advice AI passed quality and frontline staff training assessments. Later, the contact center supporting the pilot ended its after-hours service, leaving customers who can use the service only on holidays without an alternative. How should the pre-launch readiness review be updated?

learning.reason: Revisit the assumptions that supported operations, including which users are affected, any contractual obligations, and where a holiday alternative is needed. Verify that the service can be supported using the actual post-change procedures.
learning.concept: Retain successful technical assessment results while reassessing changes in external support or data required for actual service delivery.

A.text: Because the number of holiday customers is not yet known, leave those customers and the existing support out of scope and assess the system overall.
A.explanation: This cannot determine readiness for a condition with a direct impact.

B.text: Because quality is high, after the contact center changes, force automated answers only on customers who report problems.
B.explanation: Current quality and the alternatives needed under different conditions are separate considerations.

C.text: The system passed the earlier review, so consider it ready as is even though the support assumptions have changed.
C.explanation: This does not verify current operational capability.

D.text: Confirm the needs of holiday users and the response requirements, prepare an appropriate alternative, and reassess readiness under the changed support arrangements.
D.explanation: This makes use of the technical evidence already gathered while testing the changed operational assumptions.

aib-c01-d4-082@1.title: Do not treat purchasing AI capacity as proof that an experiment has succeeded
aib-c01-d4-082@1.prompt: A business unit purchased capacity for an AI service and listed several improvement ideas. However, it has not selected a representative use case or defined success criteria, and it has not tested results in its operations. What is its maturity stage, and what should it do next?

learning.reason: A provisioned environment does not produce experimental results by itself. Treat this as the envisioning stage, select a use case, define a hypothesis and measurements, set the scope, and start an experiment.
learning.concept: Distinguish maturity in envisioning from the start of measurement, and make the next stage an experiment with a defined scope and evaluation criteria.

A.text: Treat it as being at the envisioning stage, define the target workflow and the conditions for success and stopping, and run a small experiment.
A.explanation: This establishes the conditions for moving to measurement and puts the resources already acquired to use.

B.text: Treat it as being at the stage where every department can deploy the same capability because capacity was purchased company-wide.
B.explanation: Production responsibilities, procedures, and outcomes have not been tested.

C.text: Treat it as being in production and defer defining workflow hypotheses until more capacity is available.
C.explanation: This confuses procuring an environment with operating it in practice.

D.text: Since payments have begun, treat the experiment as successful and choose which departments continue based only on user counts.
D.explanation: A purchase is not evidence that a hypothesis has been tested.

aib-c01-d4-083@1.title: Investigate why the organization is not improving despite frontline corrections
aib-c01-d4-083@1.prompt: Version control and AI monitoring are in place, and frontline staff can correct errors manually. However, the corrections and their reasons do not reach the evaluation environment, so model updates repeat the same errors. Which capability should be added?

learning.reason: Record the corrections and their reasons, select valid cases, and use them in testing and improvement. Feed the results after changes back to frontline staff as well.
learning.concept: Distinguish the ability to make human corrections from the ability to turn the reasons for those corrections into reusable evaluations.

A.text: Prohibit frontline corrections and send only correctly returned results for evaluation.
A.explanation: This removes both a way to address the problem and the evidence needed to improve.

B.text: Replace the model with a new one, and consider later whether it can receive correction reasons.
B.explanation: The structure that prevents recurring errors from informing the next evaluation remains.

C.text: Share the reasons for corrections as cases, assign someone to select valid examples for evaluation, and establish a process for testing them in the next version.
C.explanation: This connects frontline corrections to preventing the errors from recurring.

D.text: Conclude that no capability is missing because frontline staff can make corrections, and report version quality only as a company-wide average.
D.explanation: Information about recurring failures is still not being used to improve the system.

aib-c01-d4-084@1.title: Invest first in capabilities that support company-wide goals repeatedly
aib-c01-d4-084@1.prompt: The organization aims to show both results and supporting evidence in audits for its current document AI and next year's business AI. One proposal is to build a dedicated interface; another is to establish shared evidence recording and train frontline staff in evaluation. The dedicated interface would cover only one business process. Which investment order best serves the goal?

learning.reason: Build evidence and evaluation capabilities needed across multiple use cases first. Confirm that they work in the current operation, then implement dedicated interfaces as each use case requires.
learning.concept: Choose capabilities that will be needed repeatedly across future use cases, then deploy use-case-specific solutions as they mature.

A.text: Build the dedicated interface first, then rebuild evidence recording separately for each other use case.
A.explanation: This does not connect a repeatedly needed capability to the current state.

B.text: Wait until next year's business process begins before addressing the current gaps in evidence.
B.explanation: This misses the opportunity to demonstrate the capability needed for current operations.

C.text: Establish shared evidence recording and frontline evaluation in the current operation, then add interfaces and operating practices for specific use cases as needed, based on that evidence.
C.explanation: This addresses the current gap while building a capability that can be reused across multiple use cases.

D.text: Improve only model speed, and leave evidence checks to individuals' discretion.
D.explanation: This does not establish a shared capability for presenting evidence in audits.

aib-c01-d4-085@1.title: Check whether accurate data is available in time for the intended use
aib-c01-d4-085@1.prompt: An AI system that notifies employees about the status of their requests is intended to improve response within one day of submission. HR's finalized records are accurate and access-authorized, but are provided in a batch at the end of each month. How should readiness for a pilot be assessed?

learning.reason: Measure when the data can actually be used against the required action deadline. Consider whether earlier approved information or a different use case is available.
learning.concept: Assess the amount and accuracy of historical data separately from its freshness at the time an action must be taken.

A.text: Declare the data ready because its volume and accuracy are sufficient, and treat a notification sent the following month as an improvement.
A.explanation: The data is not timely enough for the intended response.

B.text: Check only whether the department has viewing permission, and defer consideration of data arrival times until after the platform is implemented.
B.explanation: Authorized data is not necessarily available when it is needed.

C.text: Measure the delay between submission and data availability, then consider approved information that can be used within the deadline or a change to the use case.
C.explanation: This assesses when the data is actually available, which is part of data quality for the work in question.

D.text: Assign each month-end value to every day of that month and train and evaluate as though the value had been available on each day.
D.explanation: This uses values that were not available on those days.

aib-c01-d4-086@1.title: Set the scope for shared use when source data cannot be moved
aib-c01-d4-086@1.prompt: Three departments want to aggregate the business impact of AI together. Each department manages its own source-level records, and the applicable permissions prohibit moving those records outside the department. However, validated aggregates at agreed classification levels may be shared. Which data strategy is appropriate?

learning.reason: Each owner can retain control of source records and share only the necessary results using approved definitions and aggregation levels. Shared rules should specify quality, permitted disclosure, and responsibility for updates.
learning.concept: Sharing does not require physical centralization; validated aggregates can be shared within the scope each owner controls.

A.text: Move every department's source-level record to a shared storage location to standardize the aggregation process.
A.explanation: This violates the restriction on moving source-level records outside the department.

B.text: Keep source-level records in each department and agree on definitions and disclosure granularity. Share only aggregates whose quality has been verified by their owners.
B.explanation: This preserves each department's control while enabling joint use under consistent standards.
