C.text: Give up all cross-department comparisons, including approved aggregates, because the source-level records cannot be moved.
C.explanation: It may be possible to compare departments within the permitted scope.

D.text: Have each department share aggregates using different periods and populations, then have AI estimate the differences when combining them.
D.explanation: This fails to establish the definitions and evidence needed for joint results.

aib-c01-d4-087@1.title: Verify the conditions for resuming work on another platform
aib-c01-d4-087@1.prompt: An organization is choosing a platform for its internal AI. When the contract ends, it wants to move its configuration and approved search data to a new platform while maintaining the quality that has already been reviewed. One candidate says its assets can be exported, but has not tested whether business integrations work after migration. What is the best way to verify this?

learning.reason: Move a representative configuration and permitted data, then verify on the other platform that they are in a readable format, connect to existing workflows, and meet the same quality standard.
learning.concept: In addition to comparing candidate features, test in practice whether deliverables can be migrated, the required integrations can be established, and the same evaluation criteria are met.

A.text: Treat the generation of an export file as proof that everything will work on another platform.
A.explanation: This does not verify import compatibility, integrations, or quality.

B.text: Have the vendor keep a complete record of the work and discuss which items to retrieve only when they are needed.
B.explanation: This does not verify in advance what materials and time will be available at contract end.

C.text: Using a representative configuration, test export and import, reconnect it to business workflows, and verify quality; record the time required and any gaps.
C.explanation: This checks the conditions for continuing the work on the new platform, not just whether the export and import operations are possible.

D.text: If processing is fastest in the first year, do not assess the conditions at contract end.
D.explanation: This cannot determine whether the specified business-continuity conditions will be met in the future.

aib-c01-d4-088@1.title: Leadership defines what local champions can improve
aib-c01-d4-088@1.prompt: AI champions at each branch must wait for the same company-wide review whether they are adapting approved practice exercises to local terminology or changing how customer data is handled. An executive sponsor wants to speed up local improvements while preserving safety. How should authority be assigned?

learning.reason: Clearly delegate changes that have low impact and preserve evaluation criteria. Route changes affecting data or external parties through the existing review process, and maintain records and reporting.
learning.concept: Define the scope of routine, small improvements delegated to local teams, while leadership and the responsible departments retain decisions that change controls.

A.text: Delegate localization of approved exercises to champions within defined standards and recordkeeping requirements, while routing changes to customer data handling through the established review process.
A.explanation: This accelerates low-impact improvements while leaving decisions about important controls with the responsible teams.

B.text: Do not evaluate branch improvements; have the executive sponsor edit every piece of wording individually.
B.explanation: This centralizes decisions even for low-impact improvements that local champions could make.

C.text: Have branches make small changes in informal shared spaces, without recording any changes.
C.explanation: The organization cannot verify the delegated scope or its results, and it is difficult to distinguish these changes from unauthorized ones.

D.text: Give branches authority over both exercise text and customer data changes so that the work is locally owned.
D.explanation: This gives high-impact changes the same level of authority as low-impact exercise updates.

aib-c01-d4-089@1.title: Add a team member responsible for workforce impacts
aib-c01-d4-089@1.prompt: An insurer is introducing AI into its administrative operations. The model development owner has been selected, but no one is responsible for designing changes to customer-service representatives’ roles and training, or for feeding user complaints back into the design. Which cross-functional team should be formed?

learning.reason: Include business owners, customer-service and training representatives, technical staff, and quality or legal staff, and assign responsibility for redesigning the work and providing evidence of acceptance.
learning.concept: Assign different owners for design, user impacts, quality, and legal responsibilities.

A.text: Include business operations, customer-service and training representatives, technical staff, and legal or quality staff; assign owners for role changes, training, and user review.
A.explanation: This turns impacts on technology, frontline work, and users into distinct responsibilities.

B.text: Invite a broad range of departments to meetings, but consolidate testing and approval under a shared role with no designated owner.
B.explanation: When an issue arises, it will be unclear who makes the decision and responds.

C.text: Leave everything to the development team and decide how to handle training and complaints only after quality passes.
C.explanation: The work and users directly affected are not represented in the design.

D.text: Have the provider assess impacts on users and customer-service representatives, while the internal team only sets the launch date.
D.explanation: This does not define the internal operating model and responsibilities that remain with the organization.

aib-c01-d4-090@1.title: Explain workflow changes and how frontline feedback reaches decision-makers
aib-c01-d4-090@1.prompt: Employees received an AI launch announcement saying, “Productivity will improve,” but do not know which requests they will handle starting next month or where to report an incorrect output. What should the announcement be changed to say?

learning.reason: Explain which tasks will change, which responsibilities will continue, the planned start date, who handles exceptions, and how to submit suggestions for improvement. Give a date for the next decision on unresolved items.
learning.concept: Communicate specific roles and procedures during the transition so employees can raise concerns and help shape improvements.

A.text: Start deployment first, and explain affected job duties only after a certain number of questions have accumulated.
A.explanation: Employees will not be prepared when their work changes.

B.text: Specify the change date, tasks and responsibilities by role, where to report errors, and when decisions will be made about incorporating feedback.
B.explanation: Employees can act when the change takes effect and continue to raise issues and concerns.

C.text: Announce that every employee will use AI the same way, and decide how to handle out-of-scope requests through individual consultations.
C.explanation: Actual roles and procedures for exceptions remain unclear.

D.text: Mention only the AI brand and expected productivity, without notifying employees when their responsibilities will change.
D.explanation: The effect on day-to-day work remains unclear.

aib-c01-d4-091@1.title: Addressing uncertainty about permitted AI use through manager practices
aib-c01-d4-091@1.prompt: A department understands how to use AI, but managers say only, “Avoid mistakes,” and no one is sure what is acceptable. Many employees identify promising improvements but do not try them. What is the most appropriate first step?

learning.reason: Managers should show concrete examples of approved uses and cases that require consultation. They should enable limited trials and support employees when they are unsure how to proceed.
learning.concept: Go beyond having employees read the rules: clarify in practical terms which tasks are suitable and which require consultation.

A.text: Do not explain acceptable use cases until employees submit a certain number of new improvement ideas.
A.explanation: This asks employees to experiment while they still do not know what is acceptable.

B.text: Tell employees that any use not expressly prohibited is at their own risk, and that managers will not discuss exceptions.
B.explanation: This leaves the organization without a way to support responsible experimentation.

C.text: Set a minimum usage target and require uncertain employees to use the same approach as another department.
C.explanation: This does not resolve uncertainty about approval or departmental conditions.

D.text: Have managers and frontline staff share permitted use cases, set up limited trials and a channel for questions, and actively support decisions made through that process.
D.explanation: This directly addresses both unclear policy and concern about failure.

aib-c01-d4-092@1.title: Prioritizing training based on actual decision errors
aib-c01-d4-092@1.prompt: An audit found that many employees can generate AI-written text, but they cannot distinguish approved reference material from outdated material and sent incorrect guidance. Training time is limited. Which development approach is likely to be most effective?

learning.reason: Identify the work where errors occur, then repeatedly practice checking versions and evidence and holding content when it has not been verified, using realistic examples. Measure whether employees can perform these tasks.
learning.concept: Design training around where role-specific errors occur and their impact, rather than around general interest.

A.text: Adapt training to the topics employees are most interested in, and rely only on self-assessment for decisions about correcting or holding content.
A.explanation: This does not verify that employees can perform the required work correctly.

B.text: Use examples involving reference-version selection, checking supporting evidence, and holding content for review, then assess whether employees can make the right decisions in practice.
B.explanation: This directs limited time toward the practical skills that affect the work.

C.text: Because employees frequently ask about new features, exclude review of the older workflow where the problem occurred.
C.explanation: This does not build the ability to reduce the incorrect guidance that was actually sent.

D.text: Repeat a course focused only on text generation, which employees have already mastered, and assess whether they can write long passages.
D.explanation: This does not address the most serious weakness.

aib-c01-d4-093@1.title: Redirecting time from automated data entry to maintaining operational quality
aib-c01-d4-093@1.prompt: AI correctly assists with copying product codes. When a new product is added, an employee notices that its code resembles one for a different product and can align the registration rules with the product team. What is the most appropriate way to redesign the role?

learning.reason: Shift employees toward investigating exceptions and maintaining criteria and evaluation practices, while assigning AI only routine processing that has been verified. Continue to review changes and quality.
learning.concept: Reduce routine copying with AI and assign people to anomalies in the data and maintenance of decision criteria.

A.text: Use AI to assist with copying codes, while employees handle unusual matches, improve registration criteria with the product team, and verify quality after changes.
A.explanation: This puts the time saved through automation toward human judgment and ongoing quality improvement.

B.text: Assume that automating data entry eliminates every need for people to make decisions about product codes.
B.explanation: Ambiguities involving new products and existing data remain unresolved.

C.text: Have AI automatically update rules for new products without checking whether they are correct, while employees continue copying codes.
C.explanation: This delegates changes requiring organizational judgment to automation while retaining routine work.

D.text: Evaluate employees by how often they open the screen, without recording which unusual cases they resolved.
D.explanation: This cannot measure the operational value of the redesigned role.

aib-c01-d4-094@1.title: Revalidating when conditions differ between a pilot and production
aib-c01-d4-094@1.prompt: In an AI document-organization experiment, every document had been classified by an employee in advance. In production, the system will accept both classified and unclassified documents. The owner wants to use the experiment’s results to move to the next stage. What is the appropriate approach?

learning.reason: Retain the results for classified documents within the scope they support, and use a small follow-up experiment to measure the quality and processing time of unclassified documents and the review path. Decide on release only for the conditions that meet the criteria.
learning.concept: Understand the conditions under which evidence was obtained, and explicitly include changed assumptions in the next experiment.

A.text: Since the experiment already succeeded, release it for all documents, assuming unclassified documents will have the same quality.
A.explanation: This extrapolates to conditions the experiment did not measure.

B.text: Exclude all records of processing unclassified documents from the experiment so the success rate in the next report remains unchanged.
B.explanation: This removes a necessary condition from the evaluation.

C.text: Conclude that the experiment’s results cannot be used and return to the concept stage without measuring either classified or unclassified documents.
C.explanation: This fails to distinguish confirmed results from conditions that remain untested.

D.text: Record the original success criteria, then run an additional experiment with unclassified documents to assess outcomes and failure handling.
D.explanation: This incorporates the new production condition into the learning process before release.

aib-c01-d4-095@1.title: Connecting an Early Efficiency Gain to the Next Step in the Same Workflow
aib-c01-d4-095@1.prompt: An AI tool that organizes application documents has reduced classification time at intake. The same application then goes to another department, which checks for missing information and responds to the customer. It has not been verified whether the downstream team can understand the new handoff. How should the expansion proceed?

learning.reason: Build on the validated intake results and test the new handoff with downstream staff. Measure outcomes and workload through completion, then expand from the steps where benefits are confirmed.
learning.concept: Identify what made the initial effort successful, then determine what conditions preserve value in downstream work before expanding its scope.

A.text: Since intake is faster, assume the same proportion of work can be automated downstream and switch everything over at once.
A.explanation: The handoff requirements and downstream outcomes have not been validated.

B.text: Because the downstream work belongs to a different department, share none of the intake approach or results and build a separate product independently.
B.explanation: This duplicates effort instead of reusing a proven handoff or measurement approach.

C.text: Measure only the number of AI users at every step and do not use customer responses to decide whether to expand.
C.explanation: More usage does not demonstrate an effect on the application process as a whole.

D.text: Connect the validated classification to a small downstream segment, check whether it is understood and how exceptions are handled, and compare end-to-end application completion.
D.explanation: This checks the conditions under which the early gains help the overall workflow.

aib-c01-d4-096@1.title: Building Frontline Capability Without Having the Central Team Do Everything
aib-c01-d4-096@1.prompt: The enterprise AI center of excellence sets standards but currently performs every new quality test on behalf of the business units. As a result, new projects are delayed, and the units cannot run the tests themselves. How should the center of excellence operate?

learning.reason: Train business-unit staff using approved methods and representative examples, then conduct the first test jointly. The center should focus on maintaining standards and advising on difficult cases.
learning.concept: When work is concentrated among a small central group of experts, spread capability to frontline teams through joint practice.

A.text: Keep all testing centralized and give teams in other departments only the completed results.
A.explanation: This sustains the dependency and requires adding more expert capacity as adoption grows.

B.text: Provide standards and coaching, conduct the first test jointly with each business unit, let the unit work independently within the agreed boundaries, and have the center support difficult cases.
B.explanation: This distributes execution capability while preserving shared quality standards.

C.text: Allow only departments with long testing queues to publish without evaluation.
C.explanation: This does not maintain the quality requirements.

D.text: Leave everything to the departments and withdraw shared evaluation criteria and access to expert advice.
D.explanation: Autonomy alone does not preserve quality or enable learning across the organization.

aib-c01-d4-097@1.title: Considering More Than Continued Operation When the Work Is No Longer Meeting Its Purpose
aib-c01-d4-097@1.prompt: An AI system has high usage, but the time to complete the work has worsened for three consecutive months, and staff report that they are doing more reviews. Because usage is high, a report proposes continuing the system. Which operational decision is appropriate?

learning.reason: Analyze increased work using regular outcome measurements and frontline reports. Set improvement criteria for each use case, and evaluate stopping or simplifying any scope with no evidence of recovery.
learning.concept: Use long-term outcomes and changes reported by frontline staff to make it possible to reduce scope or discontinue a use case.

A.text: Do not record changes to the objective; instead, select whichever metric produces the best number each month.
A.explanation: It would no longer be possible to determine whether performance has improved over time.

B.text: Separate usage counts from outcomes, remeasure the effect in the workflow where review work has increased, and consider reducing the scope that cannot meet its target.
B.explanation: This supports long-term value based on actual results.

C.text: Report continued use as a success even when outcomes have been poor for months.
C.explanation: This fails to reflect the value of the actual work in the metrics.

D.text: Exclude frontline feedback from the analysis and make improvements only if the model’s ranking falls.
D.explanation: This does not investigate the specific reasons that review work has increased.

aib-c01-d4-098@1.title: Including Manual Work That Supported the Prototype in Production Responsibilities
aib-c01-d4-098@1.prompt: An AI prototype passed using a product table prepared every day. During the trial, a developer manually replaced it with the latest version, but production runs on holidays too, and responses based on an outdated table are prohibited. Choose two acceptance conditions for production operation.

learning.reason: Define the approved update path, ownership, and update target. Test, including on holidays, whether the system can withhold guidance when it cannot retrieve the latest version.
learning.concept: Specify how to sustain assumptions supported by manual updates during evaluation, and define behavior when those updates fail.

A.text: Keep the table that was manually placed for the prototype fixed in production, and replace it only after a user reports an error.
A.explanation: Prohibited guidance would continue once the table became outdated.

B.text: Define the process and ownership for updating the formally approved version, then test whether it arrives when needed, including on holidays.
B.explanation: This turns an update handled implicitly during the prototype into a sustainable operational process.

C.text: Verify that the system withholds responses and notifies the responsible person when the version is unknown or an update is overdue.
C.explanation: This demonstrates operation that avoids answering with outdated information even when an update fails.

D.text: Change the displayed update date every day without checking whether the table’s contents were updated at the same time.
D.explanation: This cannot prevent guidance based on outdated material.

E.text: Have the guidance AI guess the values in the new table and exclude update delays from existing tests.
E.explanation: The current approved values cannot be retrieved.

aib-c01-d4-099@1.title: Assessing increased human review workload and infrastructure capacity during enterprise-wide rollout
aib-c01-d4-099@1.prompt: An AI document assistant for enterprise-wide use met the inference capacity needs of one department during a pilot. When several departments use it at the same time, exceptions that require quality review are also routed to a shared intake queue used by another department. Which three measures should be checked to avoid disrupting existing work after rollout?

learning.reason: Test operating conditions in which exceptions from several departments arise at the same time, in addition to measuring response speed in isolation.
learning.concept: Validate peak concurrent demand for inference and manual review, establish prioritization and staffing for essential work, and prepare staged pauses and alternatives if capacity targets are missed.

A.text: Delete records from the busiest day after expansion and use only the average wait time on a typical day.
A.explanation: This cannot assess the usage conditions under which problems occur.

B.text: Test simultaneous use by each department and measure wait times for both inference and the review queue.
B.explanation: This reveals constraints that may not be visible when departments are measured separately.

C.text: Check queue prioritization by importance and deadline, as well as staffing and the capacity buffer needed.
C.explanation: This helps ensure that the conditions for critical existing work can still be met after rollout.

D.text: Rehearse the conditions for pausing rollout to the next department when deadlines cannot be met, and switching back to the existing workflow.
D.explanation: This helps prevent an overload from spreading its impact to existing work.

E.text: If all inference requests succeed, do not measure reviewer capacity or wait times in the existing intake queue.
E.explanation: Work can still build up for people even when the AI is operating successfully.

aib-c01-d4-100@1.title: Building leaders’ skills to approve or stop AI initiatives
aib-c01-d4-100@1.prompt: Technical AI training has been widely attended. At an executive meeting, leaders increased the budget based only on the number of inference requests, without realizing that quality requirements were below the threshold. What should be prioritized in training for executives?

learning.reason: Role-specific training should give executives practice in interpreting evidence about outcomes and risks and making decisions.
learning.concept: Use scenarios resembling real approval decisions so executives can assess business outcomes, minimum quality requirements, missing evidence, and stop criteria, and explain their reasoning.

A.text: Run approval exercises that compare usage, business value, quality criteria, and evidence, and examine the reasons for investment or deferral decisions.
A.explanation: This lets leaders practice the decisions they are responsible for making.

B.text: Have all executives practice only how to optimize long prompts, while leaving investment decisions as they are.
B.explanation: This does not address the skills related to the executives’ decision-making error.

C.text: Assume that executives do not need to understand quality or risk because specialist operators can make those decisions.
C.explanation: Executives remain responsible for deciding whether to invest, roll out, or stop.

D.text: Share departments with the highest usage as success stories and leave quality criteria to frontline training alone.
D.explanation: This still leaves executives without the information needed to make decisions at meetings.

ai-business-strategist-practice-01@1.title: Prioritizing use cases
ai-business-strategist-practice-01@1.prompt: You have several generative AI candidates. What should you compare when choosing the first pilot?

learning.reason: This considers both expected benefits and feasibility.
learning.concept: Start with a problem that can be tested on a small scale and whose success or stop decision can be measured.

A.text: Compare business value, data readiness, implementation difficulty, and risk.
A.explanation: This considers both expected benefits and feasibility.

B.text: Choose the project with the most stakeholders.
B.explanation: The number of users alone does not reveal a use case’s outcomes or risks.

C.text: Always choose a project that can use the largest model.
C.explanation: Model size does not indicate business value or implementation feasibility.

ai-business-strategist-practice-02@1.title: Measuring business outcomes
ai-business-strategist-practice-02@1.prompt: Before introducing an AI system for handling inquiries, what should you prepare to assess its impact after deployment?

learning.reason: This allows you to compare before and after deployment using common measures.
learning.concept: Combine efficiency measures with quality measures such as incorrect guidance and repeat inquiries.

A.text: Establish a baseline and targets for measures such as current response time and resolution quality.
A.explanation: This allows you to compare before and after deployment using common measures.

B.text: Record only the number of model parameters.
B.explanation: Model size is not a baseline for business outcomes.

C.text: Collect only positive comments after launch.
C.explanation: This is subject to selection bias and does not allow comparison with the pre-deployment state.

ai-business-strategist-practice-03@1.title: Human Review Before Sending
ai-business-strategist-practice-03@1.prompt: Generative AI drafts important customer-facing notifications. If incorrect content could have a significant impact on customers, which operating practice is appropriate?

learning.reason: Keep human judgment in the process for outputs that could have serious consequences.
learning.concept: Define who reviews outputs, the approval criteria, and how items are returned for revision based on their potential impact.

A.text: Automatically send any message that appears to have high model confidence, without conditions
A.explanation: Fluent wording does not guarantee accuracy.

B.text: Rely only on audit logs to manage the risk of automatic sending
B.explanation: Logs support later review but do not prevent an incorrect message from being sent.

C.text: Have a staff member check the supporting evidence and wording, then approve the message before sending it
C.explanation: Keep human judgment in the process for outputs that could have serious consequences.

ai-business-strategist-practice-04@1.title: Classifying Data for Use
ai-business-strategist-practice-04@1.prompt: When piloting AI with internal data, some documents contain personal information or are subject to contractual restrictions. What should you do first?

learning.reason: This lets you check the use case against the data's sensitivity and usage conditions.
learning.concept: Decide from the start of validation how to handle the purpose of use, access scope, retention period, and whether data is sent to third parties.

A.text: Shorten the prompts to manage confidentiality
A.explanation: Input length does not determine whether data may be used or how it must be handled.

B.text: Classify the data and limit use to what is necessary for the purpose and permitted
B.explanation: This lets you check the use case against the data's sensitivity and usage conditions.

C.text: Submit all documents at once and check the restrictions afterward
C.explanation: This could result in using content without authorization.

ai-business-strategist-practice-05@1.title: Adoption Costs and Benefits
ai-business-strategist-practice-05@1.prompt: An AI tool that summarizes internal documents reduces the time needed for each task. What should you compare to assess the return on investment of ongoing operations?

learning.reason: This lets you assess business benefits and ongoing costs using the same basis.
learning.concept: State your assumptions about task volume, retries, and review rates, and estimate costs as usage grows.

A.text: Decide based only on the model with the lowest price per token
A.explanation: This leaves rework on outputs, quality differences, and operating costs out of the evaluation.

B.text: Compare only the initial development effort during the trial
B.explanation: This does not capture the costs and benefits of continued use.

C.text: Compare the value of the time saved with the total costs of inference, operations, and review
C.explanation: This lets you assess business benefits and ongoing costs using the same basis.

ai-business-strategist-practice-06@1.title: Deciding What to Do After a Pilot
ai-business-strategist-practice-06@1.prompt: An AI pilot met its target for time savings, but incorrect guidance increased in important cases. What should you do next?

learning.reason: This accounts for both efficiency and quality when deciding whether to expand.
learning.concept: Set success and stop conditions before expansion, and do not let failures in important cases disappear into an overall average.

A.text: Make usage volume the only new success metric
A.explanation: This does not help identify or control the quality problem.

B.text: Expand the AI to all business processes based only on meeting the time target
B.explanation: This expands the scope while serious failures remain.

C.text: Analyze the causes of serious errors, limit the scope, and reassess until the errors are within acceptable bounds
C.explanation: This accounts for both efficiency and quality when deciding whether to expand.

ai-business-strategist-practice-01@2.title: Prioritizing Use Cases
ai-business-strategist-practice-01@2.prompt: The customer support and billing teams have proposed two generative AI pilots. One could have a large impact, but its data agreements have not been sorted out; the other could have a smaller impact, but is ready to proceed. How should these options be evaluated so the executive committee can make a decision?

learning.reason: This considers both the expected benefits and the feasibility of realizing them.
learning.concept: Start with a problem that can be tested on a small scale and has measurable criteria for deciding whether to continue or stop.

A.text: Choose based only on the projected first-year savings.
A.explanation: This does not account for whether the data can be used, implementation costs, or the scale of the impact.

B.text: Compare business value, data readiness, implementation difficulty, and risk.
B.explanation: This considers both the expected benefits and the feasibility of realizing them.

C.text: Always choose the use case that can use the largest model.
C.explanation: Model size does not indicate business value or implementation feasibility.

D.text: Choose the use case with the most stakeholders.
D.explanation: The number of users alone does not reveal a use case’s outcomes or risks.

ai-business-strategist-practice-02@2.title: Measuring Business Outcomes
ai-business-strategist-practice-02@2.prompt: A contact center wants AI assistance to shorten call times, without increasing repeat contacts caused by incorrect guidance. What should it prepare before starting the pilot?

learning.reason: This makes it possible to compare performance before and after implementation using consistent measures.
learning.concept: Combine efficiency measures with quality measures, such as incorrect guidance and repeat contacts.

A.text: Record only the number of model parameters.
A.explanation: Model size is not a baseline for business outcomes.

B.text: Set a target only for the activation rate of the new tool.
B.explanation: Adoption can be measured, but there is no basis for comparing business impact and quality.

C.text: Establish baselines and targets for measures such as current handling time and resolution quality.
C.explanation: This makes it possible to compare performance before and after implementation using consistent measures.

D.text: Collect only favorable comments after launch.
D.explanation: This introduces selection bias and provides no comparison with the pre-launch state.

ai-business-strategist-practice-03@2.title: Human Review Before Final Decisions
ai-business-strategist-practice-03@2.prompt: Generative AI will draft notices that affect customers’ rights. If a notice cites an incorrect policy, correcting it after it is sent is difficult. Which control is appropriate before sending?

learning.reason: This retains human judgment for outputs that could have serious consequences.
learning.concept: Define who reviews each output, the approval criteria, and the process for sending it back for revision according to its impact.

A.text: Have a staff member check the supporting evidence and the wording, then approve the notice before it is sent.
A.explanation: This retains human judgment for outputs that could have serious consequences.

B.text: Automatically send any notice whose wording appears to have high model confidence.
B.explanation: Fluent wording does not guarantee correctness.

C.text: Rely only on audit logs to manage the risks of automatic sending.
C.explanation: Logs can support an after-the-fact review, but they do not prevent an incorrect notice from being sent.

D.text: Automatically send the notices, then have a person audit a sample the next day.
D.explanation: This allows evaluation, but does not stop an irreversible notice before it is sent.

ai-business-strategist-practice-04@2.title: Preparing Data for Use
ai-business-strategist-practice-04@2.prompt: An internal search pilot includes documents that cannot be used for purposes outside their contractual terms, personal information, and public materials. Public materials and approved internal materials are sufficient for development. What should be done first?

learning.reason: This makes it possible to check the data’s confidentiality and usage terms against the intended purpose.
learning.concept: Decide from the outset how to verify the purpose of use, access scope, retention period, and whether data will be sent to third parties.

A.text: Shorten the prompts to manage confidentiality.
A.explanation: Input length does not establish whether data may be used or how it must be handled.

B.text: Input all documents at once and check the restrictions afterward.
B.explanation: This could result in using content without permission.

C.text: Index all materials and display a warning in the search results.
C.explanation: Indexing or sending the data could already exceed the contractual restrictions on its use.

D.text: Classify the data and limit it to what is needed for the purpose and permitted for use.
D.explanation: This makes it possible to check the data’s confidentiality and usage terms against the intended purpose.

ai-business-strategist-practice-05@2.title: Implementation Costs and Benefits
ai-business-strategist-practice-05@2.prompt: Pilot measurements for summarization showed that drafting time per item decreased, but operation now requires human corrections and quality audits. The business unit is deciding on next quarter’s investment. What should it compare?

learning.reason: This evaluates business benefits and ongoing costs using the same basis.
learning.concept: State assumptions about volume, retries, and review rates, and estimate how costs change as usage grows.

A.text: Compare the value of the time saved with the total costs of inference, operations, and review.
A.explanation: This evaluates business benefits and ongoing costs using the same basis.

B.text: Compare only the initial development effort during the pilot.
B.explanation: This does not capture the costs and benefits of continued use.

C.text: Count only the reduction in generation time as a benefit, excluding the time people spend making corrections.
C.explanation: This overstates the benefits realized across the entire process.

D.text: Decide solely based on the model with the lowest price per token.
D.explanation: This leaves rework, quality differences, and operating costs out of the evaluation.

ai-business-strategist-practice-06@2.title: Decision After a Pilot
ai-business-strategist-practice-06@2.prompt: A pilot in a limited number of service channels met its processing-time target but exceeded the threshold for serious incorrect guidance. The business owner must decide whether the solution can be expanded safely. What should they do next?

learning.reason: This reflects both efficiency and quality in the expansion decision.
learning.concept: Set success criteria and stop conditions before expansion, and do not let an overall average obscure failures in important cases.

A.text: Roll it out everywhere as long as overall average satisfaction remains steady.
A.explanation: This replaces the threshold for serious errors with an average metric.

B.text: Analyze the causes of serious errors, limit the scope, and reassess until they are within the acceptable range.
B.explanation: This reflects both efficiency and quality in the expansion decision.

C.text: Expand to all operations based solely on meeting the time target.
C.explanation: This widens the scope while serious failures remain.

D.text: Make usage volume the only new success metric.
D.explanation: This does not reveal or control the quality problem.

ai-business-strategist-practice-07@1.title: Causality and Sustained Business Outcomes
ai-business-strategist-practice-07@1.prompt: A department that rolled out agent assistance reduced processing time by 15%. During the same period, a pricing change increased the number of simple inquiries, and quality audit results are not yet available. Which evaluation is needed for the next investment decision?

learning.reason: This separates apparent improvement caused by a change in the mix of inquiries and can also detect a decline in quality.
learning.concept: Define business KPIs in advance for a pilot, and include a control group and quality guardrails.

A.text: Use a comparison group with similar inquiry types and workload, and measure both repeat-inquiry rates and processing time.
A.explanation: This separates apparent improvement caused by a change in the mix of inquiries and can also detect a decline in quality.

B.text: Apply the reduction rate across the company and commit to the investment.
B.explanation: This does not separate the rollout’s effect from the change in inquiry mix.

C.text: Compare before and after results using only the best-performing employees.
C.explanation: Selection bias and changes in the inquiry mix remain.

D.text: Use the number of times the assistance tool is used as a KPI and treat it as an outcome.
D.explanation: This shows adoption but is not directly tied to business outcomes.

ai-business-strategist-practice-08@1.title: Sequencing Rollouts by Risk Level
ai-business-strategist-practice-08@1.prompt: The same foundation model is being considered for summarizing internal meeting minutes and advising on whether customers should be approved for loans. Executives want to see benefits soon, but they do not allow automation of high-impact decisions before validation.

learning.reason: This balances phased value realization with controls proportionate to risk.
learning.concept: In addition to model-level approval, define the intended use, impact, and stop conditions for each business activity.

A.text: Because the model is the same, use the same approval process for both business activities and roll them out at the same time.
A.explanation: This does not account for the difference in impact between use contexts.

B.text: Automate the loan use case first because its benefits are greater, and measure quality afterward.
B.explanation: This automates a high-risk use case before validation, which is not allowed.

C.text: Assess the suitability of the loan use case based only on the cost of summarizing meeting minutes.
C.explanation: This substitutes one decision for assessments of different outcomes and risks.

D.text: Classify use cases by impact, roll out lower-risk activities first, and design validation and human approval for high-risk use cases in advance.
D.explanation: This balances phased value realization with controls proportionate to risk.

ai-business-strategist-practice-09@1.title: Identify the cause of low adoption
ai-business-strategist-practice-09@1.prompt: The support AI meets the quality standards, but frontline adoption is low. Users report more copying into a separate tab and say the exception-handling process is unclear. What should be prioritized?

learning.reason: This reduces workflow friction and operational uncertainty, making it possible to evaluate the benefits of adoption.
learning.concept: Assess adoption problems by separating model quality, workflow integration, and ownership and training.

A.text: Increase only the model size
A.explanation: The problem lies in the workflow, not in model quality.

B.text: Redesign the workflow with frontline staff, integrate the AI into existing tools, and clarify exception ownership and training
B.explanation: This reduces workflow friction and operational uncertainty, making it possible to evaluate the benefits of adoption.

C.text: Pause quality audits until adoption improves
C.explanation: Reducing safety does not remove workflow barriers.

D.text: Require everyone to use the AI while leaving the workflow unchanged
D.explanation: Usage may increase, but the extra work and exception-handling issues will remain.

ai-business-strategist-practice-10@1.title: Align data terms for AI vendors
ai-business-strategist-practice-10@1.prompt: The sales department is comparing several AI vendors. Because customer inputs will be used, it wants to manage deletion deadlines and secondary use for retraining by contract, and obtain audit evidence in case it needs to switch vendors.

learning.reason: This evaluates the organization’s data controls independently of price and performance.
learning.concept: Vendor evaluation covers not only business outcomes but also data handling and exit requirements.

A.text: Require vendors to encrypt data and nothing more
A.explanation: Encryption does not define secondary use or deletion deadlines.

B.text: Choose the lowest-priced candidate and review the contract after the pilot
B.explanation: Data already submitted could be retained under terms that have not been reviewed.

C.text: Make retention, deletion, secondary use, and audit access acceptance criteria, and compare each candidate’s contract and operational evidence
C.explanation: This evaluates the organization’s data controls independently of price and performance.

D.text: Measure only accuracy with input-output tests
D.explanation: This cannot assess contractual terms for retention or secondary use.
